docs.title: GIAP
docs.text:
GIAP (genome-integrated analysis of proteomics data) takes one assembled bacterial genome plus proteomics evidence and asks: what does genome context explain about which proteins are detected, and how abundant they are?

GIAP runs after your proteomics search; it does not search spectra itself. It:

  • places peptides and proteins on the genome, with its own error control (placement FDR);
  • builds one gene table keyed by Bakta locus tags, with detection tiers and gene q-values;
  • tests genome context: regions, autocorrelation along the chromosome, abundance islands, operons, function and the sequence determinants of abundance;
  • calls REF/ALT residues at covered codons and finds novel ORFs and start sites;
  • writes standard tables with schemas, plots with their data, and a self-contained HTML report.

Every claim carries a q-value, an FDR, an FWER or the label unestimated, and GIAP says "detected", never "expressed".

docs.text:

  • Set up the databases once with giap setup.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
How a GIAP release is prepared, approved and published. Agents prepare everything and run dry runs. Khoa is the only one who approves, publishes and sets up accounts.

Two rules for every agent

Agents never push tags, and never dispatch release.yml with dry_run=false. Tags and GitHub releases come only from the github-release job of release.yml, run by Khoa's dispatch (GIAP_SPEC.md §3.10). An agent that finds a step it cannot do without breaking one of these rules stops and asks Khoa through PROGRESS › Questions for Khoa.

Each numbered step names one actor in bold:

  • agent: a subagent in its role (docs, validation, implementer).
  • lead: the main session.
  • Khoa: the account owner.

Each step also gives the exact command or web page, and the evidence to record in PROGRESS.md. <v> is the version (PEP 440, matching ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(rc\d+)?$, e.g. 1.0.0 or 1.0.0rc1). <base> is <v> without its rc suffix (1.0.0 for both 1.0.0rc1 and 1.0.0). No step needs a token in a file or a command line (R12): trusted publishing uses OIDC, and the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN is the only credential it uses.

The workflow inputs, from .github/workflows/release.yml:

input type default meaning version string, required none must equal giap.__version__ on the dispatched commit dry_run boolean true verify, build, smoke and notes only: no upload, no tag target choice testpypi, pypi testpypi the index for an upload when dry_run is false

The workflow refuses to run in these cases:

  • it was dispatched on any ref other than refs/heads/main;
  • the version does not match the pattern above;
  • the version input differs from giap.__version__;
  • tag v<v> already exists.

The publish job needs three things: dry_run false, github.actor == 'khoa-yelo', and approval of the target environment. The github-release job also needs target == 'pypi'. A TestPyPI upload therefore never creates a tag.

docs.title: A. Once, before the first release
1. PyPI and TestPyPI pending publishers (Khoa)
docs.text:
• PyPI: https://pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/ → "Add a new pending publisher" → GitHub. Enter PyPI project name giap, owner khoa-yelo, repository giap, workflow name release.yml, environment name pypi.
  • TestPyPI: https://test.pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/ → the same form. Enter PyPI project name giap, owner khoa-yelo, repository giap, workflow name release.yml, environment name testpypi.
  • Evidence: PROGRESS line "Q-K1 done: pending publishers on PyPI and TestPyPI (date)".

docs.title: 2. GitHub environments pypi and testpypi (Khoa)
docs.text:
• GitHub → khoa-yelo/giap → Settings → Environments → New environment. Create pypi, then testpypi. For each one:
    • Deployment protection rules → Required reviewers → khoa-yelo.
    • Leave "Prevent self-review" off: Khoa both dispatches and approves.
    • Deployment branches and tags → Selected branches → main.
  • Add no environment secrets. Trusted publishing needs none.
  • Evidence: PROGRESS line "Q-K2 done: environments pypi/testpypi, reviewer khoa-yelo, main only".

docs.title: 3. Zenodo GitHub integration (Khoa)
docs.text:
• https://zenodo.org → log in with GitHub → account menu → GitHub → switch on khoa-yelo/giap. Zenodo lists only public repositories, so this needs §14.8 item 7 (making the repository public) done first. Zenodo reads its metadata from CITATION.cff. There is no .zenodo.json.
  • From then on, every published GitHub release (step 13) is archived and gets a DOI.
  • If this step is skipped, the release still works. The DOI is missing, the post-release PR (step 15) waits, and the lead records it under PROGRESS › Questions for Khoa.
  • Evidence: PROGRESS line "Q-K3 done: Zenodo integration on".

docs.title: 4. GitHub Pages (Khoa)
docs.text:
• GitHub → Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source "GitHub Actions" (Q-K9).
  • GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → Variables → New repository variable PAGES_ENABLED = true. The deploy job of docs.yml runs only on main and only when vars.PAGES_ENABLED == 'true'. Until then, docs.yml only builds the site (mkdocs build --strict) and uploads the Pages artefact.
  • Pages on a private repository needs a paid GitHub plan, so on a free plan this step also waits for §14.8 item 7 (making the repository public).
  • GitHub creates the github-pages environment itself. Leave it as GitHub sets it up.
  • Evidence: PROGRESS line "Q-K9 done", and the URL of the first green deploy job.

docs.title: 5. GHCR package visibility (Khoa)
docs.text:
• Do this after all five packages exist: ghcr.io/khoa-yelo/giap-<tool> for promotech, promoter_calculator, terminatornet, bactermfinder and ostir. A containers.yml run started by a push builds only the tools whose workflow/containers/<tool>/ or workflow/envs/<tool>.yml changed. To build all five, the lead dispatches gh workflow run containers.yml -f tools=all. Packages are private on first push.
  • For each of the five: GitHub → profile → Packages → giap-<tool> → Package settings → Danger Zone → Change visibility → Public (Q-K8).
  • There is never a giap-uniop package. UniOP is unlicensed and containers.yml refuses to build it (R5, R11).
  • Until a package is public, Apptainer pulls it on FarmShare with 401 or 403, the M11-06 smoke reports private package, and the digest PR stays a draft.
  • Evidence: PROGRESS line "Q-K8 done: five GHCR packages public".

docs.title: B. Each release: agent and lead
6. Release-prep PR m11/release-<v> (agent)
docs.text:
• Role: docs. The lead merges the PR after CI. Changes on the branch:
    • src/giap/__init__.py: __version__ = "<v>".
    • changelog.d/+known-limitations.misc.md: update it before the build. It lists the open non-gate issues (Q-K12). It must also carry the licence limit "geNOMAD is for non-commercial use only", which the fragment does not have today.
    • Run towncrier build --version <base> --date <YYYY-MM-DD> --yes. This turns the fragments into ## GIAP <base> (<YYYY-MM-DD>) in CHANGELOG.md and removes them.
    • CITATION.cff: set version: <v> and date-released: <YYYY-MM-DD>.
  • The rc path: the towncrier --version is always <base>, never <v> with rc.
    • notes.py 1.0.0rc1 reads the ## GIAP 1.0.0 ( section and adds "Release candidate 1.0.0rc1 of GIAP 1.0.0." in front of it. A ## GIAP 1.0.0rc1 (…) heading is never read, and the build job would exit 1.
    • So one ## GIAP 1.0.0 (…) section serves 1.0.0rc1 and the final 1.0.0.
    • The final 1.0.0 prep PR after an rc changes only __version__ and CITATION.cff (version, date-released). It builds no changelog: the fragments are already consumed, and the section stays as the rc PR wrote it.
    • That PR changes src/, so it is a new R. Steps 7–8 run again and overwrite validation/release/1.0.0/.
  • scripts/ci/check_changelog.py exempts this PR only through its commit subjects: every non-merge commit has to be of type chore, e.g. chore(release): <v>. If the check fails anyway, add the no-changelog label and push again. Labels are read from the push event, and a re-run reuses the old labels.
  • The merged commit is R. Release freeze from R until step 13, recorded in PROGRESS:
    • Merge only PRs whose every changed path is paperwork in readiness.py's sense: PROGRESS.md, README.md, CITATION.cff, CHANGELOG.md, or a path under validation/release/, docs/ (but not docs/methods/) or changelog.d/.
    • Any other path, such as src/, workflow/, tests/, scripts/, .github/, ci/, benchmarks/, pyproject.toml or uv.lock, makes readiness.py verify fail with fail (stale: <path>).
    • release.yml builds main's HEAD, so such a merge makes the PyPI publish fail at verify.
  • Evidence: PR URL and the SHA of R.

docs.title: 7. Evidence runs on R (agent)
docs.text:
• Role: validation, on FarmShare. Fast-forward the main checkout to R first. Source scripts/farmshare_env.sh. Before each sbatch, add up the running and pending CPUs of the giap-* jobs (R14: at most 128 CPUs, 4 GPUs and 20 jobs).
    • bash scripts/slurm/calibration_full_launch.sh origin/main: pins a worktree at R, checks the R14 budget (a launch queues 16 jobs; it refuses when its worst-case end reaches the 01:30 nightly), then submits the 15-task calibration_full.sbatch array and an afterany aggregator that writes the calibration_full and calibration_attacks rows to $GIAP_ROOT/logs/nightly.tsv. It prints array=<id> rows=<id> log=<dir> throttle=<T>.
    • sbatch --array=2 scripts/slurm/nightly.sbatch: the fast suite with the calibration_nightly tier, on origin/main. Its row goes to $GIAP_ROOT/logs/nightly.tsv, labelled calibration_nightly. A single task also posts a one-task table to the "Nightly (FarmShare)" issue. Add --export=ALL,NIGHTLY_POST=dry to print the table instead.
    • sbatch scripts/slurm/weekly.sbatch: K-12 and Nissle end to end with TE6, TE8 and TE2, on origin/main. Its rows go to $GIAP_ROOT/logs/weekly.tsv.
    • sbatch scripts/slurm/test_branch.sbatch "$PWD": the full fast suite on 16 CPUs. The last log line is PYTEST_EXIT=<code>.
  • Poll with squeue -j <id> and sacct -j <id>.
  • Evidence: every job ID and its exit status in PROGRESS.

docs.title: 8. Readiness on R, paperwork-only PR (agent)
docs.text:
• Role: validation, on FarmShare.
  • Wait until every CI check run of R on main has finished. A check that is still running has a null conclusion, and then H6 is pending. verify does not recompute H6 later, because H6's source is farmshare.

  • Work in a worktree on a new branch at R, never by committing in the main checkout:

    git worktree add -b m11/readiness-<v> local/worktrees/readiness-<v> <R>

  • In that worktree, run:

    python scripts/release/readiness.py compute --version <v> --logs "$GIAP_ROOT/logs" \
    --freeze-run <A2 freeze run dir> --out validation/release/<base>/

  • This writes readiness.json and READINESS.md. Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 fail, 3 pending.

  • Do not use --offline. Row H6 reads the commit's check runs with gh api. Without network, save that response and pass it with --check-runs <file>.
  • The directory is <base>, also for an rc. release.yml reads validation/release/${VERSION%%rc*}/readiness.json.
  • Open a PR docs(release): readiness <v> that changes only these two files, and merge it. It is paperwork, so readiness.py verify still accepts R as the readiness commit.

  • Check on the merged main:

    python scripts/release/readiness.py verify validation/release/<base>/readiness.json

    This prints commit rule: pass and overall: pass, with exit 0. - Evidence: PR URL, overall, the rows that are not pass.

docs.title: 9. Dry run of release.yml (lead)
docs.text:
gh workflow run release.yml -f version=<v> -f dry_run=true
gh run list --workflow release.yml --event workflow_dispatch --user khoa-yelo --limit 1 \
    --json databaseId,url,headSha,status,conclusion
gh run download <run id> -n release -D local/review/m11-release/r<k>/
  • Check that the listed run's headSha is main's HEAD, so it is the run just started.
  • A dry run renders the notes with notes.py <v> --draft and publishes nothing.
  • The step summary should say dry run: nothing published. It also lists the readiness overall and the sha256 of each artefact.
  • Evidence: the run URL and the head SHA in PROGRESS.

docs.title: 10. Review packet and hand-off (lead)
docs.text:
• local/review/m11-release/r<k>/ holds:
    • READINESS.md;
    • the dry-run step summary;
    • notes.md and dist/, from step 9;
    • sha256sum dist/*;
    • the list of open non-gate issues.
  • Add a PROGRESS › Questions for Khoa row "Approve release <v>". The step-8 PR is already merged, so open an issue Release <v>: approval that links the packet, label it needs-khoa, and message Khoa.
  • Evidence: the packet path and the PROGRESS row.

docs.title: 11. Written approval (Khoa)
docs.text:
• Khoa replies "approved" (§14.8 item 5). The lead copies Khoa's words into PROGRESS before any dispatch.
  • A row that needs a waiver gets an ADR with the header Status: accepted-by-khoa and the line Waives readiness <id> first. Then step 8 runs again.

docs.title: 12. Rehearsal on TestPyPI (Khoa)
docs.text:
• Required for the first release, optional later.
  • Start the run from Actions → release → Run workflow (branch main) with version=<v>, dry_run=false, target=testpypi. From Khoa's own shell, the same run is gh workflow run release.yml -f version=<v> -f dry_run=false -f target=testpypi.
  • On the run page: Review deployments → testpypi → Approve and deploy.

  • Check the install in a fresh venv:

    pip install -i https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/ giap==<v>

  • This occupies <v> on TestPyPI only. PyPI is a separate index, so step 13 is unaffected.

  • No tag and no GitHub release are created.

docs.title: 13. The release (Khoa)
docs.text:
• Start the run from Actions → release → Run workflow (branch main) with version=<v>, dry_run=false, target=pypi, then approve the pypi environment.
  • Verify fails if readiness is missing, does not verify, or is not pass (waived rows count as pass only through accepted ADRs).
  • The workflow then:
    • uploads the wheel and sdist;
    • tags v<v> on the dispatched commit;
    • creates the GitHub release "GIAP <v>" with notes.md (a pre-release for an rc).
  • Zenodo mints the DOI.
  • Evidence: the run URL, which the lead records.

docs.title: 14. PyPI install smoke on FarmShare (agent)
docs.text:
• Role: validation, inside the Slurm allocation, never on a login node. Use a fresh venv outside the checkout, with PYTHONPATH unset, and run from the main checkout's root (for the two input files):

    smoke=$(mktemp -d /tmp/giap-smoke.XXXXXX)
uv venv "$smoke/venv" --python 3.12
VIRTUAL_ENV="$smoke/venv" uv pip install giap==<v>
"$smoke/venv/bin/giap" --version
"$smoke/venv/bin/giap" version --json
"$smoke/venv/bin/giap" preflight --genome tests/data/genomes/sim100k.fna.gz \
    --proteins tests/data/recorded/miniprot/0.18/sim100k/proteins.faa

  • The expected results:

    • giap --version prints giap, version <v>;
    • the JSON has "giap": "<v>";
    • preflight exits 0.
  • Evidence: a PROGRESS line with the three outputs.

docs.title: 15. Post-release PR (agent)
docs.text:
• Role: implementer and docs. Open docs(release): DOI and badges for <v>.
  • Add CITATION.cff › identifiers: the Zenodo concept DOI and the version DOI, both from the Zenodo record page.
  • Add the README DOI badge.
  • __version__ stays <v> until the next release-prep PR.
  • If Zenodo has no record (step 3 skipped), the PR waits and the lead notes it under PROGRESS › Questions for Khoa.

docs.title: 16. Bioconda recipe (agent)
docs.text:
• Render the recipe with M11-10's scripts/release/bioconda_recipe.py, using the PyPI sdist sha256 (https://pypi.org/pypi/giap/<v>/json) and the DOI. This script is not merged yet; take its options from M11-10 once it is. Its spec writes <out>/giap/meta.yaml, so --out recipes gives recipes/giap/meta.yaml.
  • Hand recipes/giap/meta.yaml to Khoa.
  • Khoa then forks bioconda/bioconda-recipes, adds the recipe and opens the PR from their own account. Agents never open PRs in other organisations' repositories. The bioconda CI does the lint and build checks there.

docs.title: 17. PROGRESS record (lead)
docs.text:
• Add PROGRESS › Done "Release <v>" with:
    • the PyPI URL, the tag v<v>, the release URL and the DOI;
    • the Bioconda PR, the readiness file and Khoa's approval.
  • End the release freeze.
  • Run git fetch, then python scripts/dev/progress_bars.py --write, then commit and push.

docs.title: E. If something fails
docs.text:
• PyPI upload done, github-release failed:
    • First choice: Khoa opens the original run and uses "Re-run failed jobs". This reuses the same commit and the release artefact that run built. Only github-release and summary run again, and github.actor stays the original dispatcher.
    • Only if that is impossible: Khoa dispatches again with the same inputs.
      • A new dispatch rebuilds from main's HEAD at that moment. If main has moved past the paperwork set, readiness is stale and verify fails.
      • The tag does not exist yet, so the tag check passes.
      • publish reads https://pypi.org/pypi/giap/<v>/json. It skips the upload when every file already on the index has the same sha256 as the new build.
      • It stops with <file> is on the index with a different sha256 when the rebuild is not byte-identical. Then ask Khoa: the options are a patch release, or Khoa creating the GitHub release by hand.
  • Wrong artefact on PyPI: never delete it. Khoa yanks it in the PyPI web UI, and the fix ships as the next patch version.
  • Readiness fail or pending: nothing is published. Fix it through the normal feature loop, or through a waiver ADR that Khoa accepts. Then repeat steps 6–8 on the new commit.
  • Tag v<v> already exists (someone made it by hand): release.yml refuses to run. Ask Khoa.
  • Any non-paperwork PR merged after R (see the release freeze in step 6): readiness.py verify fails with fail (stale: <path>). Repeat steps 6–8 on the new commit.

docs.title: Script reference
docs.text:
These options are read from the argparse definitions in scripts/release/.

readiness.py compute:

option required meaning --version V yes version recorded in the JSON --repo DIR no, default . checkout read at HEAD (the readiness commit) --logs DIR no directory with nightly.tsv and weekly.tsv ($GIAP_ROOT/logs) --freeze-run DIR no A2 freeze run; R2 falls back to mapping/mapping_fdr.tsv there --out DIR yes writes readiness.json and READINESS.md --offline no touches no network; H6 becomes pending --check-runs FILE no a saved gh api …/commits/<sha>/check-runs response for H6

readiness.py verify READINESS_JSON [--repo DIR] checks two things:

  • the commit rule: the readiness commit is HEAD, or an ancestor that differs from HEAD only in paperwork (PROGRESS.md, README.md, CITATION.cff, CHANGELOG.md, validation/release/, docs/ except docs/methods/, and changelog.d/);
  • the repo rows, which it recomputes on HEAD.

It exits 0 on pass and 1 otherwise.

Other scripts:

  • notes.py VERSION [--draft]: run from the repository root. It reads the ## GIAP <version> (...) section of CHANGELOG.md (the base version's section for an rc) and writes notes.md. --draft falls back to towncrier build --draft and heads the notes DRAFT. It exits 1 when the section is missing (without --draft) or empty.
  • check_dist.py DIST_DIR [--version V]: checks the wheel and sdist. It prints ok <artefact> or FAIL <artefact>: <rule>: <path>. Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 violations, 2 when DIST_DIR has no wheel or no sdist.
  • update_digests.py --digests FILE --date YYYY-MM-DD --source-commit SHA [--config FILE] [--nextflow-config FILE]: used by containers.yml. It pins ghcr.io/khoa-yelo/giap-<tool>@sha256:… in workflow/conf/containers.config. With --nextflow-config, it also adds the pinned processes to the apptainer conda = '' selector.
  • check_changelog.py BASE (in scripts/ci/): a PR that changes src/ or workflow/ (except workflow/tests/) must add changelog.d/<PR>.<type>.md or changelog.d/+<slug>.<type>.md. The types are feature, bugfix, doc, removal and misc. A PR is exempt with the label no-changelog (read from the push event, so push again after adding it), or when every non-merge commit subject is of type test, ci, chore or refactor.

docs.title: Output tables
docs.text:
readiness.json has the top-level keys version, commit, computed, overall and rows. It also has notes, a list. overall is fail if any row fails, else pending if any row is pending, else pass.

Each row has these fields:

field content id R1–R10 (§13.2 criteria), H1–H6 (housekeeping: gates, version and tag, changelog, digests, licences, CI) criterion the spec's words status pass, fail, pending or waived value, threshold the reading and the rule evidence files, log rows, ADRs waiver ADR-NNNN or null source repo, farmshare or both; verify recomputes the repo rows

READINESS.md renders the same rows with the columns id | criterion | status | value | threshold | evidence | source. It is headed by the commit, the computed time and the overall status, and ends with Notes. Runs of seven or more amino-acid letters are redacted (M10-05 guard).

The release.yml step summary has two tables:

  • field | value: version, sha, readiness overall, and published. published reads dry run: nothing published, or publish skipped: actor <x> is not khoa-yelo, or the publish and release results.
  • artefact | sha256, one row per file in dist/.

docs.title: Licences of the tools GIAP runs
docs.text:
GIAP is MIT-licensed. This section follows NOTICE.md, which is the authoritative list, and readiness row H5 checks the registry against it. scripts/ci/check_imports.py fails CI if GIAP imports a GPL, AGPL or unlicensed tool.

Tool Licence (as in NOTICE.md) How GIAP uses it Bakta GPL-3.0 separate process Promotech GPL-3.0 separate process Promoter Calculator GPL-3.0 (or later) separate process OSTIR GPL-3.0 separate process TransTermHP GPL-3.0 (or later) separate process BacTermFinder GPL-3.0 opt-in; separate process antiSMASH AGPL-3.0 separate process geNOMAD non-commercial separate process; non-commercial use only UniOP unlicensed (no licence file) fetched at a pinned commit when environments are built; never vendored TerminatorNet, miniprot MIT separate process BLAST+ public-domain (NCBI) separate process fgsea MIT run by workflow/bin/giap_fgsea.R in R 4.5 (GPL-2) as a separate process; R and fgsea are never imported codon-bias MIT imported in-process (PyPI) DIA-NN proprietary (academic licence) used only by users' own searches; binaries never redistributed

What this means for a release:

  • GPL and AGPL tools run as separate programs. GIAP never imports or vendors their code (R5). The wheel and sdist carry none of their code.
  • fgsea is also ported. Its MIT code is ported to Python in src/giap/stats/fgsea.py, which runs in-process. NOTICE.md carries the MIT licence text, and no fgsea file is vendored.

  • Four GHCR images contain GPL-3.0 tools, fetched from upstream unmodified:

    • Promotech;
    • Promoter Calculator (GPL-3.0-or-later);
    • OSTIR;
    • BacTermFinder.

    NOTICE.md gives their source links at the pinned versions and commits. Each image's Dockerfile is in workflow/containers/<tool>/. The fifth image, TerminatorNet, is MIT. - UniOP is never published. There is no GHCR image for it (R5, R11). - geNOMAD: non-commercial use only. Step 6 adds this to the known-limitations fragment, so the release notes say it. - Data resources: - KEGG: academic use; giap setup --kegg downloads it on the user's machine; - RegulonDB: not redistributed; - Gene Ontology: CC BY 4.0; - NCBI COG 2020: NCBI FTP. - The contaminant library (Frankenfield et al. 2022) has no licence file. giap setup --contaminants downloads it, and it is never vendored (R11). - plotly.js (MIT) is inlined once in report.html when interactive figures are shown.

docs.title: Open questions for Khoa
docs.text:
• The actor guard cannot tell agents from Khoa. The FarmShare gh login is khoa-yelo, so a dispatch from an agent session also has github.actor == 'khoa-yelo'. The publish job's only remaining barrier is then the environment approval, and the same login could approve it through the API. Two fixes are recommended:
    • a separate agent account with write access, for the FarmShare gh login: the actor guard then works, and dry runs still dispatch;
    • or a fine-grained token without actions:write: agents can then not dispatch at all, and Khoa runs step 9.
  • PRs opened with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger CI. containers.yml opens the digest PR ci/digests-<sha7> as a draft with the workflow token, so no CI starts when it opens.
    • The normal path: ci.yml also runs on ready_for_review. Once the FarmShare Apptainer smoke passes, gh pr ready <PR> from the khoa-yelo login starts CI.
    • Fallbacks: a plain git commit --allow-empty pushed to that branch from FarmShare, or Khoa closing and reopening the PR.
    • A GitHub App token, or the agent account above, would remove the gap.
  • R3 and R4 writers (M11-03b, done). nightly.sbatch task 2 writes calibration_nightly; calibration_full_launch.sh (step 7) writes calibration_full and calibration_attacks. A collection error, a missing suite or an attack row with no attack tests fails closed. The first real full-tier run should confirm that task 13's attack test is never all-skipped.
  • Who may dispatch dry runs. The default is that the lead may: a dry run uploads nothing and creates no tag (M11-04). AGENTS.md › Releases already states the two rules above.

docs.title: ADR-0001: Import the settled decisions of GIAP_SPEC.md §2.1 and §2.4

docs.title: Context

docs.title: Decision

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)

docs.title: ADR-0003: giapsim.simulate takes an explicit output directory
docs.text:
• Status: accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: §11.3 gives the entry point as giapsim.simulate(config: SimConfig, seed: int) -> SimResult and says it "writes a directory of inputs plus truth", without naming where the directory comes from.

docs.title: Decision

docs.title: ADR-0004: One-off PR-size exemption for M0, and symlink-safe path protection
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-14)
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §0.2 R3, §14.6, Appendix A.4
  • Needs Khoa: yes (a gate exception and a change to a protected file)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
1. PR size. The guard in ci.yml fails a PR above 800 changed lines (ci/gates.yaml, pr_lines_fail), excluding lock files and fixtures. The M0 scaffold PR (#1) changes about 4,800 lines plus the 3,262-line GIAP_SPEC.md: the spec itself, the Appendix A templates, CI, the probe, the full CLI option surface of §5.1, the config model of §5.2 and the simulator. Splitting it into 6+ PRs would add review overhead without adding review value, because most of it is verbatim spec content.
  2. Hook bypass. .claude/hooks/protect_paths.py compares paths with os.path.abspath, which does not resolve symlinks. On FarmShare /farmshare/home/classes is a symlink to /home/classes, so an Edit addressed through the /farmshare/... path to ci/gates.yaml is not blocked (reproduced by the code reviewer). The hook is protected (.claude/hooks/*), so the agent may not change it on its own.

docs.title: Decision (proposed)
docs.text:
1. PR #1 (M0 scaffold) may merge with the PR-size guard failing. No gate value changes; later PRs follow the 400/800-line rule.
  2. Change two lines in .claude/hooks/protect_paths.py: 
    root = os.path.realpath(os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR", os.getcwd()))
...
rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.realpath(path), root)
    Merged with the trailer Gate-Change-Approved: ADR-0004 once Khoa sets this ADR to accepted-by-khoa.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text:
• PR #1 guard log: changed lines: 8058 (warn 400, fail 800) (includes the spec).
  • Hook today (rc 2 = blocked): project root and file path spelled the same way → 2; spelled differently (/home/classes/... vs /farmshare/home/classes/..., either direction) → 0. The session's $PWD is the /farmshare/... spelling, so the mismatch is easy to hit. With realpath on both, all four combinations give 2.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: CI remains the backstop for protected files in any case (scripts/ci/check_protected.py).

docs.title: ADR-0005: Decisions on M1 input handling left open by the spec
docs.text:
• Status: accepted (items 1–3); item 4 rejected by Khoa (2026-10-14)
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §5.3, §5.4, §7.0, §9.2
  • Needs Khoa: answered: item 4 rejected

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The M1 issue specs (docs/specs/M1-*.md) list "Questions for the lead". The lead accepts the spec-writer's proposed defaults (R10) and records them here.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Formats. Genome FASTA: U and - are errors; unsafe ID characters map to _, and IDs that collide after mapping are duplicate-ID errors. Proteins: group ID = resolved accessions joined by ;; O, digits and - are counted as "other" with a warning. proBed missing values are .; a BED score outside 0–1000 raises. VCF header ##reference=sha256:<hex>; a codon crossing the origin raises in the VCF writer (M7 decides how to report it). GFF3: every replicon gets a ##sequence-region pragma; only circular replicons also get a region feature with Is_circular=true; read_gff3 skips GIAP's own region lines. After the M1-05 review: CDS features must carry a phase (GFF3 3.1.26; overrides the issue's "phase None → ." edge case); the reader accepts strand ?, rejects duplicate attribute keys and invalid percent-escapes, and accepts only plain digits for coordinates. VCF: INFO/FORMAT keys must be declared in the header; NaN → ., bool → Flag, empty lists and | inside FLAGS items are errors; REF/ALT are uppercase [ACGTN]+, ALT ≠ REF, same length, GT within the ALT count; header text may not contain control characters; contig IDs must be safe IDs. REF is checked against the genome only when the caller passes the sequences (optional argument). A FILTER value other than PASS gets a generic ##FILTER header line; M7 replaces these with explicit descriptions when it defines GIAP's filters (docs/backlog.md).
  2. Peptide and abundance tables. Median across runs uses only runs where the peptide was quantified. The generic reader warns and drops rows with modification syntax (stripping is giap convert's job) and peptides > 40 aa. Mixed source for one peptide: database wins, with a warning. DIA-NN PG.MaxLFQ is collapsed across runs by median; intensity 0 → NA; the user passes --abundance-type maxlfq. After the M1-06 review: rows with any error-level issue (bad type, out of range, nan/inf text in q_value, pep or intensity) are dropped from the evidence frame and peptide_runs, and the issue is still reported, so a malformed q-value can never pass as evidence. Rows sharing (run, spectrum_id, stripped peptide, charge) are one spectrum's evidence: de-duplicated before intensities are summed (first row kept), with the warning duplicate_spectrum_row; different modified forms of one stripped peptide on one spectrum count once. duplicate_spectrum_id (error; rows dropped) fires only when one (run, spectrum_id) carries different stripped peptides. Summing modified forms (§5.3) applies across different spectra. protein_ids entries are stripped. Precedence when rows disagree: search_db same > other > auto; source database > denovo > auto. Abundance IDs resolve UniProt accessions as in proteins.faa; linear zeros are not "missing"; a header row is required.
  3. Preflight. Every evaluated rule is recorded (level: ok when it passes); coordinates in preflight.json are 1-based closed; exit-code precedence 1 > 2 > 3. The chromosome-size threshold reuses preflight.min_largest_contig_warn. The abundance join check runs only when at least one ID matches a protein; otherwise it is reported as deferred (info). Without --outdir, preflight prints its summary and writes nothing. A missing db_manifest.json is info under giap preflight and an error under giap run until M2 lands. Proteins of 7–40 aa become peptide rows.
  4. New warning thresholds: rejected by Khoa (2026-10-14). No new config keys. The decoy share and free RAM/disk are reported as Info only; the only resource warning is §7.0's ≥ 24 GB for genome-wide Promotech; "no row passes input.q_value_max" stays a warning (existing key). Original proposal: preflight.decoy_share_warn: 0.5 (warn when ≥ half the peptide rows are decoys); warn when no row passes input.q_value_max (no new key); preflight.min_free_ram_gb: 8 (24 GB is already implied for genome-wide Promotech, §7.0); preflight.min_free_disk_gb: 10.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: Unit tests per issue (T-PRE-* rules); no defaults change for existing keys.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: M1-10/M1-11 implement the Info-only behaviour above.

docs.title: ADR-0006: Encoding of special values in GIAP tables, and strict BED writing
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §6.6, §9.2, §9.5
  • Needs Khoa: no (fills a gap; no default, threshold or interface changes)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: §6.6 fixes %.6g for floats but does not say how infinities, NaN or list cells are written. Tables are validated with Frictionless (§9.5), whose default number type reads INF, -INF and NaN, not Python's lowercase inf. The M1-04 review also found that malformed BED12 blocks and thick ranges were silently clamped.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Floats: finite values %.6g; +inf → INF, -inf → -INF; NaN and missing → NA.
  2. List cells are joined with ;; an item containing ; or a missing item is an error. proBed's modifications field uses , as its format requires.
  3. BED/proBed writers validate instead of clamping: BED12 blocks must start at 0, be sorted and non-overlapping, and end at the record length; the thick range must lie inside the interval; names may not contain whitespace; scores are integers 0–1000 (bool rejected). Asking for BED6 output while passing thick or colour fields is an error.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: Review of M1-04 (manual mutations survived; clamping reproduced on 100–200 → 110–160).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Readers map INF/-INF back to ±inf and NA to missing.

docs.title: ADR-0007: The PR-size guard counts code, not tests or docs
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-14)
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §14.2, §14.6 (PR size), ci/gates.yaml (pr_lines_warn, pr_lines_fail)
  • Needs Khoa: yes (changes how a gate is measured; the 400/800 values stay)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
§14.2 asks for PRs of about 400 changed lines "excluding lock files and fixtures", and CI warns above 400 and fails above 800. In practice the test-first loop (R2) plus independent review makes tests the bulk of every PR. The first four M1 issues, each one small module:

PR src tests docs/other total M1-01 coordinates (#2) 157 462 211 830 M1-02 genome FASTA (#3) 169 527 92 788 M1-03 protein FASTA (#4) 123 469 81 673 M1-04 TSV/BED/proBed 329 976 126 1,431

The guard fails #2 and M1-04 for their tests (review findings added 100–300 test lines each), which pushes toward thinner tests, the opposite of R2 and the calibration culture of §8.

docs.title: Decision (proposed)
docs.text: Count only code under src/, workflow/ and scripts/ toward pr_lines_warn (400) and pr_lines_fail (800). Tests, docs, ADRs, specs, lock files and fixtures are reported in the PR summary but not gated. The values in ci/gates.yaml do not change; only ci.yml's counting does.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: With code-only counting, all four PRs above pass (157, 169, 123, 329 lines), and M1-04 sits under the 400-line warning.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Reviewers still see the full diff. A PR that adds 1,000 lines of tests for 50 lines of code is fine; a PR that adds 900 lines of code still fails.

docs.title: ADR-0008: Annotation tool pins, image digests and licences (M2-01)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §3.1, §3.2, §4, §6.3, §7.1.1, §17, R5; M2-index lead decisions 1 and 8
  • Needs Khoa: no (lead decision 1 accepted pinning source-only tools to the default-branch commit)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: §7.1.1 fixes release versions for most tools but says only "pinned commit" for the four source-only tools, and "pin by digest" for images. M2-01 needs exact values for the registry (src/giap/annotate/tools.py), the env files (workflow/envs/*.yml), workflow/conf/containers.config and the Dockerfiles. All values below were resolved on 2026-10-14 with read-only queries against the §3.2/§18 sources (git ls-remote and the GitHub API, micromamba search on conda-forge + bioconda, the PyPI JSON API, and registry v2 manifests via scripts/resolve_digest.py).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Source-only tools: default-branch HEAD on 2026-10-14. Licences read from each repository's LICENSE at the pinned commit.

Read by disassembling model.pkl at the pinned commit with pickletools.dis (no unpickling): the MLPClassifier state carries _sklearn_version = '1.1.2'. Python 3.10.14, numpy 1.23.5, scipy 1.9.3. - BacTermFinder: Python 3.9.19 (README), the requirements.txt versions of the packages its scripts import (numpy 1.23.0, pandas 1.5.0, biopython 1.81, h5py 3.7.0, joblib 1.2.0, tqdm 4.64.1; pip tensorflow 2.8.0, keras 2.8.0, protobuf 3.20.0). - Promoter Calculator: Python 3.10.14 with biopython 1.84, numpy 1.26.4, scipy 1.14.1, scikit-learn 1.5.2 (the wheel declares them without versions and ships no pickled model). - OSTIR: Python 3.10.14, numpy 1.26.4, viennarna 2.6.4.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: tests/unit/annotate/ (M2-01) checks every pin, digest format, licence and env file. The envs are not built yet: sbatch scripts/slurm/build_envs.sbatch all will confirm that each env solves, and will write workflow/envs/locks/<tool>.explicit.txt.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Upgrading any pin, digest or commit needs a new ADR, a re-run of build_envs.sbatch and the contract-test diffs (§14.6). If an env does not solve (most likely Promotech or BacTermFinder), the next fallback is the Dockerfile path (§17), recorded in a follow-up ADR.

docs.title: ADR-0009: Picked gene-level FDR rescales decoy wins by the paired share
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-14)
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §7.3.2 (decision 4, picked target–decoy tier), §8.1
  • Needs Khoa: answered

docs.title: Context
docs.text: §7.3.2 uses picked gene-level target–decoy FDR when decoy rows can be paired with genes, and falls back to MAYU only when more than 20 % of decoys are unpaired. Unpaired decoys (proteins absent from the strain, IDs that do not map to the gene model) are dropped. The statistician's review of M4-01 (PR #19; docs/methods/target-decoy.md) showed that dropping 20 % of decoys at random inflates the true picked FDR to about 1.2× nominal (0.059 at q = 0.05; 0.122 at q = 0.10).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Picked gene-level FDR rescales the decoy-win count by the paired share: with a paired fraction f = n_paired_decoys / n_decoys, each decoy win counts as 1/f. The 20 % fallback to MAYU stays as an upper guard. The paired share and the rescaling factor are reported in detection_summary.tsv.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: Before: 20 % random decoy loss → FDP ≈ 1.2 × q. After: M4-12 must show FDP ≤ q + 2 SE under 10 %, 20 % and 30 % random decoy loss (calibration suite, plus an attack null in tests/calibration/attacks/).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Cross-strain searches (pilot arm A1) keep the picked tier with an honest estimate instead of falling back to MAYU more often.

docs.title: ADR-0010: Placement FDR with per-peptide π̂ weights each decoy hit by its own π̂ (M3-10)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §7.2.5, G3, §8.4; docs/specs/M3-10-placement-fdr.md; M3-index lead decision (M3-10 Q2)
  • Needs Khoa: no (reduces exactly to the §7.2.5 formula FDR_m(e) = π̂ (D_m(e) + 1) / T_m(e) when π̂ is constant; replaces only the lead's provisional rule for the per-peptide-π̂ case the spec leaves open)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: §7.2.5 gives FDR_m(e) = π̂_wrong (D_m(e) + 1) / T_m(e) with one π̂ per stratum. De novo input has a π̂ per peptide (score bin). The lead's provisional rule (M3-10 Q2) used the mean π̂ over TARGETS with E ≤ e. The M3-10 test-author found it anti-conservative and the statistician confirmed: targets are mostly correct, low-π̂ peptides, while decoy hits are chance hits of all searched peptides.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: FDR_m(e) = (W_m(e) + c) / T_m(e), where W_m(e) = Σ π̂_j over decoy hits with E ≤ e, each weighted by its own peptide's π̂ (missing → 1; strata m ≥ 1 → 1), and c = max π̂ over the peptides of that decoy type searched. One list ordered by E per stratum, same q-value monotonisation, ties and clipping as M4-01. mapping_fdr rows report fdr_stratum = (W + c)/T and pi_wrong = (W + c)/(D + 1). Signed in docs/methods/placement-fdr.md ("π̂_wrong in the stratum FDR"). Not adopted: separate lists per score bin (valid and more powerful on large inputs, but breaks "q monotone in E within a stratum"). Database input keeps π̂ = mean PEP (estimator (a)); M3-21 measures the PEP–length correlation that could make it anti-conservative and revisits this if it is material.

docs.title: Evidence (mean FDP at q = .01 / .05 / .10; N = 4000, R = 300; * = above q + 2 SE)
docs.text: Scenario Q2 (old) mean π̂ over all searched ADR-0010 10 score bins .0143* / .069* / .130* .0098 / .050 / .100 .0095 / .050 / .100 2 bins (π = .02 / .9) .035* / .119* / .175* .0097 / .050 / .100 .0095 / .050 / .100 2 bins, chance-hit rate tied to π .054* / .168* / .253* .0163* / .085* / .172* .0093 / .049 / .100 π̂ = 1.5 π .0099 / .049 / .094 .0072 / .037 / .073 .0069 / .036 / .073 constant π̂ .0100 / .050 / .097 same same π̂ = 0.5 π fails under every rule (≈ 2q): π̂ must come from the conservative bound (M3-11). Attack: tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_placement_pi.py.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• c ≈ 1 when any searched peptide has π̂ ≈ 1: small lists accept nothing at q = 0.01 (N = 150 → 0); at N = 4000, 1063 accepted vs 1086 for the (invalid in general) mean-over-all variant.
  • stratum_qvalues(e_target, e_decoy, pi_decoy, pi_plus) replaces the target-mean interface; M3-10 tests that pinned Q2 change accordingly; M3-index decision for M3-10 Q2 is superseded.

docs.title: ADR-0011: low_complexity placement flag (M3-10)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-14, in session: "Accept as proposed")
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §9.4 (placement flags), §7.2.5; M3-index lead decision (M3-10 low_complexity)
  • Needs Khoa: yes (adds a value to an output vocabulary)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The M3-09 statistician attack showed that the chance-hit score E underestimates hits of simple-sequence (repeat-like) peptides by 1.9× at L = 8 and 15× at L = 12. Placement FDR stays valid (decoys calibrate it), but users should see which accepted placements rest on low-complexity peptides. §9.4's placement flag vocabulary has no such value.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Add low_complexity to the §9.4 placement flags: set when the peptide has ≤ 3 distinct residues (I and L counted as one). Flags stay ;-joined. No effect on q-values.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: docs/methods/placement-fdr.md (chance-hit section, signed): E vs observed for simple-sequence repeats.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: mapping outputs gain one flag value; report text explains it. No threshold or default changes.

docs.title: ADR-0012: Promoter and terminator evidence for novel ORFs (Module 6)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-14: "when there is a novel orf, check for promoter and terminator nearby"; option "Evidence + ranking" chosen in session)
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §7.6.2, §7.6.3, §7.6.5, §9 tables/novel_orfs.tsv, §7.1.5 (terminators), decision 8 (promoters); config promotech_yes, terminatornet_yes
  • Needs Khoa: yes (adds output columns and a ranking key) — answered

docs.title: Context
docs.text: §7.6.2 already gives every novel-ORF candidate start a targeted Promotech window (−200 to +20) and novel_orfs.tsv reports promoter_score (ranking key 5). Nothing checks for a transcription terminator after a novel ORF. Khoa asked that novel ORFs be checked for a nearby promoter AND terminator. ORFs inside operons legitimately lack their own promoter or terminator, so neither is a calling requirement.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Terminator downstream. For each novel ORF, look for TerminatorNet calls already made genome-wide (§7.1.5; TransTermHP when --terminators transtermhp) on the same strand whose start lies between the stop codon and +300 nt downstream (circular replicons wrap). Report the best confidence.
  2. Promoter upstream. Keep §7.6.2's targeted Promotech window at the chosen start (−200 to +20); promoter_supported = promoter_score ≥ promotech_yes.
  3. Outputs (tables/novel_orfs.tsv, after promoter_score): promoter_supported (bool), terminator_downstream (bool: best confidence ≥ terminatornet_yes), terminator_conf (float or NA), terminator_distance_nt (int or NA). Flags: promoter_supported, terminator_supported. The novel-ORF GFF3 carries the same as attributes; locus plots (V3) already draw promoters and terminators.
  4. Ranking (§7.6.5): insert "terminator confidence, descending" after "promoter score, descending" and before "length, descending".
  5. Calling rules (§7.6.3) are unchanged: promoter/terminator evidence never gates a call.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: None needed for validity (reporting and tie-break only). Calibration of the cut-offs follows M2-13/M2-15 (RegulonDB at M6, §15.4).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Module 6 specs (M6) must implement items 1–4 and test: a terminator 0–300 nt downstream on the same strand is found, one on the other strand or beyond 300 nt is not, origin wrap, NA when no call.
  • No new config keys (reuses promotech_yes, terminatornet_yes; 300 nt is a module constant).

docs.title: ADR-0013: cterm_extension locus class (M3-14, Module 6)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-14, in session: "New class cterm_extension")
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §7.2.6 (locus classes), §7.6.1 (novel candidates), §7.6.3 (classes and evidence), §9
  • Needs Khoa: yes (adds a class value) — answered

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A peptide on the same strand and in frame with an annotated CDS (or sORF) can run across its 3′ end, past the annotated stop codon — stop-codon readthrough or a mis-annotated stop. §7.6.3 has no class for it: it is not cds_outframe (that is "other frame") and not intergenic ("no annotated CDS"). The M3-14 implementation called it cds_outframe (code review, PR #50).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. New locus class cterm_extension: same strand, in frame with an annotated CDS/sORF, overlapping it and extending past its annotated stop (3′ end), including across the origin on circular replicons.
  2. The placement is assigned to that gene (like nterm_extension), and the locus is a Module 6 candidate (§7.6.1 list extended by cterm_extension). Evidence before calling (§7.6.3 row): the in-frame continuation to the next stop and a peptide spanning the annotated stop; labelled readthrough_candidate. The annotated stop's codon is reported.
  3. Downstream ORF reconstruction (§7.6.2) applies unchanged; annotation_patch.gff3 writes it like an N-terminal extension (existing locus tag, new end, Note=cterm_extension).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: M3-14 classifies it; Module 6 specs implement items 2–3. Output vocabularies (§9 locus classes, novel ORF classes) gain one value. No thresholds or defaults change.

docs.title: ADR-0014: Checksum sources for the Bakta full DB and the Promotech model (M2-08)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §3.2, §3.9, R6; docs/specs/M2-08-giap-setup-core.md question 1
  • Needs Khoa: no (fills a gap: the spec gives no checksum for these two artefacts; no default, threshold or interface changes)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: R6 requires every downloaded artefact to be checksummed. §3.9 gives the Bakta light DB MD5 but not the full DB's, and Promotech's www.cs.mun.ca directory publishes no checksum.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: src/giap/data/db_sources.yaml pins: - Bakta full DB v6.0 db.tar.xz: MD5 4c1115e40abfa2b464ae5dd988bdd88e from the Zenodo record 14916843 metadata (the record lists MD5 for every file; bakta_db checks it too). - geNOMAD DB v1.9 genomad_db_v1.9.tar.gz: MD5 67244b528bb8bed464d1ca147136d33e (Zenodo 14886553). - Promotech RF-HOT.zip: SHA-256 fcd96ffe5a43b579af965839ee2bb896de94de3601978d88bcabd32c4fb5093f, recorded on the first download (2026-10-14, job 1846845, zip integrity verified). Trust-on-first-use: a later download with a different hash is a mismatch, not an update; changing the pin needs a new ADR.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: $GIAP_DB_DIR/prefetch_manifest.tsv (prefetch job 1846845): all three verified against these values.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: giap setup verifies against these pins and adopts the prefetched copies without re-downloading.

docs.title: ADR-0015: Two-block confirmation for calibration gates (M4-05)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-14, in session: "Two-block confirmation")
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: §8.4 (calibration criteria), §12 (nightly), tests/calibration/tolerances.yaml (unchanged)
  • Needs Khoa: yes (changes what a calibration gate means) — answered

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Each §8.4 check run on a method exactly at level raises a false alarm about 2.7 % of the time at R = 1000, and 8–9 % at α = 0.01 with R = 50–100. With ~46 checks per nightly run, P(at least one red check | every method correct) ≈ 0.75 (statistician, PR #54, docs/methods/calibration.md).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: A check that fails on replicates 0..R−1 is re-run once on the fresh block R..2R−1 (same suite seeds, SeedSequence([calibration_base, crc32(suite), rep]), so the second block is independent and reproducible). The gate fails only if BOTH blocks fail; a first-block failure that the second block does not confirm is logged as unconfirmed (visible in the nightly summary, not red). Applies to the nightly/full runs and to the per-PR fast subset alike. Thresholds, R and k in tolerances.yaml are unchanged.

docs.title: Evidence (statistician)
docs.text: False alarms per nightly run ≈ 0.75 → ≈ 0.04. Power vs 1.5× FDR inflation: at α = 0.05 0.92 → 0.85 (single check); realistic BH runs at full R = 300 stay at 1.0 for q ≥ 0.05.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The harness implements the confirmation; records carry block (1 or 2) and status (pass | unconfirmed | fail). Worst case doubles the replicates of a failing suite.

docs.title: ADR-0016: The PR-size gate does not count workflow/tests/ (amends ADR-0007)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-14, in session: "Exclude workflow/tests/")
  • Date: 2026-10-14
  • Spec sections: R-size rule (§14.6), ADR-0007, ci/gates.yaml (values unchanged)
  • Needs Khoa: yes (changes what an accepted gate counts) — answered

docs.title: Context
docs.text: ADR-0007 gates PR size on code only (src/, workflow/, scripts/). nf-test specs and their data must live under workflow/tests/, so they were counted as code: M2-07 is 762 code lines but 1,228 by the gate. The role guard already treats workflow/tests/ as tests (PR #40).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: The size gate counts src/, workflow/ (excluding workflow/tests/) and scripts/. workflow/tests/ is reported with the other non-gated lines. pr_lines_warn / pr_lines_fail in ci/gates.yaml are unchanged.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: One CI step changes (.github/workflows/ci.yml, "PR size"). Code under workflow/ (modules, subworkflows, configs, main.nf) still counts.

docs.title: ADR-0017: Unversioned sources (KEGG REST) are recorded, not pinned
docs.text:
• Status: accepted (lead)
  • Date: 2026-10-15
  • Issue: M2-09 (PR #67)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: §3.2 asks every downloaded resource to be checksum-verified. KEGG REST tables (/link/pathway/ko, /list/pathway) are unversioned and change without notice, so no checksum can be pinned in advance. ADR-0014 covers the pins of versioned resources only.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Unversioned sources carry version: "" and checksum: "" in db_sources.yaml. At download, giap setup validates the content (KEGG link/name format checks), records the retrieval date as version and the sha256 of the bytes in db_manifest.json, and giap setup --check verifies against that recorded checksum. Every run report states the KEGG retrieval date.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: KEGG-derived results are reproducible from the recorded manifest, not from the package alone; two installs on different dates may differ. All other sources stay pinned.

docs.title: ADR-0018: Region tests robust to detectability confounding
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-15)
  • Date: 2026-10-15
  • Issue: M4-17 (PR #89); statistician review https://github.com/khoa-yelo/giap/pull/89#issuecomment-6198595819

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Under the attack-2 scenario (detection depends on abundance; prophage genes are short), the region tests of GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.5 are anti-conservative (statistician, Slurm runs under local/scratch/review-m4-17): - (b) HL abundance shift: prophage HL rejects 0.21–0.25 at α = 0.05 (bias ≈ +0.75 log2). - O−E detection: when a region's p_detect sits nearer 0.5 than the replicon's, plain O−E rejects 0.074 at α = 0.05 (A2 only covered the conservative direction). Also §8.1 says "BH within type"; the code (and the test-author) use BH within (type, stat).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. §7.3.5(b): abundance is residualised on the M4-13 detectability covariates (log length, n_obs, GRAVY) before the HL/circular-shift test (statistician: 0.067 at α = 0.05, R = 300).
  2. The O−E test statistic is the studentised sum Σ(d − p)/√Σ p(1 − p) (0.048 at α = 0.05); the reported effect stays O−E.
  3. BH families are (region type, statistic): two statistics per type are different hypotheses; this is at least as strict as "within type" for each statistic.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Region-test p-values change on real data where detectability differs between regions; methods note and report text follow. Calibration gates (C1, A2 both directions) verify level under attack 2.

docs.title: Amendment 1 (accepted-by-khoa 2026-10-16)
docs.text:
Statistician review round 2 (https://github.com/khoa-yelo/giap/pull/89#issuecomment-6205786444; docs/methods/region-tests.md "Review round 2"; local/scratch/review-m4-17/v2): residualisation (decision 1) removes the bias (prophage HL −0.08 log2 vs +0.74 raw) but HL stays anti-conservative because a region's detected-gene count differs from that at shifted positions (≈ 7 vs ≈ 22 of 40), so the raw HL's spread under the shift null is wrong; this holds even when detection ignores abundance (new attack null A2-HL-MAR: 0.147 / 0.151 at α 0.05), and no covariate fit fixes it (oracle correction 0.131).

Decision 1 is extended: the circular-shift p-value is computed from the studentised statistic T = HL / √V at every shift, V a per-TU variance estimated once per replicon (formula in the methods note); the reported HL effect and CI are unchanged (residual scale). Evidence at α 0.01/0.05/0.10: A2-HL 0.005/0.019/0.046 (1,000 genes, R 4000) and 0.003/0.021/0.047 (4,500, R 2000); A2-HL-MAR ≤ 0.038 at 0.10; C1 pooled at level; power without confounding unchanged (0.166 vs 0.156).

docs.title: Amendment 2 (accepted-by-khoa 2026-10-16)
docs.text:
Statistician final review (https://github.com/khoa-yelo/giap/pull/89#issuecomment-6208970265; local/scratch/review-m4-17/v3): amendment 1's per-TU variance V depends on the TU labels, so a region whose TUs are fragmented more finely than the rest of the replicon (new attack A-TU) is anti-conservative: 0.019 / 0.071 / 0.128 at α 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 (full mode, Slurm 1850492).

Proposed: V is estimated label-free from the lag autocovariance of the residual abundance along the replicon (formula in docs/methods/region-tests.md, statistician's v3 section); T = HL/√V as in amendment 1; reported HL effect and CI unchanged. Statistician: passes every scenario (A2-HL, A2-HL-MAR, A2-mid, A-TU, C1) with the same power. Alternative: waive A-TU (xfail, documented limitation).

docs.title: ADR-0019: Stratum-0 π̂_wrong for database input from exact-match shares per length class
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-20)
  • Date: 2026-10-20
  • Issue: M3-21 (branch m3/calibration-gate); statistician validation, Slurm 1860123, 1860138, 1860180 (scripts and outputs under local/scratch/stat-m321-m418-m419/b2/)
  • Spec sections: §7.2.5 step 4 (database, m = 0), §5.3 (run aggregation, unchanged), §8.1 "Peptide placed at a locus", §8.4 "Placement FDR" and "De novo precision", §8.5; extends ADR-0010

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
§7.2.5 step 4 sets the stratum-0 π̂ for database input to the mean PEP of the input peptides. M3-21 found two defects:

  1. B2: cross-strain input. With search_db = other, some correct identifications are database-strain sequences that span a strain difference. They have no exact true locus, so an exact chance hit elsewhere is a false stratum-0 placement. Their PEP measures identification error only, so it is small. Mean PEP counts only the identification errors among peptides without an exact origin, which under-estimates false placements by about (π_wrong + δ)/π_wrong; δ is the spanning share of correct identifications.
  2. Run collapse. §5.3 collapses a peptide's runs with pep = min. The mean of min-collapsed PEP is not a peptide-level wrong share: with 3 runs M3-21 measured π̂ ≈ 0.0026 against a true wrong share of ≈ 0.024 (Slurm 1860161). No PSM-level aggregation (min, mean, max, product) is calibrated in general.

A single pooled π̂ is also invalid when the no-origin share correlates with the chance-hit rate, which changes by about ×14 per residue of length (short wrong identifications; an input padded with long exact peptides).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Estimator. Stratum 0, database input. The population P is the stratum-0 database population: all database rows except same_db exact peptides (unchanged from M3-10). For each length class ℓ of mapping.length_classes:
  2. n_ℓ = number of peptides of P in class ℓ;
  3. k_ℓ = number of them with no exact target hit (m_T ≠ 0, or no hit at all);
  4. r_ℓ = share of them with an exact decoy hit;
  5. π̂_ℓ = 1 if r_ℓ = 1; otherwise π̂_ℓ = min(1, U_ℓ / (1 − r_ℓ)), where U_ℓ is the one-sided 95 % Clopper–Pearson upper bound of k_ℓ/n_ℓ (U_ℓ = 1 when k_ℓ = n_ℓ).

This is the database analogue of the de novo precision estimator with c_l = 1: a peptide with an exact origin always matches; one without matches at the decoy rate. The upper bound mirrors step 4's "1 − lower 95 % bound". Edge cases: r_ℓ = 0 gives π̂ = U_ℓ; m < r is clipped to 1; an empty class has no weight and does not enter c. 2. Entry into the FDR. Every peptide of P carries the π̂ of its class. The stratum-0 FDR is ADR-0010's FDR_0(e) = (W_0(e) + c)/T_0(e), with W summing π̂ over decoy hits and c = max π̂_ℓ over classes with n_ℓ > 0. A peptide outside every class gets π̂ = 1. PEP and the q-value fallback are not used for the stratum-0 database π̂. m ≥ 1 is unchanged (π̂ = 1). 3. Run aggregation. §5.3's pep/q_value = min stays for ranking, detection and evidence; placement no longer reads it. 4. Outputs. mapping_fdr.tsv columns are unchanged; pi_wrong = (W + c)/(D + 1) per row now reflects the class π̂. detection_summary.tsv gains QC rows: the stratum-0 unmapped share k/n (the §7.5.1 genome-inconsistent rate), overall and per class. Run warning input_prefiltered when k falls below the 0.001 binomial quantile of n × (row-level mean PEP) × (1 − r): an input already filtered to genome matches cannot be calibrated by any genome-based π̂. 5. De novo precision estimand (§8.4 "known precision per bin"). The estimand is the correct share among distinct de novo peptides per GIAP score bin (bins on the aggregated, max score); a distinct peptide is correct when its string (I = L) equals the true_peptide of at least one of its reads. Calibration gates against that realised share; giapsim's per-read truth/denovo_precision.tsv is the per-spectrum design precision, a different quantity.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
FDP = mean over replicates; failing = some level with mean FDP > q + 2 SE.

  • List level through placement (Slurm 1860138, 1860180; N = 4,000, R = 300 and N = 300, R = 1,000; δ ∈ {0, .02, .05, .1, .2, .3} × π ∈ {.005, .01, .05} × q ∈ {.01, .05, .10}). Failing cells of 18:
Scenario mean PEP (spec) pooled exact share (± bound) per class, no bound this ADR flat chance rate p = 0.25 13 (9.97×) 0 0 0 flat p = 0.05 6 (2.44×) 0 0 0 long peptides span more 6 (2.54×) 0 0 0 short wrong / spanning peptides 13 (8.56×) 13 (2.4×) 2 (1.03×) 0 padding with long exact peptides 10 (4.81×) 10 (2.4×) 10 (1.09×) 0 N = 300 13 (9.96×) 0–1 0 0 PEP deflated 10× (min-collapse) 14 (11.2×) 1–13 1–5 0

Power at δ = 0 relative to mean PEP: 0.984–1.0 (N = 4,000), 0.85–0.97 (N = 300); π̂ = 1 instead gives 0.43–0.84 and 0.25. An oracle using the true unweighted no-origin share fails the short-peptide and padding scenarios (2.19×, 2.02×), so no pooled π̂ can work there. - Genome level, real chain (Slurm 1860123; giapsim 100 kb / 1 Mb, R = 300; 5 Mb, R = 100; tryptic, 7-mer and M3-18 strain arms with realised δ 0.03–0.24). Stratum-0 FDP ≤ 0.0022 for every rule, but the estimated/true false count is 0.03–0.46 under mean PEP (q-values 6–30× too small) and 0.96–2.4 under this estimator. FDP exceeds q once the list binds: short-peptide-heavy input, very large genomes, or q < ~0.005. - Run collapse. With input PEP × 0.1 this ADR's results are unchanged. - Limitation. If the upstream pipeline keeps only genome-matching peptides, every genome-based rule fails, mean PEP included (FDP 0.061 at q = 0.01, δ = 0.2); hence the warning in decision 4.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• placement_fdr.placement: the database stratum-0 π̂ comes from the class estimator, not pi_wrong_database. Stratum-0 q-values and fdr_stratum become honest under cross-strain input. Genome-scale acceptance at q = 0.01 is unchanged in simulation; small or binding lists lose up to ~15 % power at δ = 0.
  • ADR-0010's forwarded item (mean PEP correlated with chance-hit rate) is resolved along length.
  • Tests to update with the implementation: database examples in tests/unit/test_placement_fdr.py; the known_pi / calibrated_pep / max_q expectations in tests/calibration/test_placement_fdr_lists.py; the reference rule in tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_placement_same_db.py; re-verify test_placement_fdr_genome.py. New attack: tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_placement_strain_span.py. Strict xfails to flip: the 1-Mb related_dbstrain estimate check and test_database_stressed_stratum0_estimate_covers_false_placements (1-Mb stressed arm; W0/V0 ≈ 0.2 under mean PEP, ≈ 1.04 under this rule, statistician review of #113 round 2).
  • GIAP_SPEC.md §7.2.5 step 4 is superseded by this ADR; docs/methods/placement-fdr.md (new section "Cross-strain input and run collapse") and docs/methods/denovo-precision.md (estimand) are updated.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• Pooled π̂ = max(mean PEP, 1 − (m − r)/(1 − r)) (the first candidate): fails length-correlated input and padding (2.4×) and is marginal on small lists.
  • π̂ = 1 for search_db = other: valid everywhere, including pre-filtered input, and free at genome scale in simulation, but loses 16–75 % power on binding lists. Kept as the fallback if Khoa prefers simplicity.
  • Change the run aggregation of PEP (mean or max across runs): no aggregation is calibrated when run counts differ between correct and wrong peptides, and it does not address B2.

docs.title: ADR-0020: Autocorrelation nulls recompute the detrend; residual join count; no CI for lag statistics
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-20)
  • Date: 2026-10-20
  • Issue: M5-05 (also M5-01, M5-02); statistician attack check, Slurm 1860199, 1860281, 1860305, 1860318 (scripts and outputs under local/scratch/stat-m5/sims/)
  • Spec sections: §7.3.5(c), §8.1, §8.2, §8.3

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Simulations on giapsim M4-07/08 truth (B = 499–1,000): - Permuting the LOESS residuals without recomputing the trend (§7.3.5(c) "detrend then permute", M5-05's "no re-detrending per permutation") is anti-conservative. At 1,000 genes, R = 1,000: gene-label null pooled rejection over 20 lags 0.026 / 0.096 / 0.162 at α 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10, BH-family FDR 0.136; TU-block null pooled 0.155 at 0.05, family 0.27. At 4,500 genes still 0.062 / 0.085 at 0.05. The smoother puts a negative autocorrelation (mean observed I₁ ≈ −0.042) into the observed residuals that permuted residuals lack (null mean ≈ −0.002). - The raw join count rejects 0.082–0.092 at lag 1 (0.084–0.086 pooled) at α 0.05 under both nulls when short genes cluster in a prophage (short_genes_in = prophage, R = 500): detectability, not expression, clusters. §8.2 already requires detection tests to adjust for detectability. - No interval for a lag-k Moran's I reaches 95 % coverage (test inversion 0.85–0.93 under TU null and AR 0.5/0.9 at lags 1/5/20, R = 150; a bootstrap CI of I_k is uncalibrated too).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Per replicon: y = centred log2 abundance of genes with values. A wide trend is removed once: y_w = y − LOESS(y; span 0.30). The statistic is Moran's I of x = y_w − LOESS(y_w; span context.autocorr.loess_span = 0.10) along the ordinal of genes with values (circular padding as in M5-01).
  2. Each null replicate permutes y_w (gene label: among genes with values; TU block: whole TUs, values and gaps together) and applies the same 10 % LOESS before computing I_k, so observed and null are the same function of the data.
  3. The join count test uses the residual statistic Σ over valid lag-k pairs of (d_i − p_i)(d_j − p_j), with p = cross-fitted p_detect, permuted together with d under both nulls. value reports the raw BB_k; effect = residual statistic − its null mean (raw effect, adjusted test, as ADR-0018 decision 2).
  4. Autocorrelation rows report effect = statistic − null mean and ci_low / ci_high = NA with flag ci_unestimated — a deviation from §8.2 for autocorrelation.tsv only. The null envelope (null_lo, null_hi) is reported for the V10 figure.
  5. Calibration gates per (statistic, null) and α ∈ {0.01, 0.05, 0.10}: lag-1 level, lag-20 level, and the BH family's any-rejection rate under the complete null (FWER-style bound). The pooled 20-lag rate is recorded, not gated (lags are positively correlated; pooling hid a lag-1 failure).

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• Decisions 1–2: TU null lag-1 rates 0.005 / 0.052 / 0.092, pooled 0.0115 / 0.0488 / 0.0973; gene-label null with a 2 log2 ori–ter cosine gradient pooled 0.010 / 0.051 / 0.104 (R = 400).
  • Alternatives measured: permute raw values then detrend each replicate fails the gradient attack (TU-null lag-1 0.946); double detrend without the wide pre-trend is 0.072 at lag 1 (bound 0.064, R = 1,000).
  • Decision 3: residual join count pooled at α 0.05: 0.051 (short-gene prophage), 0.050–0.052 (label and TU nulls, R = 1,000).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Runtime: one (B × n)·(n × n) smoother product per null (≈ 6 × 10⁹ flops at 4,500 genes, inside M5-05's 30 s budget). giap.stats.smooth.loess_detrend must accept positions 0…n−1 so the smoother matrix is shared by every replicate.
  • p-values on real data drop for lag-k structure the detrend created. Interpretation note: at ρ 0.9 the 10 % detrend creates a real negative I₂₀ (effect −0.195 at 1,000 genes); large-lag negative values are a span artefact under strong short-range correlation.
  • New flag ci_unestimated (vocabulary through M5-09).
  • New statistician attack file tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_autocorr.py: (a) TU null + 2 log2 cosine, (b) label null + gradient, (c) short-gene prophage under the TU null (join count gated), all gated at level; (d) the no-detrend version of (a) recorded as teeth (pooled 0.34).

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• Spec as written (detrend once, permute residuals): anti-conservative (above).
  • Permute raw, detrend per replicate: fails under an ori–ter gradient with weak TU structure.
  • Double detrend without the wide pre-trend: 0.072 at lag 1.
  • Bootstrap CI for I_k: needs blocks ≫ k, biased toward 0 at joins, uncalibrated.

docs.title: Amendment 1 (accepted-by-khoa, 2026-10-20): Pearson residual join count
docs.text:
Supersedes decision 3's statistic. Statistician review of PR #116 (Slurm 1861073, 1861078; scripts and outputs under local/scratch/review-116-stat-sims/) found Σ(d − p)(d − p) anti-conservative when low p_detect clusters along the replicon: the permutation null cannot reproduce the clustered p(1 − p) variance. Circular n = 1,000, 30-gene islands with p ~ U(0.01, 0.05) amid p ~ U(0.3, 0.9), α = 0.05: rejection 0.059 / 0.074 / 0.086 / 0.105 at 10 / 20 / 30 / 50 % island share (both nulls).

  • The join count test uses r_i = (d_i − p_i)/√(p_i(1 − p_i)) and the statistic Σ over valid lag-k pairs of r_i r_j, with p unclipped and permuted together with d under both nulls. Genes with p ∈ {0, 1} (or NaN) have no residual and are treated as missing (they join no pair).
  • Evidence: level 0.045–0.056 in every scenario above and in the original attack set; about 10 % power cost; at very small p (0.001–0.005) α = 0.01 gives 0.019 (recorded, not gated).
  • A floor on p in the denominator is rejected: it reintroduces the clustering failure.
  • value still reports the raw BB_k; effect = Pearson statistic − its null mean.
  • The engine attack file tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_autocorr_engine.py carries the low-p-island arms (pass with the Pearson statistic) and a must-fail arm (raw residual, 50 % islands).

docs.title: ADR-0021: Block length for the island scan and the ori–ter CI
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-20); decision 2 amended and accepted-by-khoa 2026-10-20 evening (option B: the uncalibrated flag is dropped). See "Amendment 1".
  • Date: 2026-10-20
  • Issues: M5-02, M5-06, M5-07, M5-08; statistician attack check, Slurm 1860199, 1860281, 1860305, 1860318 (local/scratch/stat-m5/sims/)
  • Spec sections: §7.3.5(d) step 5, §7.3.5(e), docs/methods/bootstrap.md "Block length"

docs.title: Context
docs.text: With the spec's ℓ̂ (the first lag at which TU-level Moran's I is not significant, bounded to [1, 20]), island FWER (share of replicates with ≥ 1 island) on a 4,500-gene chromosome + 60-gene plasmid (B = 500, R = 400) is 0.028 / 0.205 / 0.26 / 0.27 at ρ 0 / 0.5 / 0.9 / 0.95, and 0.15 at the fast-gate setting (1,000 genes, ρ 0.5). ℓ̂ marks where correlation stops being detectable, not the block length a window-sum maximum needs; the maximum is driven by extreme 2-TU windows of single-gene TUs. Fixed blocks ≥ 10 TUs copy the observed extreme window into ≈ 63 % of replicates, so FWER and power go to 0. The same ℓ̂ under-covers the ori–ter slope CI (0.88–0.93 at ρ 0.5). Rejected alternatives (Gaussian null with the empirical ACF, sieve AR bootstrap 0.32 / 0.80, ACF-studentised scan 0.31 / 0.70 with V ≤ 0 on the plasmid, TU-size-standardised scores 0.18 at ρ 0) all failed.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Block length ℓ' = min(20, 2ℓ̂ + 1, T) per replicon (T = number of scored TUs), with ℓ̂ as in the spec, for both the island circular block bootstrap and the ori–ter slope CI. An integer context.islands.block_len overrides it unchanged.
  2. Validity domain: islands on replicons with fewer than 1,000 scored TUs carry the §9.4 flag uncalibrated (statistician's option b). The M5-07 gate is claimed for replicons with ≥ 1,000 scored TUs; smaller replicons are recorded, not gated.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• Island FWER with ℓ': 0.003 / 0.040 / 0.023 / 0.023 at ρ 0 / 0.5 / 0.9 / 0.95 (R = 300; bound 0.075); 0.013 at 1,000 genes, ρ 0.5.
  • Attacks at level (R = 300): ori–ter gradient 0.04, large TUs 0.013, abundance-driven detection 0.04, short-gene prophage 0.04, draft assembly (500 + 133 × 30-gene linear contigs) 0.003 (spec rule 0.09).
  • Ori–ter pooled-slope CI coverage 0.96 at ρ 0.5 (spec rule ≈ 0.905). Corrected 2026-10-21: that 0.96 was an R = 50 fluctuation. Re-measured with the merged implementation at R = 300 (Slurm 1863166) the same cell gives 0.943 (SE 0.013); ρ 0 gives 0.925, ρ 0.9 0.900, no gradient 0.917, 1,000 genes 0.905, and the arms 0.875–0.945. The estimator is unbiased (−2.4239 against the closed form −2.4317); the interval is 1–5 points narrow throughout.
  • Power (4,500 genes, ρ 0.5, R = 100): 20 TUs × 2 SD 0.18, 20 × 1.5 0.06, 10 × 2 0.04, 5 × 2 0.00 — low because ≈ 45 % of genes are censored independently of abundance in giapsim defaults; power stays recorded, not gated, and is also run with detection = "abundance".
  • Open limitation: 1,000 genes at ρ 0.9 gives FWER 0.13 (spec rule 0.55), because ℓ̂ ≈ 1.3 there (Moran's I cannot detect the diluted correlation on ≈ 555 TUs); hence decision 2.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• M5-07's planning target (power ≥ 0.8) will not be met under giapsim defaults; the report says so.
  • The effect CI stays the spec's TU-bootstrap CI; the methods note says it is conditional on the selected window (winner's curse) and ignores within-window autocorrelation; M5-07 records its coverage.
  • The sim1000_island golden (M5-11) is checked against ℓ' before it is frozen.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• (a) Accept the small-replicon limitation and gate only the full-gate sizes, without a flag.
  • (c) ℓ = 20 on replicons with < 1,000 scored TUs: valid but no power there.
  • The spec's ℓ̂ unchanged: anti-conservative (above).

docs.title: Amendment 1 (accepted-by-khoa, 2026-10-20): the validity domain is a dependence regime, not a size
docs.text:
Supersedes decision 2. Evidence: M5-06 statistician re-measurement, R = 1,000 per cell, B = 199, through the M5-06 oracle on the merged engines (Slurm 1861482, 1861494, 1861551, 1861552; scripts and outputs under local/scratch/m5-06-stat/). The original numbers reproduce (4,500 genes: 0.037 at ρ 0.5 against the ADR's 0.040; 0.024 at ρ 0.9 against 0.023); the inference from them was wrong.

  1. Validity domain. The island FWER is claimed for the dependence regime the calibration covers, not for a replicon size. It is claimed for giapsim ar1_background at ρ ≤ 0.5 at every size measured (557 / 1,001 / 2,501 scored TUs: 0.020 / 0.031 / 0.037), for the 4,500-gene chromosome at ρ = 0.9 (0.024, where ℓ̂ ≈ 8 makes ℓ' = 17 span the 20-TU windows), and for the §8.5 attacks that stay in that regime. It is not claimed where strong TU-level autocorrelation is resolved by Moran's I only to a short lag (ℓ' ≤ 7): giapsim ρ = 0.9 gives 0.113 at 557 TUs and 0.095 at 1,001 TUs, and 1,000 single-gene TUs give 0.068 / 0.110 / 0.208 / 0.327 at ρ = 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.9 / 0.95 (bound 0.0638). The scored-TU count decides nothing on its own — 400 TUs at ρ 0.5 give 0.005, 1,000 TUs at ρ 0.9 give 0.095–0.208, 2,500 TUs at ρ 0.9 give 0.024 — it enters only through the power of the ℓ̂ test, together with ρ, the TU size distribution and the censored share (the same ρ = 0.9 replicon gives ℓ̂ = 9 and 0.007 uncensored, ℓ̂ = 2 and 0.208 at 55 % detected).

Two mechanisms, both measured at 1,000 TUs, ρ = 0.9, with the block forced: autocovariance beyond the block (uncensored, Î₁ = 0.78: 0.576 at block 5 against 0.016 at block 19) and local-scale heterogeneity at matched variance (45 % censored, variance ratio ≈ 1.0 yet 0.158 at block 5; block SD q90/q10 1.73 at ρ 0.9 against 1.24 at ρ 0). A long block fixes both and costs all the power, which decision 1 rejected.

2a. No flag. uncalibrated is dropped (Khoa, option B): no per-replicon statistic certifies the domain, so a flag would give false reassurance. ℓ̂, ℓ', the lag-1 Moran's I of the detrended TU scores, a Bartlett variance ratio of the window sums and a local-scale ratio all fail as keep/flag rules, and selecting on them is adverse — giapsim ρ = 0.9 at 557 TUs is 0.113 overall but 0.220 among the replicates that look calmest (ℓ̂ ≤ 1, flat local scale), because a small ℓ̂ is exactly what makes the block too short; the same rule flags 94 % of the perfectly calibrated 2,501-TU ρ = 0.5 cell. Instead: docs/methods/islands.md states the domain above, and the §9.4 run report carries ℓ̂, ℓ' (block_len) and Î₁ per replicon so a reader can see where their data sit.

docs.title: Measured and rejected
docs.text: Local standardisation (dividing the detrended scores by a LOESS fit of |residual| before the scan and the bootstrap) reduces the inflation (ρ 0.8: 0.106 → 0.032 at a 10 % span; ρ 0.9: 0.188 → 0.084, still a breach, because the autocovariance mechanism remains) but absorbs the signal: power on a planted 20-TU × +2 SD island at ρ 0.5 falls from 0.103 to 0.003.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• M5-07 keeps its gate cells (ρ ∈ {0, 0.5, 0.9} at 4,500 genes) and adds recorded, not gated cells at 1,000 and 1,800 genes × ρ = 0.9.
  • docs/methods/islands.md gains the domain statement and the two mechanisms.
  • M5-06 and M5-09 drop uncalibrated; the §9.4 run report gains the per-replicon ℓ̂, ℓ' and Î₁.
  • Backlog: a scale-aware or variance-corrected island null.

docs.title: ADR-0022: UniOP and TerminatorNet cut-offs and the distance-model refit on RegulonDB 14.5.0 K-12
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-23, max-F1; M6-12 lead decision 10; 2026-10-24, UniOP pair_threshold 0.5)
  • Date: 2026-10-23 (run 2026-10-24 01:05 UTC, Slurm 1879748)
  • Spec sections: §15.4 steps 3–5, §7.1.3, §7.1.5, §7.4.5, §7.4.6, §7.4.7; spec docs/specs/M6-12-uniop-terminator-cutoffs.md with lead decisions 1–10; methods docs/methods/operons.md › "K-12 cut-off calibration (M6-12)"
  • Needs Khoa: yes (a protected file, src/giap/data/calibration.yaml, and two defaults change). Khoa decided the cut-off rule on 2026-10-23: max-F1 as §15.4 specifies, no one-SE rule.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
§15.4 asks for three numbers from RegulonDB on K-12 MG1655, recorded in calibration.yaml with the RegulonDB version, date, AUROC, precision and recall: 1. the UniOP AUROC and pair cut-off: "the smallest threshold with precision ≥ 0.90 (if none reaches 0.90, the threshold with maximum F1)"; 2. the distance-model refit, p(operon | d) = 1/(1 + exp((d − d₀)/s)) (§7.1.3, placeholder 50 / 20); 3. the TerminatorNet confidence cut-off, by the same rule, with precision against RegulonDB terminators within ±50 bp on the same strand.

Release of record: RegulonDB 14.5.0 (2026-01-28), as Khoa decided on 2026-10-21 (§15.3 says "v12"). Until now calibration.yaml held the placeholders (d0: 50, s: 20, terminatornet_yes: 0.5, both calibrated: false), every run carried the flags uncalibrated:operon_distance and uncalibrated:terminatornet_yes, and annotation.uniop.pair_threshold was the uncalibrated 0.5.

The cut-off rule follows lead decision 1 (the stable reading of "smallest t with precision ≥ 0.90": every candidate at or above t* has precision ≥ 0.90), with max-F1 as the fallback, ties to the smallest t.
