Khoa's decision 10 keeps max-F1 exactly as §15.4 specifies; the one-SE rule the statistician raised for TerminatorNet's flat F1 curve (methods R3) is not adopted, and the flatness is reported below as context only.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Record these values (all from cutoffs.json, unrounded; the floats are Python's shortest round-trip repr and must not be rounded, because the pipeline compares with ≥):

Key Value Rule that fired Mirrors uniop_pair_threshold.value (new) 0.5 Khoa, 2026-10-24 (the precision_0.90 rule gave 0.529415) defaults.yaml annotation.uniop.pair_threshold; config/model.py UniopConfig.pair_threshold operon_distance.d0 102.68667744326773 IRLS refit, converged — (read by steps/operons.py) operon_distance.s 47.16037265004493 IRLS refit, converged — terminatornet_yes.value 0.9999999999961204 max_f1 (no candidate reaches 0.90) defaults.yaml annotation.terminators.terminatornet_yes; config/model.py

All three entries become calibrated: true with the ADR-0022 provenance. The proposed file is $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m612c/calibration.yaml.proposed (with calibration.yaml.diff); the lead commits it in PR-C with Gate-Change-Approved: ADR-0022.

Downstream changes. - TUs and pair classes keep pair_threshold 0.5 (classify, build_tus, the flag code); the value is now recorded as calibrated. - The distance fallback (UniOP missing or failed) uses d₀ = 102.69 bp, s = 47.16 bp instead of 50 / 20: much more permissive at 40–150 bp (see the binned table). - Terminator "yes" (§7.1.5, §7.4.5) needs TerminatorNet confidence ≥ 0.9999999999961204, that is a saturated network output; 727 of 2,447 eligible K-12 calls (29.7 %) pass, against all 2,447 at 0.5. - The run flags uncalibrated:operon_distance and uncalibrated:terminatornet_yes disappear; manifest.calibration gains a third key, uniop_pair_threshold. - The §8.6 full sensitivity variants stay at UniOP thresholds 0.3 and 0.7 (decision 2, Q7): t* = 0.529 < 0.7, so no backlog note is due.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Run. validation/calibrate_cutoffs.py (part B, #264) at worktree HEAD 3db69d9b, Slurm 1879748 (wheat-05, 59 s wall), output $GIAP_DATA_DIR/regulondb/14.5.0/calibration/ (not committed, R6/R11). Rerun 1879749 with the same seed into $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m612c/rerun/: cutoffs.json identical apart from date; the three TSVs byte-identical. - cutoffs.json sha256 edcf9044eafe5f1f3f31aab93c759a035efd25ffa240bd199a637640e843d6eb - uniop_curve.tsv 87054f2e…11, terminatornet_curve.tsv b4de9758…1f, terminatornet_calls.tsv 705903eb…97 - seed 20261014 (giap.rng.for_step("m6_12_cutoffs", seed)), B = 2,000, R = 200, cluster directon, 773 directons holding labelled pairs. - Identities checked by the driver: truth SHA-256s TUSet c96c8a3b…39fc, TerminatorSet 9d916ffe…f366, GeneProductSet 3c2c6be3…9dde; genome (normalised) 918f35c7…14f2; UniOP pin 3ed14dfc (ADR-0008), uniop.pred 7d852a93…5ee0, uniop_cds.gff ea587089…2906 (map rebuilt by coordinates, 4,372 / 4,372); TerminatorNet commit 72180309 (ADR-0008), terms.tsv.gz 9be61c75…a2ff.

UniOP (the M6 gate's third clause, "UniOP-alone AUROC recorded", §13 row M6). 95 % CIs are directon-bootstrap percentile CIs; the iid (single-pair) line is for comparison only.

Quantity Estimate 95 % CI (directon) iid CI labelled pairs L; P / N; without p 2,739; 1,730 / 1,009; 0 — — AUROC 0.911 (0.910877249265283) [0.898, 0.923] [0.900, 0.922] t* (precision_0.90; literal reading identical) 0.529415 bootstrap re-selected t*: 2.5 / 50 / 97.5 % = 0.457, 0.529, 0.610 — precision at t* (fixed t*) 0.9017 (TP 1,467, FP 160) [0.884, 0.918] [0.887, 0.916] recall at t* (fixed t*) 0.8480 [0.827, 0.868] [0.831, 0.864] F1 at t* 0.8740 — — precision of the whole rule, 10-fold directon CV 0.9001 — —
  • The precision CI holds t* fixed: it is a CI for the precision of the threshold 0.529415, not for the precision achieved by the rule. The rule chose t* because the observed precision there is ≥ 0.90, so the point estimate is optimistic; the cross-validated precision of the rule (0.9001) puts the optimism at about 0.002, against a CI half-width of 0.017.
  • t* itself is known only to about ±0.08 (the re-selection quantiles); the precision of the cut-off is what is stable.
  • Precision 0.90 is cumulative, not per-pair: it is the share of operon pairs among all pairs with p ≥ t*. Pairs just above the cut-off (p in [0.529, 0.65), 122 pairs) are operon pairs 49 % of the time.
  • pair_threshold is K-12-tuned. Precision depends on prevalence (K-12 labelled π = 0.632): at the same TPR / FPR, a genome with π = 0.5 would see about 0.84 and one with π = 0.4 about 0.78. AUROC is prevalence-free but not genome-free.
  • UniOP's training data: unknown here (not verified in M6-12). If UniOP's development used K-12 operons from RegulonDB, this AUROC is partly in-sample for the tool.
  • Khoa's decision, 2026-10-24: UniOP uses 0.5. On the K-12 curve 0.5 gives precision 0.896, recall 0.853 and F1 0.8739 (TP 1,476, FP 172), against 0.902 / 0.848 / 0.8740 at the precision_0.90 threshold 0.529415: the same operating point, so the round value is kept and rule is recorded as khoa_fixed_0.5. Khoa also asked whether TerminatorNet could use 0.5; it cannot without a large change. At 0.5 every eligible candidate is called (recall 1.0), FP rises from 563 to 2,154 and precision falls from 0.226 to 0.120, close to the 0.091 coincidence rate, so TerminatorNet keeps the max-F1 value.
  • Context for decision 10, not the recorded value. The max-F1 threshold on the UniOP curve is 0.25114 (F1 0.8743, precision 0.848, TP 1,562, FP 281), against F1 0.8740 at 0.529415. §15.4 applies max-F1 only when no threshold reaches precision 0.90; UniOP reaches it, so the recorded rule is precision_0.90. F1 is flat here too: every candidate from 0.069 to 0.707 is within 1 % of the maximum.

Distance model (the fallback when UniOP is missing).

Quantity Estimate 95 % CI (directon) iid CI d₀ (bp) 102.69 [94.59, 111.47] [96.08, 110.31] s (bp) 47.16 [41.19, 53.64] [41.85, 53.12] converged / reason true / none — — AUROC of −d 0.907 (0.9067313255841931) [0.892, 0.920] [0.894, 0.918] AUROC(UniOP) − AUROC(−d), paired 0.0041 [0.0009, 0.0077] [0.0007, 0.0079] log-loss on L, refit / placeholder (50, 20) 0.407 / 0.616 in-sample, no CI —
  • The refit used the damped Newton from (logit ȳ, 0) after the exact separation check (lead decision 6, B1); the plain Newton of the spec's first draft diverges on these data.
  • The percentile CIs of d₀ and s under-cover slightly (about 0.92 on synthetic data, part A); they are recorded, not gated.
  • UniOP beats distance alone by 0.004 AUROC; the paired CI excludes 0, so the gain is real but small.
  • The fallback does not deliver 0.90 precision at pair_threshold. p_dist ≥ 0.529415 means d ≤ 97.1 bp; on L that calls 1,878 pairs with precision 0.839 and recall 0.910.
  • The linear-logit family misfits K-12 (it is fixed by §7.1.3). Observed vs fitted operon share by intergenic-distance bin (counts and shares only):
d (bp) n observed refit placeholder (50, 20) < −20 47 0.745 0.947 0.983 [−20, 0) 566 0.979 0.907 0.939 [0, 20) 576 0.965 0.879 0.884 [20, 40) 222 0.914 0.830 0.750 [40, 60) 173 0.549 0.751 0.495 [60, 80) 172 0.442 0.669 0.278 [80, 100) 136 0.449 0.566 0.122 [100, 150) 289 0.273 0.398 0.033 [150, 200) 165 0.164 0.189 0.003 [200, 300) 218 0.119 0.057 0.000 ≥ 300 175 0.103 0.004 0.000

The refit is too flat: it under-predicts at −20 to 40 bp, over-predicts at 40 to 150 bp, and is too confident beyond 300 bp, where about 10 % of labelled pairs are still operon pairs. It is still far better than the placeholder, which puts almost no operon mass beyond 100 bp.

TerminatorNet. Wilson 95 % intervals, plus the window-cluster bootstrap interval (each gene's downstream window is a cluster) for precision.

Quantity Estimate 95 % CI calls; eligible (inside a same-strand downstream window) 8,294; 2,447 — RegulonDB terminators; window-eligible 375; 295 — t* (max_f1; no candidate reaches 0.90 under either reading, literal_threshold null) 0.9999999999961204 — calls ≥ t*: TP / FP 164 / 563 (727 calls) — precision at t* (a lower bound, see below) 0.226 Wilson [0.197, 0.257]; window [0.196, 0.258] coincidence rate c at t* (placement null, R = 200) 0.0906 MC SE 0.0008 coincidence-corrected precision bound (obs − c)/(1 − c) 0.148 — … at the Wilson lower limit / at the window lower limit 0.117 / 0.115 (precision_lower_bound_window, the 97.5 % one-sided bound) — recall over window-eligible truth 0.556 (164 / 295) [0.499, 0.612] recall over all 375 terminators 0.443 [0.393, 0.493] recall, rho-independent 0.580 (156 / 269) [0.520, 0.637] recall, rho-dependent 0.308 (8 / 26) [0.165, 0.500] F1 at t* (call-level) 0.322 — AUROC matched vs unmatched eligible calls (diagnostic, not recorded in the yaml) 0.677 not estimated
  • RegulonDB is incomplete, so this precision is a lower bound, except for coincidental matches: a false call can land within 50 bp of a listed terminator by chance, because both concentrate just past stop codons. The offset-preserving placement null puts that chance at c = 0.091, and the coincidence-corrected bound is 0.148 (0.115 at the window-bootstrap 97.5 % lower limit). The true precision of terminatornet_yes on K-12 lies above about 0.115 with 97.5 % confidence; RegulonDB cannot say how far above.
  • The 0.90 target is unreachable against RegulonDB: the best precision at any candidate is 0.229. terminatornet_yes is a max-F1 cut-off, not a 90 % cut-off, and carries no precision guarantee on any genome.
  • Recall is low by construction: RegulonDB includes Rho-dependent terminators, which TerminatorNet does not model.
  • Flat F1 (context only; Khoa decided max-F1, 2026-10-23). F1 rises from 0.214 at 0.5 to 0.310 at 0.9 and is flat above: 0.314 at 0.99, 0.313 at 0.999, 0.315 at 0.99999, maximum 0.322 at 0.9999999999961204. The 45 candidates within 1 % of the maximum all lie in [0.9999999999689556, 0.9999999999999982]; the 210 within 5 % lie in [0.8814, 1.0]. The argmax therefore sits on saturated network outputs, and its decimals beyond about the 4th are noise; on another genome or TerminatorNet build the float pattern near 1.0 can differ. The value is recorded exactly, which is correct for K-12. A one-SE rule was considered and not adopted (decision 10).
  • The rule's F1 is call-level (recall = TP over all matched eligible calls), as specified; the reported recall is truth-level.

Gate and tests run with the proposed values (scratch copies under $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m612c/; calibration.yaml itself was not edited): - tests/calibration -m calibration, targeted to the cut-off, coincidence, operon-FDR and operon-simulation suites with their attacks (7 files, 20 tests, including the directon-clustered AUROC null at R = 500): 20 passed on the unchanged branch (Slurm 1879917), with only the proposed calibration.yaml (1879918), and with the full PR-C mirrors (1879919). No tolerance was changed. The untargeted tests/calibration -m calibration hit the 3 h limit on one shared 16-CPU node in both variants (1879781, 1879783) at about 95 %, with one failure each that the log does not name; no calibration suite reads calibration.yaml or the two defaults, so that run is not evidence for or against these values, and the lead's PR-C fast suite remains the check. - C0 and the tests that read the defaults: the C0 agreement test test_calibration_and_defaults_agree passes non-vacuously when defaults.yaml and config/model.py carry the mirrors (Slurm 1879784), and fails, as designed, when only calibration.yaml changes (Slurm 1879782). test_model_defaults_equal_defaults_yaml passes. Other failures are listed under Consequences.

Multiple testing. M6-12 produces no p or q values; every output is an estimate with a CI or a cut-off from a fixed rule, so there is no §8.1 family. The exceptions without a CI are the in-sample log-losses (descriptive), t* (its bootstrap quantiles are given) and the TerminatorNet AUROC diagnostic.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One genome, one truth set: every CI here is over resampled directons (or windows) of K-12 and describes K-12's uncertainty, not genome-to-genome transfer. d₀ and s transfer worse than AUROC (β₀ absorbs K-12's prevalence and intergenic statistics).
  • Label noise in RegulonDB biases AUROC and precision towards the base rate (conservative); study bias towards well-studied operons may do the opposite.
  • A later RegulonDB release reruns the driver into regulondb/<release>/calibration/ and needs a new ADR.
  • PR-C needs test changes beyond C0 (lead work, role guard). With the proposed values, the following tests fail; none is a statistical failure, all pin placeholders or the two-key set:
  • tests/unit/test_operons.py::test_calibration_yaml_entries converts every non-calibrated, non-provenance field to float, so the spec's string fields regulondb_version, date and rule raise ValueError (spec § "What changes in protected files" vs C0's test). Either the test skips string metadata or the yaml folds them into provenance.
  • tests/unit/manifest/test_content_blocks.py::test_calibration_lists_both_bundled_keys_and_flags_them and tests/integration/test_mvp03c_manifest_content.py::test_calibration_block[local|nextflow] pin the key set to {operon_distance, terminatornet_yes} and (the first) require both uncalibrated:* flags.
  • tests/unit/test_operon_steps.py (4 tests: ..._falls_back[empty|header_only], ..._without_uniop_pred_falls_back, ..._uses_uniop_and_distance_model_for_wrap) pin the distance-model probabilities of d₀ = 50, s = 20.
  • With the terminatornet_yes mirror at 0.9999999999961204, tests that read the default implicitly with toy confidences such as 0.9: tests/unit/operons/test_flags.py (10 tests), tests/unit/novel/test_novel_evidence.py (2) and tests/unit/novel/test_novel_evidence_review_180.py (1). The spec's last acceptance criterion asks PR-C to list these; they should pass explicit thresholds.

docs.title: ADR-0023: KEGG global and overview maps are excluded from the KEGG collection
docs.text:
• Status: accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Spec sections: §7.7.1, §7.7.4
  • Needs Khoa: no. This fills a gap in §7.7.4, which says "KEGG pathways" without saying which, and it changes no default, threshold or interface. It is the M8 index's ADR-C, lead-level once the lead accepted the M8-03 default (lead decision 1).

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
KEGG's "Global and overview maps" are unions of many metabolic pathways. Some examples: - map01100, Metabolic pathways - map01110, Biosynthesis of secondary metabolites - map01200, Carbon metabolism - map01310, Nitrogen cycle - map01320, Sulfur cycle

They overlap nearly every metabolic set. Where they survive the 500-gene size cap, they dominate the BH family with redundant, uninterpretable hits. In the KEGG link file, every path:map row is also duplicated as a path:ko row.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The KEGG collection keeps only path:map links. It drops these maps: - map011xx; - map012xx; - map01310; - map01320.

These are KEGG's "Global and overview maps" group as of the installed release. A KO whose only links are to these maps belongs to no KEGG set. The exclusion is recorded here and in docs/methods/function-collections.md. Pass 1 emits no per-run count, so spec M8-03's "excluded and counted" becomes "excluded and documented".

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: The code review of #159 found that map01310 and map01320 (with 39 and 53 KO links) passed the original map011xx/map012xx rule. tests/unit/function/test_collections_review.py pins the full list, along with neighbouring maps that are kept.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A KEGG release that adds a new overview map must update the pattern (giap.function.collections._OVERVIEW) and this ADR.
  • A future kegg_overview_excluded: N run flag would be an additive change.

docs.title: ADR-0024: annotation.precomputed.rbs_novel, a precomputed second-round OSTIR layer
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-21, in session: "3 c 4 a. The rest keep recommended")
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Spec sections: §6.4, §7.6 (second-round OSTIR), §13
  • Needs Khoa: yes (a new config key, which changes the config interface). Answered: option (a).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The local executor reads every tool result from a precomputed layer, and a missing layer is an error (§6.4). Second-round OSTIR scores start codons that exist only after mapping, and these are not keyed by locus_tag.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Add annotation.precomputed.rbs_novel to defaults.yaml, null by default. - It holds a TSV keyed by position (contig, strand, 1-based first base of the start codon in transcription direction), with the OSTIR columns of the rbs layer. - Nextflow honours the key the same way as the other precomputed layers, and runs OSTIR itself only when the key is null (M7-08 lead decision 6). - Rejected: START_<contig>_<pos1>_<p|m> rows in the rbs layer. That needs no new key, but it overloads locus_tag.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text:
• Before: the local executor could not run NOVEL.
  • After: the M7-08 tests run it from a layer the simulator writes.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The input-path keys gain one entry. No threshold changes.

docs.title: ADR-0025: GSEA on genomically clustered sets: a flag and a restricted claim in pass 1, a rotation null in hardening
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-21, in session: "3 c 4 a. The rest keep recommended")
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Spec sections: §7.7.4, §8.2, §8.5
  • Needs Khoa: yes (a claim restriction and a new flag). Answered: option (c) now, (a) in hardening.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The M8-05 TU-collapsed GSEA permutes TU labels, which assumes TUs are exchangeable. Positional autocorrelation between neighbouring TUs breaks that for sets whose TUs are adjacent on the genome. Real COG, KEGG and GO sets often cluster this way (superoperons, flagellar regions).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Pass 1.
  2. Rows of sets whose member TUs are genomically clustered carry a genomic_cluster flag.
  3. The flag is defined in the M8-05 follow-up, from TU order along each replicon. The statistician signs off the definition.
  4. The methods note states the claim: p-values are valid under TU exchangeability, and there is no level claim for flagged sets.
  5. Hardening pass. A circular-shift (rotation) null for set p-values, as the region tests use, replaces the restriction.
  6. The positional-autocorrelation attack in tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_gsea_structure.py is a strict xfail until (2) lands. The scattered-set arm is gated.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: Statistician probe (R = 2,000 per arm, Slurm 1865631, 1865650, 1865653), rejection rate at α = 0.05: - AR(1) φ 0.5, one run of 15 adjacent TUs: 0.186. - AR(1) φ 0.5, five runs of 3 TUs: 0.130. - AR(1) φ 0.2, one run of 15 TUs: 0.085. - AR(1) φ 0.5, 15 scattered TUs: 0.0555.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A new flag value in the §9.4 vocabulary, through the schema.
  • The report and V14 must not present flagged rows as calibrated.

docs.title: ADR-0026: Abundance GSEA is conditional on detection (restricted claim and flag)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-21, in session: "3 c 4 a. The rest keep recommended")
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Spec sections: §7.7.4, §8.2
  • Needs Khoa: yes (a claim restriction). Answered: option (c).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Only detected genes are ranked. When a set's genes are harder to detect, its detected members are selected for high abundance, so the set looks enriched without any true difference.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• GSEA results are stated as "conditional on detection, with no p_detect adjustment" in the methods note, the report and V14.
  • Rows of sets whose detection rate differs from the background carry a flag. The M8-05 follow-up defines the flag and its threshold, and the statistician signs them off.
  • Censored ranks for undetected genes (blom_scores(x, censored_mask)) and a p_detect-weighted null are left for a later ADR.
  • The detectability-confounding attack is a strict xfail.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: Statistician probe, rejection rate at α = 0.05: - detection logistic(2(a − 1.5·[in set] + 0.5)): 0.786; - weaker confounding (shift 1.0, slope 1): 0.137.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One new flag value.
  • "No significant set" is never reported as "no enrichment".

docs.title: ADR-0027: GSEA reports NES without a confidence interval (§8.2 deviation)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-21, in session: "3 c 4 a. The rest keep recommended")
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Spec sections: §8.2, §7.7.4, §9 tables/enrichment_gsea.tsv
  • Needs Khoa: yes (a deviation from §8.2). Answered: option (a).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: §8.2 asks every effect for a CI. fgsea's normalised enrichment score has none.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• NES is a descriptive effect size. Every GSEA row carries ci_unestimated.
  • log2err is a Monte Carlo precision label only.
  • No second effect size with a CI is added.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: The M8-05 tests pin ci_unestimated on every row.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The report shows NES without an interval.

docs.title: ADR-0028 (ADR-B): GSEA ranks median-centred TU scores
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-21, in session: "3 c 4 a. The rest keep recommended")
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Spec sections: §7.7.4
  • Needs Khoa: yes (a methods choice). Answered: option (a).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Each TU's score is its mean log2 abundance. All of these are positive, so under scoreType = std the test becomes effectively one-sided.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Rank TU scores centred on their median (M8-05 lead decision 1).
  • Imputed values count in the TU mean (decision 2); the §8.6 reruns vary the imputation.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text:
• The statistician's probe: centring changes the weights only, so the level under exchangeability is unchanged.
  • Rejection at α = 0.05 is 0.0526 under the null (R = 10,000) and 0.0475–0.049 at 20–60 % median imputation.
  • M8-15 runs a centred-versus-raw level and power arm.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: None beyond M8-05.

docs.title: ADR-0029: Detection ORA uses the conditional Poisson-binomial null, counted in TUs
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-21, in session: "3 c 4 a. The rest keep recommended")
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Spec sections: §7.7.3, §8.4
  • Needs Khoa: yes (replaces the Wallenius gate the spec names). Answered: option (a).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Two problems with the Wallenius approach: - Wallenius's noncentral hypergeometric only approximates the exact null when each gene has its own detection probability. That null is the conditional Poisson-binomial: the number detected in the set, given the total number detected (M8-01 lead decision 5). - Genes in one TU are detected together. Counting them as independent genes is anti-conservative.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• The ORA p-value is computed under the conditional Poisson-binomial null.
  • The unit is the TU: a TU is detected when any of its genes is, with probability 1 − ∏(1 − p_detect).
  • Wallenius (M8-01) stays as the classic weighted p (p_classic, odds_weight) and for golden parity with R.
  • M8-04 implements this. Until its calibration passes, ORA rows carry no calibrated claim.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: The M8-01 statistician review. M8-04's calibration arms are the gate.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: M8-04's design changes. M8-15 covers TU-level ORA.

docs.title: ADR-0030: Detection-limit model (M6-02): the pass-1 calibration choices
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-21, in session: "3 c 4 a. The rest keep recommended")
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Spec sections: §7.4 (detection limit), §8.4; docs/specs/M6-02-detection-limit-model.md decisions 5–9
  • Needs Khoa: yes (a protected tolerance key and event definitions). Answered: accept all for pass 1.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. CITL gate.
  2. DL1 gates calibration-in-the-large at |CITL| ≤ 0.2. CITL is the intercept of d on logit(p̂), with the slope fixed at 1.
  3. The gate uses the new protected key detection_limit_citl_max_abs: 0.2 in tests/calibration/tolerances.yaml, added in a follow-up commit with Gate-Change-Approved: ADR-0030.
  4. CITL is also recorded at k_min = 2.
  5. N1. The one-detected event in the operon test means "fewer than k_min observable peptides seen" for the partner, not the gene-level FDR call.
  6. Replicate model in pass 1.
  7. With exactly 2 runs the replicate model is usable = False (replicate_two_runs).
  8. The replicate p_detect stays the pooled per-run q.
  9. For hardening: widening training to every gene seen in at least one run (which makes 2 runs usable), and 1 − (1 − q)^R.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: The M6-02 statistician review and its re-check (68860bd, PR #157).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• test_detection_limit_citl.py moves from record-only to gated once the key lands.
  • M6-05H uses the N1 definition.

docs.title: ADR-0031: Determinants ΔR² bias tolerance 0.05; the ΔR² interval stays ci_unestimated
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-21, in session: "3 c 4 a. The rest keep recommended")
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Spec sections: §7.8, §8.2; docs/specs/M8-08-determinants-models.md decisions 5–6
  • Needs Khoa: yes (a protected tolerance key). Answered: as recommended.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Add the protected key determinants_delta_r2_max_abs_bias: 0.05 to tests/calibration/tolerances.yaml, in a follow-up commit with Gate-Change-Approved: ADR-0031.
  • On simulated data, a planted block's mean ΔR² must be within 0.05 of truth, and every noise block's within 0.05 of 0.
  • The ΔR² t-interval over CV repeats is not calibrated, because the repeats share data. ΔR² rows keep ci_unestimated.
  • A calibrated ΔR² CI is hardening work.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: tests/calibration/test_determinants_models_calibration.py (calibration_nightly) gates on the key.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The M8-08 calibration gate becomes active once the key lands.

docs.title: ADR-0032: Univariate determinants CIs stay ci_unestimated in pass 1; a calibrated SE in hardening
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-21, in session: "Take your recommendations")
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Spec sections: §7.8, §8.2, §8.5; docs/specs/M8-08-determinants-models.md decision 7
  • Needs Khoa: yes (an uncalibrated interval). Answered: option (a) now, (b) in hardening.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Under a TU-structured null, the TU-block bootstrap 95 % CIs of Spearman ρ and AUROC miss at 0.065–0.072. The bound is 0.064 (statistician, Slurm 1866223 and 1866311). The bootstrap SE is 5–9 % low, and percentile, normal and basic intervals all miss alike.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Pass 1: every univariate row carries ci_unestimated. The numbers are descriptive screening statistics with no discovery claim. The attack test records the level and does not gate it while the rows are flagged.
  • Hardening: a studentised TU-level bootstrap or a cluster-jackknife SE. Once its attack passes, the flag is removed.
  • Rejected: TU-collapsed statistics, because they change what the number means.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text:
• tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_determinants_tu_null.py, fast tier (Slurm 1866499): ρ 0.09 and AUROC 0.07 at R = 100.
  • The gene bootstrap misses at 0.25–0.27.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The report and V15 show these CIs as uncalibrated.

docs.title: ADR-0033: Elastic-net ΔR² is the primary block attribution; LightGBM early stopping in hardening
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-21, in session: "Take your recommendations")
  • Date: 2026-10-21
  • Spec sections: §7.8, §5.2 (LightGBM parameters), §9 tables/determinants_model.tsv
  • Needs Khoa: yes (what the report presents as the attribution). Answered: option (c), plus (a) in hardening.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: With the §5.2 LightGBM parameters at n = 400–600 genes: - CV R² is −0.27 under the null. - In a planted world, ΔR²(codon) is 0.97 against a true 0.80. The elastic net is unbiased in both worlds, and the M8-09 permutation p stays valid for both models.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Pass 1: the elastic-net ΔR² is the primary block attribution in the report and V15.
  • LightGBM ΔR² and SHAP shares are reported as secondary, nonlinear checks. Their rows are not gated against truth.
  • determinants_delta_r2_max_abs_bias (ADR-0031) gates the elastic net.
  • Hardening: LightGBM early stopping inside the inner CV, with the number of trees chosen per fold. The LightGBM bias is then re-measured, and if it passes the bias gate the LightGBM ΔR² becomes primary again.
  • The §5.2 defaults stay unchanged until that evidence exists.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: Statistician probe p3_cv.py (Slurm 1865752, 64 replicates) and the planted calibration world.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• M8-10 and M9 present the elastic net first.
  • SHAP (M8-09) stays a LightGBM output, with a caveat.

docs.title: ADR-0034: The determinants permutation null p is null_uncalibrated in pass 1; a structure-aware null in hardening
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-22, in session: "Flag it (Recommended)")
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §7.8, §8.4, §8.5; docs/specs/M8-09 (rule 6); statistician review of #173
  • Needs Khoa: yes, because a p-value ships uncalibrated. Answered: flag it now, a structure-aware null in hardening.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The M8-09 null permutes TU response blocks within TU-size groups. It is valid when TUs are exchangeable, and in that world it holds level at R = 200, α 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10: - LightGBM: 0.010 / 0.040 / 0.105. - Elastic net: conservative, 0 / 0.005 / 0.020.

Real proteomes also have inter-TU autocorrelation along the genome and detection selection. Under the statistician's §8.5 attacks (R = 100, B = 99; Slurm 1867304, 1867334, 1867348, 1867349) the null fails. Rejection rates against the bounds 0.030 / 0.094 / 0.160:

Attack LightGBM Elastic net inter-TU AR(1) abundance with an AR(1) covariate 0.02 / 0.12 / 0.23 0.05 / 0.12 / 0.13 the same plus replichore_position 0.80 / 0.95 / 0.96 0.33 / 0.41 / 0.43 detection depends on abundance and length, y independent of X 0.21 / 0.53 / 0.69 0.64 / 0.83 / 0.86

The statistician tried three alternatives, and none fixes every arm: - Circular shifts within size groups: not enough. - Spatially contiguous TU folds: fix the AR(1) arm (elastic net 0.02 / 0.06 / 0.06), but not the arm with replichore_position. - Stratifying by detectability: still 0.46 at α 0.05 in the detection arm.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Pass 1: every null result carries null_uncalibrated, and M8-10 carries it onto the null_p row. The p is valid only for exchangeable TUs and is not a discovery claim. A NaN observed R² also gets unestimated. The attack test (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_determinants_null.py) records the level, and does not gate on it, while every result is flagged (the ADR-0032 pattern).
  • Hardening:
  • spatially contiguous CV folds for both the observed CV and the null;
  • a decision on positional features (replichore_position): drop them, or condition the null on them;
  • a detection-selection model.

The flag is removed only when every attack arm passes. - Rejected: shipping the p unflagged with a caveat in the methods note only. The p would then read as a discovery claim.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text:
• Statistician probes: $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m809-null/ (probe*.py, results*.jsonl, summ.py, the sbatch files). In the original runs the attack arms failed at the fast tier: 5 of 6 cases in Slurm 1867349.
  • The attack file runs at the fast tier, R = 20. Unflagged, 5 of its 6 cases fail; flagged, it records the rates.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The report and V15 show the null p as uncalibrated, alongside the ADR-0032 univariate CIs.
  • The ΔR² attribution (ADR-0033) is unaffected: it is an effect size, not a test.

docs.title: ADR-0035: The ORA TU detection probability is a cross-fitted TU-level recalibration of q = 1 − ∏(1 − p̂)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-22, in session: "TU recalibration (Recommended)")
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §7.7, §8.4, §8.5; ADR-0029; docs/specs/M8-04-category-summary-ora.md (lead decision 4)
  • Needs Khoa: yes (lead decision 4: a failed TU-packed arm sends the TU-detectability formula to Khoa). Answered: TU recalibration.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ADR-0029 counts ORA in TUs. Each TU has detection probability q = 1 − ∏(1 − p̂) over its eligible genes, and the test is the conditional Poisson-binomial law of K given N (M8-04a). That primitive is exact for any q (statistician, #172). The problem is the q formula itself. When genes of a TU share a detection effect, or p̂ is miscalibrated at gene level, q is biased, and the bias grows with TU size.

The statistician's attack used p̂ equal to the exact marginal over a shared TU effect of strength c, with 3,000 p values per cell. Bounds are 0.0136 at α 0.01 and 0.058 at α 0.05. Slurm 1867453 and 1867454; files in $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m8-04a-review/.

Scenario Categories Tail α 0.01 α 0.05 c 1.5 large TUs under 0.107 0.248 c 1.5 single-gene TUs over 0.019 0.079 c 2.5 large TUs under 0.278 0.490 c 2.5 single-gene TUs over 0.044 0.143 c 0, gene-level p̂ intercept +0.5 large TUs under 0.0137 0.067

With p̂ = p_true, every category type is at level. Random whole-TU categories (spec arm 4) do not show the bias.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. q is recalibrated. M8-04b fits a logistic model of observed TU detection on logit q and log(eligible gene count). The fit is cross-fitted on M4-13's TU folds, so a TU's own detection never enters its q. The fitted value is the TU detection probability passed to the conditional law. The statistician's in-sample probe of this fit restored level.
  2. Numerics are part of the decision.
  3. TuUniverse carries the log complement Σ log1p(−p̂), with q = −expm1(Σ).
  4. tilt_pair accepts a complement input, so it never re-derives 1 − q from a rounded q.
  5. A p̂ of exactly 0 or 1 from M4-13 is clipped to [1e-12, 1 − 1e-12] and flagged, never treated as certain.
  6. The degenerate-case table drops "unreachable from M4-13".
  7. Gated arms. M8-14 and M8-15 add two arms, both scored by level in each direction:
  8. 4b: the TU-packed generator, with categories built from TUs of at least 4 genes and from single-gene TUs.
  9. 4c: a gene-level p̂ intercept shift of ±0.5.

The calibration switches from tilt to tilt_pair, and a tilt-stress level arm is added. If 4b or 4c fails after recalibration, the ORA rows get ora_uncalibrated, following the ADR-0034 pattern, until a hardening fix lands. 4. Rejected options. - Flag and ship the uncalibrated q: ORA would become descriptive only. - Gene-level ORA as primary: it ignores operon co-detection, which ADR-0029 was adopted to handle.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text:
• Before: the table above.
  • After: an in-sample recalibration probe at level (statistician, #172). The cross-fitted version is gated by arms 4b and 4c in M8-15.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• M8-04b gains one logistic fit per run, which is cheap. The ORA columns and the §9.3 schema do not change.
  • M4-13's p̂ calibration is no longer assumed at TU level. The methods note must say that conditioning on N cancels only a common TU-level odds factor.

docs.title: ADR-0036: M8 function tables carry four columns and five run flags beyond GIAP_SPEC.md §9.3 and §9.4
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-22, in session: "accept")
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §7.7.2, §7.7.3, §9.2, §9.3 (category_summary.tsv, enrichment_detection.tsv), §9.4 (Run scope); amends ADR-0029; docs/specs/M8-06-function-step-and-run.md (questions 4 and 9, lead decisions 1 and 2); docs/specs/M8-04-category-summary-ora.md (lead decisions 3 and 13); M8-index "ADR-A" (index decision 12)
  • Needs Khoa: yes (answered 2026-10-22: accept). It adds columns to two §9.3 dictionaries and five tokens to the §9.4 run vocabulary. The lead's default is option (a). M8-06a goes ahead on that default (M8-06 lead decision 2). If Khoa rejects this ADR, only the two table schemas and the COLUMNS tuples change.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• §9.3 lists these columns:
  • category_summary.tsv: collection, category, name, n_genes, n_detected, expected, o_minus_e, ci_low, ci_high, median_abundance_log2, coverage. There is no flags column.
  • enrichment_detection.tsv: collection, term, name, direction, n_universe, n_in_set, n_detected, k_detected_in_set, odds_weight, p_classic, parent_group, coverage, plus the §9.2 test columns.
  • ADR-0029 changed what these columns mean. The ORA unit is the TU and the null is the conditional Poisson-binomial (CPB). The four count columns are now counted in TUs. p_classic is now the gene-level Wallenius tail, kept only for comparison and goseq parity. In §7.7.3, p_classic meant "the non-elim p of the reported test". Under ADR-0029 that quantity has no column.
  • M8-index ADR-A (index decision 12) added a flags column to enrichment_detection, enrichment_gsea and determinants_model, because R4 needs an unestimated token somewhere. It does not cover category_summary. ADR-A was recorded as a lead-level decision in the M8 index, not as an ADR file.
  • The code in PR #179 (origin/m8/ora) and the schemas on origin/m8/function-step already contain the four extra columns:
  • src/giap/function/summary.py COLUMNS ends in flags;
  • src/giap/function/ora.py COLUMNS has n_in_set_genes and k_detected_in_set_genes after k_detected_in_set, and p_noelim after p_classic;
  • src/giap/schemas/tables/category_summary.schema.json and enrichment_detection.schema.json match those tuples. A schema-equals-COLUMNS test pins them (M8-06 lead decision 3).
  • Five run-level tokens come out of the function step, through df.attrs["run_flags"] and the M8-06 step guard. §9.4's Run scope lists only anti_sd_default, c_assumed, layer_missing:<layer>, bakta_db_light and operon_source_distance_model.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Option (a): accept all four columns and all five run tokens as written on origin/m8/function-step. Every addition is non-breaking under §9.2's semantic versioning: a new column goes last or next to its partner, and no existing column is renamed or retyped.

docs.title: 1. Columns
docs.text:
Table Column Position Type and constraints (schema) Meaning Why it is needed category_summary flags last ;-joined tokens; pattern allows only ci_few_units today Row flags. ci_few_units: the category has fewer than CI_MIN_UNITS = 10 TUs (summary.py), so the TU block-bootstrap CI is not computed and ci_low/ci_high are NA. §9.2 requires flags in a flags column. R4 requires every NA to say why. Without the column, an NA CI is unexplained. ADR-A gave the other M8 tables this column but missed this one. The column also gives a home to any later CI-coverage token (statistician, #179: percentile CIs cover 0.886 at 10 TUs; backlog). enrichment_detection n_in_set_genes after k_detected_in_set int ≥ 0, required Eligible genes in the term: the gene-level n that p_classic (Wallenius on genes) uses. ADR-0029 moved n_in_set to TUs. Without this column the inputs of p_classic are not in the table, so it cannot be checked or compared with goseq. The M8-13 hardening golden test compares these counts with goseq's per-category counts (M8-04 "Hardening owed"). Readers also see partial-membership dilution as the gap between n_in_set (TUs) and n_in_set_genes. enrichment_detection k_detected_in_set_genes after n_in_set_genes int ≥ 0, required Detected eligible genes in the term: the gene-level k behind p_classic. Same as n_in_set_genes. The gene-level k cannot be recovered from the TU counts, because a detected TU can hold one detected member gene or several. enrichment_detection p_noelim after p_classic number in [0, 1]; NA when the law is undefined The CPB tail, in TUs, for the row's direction, on the term's full TU set before elim (M8-04 §6). For rows without elim (under, cog, kegg, go_slim) it equals p_value. For GO over rows it is the pre-elim p, and p_value is the elim p. It restores §7.7.3's "classic" (non-elim) p of the reported test, which ADR-0029 took out of p_classic. It shows when a GO parent is significant only through a child elim removed. It is descriptive only: it is never adjusted and never enters BH (M8-04 §5; methods note docs/methods/function.md on origin/m8/ora, "Tests per term"). This matters because it is not FDR-safe. With one planted child per parent it rejects 0.0093 / 0.0556 / 0.1172 at α 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10, against bounds 0.0118 / 0.0540 / 0.1055, while elim stays at 0.0008 / 0.0073 / 0.0189 ($GIAP_ROOT/stat/m804b/probe_elim.py, elim.log, 12,000 parents, R = 600; the job ID is not recorded in the log: owed).

The schema descriptions say which columns are in TUs (n_universe, n_in_set, n_detected, k_detected_in_set) and which are in genes (the two _genes columns). §9.2 puts units in column names only for physical quantities.

docs.title: 2. Run-scope flag tokens
docs.text:
These tokens go in the function.run_flags event now (M8-06 question 9, lead decision 1). They join the §9.4 Run vocabulary through the manifest schema during hardening, as operon_source_distance_model did.

Token Emitted when Source Also a row token? tu_recal_skipped ADR-0035's cross-fitted TU recalibration did not run: folds is None or empty (M4-13's constant model; tu_folds.parquet has only a header), a fold's training TUs have fewer than MIN_CLASS = 10 detected or undetected TUs, or the Newton fit failed. q falls back to q_raw. ora.tu_universe yes: every enrichment_detection row of that run (M8-04 decision 13) too_few_ranked_tus Fewer than 2 TUs have an abundance score, so enrichment_gsea.tsv is written with only a header. gsea.gsea_table no no_eligible_genes The gene table has no eligible (non-partial) gene, or is empty. All three tables are written with only a header (M8-06 step 2 guard). steps/function no p_detect_clipped At least one M4-13 p_detect was exactly 0 or 1 and was clipped to [1e-12, 1 − 1e-12] for the null (ADR-0035 decision 2). ora.tu_universe yes: rows whose full TU set holds a clipped TU null_degenerate The observed detection has probability 0 under the TU null (an undetected TU with q = 1). Every ORA p is NA and a UserWarning is raised. ora.detection_enrichment yes: every row, with unestimated

The run-only tokens (layer_missing:*, bakta_db_light, tu_recal_skipped, too_few_ranked_tus, no_eligible_genes) are not added to the category_summary or enrichment_gsea row patterns.

docs.title: 3. ADR-0029 amendment line
docs.text: ADR-0029 now reads with this addition: "enrichment_detection.tsv counts are in TUs. p_classic is gene-level Wallenius, with its gene counts in n_in_set_genes and k_detected_in_set_genes. p_noelim is the full-set TU CPB p. Only p_value enters BH."

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• (a) Accept all four columns and the five run tokens (lead default; chosen above). Non-breaking. It matches the code and schemas already under review. Nothing is lost.
  • (b) Drop some columns and fold them into flags or the methods note. Rejected.
  • p_noelim and the gene counts are numbers, and a flag cannot carry a number.
  • The methods note is per method, not per row. Without the gene counts, p_classic cannot be checked against goseq for a single term. Without p_noelim, a reader cannot tell an elim-reduced GO parent from one with no signal.
  • The gene counts cannot be re-derived from the published tables: that needs the gene table and the collection resources.
  • Dropping category_summary.flags leaves NA CIs unexplained (R4).
  • (c) Put the extra columns in a sidecar table (for example tables/enrichment_detection_detail.tsv). Rejected.
  • It adds a fourth function table, a schema, a join key (collection, term, direction) and a publishing rule. M6-08 decision 7 publishes only the three tables/*.tsv files.
  • It splits one row's statistics across two files, so a reader of p_classic would need a join to see its inputs.
  • It solves no compatibility problem, because the added columns are already non-breaking.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text:
• Before: §9.3 has no home for the gene-level inputs of p_classic after ADR-0029, for the non-elim CPB p, or for the reason a category_summary CI is NA.
  • After:
  • the columns are in summary.COLUMNS and ora.COLUMNS (origin/m8/ora) and in both schemas (origin/m8/function-step), pinned by the schema-equals-COLUMNS test (M8-06 lead decision 3);
  • the run tokens are covered by M8-06 examples 1 and 4–7 (tu_recal_skipped, no_eligible_genes, layer_missing:*) and by #179's skip-path and degenerate-run tests;
  • the elim-versus-p_noelim rates above are the evidence that p_noelim must stay out of BH.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• §9.3 reads as amended for these two tables. The §9.4 Run row gains five tokens, registered through the manifest schema during hardening.
  • Report and V7 legends label p_noelim and p_classic as "not adjusted; not a discovery claim".
  • Rejecting this ADR, wholly or in part, changes only the two schemas, the COLUMNS tuples and their pinning test. No statistic changes.
  • Open for the lead:
  • The function row tokens (ci_unestimated, unestimated, odds_out_of_range, elim_empty, ora_uncalibrated, ci_few_units and GSEA's size_filtered, genomic_cluster, detection_confounded) are not in any §9.4 scope either. They are registered only in the table schemas, which §9.4's title allows ("extend only through the schema"). Should §9.4 gain a "Function" scope row in hardening?
  • ADR-A (index decision 12) exists only as a decision in the M8 index. Should it become an ADR file, or should this ADR be read as covering it for the function tables?

docs.title: ADR-0037: The ORA TU detection recalibration becomes a flexible cross-fitted ridge logistic (pass 2)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-22, in session: "accept")
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §7.7.3, §8.4, §8.5; amends ADR-0035 decisions 1 and 3; ADR-0034 (flag pattern); ADR-0015 (blocks); docs/specs/M8-04-category-summary-ora.md (lead decisions 12 and 13); docs/methods/function.md "Detection enrichment" (origin/m8/ora)
  • Needs Khoa: yes (answered 2026-10-22: accept). It changes the model behind every ORA p-value, and it sets the rule for lifting ora_uncalibrated.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ADR-0035 is in place, but its model is not calibrated. - ADR-0035 recalibrates the TU detection probability with a cross-fitted logistic regression on [1, logit q_raw, log n], where n is the TU's eligible-gene count. - PR #179 implements it with a damped Newton fit (M8-04 decision 13). - The conditional law is exact for whatever q it is given. Q itself is still misfit, so pass 1 puts ora_uncalibrated on every ORA row (decision 13; ora.CALIBRATION_FLAGS).

Pass-1 failures. The statistician re-checked #179 at c1e3ca0 with R = 2,000 per world, split into ADR-0015 blocks (replicates 0–999 and 1000–1999). Source: $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m804b/recheck/pr179_recheck_comment.txt and summ_blocks.txt, Slurm 1867941 and 1867942. Rates are at α 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10, with the flag ignored. Every row below is above the §8.4 bound in both blocks.

What holds at level in both blocks: - the null world, 4c at a = ±0.5 and slope b = 1.4 (slope b = 0.7 fails one cell at α 0.10; see decision 7); - random whole-TU and single-gene categories in every world; - the oracle q (the exact TU marginal, on the same detections) in every cell of all 13 worlds.

So the failures come from the 3-parameter model, not from the conditional law. Any category selected on TU size or on q is at risk (methods note, "Pass-1 limit").

How these numbers were obtained and what they do not show: - The 4b c 2.5 large-under row is the statistician's own figure. The lead recomputed the other rows by running $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m804b/summ.py, unchanged, on the seven flex_*.jsonl files. That pass found no flexible-model cell above its bound in any world, in either direction, at any α. - Splitting the same records at replicate 1000 (recheck/summ_blocks.py, unchanged) also gives no exceedance. Those are 1,000 and 2,000 replicates, not two equal ADR-0015 blocks, and no statistician has reviewed that split. - The flexible model has no measured rates yet in the null world, 4b c 3.5, 4c at a = ±0.5, or slope b = 0.7 and 1.4 (owed). - Its power has not been measured against the 3-parameter model on any planted-effect arm (owed). - Many cells are well below α, for example big_large under at 0.0008 against α 0.01. The model may be conservative there.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Adopt the flexible model as the pass-2 replacement for ADR-0035 decision 1's model. The cross-fitting, the conditional law, the tilt and the numerics of ADR-0035 decision 2 do not change. Each detail below is marked [probe] when probe_flex.py fixes it, or [proposed] when it is a default this ADR proposes.

docs.title: 1. Design matrix (12 columns)
docs.text:
For TU t, with ℓ_t = logit q_raw,t = log q_raw,t − log_comp,t and n_t = the TU's eligible-gene count (TuUniverse.n_genes):

x_t = [ 1, ℓ_t, (ℓ_t − κ₁)₊, (ℓ_t − κ₂)₊, (ℓ_t − κ₃)₊, (ℓ_t − κ₄)₊, 1{n_t = 2}, 1{n_t = 3}, 1{n_t = 4}, 1{5 ≤ n_t ≤ 6}, 1{n_t ≥ 7}, ℓ_t · log n_t ]

  • [probe] design():
  • the intercept, the linear ℓ term, 4 hinges, 5 size indicators with n = 1 as the reference level, and the interaction ℓ · log n;
  • no separate log n main effect, because the indicators carry the size effect;
  • (a)₊ = max(a, 0).
  • [probe docstring vs code] The module docstring says "5 quantile knots" and "{1,2,3,4,5-6,7+}". The code uses 4 knots and 5 indicators, with size 1 absorbed into the intercept. This ADR adopts what the code does, because that is what was measured.
  • The fitted η_t = x_t·β̂ gives q_t = expit(η_t) and comp_t = expit(−η_t), each computed directly (ADR-0035 decision 2, unchanged).

docs.title: 2. Knots (cross-fitted)
docs.text:
• [probe] For each fold j, the knots κ₁…κ₄ are the 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 quantiles of ℓ over the training TUs only (fold ≠ j). They use numpy's default linear interpolation (np.quantile).
  • [probe] The held-out fold's design uses the training fold's knots. A held-out TU's ℓ never affects its own knots.
  • [proposed] Repeated knots, which happen when many training TUs share one q_raw, are de-duplicated. A knot at or above the largest training ℓ is dropped, because its hinge column would be all zero. The probe does neither and relies on the ridge to absorb the collinear or empty columns.

docs.title: 3. Size bins
docs.text:
• [probe] n_t is the eligible-gene count, not tu_size. The bins are {1} (reference), {2}, {3}, {4}, {5, 6}, {7, …}.
  • [proposed] No upper cap. The probe codes the top bin as (7, 99), so a TU with ≥ 100 eligible genes would land in the reference bin. That cap never mattered in the probe, because the generator caps TU sizes at 8 (probe.py world). Production uses n ≥ 7 with no cap.
  • [proposed] Thin bins are merged. A bin whose training TUs number fewer than MIN_BIN_TUS = 10 is merged into the next smaller non-reference bin: 7+ into 5–6, then into 4, then into 3, then into 2. A non-reference bin with no smaller bin left is merged into the reference. This happens per fold, and held-out TUs follow the same merge. The probe leaves a thin bin in place, and the ridge shrinks its coefficient to near 0, so a held-out TU in that bin is predicted as a single-gene TU. That is the opposite of the size effect the bin exists to capture.

docs.title: 4. Ridge penalty
docs.text:
• [probe] The penalised log-likelihood is Σ_t [y_t η_t − log(1 + e^{η_t})] − ½ λ Σ_{k ≥ 1} β_k², with λ = 1e-4. The intercept is not penalised. The columns are not standardised.
  • The penalty shrinks the ℓ slope toward 0, not toward the identity slope of 1. At λ = 1e-4 against roughly a thousand training TUs this is negligible, and it is what was measured.
  • [proposed] λ is a module constant (RECAL_RIDGE), not a user parameter. A different value needs a new calibration run.

docs.title: 5. Solver
docs.text:
• [probe] The probe uses plain Newton on the penalised objective: the gradient is Xᵀ(y − μ) − λβ and the Hessian is XᵀWX + λI′ (I′ has 0 for the intercept). It starts at β = 0, runs at most 100 iterations and stops when max |step| < 1e-9. It has no step halving and no failure return, so a non-converged fit is used silently.
  • [proposed] Production reuses #179's damped Newton (ora._logistic_mle, decision 13) with the penalty added to the objective, the gradient and the Hessian:
  • it starts at the identity: intercept 0, ℓ slope 1, every other coefficient 0;
  • each step is halved until the penalised log-likelihood does not decrease beyond LL_NOISE;
  • it has converged when the full step is below NEWTON_TOL = 1e-10, within MAX_NEWTON = 50 iterations and MAX_HALVINGS = 60 halvings;
  • it returns None on a non-finite step or no convergence.

With λ > 0 the penalised objective is strictly concave once the intercept column is non-zero, so the Hessian is non-singular and the stationary point is unique. The #179 re-check's argument that the slack cannot fake convergence carries over (recheck/newton_summary.txt). - [proposed] An independent per-fold oracle test (scipy minimize on the same penalised objective, about 1e-8 relative) replaces test_ora_recal_oracle.py's unpenalised oracle.

docs.title: 6. Skip rules and the minimum TU count
docs.text:
The model has p = 12 coefficients, against 3 for the pass-1 model. With 5 folds, each fit sees about 4/5 of the TUs. The small-genome world (321–410 TUs, recheck/res_small_c2.5.jsonl) therefore fits 12 coefficients on about 260–330 training TUs, and the flexible model was at level there. How many detected and undetected training TUs it had is not logged (owed).

The proposed ladder is evaluated per run. Every fold must meet a rung for the run to use it.

  1. Flexible model. Used when every fold's training TUs have min(detected, undetected) ≥ EPV × (p_j − 1). Here p_j is the column count after the knot and bin reductions of 2 and 3. [proposed] EPV = 10 events per non-intercept column, the usual logistic rule of thumb, which is 110 per class at full size. Whether the 800-gene world meets 110 per class is unmeasured. If it does not, the statistician should re-run the small world at a lower EPV before this rung is fixed (owed).
  2. Reduced model. Used when rung 1 fails but every fold still has min(detected, undetected) ≥ MIN_CLASS = 10, the pass-1 rule. The run uses the ADR-0035 3-parameter model. Every row keeps ora_uncalibrated permanently, and the run adds [proposed] the new token tu_recal_reduced (run flag and row flag; it is registered through the schemas, as in ADR-0036).
  3. Skip. As in pass 1: folds is None or empty, a fold has fewer than MIN_CLASS of either class, or a fit fails. q = q_raw, and every row and the run carry tu_recal_skipped.
  4. [proposed] A failed flexible fit does not fall back to the reduced model. It skips. A silent change of model is what B3/B4 warned against.
  5. [proposed] Complete separation of the training classes by the fitted training η is also a skip. Ridge keeps β finite, but the fitted q would be meaningless.

Skipped and reduced fits keep ora_uncalibrated permanently. It does not depend on the lift below. As the #179 re-check carry-over requires, the commit that empties CALIBRATION_FLAGS must add the flag explicitly on these paths. test_ora_review_179.py pins this.

docs.title: 7. Lift rule for ora_uncalibrated on fitted rows
docs.text:
The flag comes off rows fitted with the flexible model only when all of the following hold in one recorded full-tier run: - every cell of arms 4b, 4c, 4d, 4e and 4f, of the combination world (4b + 4c), of size-dependent co-detection (csize) and of the small genome passes the §8.4 bound in both blocks, at every α in {0.01, 0.05, 0.10} and in both directions. Cells include the low-q (loq_any) and ≥ 2-gene (big_multi) categories, not only large and high-q ones (re-check "Pass-2 target"); - each block has R ≥ 1,000; - the rates are logged per cell and per block, with the commit and Slurm job ID, in the calibration records. Full-tier rate logging is owed (backlog).

This is stricter than an ADR-0015 gate, where a failure only in the first block counts as unconfirmed, not as a fail. Here an unconfirmed cell also blocks the lift.

[proposed] Two more conditions: - The slope b = 0.7 world (gene-level p̂ too steep) joins the cells that must pass. In recheck/summ_blocks.txt its big_large under cell fails at α 0.10 in both blocks: 0.1185 and 0.1175 against 0.1134 (Slurm 1867941 and 1867942). The re-check comment's table does not list it. - The cells at level today must stay at level under the same rule: the null, slope b = 1.4, 4c, and the random whole-TU and single-gene categories.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• (a) The flexible model (proposed above). It is the only candidate with measured rates at level in the cells where pass 1 fails (see Context).
  • Cost: 12 coefficients per fold instead of 3, and still one Newton fit per fold per run.
  • Risks:
    • the small-genome and rule-count limits (decision 6);
    • its power and its null-world rates are not yet measured;
    • its form was chosen by looking at the same attack worlds it was scored on, so the full-tier run has to use fresh seeds.
  • (b) Keep the 3-parameter model and the flag permanently. Rejected. ORA would never become a discovery claim. Its failures are in routine category kinds within [5, 500], such as high-q operons, categories of 100–200 multi-gene TUs, and deep-coverage runs, and they reach 0.07–0.08 at α 0.01 (combo large_hiq under, 0.0807 / 0.0810; csize large under, 0.0743 / 0.0788). This is ADR-0035's rejected "flag and ship" option, made permanent.
  • (c) A nonparametric recalibration: isotonic regression, or a GAM. Not chosen.
  • Isotonic regression in ℓ alone cannot express the size effect that csize and combo need. A version per size bin multiplies the small-sample problem of decision 6, and its step function puts ties at the bin edges.
  • A GAM, for example a spline in ℓ by size with a penalty chosen by cross-validation, is close in spirit to (a). It adds nested tuning inside each cross-fit fold and possibly a new dependency (licence check under the import rules: owed).
  • Neither has measured rates (owed). (a) is a fixed-basis, lightly penalised version of the same idea, with evidence.
  • (d) A stratified exact TU marginal: model the oracle q directly. Not chosen for pass 2.
  • The statistician notes that the oracle q, 1 − E_u ∏_g (1 − expit(η_g + c·u)), is at level in every cell of every world.
  • It is not computable from GIAP's inputs as they stand. It needs the per-gene conditional linear predictor η_g and the strength and distribution of the shared TU effect, c and u ~ N(0, 1). M4-13 provides only the marginal p̂, and the probe computes the oracle from the generator's true η and c with 40-node Gauss–Hermite quadrature (probe.py world).
  • Making it computable needs three things:
    • a TU random-intercept detectability model in M4-13, which is a change to another module and needs its own ADR;
    • an estimate of c, per size stratum, because csize shows c varies with size;
    • a per-gene inversion of p̂ = E_u expit(η_g + ĉ u) for η_g.
  • Its level would then depend on the estimation error in ĉ and on the logit-normal shared-effect form. That form is exactly the generator's, so the attack worlds cannot test it fairly.
  • It is the principled long-term target and a backlog candidate, not a pass-2 fix.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text:
• Before (pass 1, 3-parameter model): the Context table. Source: recheck/pr179_recheck_comment.txt and summ_blocks.txt, Slurm 1867941 and 1867942, R = 2,000 in two blocks, commit c1e3ca0.
  • Comparator (flexible model, prototype):
  • the Context table: probe_flex.py, flex_*.jsonl, Slurm 1867892 and 1867900, R = 3,000 pooled, worktree 3f82e0f, recomputed with summ.py;
  • the statistician's figure for 4b c 2.5 large under is 0.0053 / 0.0303 / 0.0623 (pr179_comment.txt);
  • the combo and hidet "recal" columns in those files used the old undamped Newton, which skipped 2,898 and 417 replicates. The flex columns were computed on every replicate whatever the PR model did.
  • After: owed, all of it.
  • The full-tier run of the decision 7 cells with the production implementation (decisions 1–6), in two blocks of R ≥ 1,000, with logged rates.
  • The worlds the flexible model has not been run on (null, 4b c 3.5, 4c ±0.5, slopes).
  • Power against the 3-parameter model on a planted-effect arm.
  • The small-genome class counts under the EPV rung.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Code: ora._recalibrate gains the design of decisions 1–3, the penalised damped Newton of decision 5 and the ladder of decision 6. TuUniverse.flags may hold tu_recal_reduced. The enrichment_detection schema's flag pattern gains tu_recal_reduced. The ORA columns do not change.
  • Tests:
  • a per-fold penalised oracle;
  • knot and bin edge cases: tied ℓ, an empty top bin, a TU with ≥ 100 genes;
  • the rungs of the ladder;
  • the explicit ora_uncalibrated on the skip and reduced paths.
  • Calibration: M8-15's attack file gains every decision 7 cell at the full tier, with rate logging. The fast tier stays a smoke test, because it cannot resolve 4b or 4f (re-check M5).
  • Methods note: "Recalibration" and "Pass-1 limit" are rewritten, and the note states that skipped and reduced runs remain uncalibrated.
  • Until the lift: nothing changes for users. Every row keeps ora_uncalibrated.
  • Questions for the lead and Khoa:
  • The statistician wrote "8 worlds", but there are 7 flex_*.jsonl world files. Which is the eighth? Possibly deep coverage counted twice, with and without the PR-skipped replicates.
  • Is EPV = 10 acceptable, given the risk that real small genomes fall to the reduced model?
  • Should the reduced rung exist, or should anything below rung 1 skip?
  • Should the decision 7 lift rule really be stricter than ADR-0015, so that an unconfirmed cell also blocks the lift?

docs.title: ADR-0038: GSEA runs R fgsea as an external tool
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-22)
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §7.7.4, §7.7.5, §11.5, G15, R5
  • Needs Khoa: no (Khoa decided the dependency, §2 decision G15 and item 5 on 2026-10-22)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: G15 and §7.7.4 make the abundance GSEA a Python and numba port of fgsea 1.36.2. R fgsea was only a fallback, used when the port misses the §11.5 golden tolerances. Port part I (fgsea_simple, M8-02) is merged. Part II, the multilevel stage (M8-11, PR #193), was written without the fgsea source: the R6 question about bioconductor.org is still open. So its sign correction and p-value indexing are unverified against fgsea. On 2026-10-22 Khoa decided that the pipeline calls R fgsea instead of a port.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Engine. enrichment_gsea.tsv comes from fgsea::fgseaMultilevel 1.36.2 run in R 4.5.
  2. It runs as a separate process in its own environment, workflow/envs/fgsea.yml: conda-forge and bioconda only, r-base, bioconductor-fgsea=1.36.2 and r-data.table, with an explicit lock in workflow/envs/locks/.
  3. It needs no Bioconductor data packages, so nothing is downloaded from bioconductor.org.
  4. Apptainer profiles use the BioContainers image of the same version, pinned by digest.
  5. What stays in Python. giap.function.gsea keeps its existing jobs and hands each collection to R as two TSVs, the TU scores and the sets in long form:
  6. the TU collapse, the set construction and the size limits (function.gsea_size);
  7. the redundancy re-test sets;
  8. BH within collections, the leading edge mapped back to genes, flags and the table writer.
  9. The R script. It lives in workflow/bin/giap_fgsea.R and never in src/ (R5).
  10. It calls fgseaMultilevel(sampleSize, eps, nPermSimple, minSize, maxSize, scoreType = "std", nproc = 1) with the function.gsea defaults, which are unchanged: 101, 0, 1000.
  11. It writes ES, NES, pval, log2err, size and leadingEdge, plus R.version.string and packageVersion("fgsea") for provenance.
  12. The seed is one integer from giap.rng.for_step("function.gsea", seed) passed to set.seed. With nproc = 1 (SerialParam), a rerun is byte-identical.
  13. Interfaces. METHOD = "fgsea_multilevel". The table columns, flags and schema are unchanged. The engine is still an injectable callable, so unit tests use fakes or recorded outputs (§11.4) and never R. A slow integration test and an nf-test run the real environment, on Slurm only.
  14. ORA. The detection ORA stays on scipy.stats.nchypergeom_wallenius. It is analytical and exact, not a port of an approximation, and it is still checked against goseq by the §11.5 golden data (#192). Calling goseq in the pipeline would pull in bioconductor-genelendatabase and bioconductor-go.db, whose install scripts download from bioconductor.org. The elim GO redundancy also needs many dependent re-tests, so each one would cost an R round trip.
  15. The port. PR #193 (multilevel port) is not merged and stays open as a draft for reference. The merged fgsea_simple stays until the R engine lands; the hardening pass then removes giap.stats.fgsea and its kernels, unless Khoa wants a no-R fallback.
  16. Golden data. The §11.5 fgsea golden outputs (#192) become a contract test of the wrapper. On the frozen inputs with GOLDEN_SEED, giap_fgsea.R must reproduce make_golden_r.R's fgsea table exactly. The goseq golden data keep validating the scipy ORA.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after)
docs.text:
• Before: the multilevel p-values come from an unverified reimplementation (#193 notes the missing source check).
  • After: by construction they are fgsea's own numbers; the remaining risk is the wrapper, which the contract test in item 7 covers.
  • Licence: fgsea is MIT and R is GPL-2. Both run only as separate processes, as R5 requires; check_imports.py and check_no_rscript.py still hold.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A new tool environment (about 1 GB) and an R start-up of a few seconds per function step. Runtime is otherwise the same order as fgsea itself.
  • function gains an external-tool dependency. giap check/preflight must report a missing fgsea environment the same way as other tools do.
  • G15 and §7.7.4 are superseded on the engine. The spec text stays read-only; this ADR overrides it.
  • The M8-11 multilevel calibration tests (#193) do not land. GSEA calibration (null uniformity, the operon-packing attack null) runs against the R engine on Slurm instead.

docs.title: ADR-0039: bioconductor.org as a download source for the R golden environment
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §3.2, R6, §11.5
  • Needs Khoa: yes (download source; decided by Khoa on 2026-10-22)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The §11.5 golden environment installs goseq from bioconda (scripts/golden/golden_r.explicit.txt, PR #192). goseq depends on two Bioconductor data packages, bioconductor-genelendatabase and bioconductor-go.db. Their bioconda post-link scripts download the package tarballs from bioconductor.org and check them against md5 sums. bioconductor.org is not listed in §3.2, so #192 was held under R6.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• bioconductor.org is added to the §3.2 sources, for one purpose only: the tarballs that bioconda post-link scripts fetch while building the R golden environment (§11.5, golden-r.yml, scripts/slurm/golden_r.sbatch).
  • Everything else in R6 still applies:
  • The artefacts are pinned. The conda packages are fixed by the explicit lock, with md5 sums.
  • The post-link checksum must pass.
  • No mirrors and no disabled TLS.
  • A failure is logged under PROGRESS.md › Blocked.
  • The pipeline's own environments never use this source. ADR-0038's fgsea environment needs no Bioconductor data packages, and the pipeline does not call goseq.
  • Nothing fetched from bioconductor.org is committed; only the golden outputs are.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: • The goseq golden data in #192 (Slurm 1868639) were produced this way. The md5 checks of both post-link downloads passed.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: • Any other use of bioconductor.org needs a new ADR.

docs.title: 192 is unblocked. The goseq Wallenius golden comparison (§7.7.5) validates the scipy ORA (ADR-0038
docs.text: item 5).

docs.title: ADR-0040: The manifest runs after the graph; finalize is split between the graph and the run tail
docs.text:
• Status: accepted (lead-level, 2026-10-22)
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §6.2 (rows finalize, manifest), §6.3 ("one process per Python step", Error strategy), §6.7, §9.1, §9.5; docs/specs/MVP-03-manifest-finalize.md (D-A, D-B, lead decisions 2, 3 and 13)
  • Needs Khoa: no. No default, threshold, output file, config key or protected file changes. The run order of giap run gains a tail; every §9.1 output keeps its path.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
§6.2 lists finalize and manifest as ordinary steps, and §6.3 runs every Python step as a Nextflow process. Three facts make that impossible for the manifest and awkward for finalize: - The Nextflow trace.tsv is complete only after Nextflow exits, and the manifest's steps[] and tools[] come from it. - A failed run must still get a manifest (§6.3 exit 4; MVP-03 example 11). A process downstream of the failed task never runs. - The set of tables that a run published, which the Frictionless descriptor must list, is known only once the graph has ended.

M9's in-graph plots and report processes (M9-02 item 8) read tables/genes.tsv, so that table cannot wait for the tail.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. manifest runs in the run tail. The step is registered (giap _step manifest works on files alone), but neither executor plans it: giap.runner.local.TAIL_STEPS = ("manifest",), and workflow/ has no MANIFEST process. giap run calls the tail under both executors after the graph, also after a failed step. The order is: rotate logs/events.jsonl → preflight → write OUT/work/provenance.json (the provenance core) → graph → tail. A preflight exit (1, 2, 3) writes no manifest. A tail error after a successful graph is exit 4 (step manifest failed; log: OUT/logs/manifest.log). After a failed graph a tail error is only logged and the original failure is kept.
  2. finalize is split. The in-graph finalize step owns tables/genes.tsv, and context_stats drops its genes_tsv output (MVP-03b). The descriptor half of the §6.2 row (OUT/schemas/datapackage.json plus the schema copies) is a function of the run tail, run before the manifest.
  3. The manifest schema keeps its repository name src/giap/schemas/run_manifest.schema.json. §9.5 calls it manifest.schema.json, but the repo and tests/unit/test_schemas.py use the former name (lead decision 13).

Alternative rejected: run finalize, plots, report and manifest all in the tail. That is simpler and executor-identical by construction, but it overturns M9-02's accepted report.nf design.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: • MVP-03a tests: tests/unit/manifest/test_manifest_cli_local.py and test_manifest_cli_nextflow.py pin the run order, the rotation, the failure exits and the "no manifest after preflight" rule under both executors. tests/integration/test_mvp03_manifest_executors.py (example 10) checks that stable_view is equal across executors. test_mvp03_manifest_resume.py (examples 11 and 12) covers the failed run and -resume.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• §6.3's "one process per Python step" has one exception, manifest. The tail is identical under both executors because it runs in the giap run process.
  • The manifest's provenance_digest is the SHA-256 of OUT/work/provenance.json, written before launch, so the in-graph report (M9-16) can stage it and print the same digest (lead decision 6).
  • MVP-03b adds finalize.nf and the datapackage writer of the tail. Later tail work (for example the pass-2 Frictionless validation of published tables) goes in the same tail.

docs.title: Amendment 1 (M9-16b, 2026-10-23; lead-level, no output path, default or config key changes)
docs.text:
• The tail re-renders the report after the manifest. After run_manifest.json is written with status == "completed", giap run (under either executor) re-renders OUT/report/report.html from OUT/ and the existing OUT/plots/. It draws no plot, and it writes atomically (report/.report.html.tmp, then os.replace). giap report uses the same rerender_report. The tail is therefore no longer the manifest alone (decision 1).
  • One-way dependency. The report depends on the manifest, never the reverse.
  • The report prints the manifest's file SHA-256 and its provenance_digest.
  • The manifest records no checksum of report/ or plots/.
  • A future output-checksum field must leave out report/, or be added after the re-render with an ADR.
  • The re-render is not a registered step: it does not appear in steps[] and emits no event to logs/events.jsonl.
  • Exit 4 on failure. A re-render failure after a completed graph and a written manifest is exit 4 (logs/report_tail.log): the same rule as a tail error after a successful graph. report.html keeps the in-graph page and the manifest is unchanged.
  • Skipped when the run did not complete. There is no re-render after a failed graph (exit 4/5), a failed manifest write, or a preflight exit (1/2/3). Work-directory copies keep the in-graph page, so -resume still caches REPORT_HTML.

docs.title: ADR-0041: Run-scope tokens beyond the §9.4 Run row
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §9.4 (Run row), §7.1, §6.7
  • Needs Khoa: yes (vocabulary; decided by Khoa on 2026-10-22)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: run_manifest.json (MVP-03, ADR-0040) collects run-scope flags. Four tokens that steps already emit, or that the manifest adds, are not in the §9.4 Run row. ADR-0036 treated additions to that row as Khoa-level, so MVP-03a kept them in RUN_FLAGS_PENDING. The schema accepts them, and the vocabulary test names them as pending.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The §9.4 Run row gains these four tokens:

Token Emitted by Meaning input_prefiltered placement the peptide input was already FDR-filtered upstream, so the placement FDR is conditional on that filter cai_reference_missing codon_usage no ribosomal-protein reference set was found, so CAI is NA no_detection_limit_model operons the detection-limit model was not fitted, so missed-operon calls fall back (also a pairs row token) uncalibrated:<key> the manifest (MVP-03c), from src/giap/data/calibration.yaml the claim <key> has no passing calibration on record (§7.1 "uncalibrated in the manifest", parameterised by claim)
  • RUN_FLAGS_PENDING becomes part of the accepted run vocabulary.
  • Steps that only log cai_reference_missing or no_detection_limit_model now emit an event (MVP-03a).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The manifest schema pattern is unchanged. The vocabulary test moves the four tokens from pending to accepted in a follow-up to #196.
  • The report (M9-16) lists them with the other run flags.

docs.title: ADR-0042: Calibration replicate counts for variants and compare
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §8.4, §12, §7.5.4, §7.9.3; M7-10, M7-13, M9-22
  • Needs Khoa: yes (protected tests/calibration/tolerances.yaml; decided by Khoa on 2026-10-22)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Two calibration claims have no replicates_fast or replicates_full key: - the variant suites: the M7-10 class error rates and the M7-13 F1 gate (f1_min.variants_high = 0.90 already exists); - the TU-block bootstrap CI for Spearman ρ in giap compare (M9-22).

Without a count neither suite can gate.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Add to tests/calibration/tolerances.yaml: - variants: 20 (fast) and variants: 100 (full). - Each replicate is a full simulation, alignment, pileup and calling, the same cost class as detectability and determinants (20/100). - At F1 ≈ 0.93 with a replicate spread of ≈ 0.03, the fast standard error is ≈ 0.007, enough to catch a drop below 0.90 at se_multiplier 2. - compare: 100 (fast) and compare: 1000 (full). - Replicates are cheap: table arithmetic on simulated pairs, like ora (100/1000). - At 1,000 replicates, 95 % coverage is measured to about ±1.4 %.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The M7-10 and M7-13 suites, and tests/calibration/test_compare_rho_ci.py (M9-22), gate instead of recording.
  • The values are applied in a follow-up PR carrying Gate-Change-Approved: ADR-0042.

docs.title: ADR-0043: Plot support files under OUT/plots/support/
docs.text:
• Status: accepted (lead)
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §7.9.4, §9.1, §9.2, §10.2 (V1, V2); docs/specs/M9-03-plot-support-run-inputs.md
  • Needs Khoa: no (a non-breaking addition to §9.1; no gate, threshold or protected file changes)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: V1 draws GC skew and oriC/terminus marks, and V2 draws oriC and terminus lines. None of these is in a §9.1 file: GC skew needs the genome sequence, and the oriC call is in the intermediate features.parquet. giap report OUT must rebuild every plot from OUT/ alone (§7.9.4) and has no genome argument (§5.1).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. A support file holds data that a plot needs, that no §9.1 file holds, and that only a step with the run's inputs (or a fitted model, M9-17) can compute. It lives under OUT/plots/support/.
  2. Format: TSV per §9.2. A table larger than 2^20 bytes is written as .tsv.gz with gzip mtime=0, so the bytes are deterministic. Exactly one of <name>.tsv and <name>.tsv.gz exists; a rewrite removes the other.
  3. Each support file is one Frictionless resource in datapackage.json, with the custom property role: plot_support and schema: plot_support/<name>.json (relative to src/giap/schemas).
  4. Positions are 1-based as written, like every published table (spec §6.5).
  5. The producing step writes it during giap run; giap report reads it and never writes or recomputes it. Missing support data gives the plot's empty state, not an error.
  6. A support file is not a result table: it has no §9.2 test columns and makes no claims.

The first two support files are replicon_landmarks (oriC, terminus) and gc_skew (10 kb windows), both written by the plots step (M9-03).

docs.title: Evidence (before → after)
docs.text:
• Before: V1/V2 could draw GC skew and oriC/ter only during giap run, so giap report OUT would produce different plots from the same run.
  • After: both entry points read the same support files; M9-03's step tests pin that giap report leaves them byte- and mtime-identical.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• §9.1 gains an optional plots/support/ directory; existing consumers are unaffected.
