  • M9-17 (plot support from fitted models) follows the same rules.

docs.title: ADR-0044: The Wallenius golden reference is the exact distribution, not goseq
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-23)
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §7.7.5 (criterion 1), §13 row M8, §11.4–11.5; M8-13 §1.1, question 3
  • Needs Khoa: yes (changes the reference of a §7.7.5 criterion and adds a key to the protected tests/calibration/tolerances.yaml)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
§7.7.5 criterion 1 compares GIAP's Wallenius p-values with goseq's at relative 1e-6 (golden_r.wallenius_rel_tol). On the committed M8-12 golden data (goseq 1.62.0, BiasedUrn 2.0.12, default precision = 1e-7), 36 of the 300 tails differ by more than that (M8-13 F3). The counts match for all 150 categories, and the odds match goseq's weight identity to 9e-16.

The statistician built a reference from the definition of Wallenius' distribution. No goseq or BiasedUrn code was used or read. It was computed two independent ways: - R1, urn recursion. The definition: N sequential draws without replacement, each red ball drawn with probability ω·r/(ω·r + w). Run in float64 and in 80-bit long double. Every term is a sum of products of positive factors, so nothing cancels. The two precisions agree to 3.8e-15 relative on all 300 tails. - R2, exact rational integral. f(x) = C(m₁,x) C(m₂,N−x) ∫₀¹ (1 − t^{ω/D})^x (1 − t^{1/D})^{N−x} dt, with D = ω(m₁ − x) + m₂ − N + x. The integral is expanded exactly as D Σⱼ (−1)ʲ C(x,j) B(ωj + D, N−x+1), where B(a, m+1) = m!/∏ᵢ₌₀ᵐ(a+i). This is exact in rationals because the float ω is a dyadic rational. The alternating sum is evaluated in fixed point with ≥ 200 surviving bits, so the cancellation is controlled.

R2 equals R1 to every printed digit (rel < 1e-15) on all 9 tails checked: - CAT_002 under; - CAT_003 over; - CAT_004 over and under; - CAT_011 over; - CAT_012 over; - CAT_013 under; - CAT_105 over; - CAT_137 over.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
On the 300 golden tails:

> 1e-6 against the exact reference max relative error max absolute error GIAP (wallenius_tails, scipy 1.18.1 pmf + fsum) 0 7.1e-12 5.8e-12 goseq / BiasedUrn 36 0.49 (and 1.0 where it returns 0) 2.6e-6

The failing tails, reference against goseq:

tail exact GIAP goseq goseq rel. error CAT_004 over 4.169558e-07 4.169558e-07 2.141283e-07 0.49 CAT_011 over 4.437464e-27 4.437464e-27 3.746333e-27 0.16 CAT_012 over 2.228390e-10 2.228390e-10 2.117715e-10 0.050 CAT_013 under 1.059794e-17 1.059794e-17 0 1 CAT_137 over 1.935414e-02 1.935414e-02 1.935152e-02 1.4e-4 31 others, p 0.1–0.99 — rel ≤ 5e-12 — 1.4e-6 – 1.8e-5

What goes wrong in goseq, from its outputs alone (goseq computes over = dWNCHypergeo(k) + pWNCHypergeo(k, lower.tail = FALSE) and under = pWNCHypergeo(k)): - The point mass is accurate. over + under − 1 equals the exact pmf(k) to 5.5e-8 relative on every category with pmf(k) > 1e-6. On CAT_004 and CAT_011, goseq's whole over-p equals pmf(k) to 1e-14 absolute. - The cdf has an absolute error of up to 2.6e-6. The lower and the upper tail are off by the same amount with opposite signs, as they would be if upper = 1 − lower. This is about 26× the nominal precision = 1e-7. - Small tails inherit that absolute error and lose all relative accuracy: - on CAT_004 and CAT_011 the P(X > k) part is exactly 0, so goseq's over-p is pmf(k) alone, about half of the true value; - on CAT_012 the P(X > k) part is only its first term; - on CAT_013 the lower tail is 0, although the true value is 1.06e-17. - goseq is not uniformly bad. CAT_010's 6.07e-46 tail agrees to 5.5e-8. The error depends on BiasedUrn's internal method choice, which this ADR does not need to identify.

Conclusion: no GIAP change can satisfy "relative 1e-6 against goseq" on these data. The reference fails it, by up to a factor of 2, and it says 0 where the truth is 1e-17. GIAP is right on every golden tail.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Criterion 1's reference becomes the exact Wallenius distribution, computed from the definition and never by the method GIAP uses in the same regime:
  2. Tails < 1e-3: by R2. These have few support points, so this is cheap. GIAP's ADR-0045 path for tails < 1e-6 is R1, so R2 keeps the comparison independent.
  3. Tails ≥ 1e-3: by R1 in 80-bit precision. GIAP uses scipy's pmf there.
  4. Larger tails: taken as 1 − smaller tail + pmf(k), with pmf(k) by R2. This is exact because Σ f = 1, which is verified on ≥ 3 categories.
  5. R2 spot checks: on ≥ 10 tails ≥ 1e-3, recorded.
  6. Cost: R2 for one pmf is about x(N − x) big-integer products. Full R2 on CAT_001 (n = 2,100) would take hours, which is why R2 is not used for every tail.

The result is committed as tests/data/golden/wallenius/exact_tails.tsv.gz (category, tail, 17-digit value) by scripts/golden/make_wallenius_exact.py. This is pure Python (fractions, integers, numpy long double), with no R and no scipy. It runs once on Slurm (≤ 4 CPUs, ≤ 1 h) and has a PROVENANCE entry. The comparison is |p − p_exact| ≤ wallenius_rel_tol · p_exact on all 300 tails, with the tolerance unchanged at 1e-6. Today GIAP passes this with a margin of 1.4e5. 2. goseq stays as a second reference, at its demonstrated accuracy. A new key golden_r.wallenius_goseq_abs_tol: 1.0e-5 is added. The rule is |p − p_goseq| ≤ max(wallenius_rel_tol · p_goseq, wallenius_goseq_abs_tol). The value is 3.8× goseq's largest observed absolute error (2.6e-6), and it holds for p_goseq = 0 as well. It keeps the R-parity check, and it still catches gross faults. With an inverted ω (M8-13 example 10), the goseq rule fails 288 of 300 tails (145 of 150 categories). The exact rule fails 293 tails (all 150 categories). The 5 categories the goseq rule misses are the deep-tail ones (CAT_010–013 and CAT_004), where only the exact rule has teeth. It replaces M8-13's interim wallenius_abs_floor; no separate floor is needed. 3. Counts and odds against goseq are unchanged (exact counts; ω to relative 1e-12). 4. The vacuity floor (M8-13 A5): ≥ 2 exact tails in (0, 1e-20) (CAT_010, CAT_011 today) and ≥ 1 in (1e-20, 1e-8) (CAT_012, CAT_013).

docs.title: Alternatives rejected
docs.text:
• Loosen wallenius_rel_tol. Any relative tolerance that goseq meets (> 0.49, or ∞ for the 0) makes criterion 1 vacuous in the tails it is meant to test.
  • Rerun goseq with a tighter BiasedUrn precision. goseq's interface has no precision argument, so this needs a patched goseq call (a fork of the reference). Its accuracy would then have to be proved against the exact reference anyway.
  • Compare against R1 for every tail. R1 is the algorithm proposed for GIAP's far tails (ADR-0045). If ADR-0045 is adopted, R1 would test GIAP against itself. R2 is a different method (closed form) and stays independent.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• M8-13 §1.1 item 4 is rewritten around the exact reference, plus the goseq rule above. A1 then depends only on this ADR.
  • tolerances.yaml gains one key, applied in the test PR with Gate-Change-Approved: ADR-0044.
  • §7.7.5 criterion 1 reads "against the exact distribution (and against goseq within its documented accuracy)". The spec text is not edited; this ADR overrides it.
  • docs/methods/function.md "M8-13 golden" is updated: the 1e-6 comparison against goseq cannot hold because of goseq, while GIAP's scipy pmf is within 1e-11 on every golden tail.

docs.title: ADR-0045: Wallenius far tails by the exact urn recursion
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-23; lead recommendation)
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §7.7.3, §8.2–8.3; M8-01 lead decision 2 (hardening owed); docs/methods/function.md "Far-tail precision of scipy's pmf"
  • Needs Khoa: no (no default, threshold, interface or dependency change; outputs become more accurate). The lead approves it.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
giap.stats.wallenius.wallenius_tails sums scipy's nchypergeom_wallenius.pmf, which uses Fog's precision constants. On the M8-13 golden data it is within 7.1e-12 of the exact distribution on all 300 tails, including 6e-46 (ADR-0044). Elsewhere it is not.

The statistician checked 40 random urns (M 200–3,000, ω ∈ [e⁻¹, e]) against the exact urn recursion in 80-bit precision (about 17,000 tails). The worst relative error per decade of the true tail:

true tail worst relative error 1e-5 – 1e-3 ≤ 5.4e-10 1e-6 – 1e-5 6.7e-9 1e-7 – 1e-6 2.7e-8 1e-8 – 1e-7 6.2e-7 1e-9 – 1e-8 3.5e-6 1e-11 – 1e-10 1.5e-4 1e-14 – 1e-13 0.11 1e-19 – 1e-15 1 (p = 0 returned)

The worst case is (M, n, N, ω) = (902, 151, 115, 1.98), lower tail. Its absolute error is a near-constant ~8e-15, so scipy's pmf has an absolute floor rather than relative accuracy. This matches the M8-01 measurement in docs/methods/function.md.

So GIAP reports p with relative error above 1e-6 below about 1e-8, and p = 0 for true values near 1e-15. BH and elim decisions are unaffected (function.md "BH" and "elim"). But: - the reported p_classic and p_value are wrong in the last decades; - an exact-reference golden test (ADR-0044) passes only because the golden tails happen to be benign.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. wallenius_tails keeps scipy's pmf when the requested tail is ≥ _EXACT_BELOW = 1e-6 (worst measured error there 6.7e-9). Below it, it recomputes the category's full pmf by the exact urn recursion. That recursion is the definition of Wallenius' distribution:
  2. p₀(0) = 1;
  3. each draw d moves mass from r red balls drawn to r + 1 with probability ω(m₁ − r) / (ω(m₁ − r) + m₂ − (d − r)).

The tail is the fsum of the recursion's pmf. 2. Why the recursion: every term is a sum of products of positive factors, with no subtraction. So float64 is accurate to about N·ε relative per entry. It agreed with 80-bit precision to 3.8e-15 on every golden tail and with the exact rational integral to < 1e-15 (ADR-0044 R2). 3. Underflow. If the float64 tail is < 1e-290, the recursion is rerun in log space (np.logaddexp) and exponentiated. A 0 can then only mean a true tail below float64's range (< 2e-308). No new column or flag is added. 4. Odds range. The recursion has no odds limit. ODDS_RANGE stays as it is for the scipy path. A later ADR may drop it once the recursion is the sole path. 5. Cost. The recursion is O(N · min(n, N)) per category, about 36 ms at N = 1,456 against 1 ms for scipy. On the golden data it runs for 5 of 150 categories (+0.2 s). GIAP universes are a few thousand genes, so a GO run with ~5 % deep-tail categories adds seconds.

docs.title: Evidence required before acceptance (test-author, then implementer)
docs.text:
• A unit test against an independent oracle: the exact rational integral of ADR-0044, in tests/helpers/. It checks ≥ 10 urns, every k with a tail < 1e-6, and relative 1e-10.
  • The xfail in tests/unit/stats/test_wallenius.py ("scipy's Wallenius pmf loses relative accuracy in some far tails") becomes a strict pass.
  • tests/calibration/test_wallenius_calibration.py is unchanged and still passing.
  • A benchmark of the function step on the largest M8 fixture, with < 10 % added wall time.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The "Far-tail precision" section of docs/methods/function.md is replaced by the new error bound (≤ 1e-12 relative down to 1e-290).
  • enrichment_detection.tsv no longer contains p = 0 from pmf truncation.
  • It is independent of ADR-0044. ADR-0044 is needed for the gate whatever happens here. This ADR is needed for the reported numbers to be right where the golden data do not reach.

docs.title: ADR-0046: giap compare output layout (ADR-M9-B)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted (lead-level, 2026-10-22)
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §5.1, §7.9.3, §9.2, §9.5
  • Needs Khoa: no (layout of new outputs; no default, threshold or protected file changes)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: §7.9.3 names three comparison tables but places only compare_detection.tsv under tables/, does not say how a gene x run matrix is laid out for any run count, how genes are joined, or where the genome digest comes from before run_manifest.json existed (M9-22 spec, ADR-M9-B).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. All three tables live under CMP/tables/: compare_detection.tsv, compare_abundance.tsv, compare_stability.tsv, each with a Frictionless schema in giap/schemas/tables/.
  2. compare_detection.tsv is long, with section in {matrix, intersection}; per-run columns would make the schema depend on the run count. Intersections are exact (UpSet) sets.
  3. Genes are joined by locus_tag; every run must have the same locus-tag set (exit 1 with the counts and the symmetric-difference size otherwise).
  4. Genome identity: the sha256 of the role = genome input of run_manifest.json when that file exists, else of preflight/preflight.json; no digest is exit 1 ("cannot verify the genome"); differing digests are exit 1 naming both labels and hashes.
  5. The ADR number replaces the placeholder "ADR-M9-B" of the M9-22 spec (0044 and 0045 are taken on an open branch).

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text: tests/unit/test_cli_compare.py (every exit-1 row, manifest over preflight, schema validation, byte-identical reruns); tests/unit/compare/.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: V16 and report/compare.html (M9-23) read these three files, plus each run's tables/genes.tsv for the per-gene log2 values of the V16 panel (b) scatters (amended 2026-10-23, M9-23 lead decision 3; the three tables hold no per-gene abundance). Runs annotated separately (different locus tags) cannot be compared until a locus-tag mapping exists (backlog).

docs.title: ADR-0047: Decoys above q_value_max leave the picked competition (reading of §5.2)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-22: the reading, and the defaults.yaml comment reworded)
  • Date: 2026-10-22
  • Spec sections: §5.2, §7.3.2; M4-12 decision 1; M4-24
  • Needs Khoa: yes, for the wording change to the protected src/giap/config/defaults.yaml comment; Khoa approved it on 2026-10-22. The code already behaves this way.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: §5.2 and the input.q_value_max comment in defaults.yaml say that rows above the cut-off are "still used to estimate FDR". Since M4-12, detection.pair_decoys has excluded decoys with q > q_value_max before pairing and picking. The M4-24 spec (unscored decoys) had to say which reading holds.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• Decoys above q_value_max are excluded before pairing and picking. They stay in C9 and in preflight's q-range summary. That is how "still used" is read: kept, not discarded at input.
  • With q in the shared key (M4-24 rule 1), the exclusion changes no gene q of a target that has a q. It changes only f, the 80 % guard and the decoy counts.
  • The filter applies only when some C9 target row carries q (M4-24 rule 6, a symmetry rule).

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• M4-24 examples: the DIA-NN-shaped input and the sim50k golden are byte-identical under this reading.
  • Slurm 1869554: on sim100k, scored decoys give the same detection counts with and without the filter at α 0.01 and 0.05.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No code change for the filter itself.
  • The input.q_value_max comment in defaults.yaml now reads "not evidence; kept in C9 and in preflight's q range", a protected-file change with Gate-Change-Approved: ADR-0047. The default value is unchanged.

docs.title: ADR-0048: Replicate counts for the 1-Mb novel-ORF gate (M7-13 G3/G4)
docs.text:
• Status: proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-23
  • Spec sections: §8.4 (suite "Novel-ORF class FDR", 50 / 300; "set R and the genome sizes to fit" the 10-minute budget; one suite per array task), §7.6.4, §7.6.6, §13 gate M7; M7-12 decision 26, M7-13 Q1
  • Needs Khoa: yes (protected tests/calibration/tolerances.yaml)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• G3 (novel-ORF F1) and G4 (class FDR) can only be measured at 1 Mb with NOVEL_PER_CLASS_GATE = 300 ORFs per class: the picked class q (D + 1)/T cannot fall below 1/T, so the default counts (16 at 300 kb, 40 at 1 Mb) call nothing at α = 0.01 (M7-12 decision 26, statistician round 3 on #225).
  • Each gate replicate is one 1-Mb simulation and a GIAP run per regime (database and de novo), assumed ≈ 90 s each (to be measured in M7-13a).
  • replicates_fast.novel_orfs = 50 is shared with the cheap simulator checks of the same suite (test_sim_m7_*, test_attack_m7_sixframe_picked.py). At 50 × 2 × 90 s ≈ 2.5 h single-core the gate cannot run as a fast (nightly) test, and its 300 full replicates (≈ 15 h CPU) need a sharded array task of their own, not task 11's 2-hour slot shared with the other tests.

docs.title: Decision (proposed)
docs.text:
Add to tests/calibration/tolerances.yaml: - replicates_fast.novel_orfs_gate: 10: pooled over ≈ 600 recall-truth ORFs per replicate, F1 has an SE well below 0.01; at q = 0.10 with ≈ 150 calls per class the FDP SE over 10 replicates is ≈ 0.008. - replicates_full.novel_orfs_gate: 300: the §8.4 full count, unchanged. - The key is appended after compare, so it becomes array task 15 (--array=0-15); existing task numbers do not move.

Until Khoa decides, M7-13 uses the module constant GATE_R = MappingProxyType({"fast": 10, "full": 300}) in tests/calibration/_m7_gate.py and logs under suite novel_orfs (task 11). Accepting this ADR replaces the constant by C.replicates("novel_orfs_gate", full) in a PR carrying Gate-Change-Approved: ADR-0048.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• Keep 50 / 300 under novel_orfs: the fast gate runs ≈ 2.5 h every night; the full gate needs hand-submitted shards of task 11, mixed with the other novel_orfs tests.
  • Run G3/G4 fast at 300 kb: vacuous at q = 0.01 (class q floor), so not a gate.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: To be added by M7-13a: measured per-replicate cost at 1 Mb, and F1 / FDP SE at R = 10.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The fast tier for G3/G4 is a 10-replicate nightly check; the per-PR subset keeps only a one-replicate smoke test.
  • The full tier gets its own array task, submitted sharded (--shard K/10, then --merge).

docs.title: ADR-0049: M7 variant-call precision under de novo errors (G1, A6a, A6b, A6c)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-23)
  • Date: 2026-10-23
  • Spec sections: §7.5 (call rule, flags), §8.4 (f1_min.variants_high 0.90), §8.5 attack 6, §13 gate M7
  • Needs Khoa: yes. The fix changes the variant call rule, and the gate threshold must not be widened (R3).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The M7-13a test-author's reference run (Slurm 1872235) shows the M7 variants gate failing on the current call rule: - G1: F1 is 0.838 at 100k with R = 20 (P 0.776, Rc 0.910), and 0.852 at 1M over 10 replicates. Both are below f1_min 0.90, and precision is the cause. The non-mass_equivalent subset has P 0.951 and Rc 0.675. - A6a: 0–3 isobaric non-swap ALTs per replicate are not flagged mass_equivalent. An N-terminal block read such as AG→Q aligns as the substitution G>Q. - A6b: at random adjacent swaps the share of replicates with a high call is 0.95. Two overlapping true peptides that carry the same swap give two distinct peptides. - A6c: systematic swaps are expected to fail (M7-13 risk 1). - Rows outside G1 (statistician, #255). Besides the 669 gated substitution predictions, GIAP emits 277 high rows that are not substitutions (block 218, swap 49, frameshift 10). §7.5.6 speaks of "high ALT calls", so if these are false, precision over all high rows is 0.549 (F1 0.685). Whether G1 covers them (M7-13 Q2 scopes G1 to substitutions) is part of the choice.

docs.title: Options (for Khoa)
docs.text:
1. Call rule: mass_equivalent substitutions and swap-type ALTs never reach high without support from a peptide that is not mass-equivalent (or a reference spectrum).
  2. Alignment: treat N-terminal two-residue block reads as blocks, and flag them mass_equivalent.
  3. Distinct-peptide support: require that the distinct supporting peptides disagree at more than the swapped pair (for example, different cleavage ends).
  4. Gate scope: gate G1 on the non-mass_equivalent set. This changes what §8.4 measures. On current evidence it also fails: F1 0.790 (P 0.951, Rc 0.675). Option 1 is likely to cost recall the same way, since it removes the same calls from high.

docs.title: Decision (Khoa, 2026-10-23)
docs.text:
1. Mass-equivalent calls stay in high, flagged. A substitution, block or swap whose ALT is mass-equivalent to the reference keeps its tier if it meets the current call threshold, and carries the mass_equivalent flag. The call rule's thresholds are unchanged.
  2. Flag coverage (option 2). N-terminal two-residue block reads such as AG→Q are treated as blocks and flagged mass_equivalent. Swap-type ALTs are flagged too.
  3. Swap support (option 3 not taken). Overlapping peptides that carry the same swap still count as distinct support. Swaps are flagged, not demoted.
  4. G1 scope. G1 (f1_min.variants_high 0.90, unchanged) scores unflagged high calls against identifiable truth: truth variants that are mass-equivalent to the reference leave the recall denominator too. Flagged calls are reported, not scored. Before this applies, the statistician recomputes G1 under this scope (before and after the flag changes) and records it here; the tolerance is never widened (R3).
  5. Attacks. A6a: every isobaric non-swap ALT is flagged mass_equivalent. A6b: every random adjacent swap call is flagged (replaces "no high call"). A6c: unchanged (expected fail).
  6. Rows outside substitutions (block, swap, frameshift high rows): out of G1 (M7-13 Q2); their precision is recorded per type. Open: whether they get their own gate (backlog).

docs.title: Evidence (statistician, Slurm 1874972; local/stat/adr0049/)
docs.text:
scope 100k b1 100k b2 1M (a) all high vs all truth 0.848 0.838 0.852 (b) unflagged vs all truth 0.786 0.790 0.804 (c) unflagged vs identifiable truth 0.933 [0.916, 0.950] 0.927 0.932 [0.924, 0.941] (d) (c) + decided flags 0.934 [0.917, 0.950] 0.927 [0.905, 0.949] 0.933 - Identifiable-truth rule: a truth row leaves the recall denominator when giap.variants.flags.mass_equivalent(ref_aa, alt_aa, variants.mass_equivalent_tol_da) is true (the same test, including the B.5 modification deltas, that sets the call flag). It removes 26 % of recall-eligible truth at 100k (800 → 593) and 24 % at 1M, mostly residue-plus-modification matches (V>L, N>K, D>E, S>T, G>A …), not plain isobaric residues. - 37 % of high substitution calls are flagged and reported but not scored. - Residual false positives are mostly unannotated start-codon M calls (ALT M at the peptide N-terminus over ref L) and reversed-stretch decompositions; residual false negatives are mostly candidate-tier rows (call threshold, not flags). ## Implementation rules (from the evidence) - A6a: flag a substitution when an ALT peptide also aligns as the 2→1 block ref[p-1:p+1] → alt with its prefix shifted by one (q = 0, or P[:q] == ref[p-1-q:p-1]). This fixes 24 of 24 unflagged isobaric rows. No right-hand or looser form (they flag true positives by chance). - A6b: flags_for (src/giap/variants/flags.py) flags every swap row mass_equivalent (75 of 75).

"Identifiable" (Khoa, 2026-10-23): it uses the modification-inclusive mass_equivalent test above, not a strictly isobaric-residue rule. The report states the share of truth this removes (26 % at 100k, 24 % at 1M).

docs.title: ADR-0050: ORF-level q in the de novo subgroup regime under exact systematic errors (G4-k3, attack GC)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-23)
  • Date: 2026-10-23
  • Spec sections: §7.6 (novel ORFs), §8.4 (class FDR), §8.5 (attacks), §13 gate M7; M7-11 decision 3; M7-13 rule 8
  • Needs Khoa: yes. Options 4 and 5 change a gate generator or the call rule (R3); option 3 records a limitation of the class FDR.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
M7-11 decision 3 sets a de novo ORF's class q to the minimum of its peptides' subgroup q. The methods note flags this as anti-conservative ("k chances"). M7-13 rule 8 (G4-k3) measures it: 20 false ORFs per six-frame class, 3–5 wrong de novo reads each (k//2 reversed stretches, the rest exact segment products).

Full tier (R = 300, Slurm 1875441 / 1876296 / 1877124), confirmed in both blocks:

Check Block 1 FDP Block 2 FDP Bound intergenic, q 0.01 0.0168 0.0153 0.0114 cds_outframe, q 0.01 and 0.05 0.0747 0.0749 0.0102 / 0.0502 antisense, q 0.01 and 0.05 0.0719 0.0719 0.0102 / 0.0502

FDP is flat in q: the false ORFs sit at the top of the list (median minimum peptide q 5e-4). Attack GC (exact products of GC-poor intergenic segments) fails at q 0.01 by the same mechanism (0.0122 / 0.0126 against 0.0112).

Decomposition (100 paired replicates): - exact products only: FDP 0.075 / 0.072, which is the whole failure; - reversed stretches only: FDP 0.0098 / 0.0135 / 0.0140 against about 0.011–0.0125, a residual excess at q 0.01 only.

Why no decoy can fix it: a de novo read that exactly equals a non-coding translation cannot be told apart from translation evidence by any decoy-based estimate, because a reversed or shuffled genome decoy matches it exactly only by chance. The FDR estimand assumes wrong reads behave like decoy hits. That holds for error-bearing reads, up to the k-chances effect, and fails for exact systematic errors.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
1. Picked ORF-level competition on the genome decoy (target ORF against its mirrored decoy ORF, aggregated score). Addresses the k-chances excess (the reversed-stretch arm). It cannot fix the exact arm, because an exact target ORF always beats its decoy.
  2. Per-ORF Bonferroni over peptides (q_orf = min(1, k·min q)). Measured: no fix (cds_outframe 0.076, antisense 0.074), and worse for intergenic (0.0243 against 0.0174 at q 0.01), because it drops true multi-peptide ORFs.
  3. Keep decision 3 and declare a documented limitation: exact systematic de novo errors are outside what the class FDR controls.
  4. G4-k3 (cds_outframe and antisense at 0.01 and 0.05, intergenic at 0.01) and GC at 0.01 become strict xfails naming this ADR.
  5. De novo-only calls with no database or RBS/TIR support are flagged.
  6. Re-specify rule 8 and attack GC to error-bearing wrong reads only (a chance-hit null), and keep the exact arm as a recorded diagnostic. This changes a gate's generator, so it needs Khoa (R3 forbids relaxing a check). The reversed-only arm still shows an excess at q 0.01, so option 1 or 3 would still be needed.
  7. Require independent support for de novo-only six-frame calls (≥ 1 database PSM, or a planted RBS/TIR pass). This changes the call rule and power (G3) and needs an M7-11 amendment.

docs.title: Lead's interim default (reversible; pending Khoa)
docs.text:
Option 3's test side only: the failing G4-k3 and GC q 0.01 checks become strict xfails naming ADR-0050, so a fix shows as XPASS. The flag for unsupported de novo-only calls is not added until Khoa decides. The gate (M7-13c) lists these as open known failures, not as met.

Source: the M7-13b statistician's full-tier report (2026-10-23); its scripts and logs are in local/stat/m713b-full/.

docs.title: Decision (Khoa, 2026-10-23)
docs.text:
1. Option 3 now:
  2. exact systematic de novo errors are a documented limitation of the class FDR;
  3. G4-k3 (cds_outframe and antisense at 0.01 and 0.05, intergenic at 0.01) and attack GC at q 0.01 stay strict xfails naming this ADR;
  4. the M7 gate (M7-13c) lists them as accepted known failures, so the gate can read "met" with them open.
  5. The flag: de novo-only novel-ORF calls with no database PSM and no RBS/TIR support are flagged. That is M7-17, m7/denovo-support-flag.
  6. Option 1 later: picked ORF-level competition on the genome decoy goes to the backlog for the reversed-stretch arm. It cannot fix the exact arm.
  7. A6c (ADR-0049): stays a strict xfail as an accepted known failure (Khoa, 2026-10-23). It is recorded in M7-13c part 2.

docs.title: ADR-0051: DIA-NN 2.3.1 Academia (Apptainer image) instead of the spec's 2.7.0
docs.text:
• Status: proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-23
  • Spec sections: §15.1 (arms A1, A2: "DIA-NN 2.7.0"), §15.2 steps 3, 5 and 7 and the DIA-NN template, §3.3 (GIAP_TOOLS_DIR), §3.6 (needs_diann: "DIA-NN 2.7.0 under $GIAP_TOOLS_DIR"), §14.8 item 6, §0.1 item 4, §17 rows on DIA-NN; R5, R6, R11, R13
  • Needs Khoa: yes. This changes a dependency version and the way it is installed (§14.8 items 1 and 6). It writes down Khoa's 2026-10-20 acceptance of the M3-24 README and does not replace it.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The spec names DIA-NN 2.7.0 in four places: - the arms (§15.1); - the install step: "Khoa: accept the DIA-NN 2.7.0 licence and unpack the Linux binary under $GIAP_TOOLS_DIR/diann-2.7.0" (§15.2 step 3, §0.1 item 4, §14.8 item 6); - the test marker (§3.6); - the recorded-sample path tests/data/recorded/diann/2.7.0/ (§15.2 step 7).

What exists is different. Khoa supplied an Apptainer image of 2.3.1 Academia and pointed at their reference script /farmshare/home/classes/bios/270/jordan/run_2step.sh (M3-24 lead decision 1). The M3-24 pilot kit is written against it.

Every fact below was read from disk. Nothing was inferred about DIA-NN versions that are not on disk.

From validation/pilot/README.md (M3-24, #122): - version string DIA-NN 2.3.1 Academia, compiled 2025-12-05; - the image /farmshare/home/classes/bios/270/jordan/diann_2.3.1.sif (532 MB), with sha256 1946452d56d2fb0f66e05ced473df88e53484e28040f1ecbd83c4a43405a6381 (pinned 2026-10-20) and the binary /diann-2.3.1/diann-linux; - the module apptainer/1.4.4, binding /home/classes, /scratch and /farmshare; - the section "Version actually used" says: "Khoa reviewed and accepted the flag table and this section on 2026-10-20 ('looks fine') … 2.3.1 Academia is the version of record unless he says otherwise." It adds: "If a 2.7.0 build arrives later, only diann_A1.cfg, diann_A2.cfg and this section change."

The README also documents the two-step workflow (M3-24 decision 4): "In DIA-NN 2.x, combining --fasta-search --predictor with raw files in one call disables the FASTA digest". Step 1 therefore predicts a library from the FASTA files, and step 2 searches the runs against it. Khoa's reference script carries the same note.

The cfgs (validation/pilot/diann_A{1,2}.cfg) deviate from the §15.2 template. All of this is listed in the README: - --met-excision is left out, because GIAP's digest keeps the initiator Met; - --lib "" is not used; - added: --min-pr-mz 300 --max-pr-mz 1800 --min-fr-mz 200 --max-fr-mz 1800, --peptidoforms and --verbose 1; - added in step 2: --matrices, plus --gen-spec-lib --out-lib <arm>_empirical.parquet; - Khoa's --reanalyse and --rt-profiling are not used, because match-between-runs weakens run-level FDR control.

Checked on 2026-10-23, in the session allocation: - The shared image is 532,586,496 bytes, mode -rwxrwxrwx, owner khoang99, group operator, mtime 2026-07-09 18:20 −0700. Its directory is drwxrwxrwx. - The sha256 still equals the pin. - apptainer inspect gives the labels build date Tuesday_6_January_2026_19:18:54_PST, bootstrap docker, from khoayelo189/diann:2.3.1. - /diann-2.3.1/ holds diann-linux (25,747,216 bytes), libtimsdata.so, ThermoFisher.CommonCore.*.dll, libtorch_cpu.so, models/*.pt and diann-stats.py. - find / -maxdepth 3 -iname '*licen*' inside the image finds no licence file. - $GIAP_TOOLS_DIR (local/tools) is empty: no diann-2.7.0. module avail diann finds nothing. - run_2step.sh collects *.raw files (Thermo) and a human FASTA. GIAP has not yet run this image on timsTOF .d data.

What is not known from anything on disk: - whether a 2.7.0 build is available to Khoa; - how 2.7.0 differs from 2.3.1 in flags, report columns or scoring; - who built khoayelo189/diann:2.3.1, and from which DIA-NN release archive; - the text of the Academia licence.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
1. Adopt 2.3.1 Academia as the version of record (the M3-24 kit, index decision 2). The pilot runs now. The spec's 2.7.0 paths are read as their 2.3.1 equivalents:
  2. the shared image, verified against the pin and copied read-only to $GIAP_ROOT/images/diann_2.3.1.sif (index lead decision 2, M10-02), in place of $GIAP_TOOLS_DIR/diann-2.7.0;
  3. tests/data/recorded/diann/2.3.1/ in place of …/2.7.0/.
  4. Wait for 2.7.0 under $GIAP_TOOLS_DIR/diann-2.7.0, installed by Khoa. This follows the spec to the letter. M10 pass 1 stops at M10-01 until then. The flag table would need Khoa's check again against the 2.7.0 documentation, and the effect on the gate's timeline is unknown.
  5. Run 2.3.1 now and re-run on 2.7.0 if it arrives. Option 1 now. When a 2.7.0 build exists, only the cfgs, the README, the image or binary pin and the recorded sample's version directory change. DIA-NN, the conversion and the A1/A2 arms run again before the report freeze (M10-14), and both versions' numbers are kept in the pilot report.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Proposed: option 1, with option 3 kept open. The pilot (M10-02 … M10-05) runs on 2.3.1 Academia from the read-only copy. The version string, the image sha256, the two-step workflow and the template deviations above are the record. A 2.7.0 build is not awaited. If Khoa provides one, option 3 applies, and this ADR is amended with the new pin and the re-run's job IDs.

Image handling (M10-02): - every DIA-NN job checks the copy's sha256 against validation/pilot/diann_image.sha256 and refuses a writable copy; - the install job hashes the copy it made, not only the world-writable source; - a mismatch is a Blocked row and a question to Khoa, never a re-pin or a download from elsewhere (R6); - the image, and every file inside it, is never committed (R11).

docs.title: Questions for Khoa
docs.text:
1. Do you accept 2.3.1 Academia as the version of record for the pilot (option 1/3), or should the pilot wait for 2.7.0 (option 2)?
  2. The copy is made by the agent from your image, under $GIAP_ROOT/images/, not under $GIAP_TOOLS_DIR. §14.8 item 6 reserves installing DIA-NN to you. Is a verified, read-only copy of the image you supplied acceptable?
  3. The image's labels name khoayelo189/diann:2.3.1 on Docker Hub as its source. Can you confirm that this image is yours, built from an official DIA-NN 2.3.1 release?
  4. The image has no licence text. §15.2 step 7 allows committing a 1,000-row sample of each report, because DIA-NN output tables are not binaries. Does the Academia licence you accepted permit that?
  5. If PXD078459 turns out not to be diaPASEF (M10-01), the settings change in an amendment to this ADR, with your check of the flags.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• validation/pilot/README.md ("DIA-NN: the container", "Version actually used", "The two-step DIA-NN workflow", "§15.2 template flags that the cfg files do not use");
  • docs/specs/M3-24-pilot-kit.md lead decisions 1–7 and 9;
  • tests/unit/test_m3_24_pilot_kit.py: the version string, the pin, the cfg-versus-digest checks, and the re-hash of the image on disk (test_the_pinned_sha256_is_still_the_image_on_disk);
  • docs/specs/M10-index.md: decision 2 and lead decisions 2–3;
  • docs/specs/M10-02-diann-searches.md: "What exists", the facts checked on 2026-10-23.

No search has run yet, so there are no before/after metrics. The first evidence will be the M10-02 job IDs and check.json results.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The spec text is not edited (R13). Once this ADR is accepted, it overrides the 2.7.0 mentions listed under "Spec sections" for the pilot.
  • needs_diann and the capability probe still look for the jordan path or diann-2.7.0. Teaching them the copy is a backlog chore (M10-02 Q8).
  • The contract-test sample lives under tests/data/recorded/diann/2.3.1/. A later 2.7.0 run adds …/2.7.0/ and keeps the old one only if both are tested.
  • The pilot report states "DIA-NN 2.3.1 Academia" for A1 and A2, and cites this ADR.
  • Risk: 2.3.1 might differ from 2.7.0 in report columns. The converter's contract test on the real sample (M10-03) catches any column difference that matters to GIAP.

docs.title: Amendment (2026-10-24, M10-03, PR #288)
docs.text: Khoa ruled on 2026-10-23 that no row-level DIA-NN content is committed, and on 2026-10-24 that aggregates (counts, hashes, named example genes) may be. This replaces §15.2 step 7's committed recorded sample for DIA-NN: - The converted tables (a1.tsv.gz, a2.tsv.gz and their abundance tables) and any sample drawn from the reports stay under $GIAP_ROOT/pilot/, never in the repository. - What is committed is the conversion record in validation/pilot/README.md › "Conversion (M10-03)": the job IDs, the sha256 of every input report and output table, and the row counts. - The contract test (tests/contract/test_m10_03_diann_contract.py) runs on FarmShare against the $GIAP_ROOT copies; CI runs the converter's unit tests on synthetic fixtures. The tests/data/recorded/diann/2.3.1/ path named above therefore holds no data rows.

docs.title: ADR-0052: PR CI under 20 minutes; calibration, integration and coverage move to the nightly
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-23)
  • Date: 2026-10-23
  • Spec sections: §12 (the ci.yml and nightly.sbatch rows), §14 (feature loop)
  • Needs Khoa: yes (Khoa asked for it: "we want 15 mins on all or 20 mins max … cut down on the tests, move to nightly", 2026-10-23)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• PR CI is the bottleneck of the merge queue. The single calibration-and-coverage job took 85 min. Splitting it into 6 coverage shards (#273) still left 10–56 min shards. The slowest is one calibration test of about 25 min (test_gene_fdr_one_replicate_through_real_mapping, Slurm 1879345 --durations).
  • The unsharded test matrix (ubuntu 3.11, ubuntu 3.13, macOS 3.12) took 12–25 min per job.
  • Runner limits: a free account runs about 20 jobs at once, 5 of them on macOS.
  • The Slurm fast suite already runs everything: agents run the whole fast suite, calibration included, on Slurm (scripts/slurm/test_branch.sbatch) before a PR opens.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. PR CI (ci.yml on pull_request) runs:
  2. lint;
  3. guards;
  4. nf-test in stub mode;
  5. the unit, property, golden, contract and snapshot tests on ubuntu 3.13, in 4 parallel shards (scripts/ci/shard_tests.py; tests/calibration, tests/integration and tests/e2e excluded).

The target is every job ≤ 15 min, and the whole run ≤ 20 min. 2. On pushes to main only: Python 3.11 and macOS 3.12 (test-compat). 3. Moved to the nightly: the fast calibration subset and the coverage gate. Nightly task 2 (scripts/slurm/nightly.sbatch) runs the whole fast suite, calibration_nightly included, with --cov-fail-under from ci/gates.yaml coverage_min. That value is unchanged (R3). A nightly failure becomes a top-priority issue (§12). 4. Before a PR opens: agents still run the full fast suite on Slurm, so calibration is checked before review, and the nightly is the backstop for anything merged since.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Later detection: a calibration or coverage regression can merge and is found by the next nightly, at most about 24 h later, instead of blocking the PR. 3.11 and macOS regressions are found after the merge.
  • Gate values unchanged: ci/gates.yaml and the tolerances are untouched; only where the checks run moves.
  • Budget: the nightly's task 2 grows from the calibration_nightly tests to the whole fast suite: about 35–50 min on 16 CPUs, within its 6 h.

docs.title: ADR-0053: Bit-identical speed-ups of the determinants step; two new benchmark baselines
docs.text:
• Status: proposed
  • Date: 2026-10-23
  • Spec sections: §7.8.2 (steps 1, 3, 4), §6.6, §8.2, §12
  • Needs Khoa: no (no default, threshold, interface, dependency or protected file changes; outputs byte-identical)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The per-commit fast suite took 1,956 s on 16 CPUs (Slurm job 1879345, barley-01, no coverage). One test, tests/calibration/test_gene_fdr_real_mapping.py::test_gene_fdr_one_replicate_through_real_mapping, took 1,532 s and was the suite's critical path. Profiling (cProfile; py-spy and scalene are not installed in the shared venv) showed that giap run --executor local spent most of its time in the determinants step: on the 500-kb replicate, cross_validate 682 s, null_p (1,000 permutations) about 1,000 s, univariate 44 s. On sim50, determinants took 60 s of an 84 s run.

Causes: 1. ElasticNetCV calls enet_path per inner fold with check_input=True, which re-validates the Gram matrix once per alpha (check_array); that was about 65 % of every elastic-net fit. 2. The elastic net holds the GIL: threading its permutation refits was slower than one thread (0.21 s per permutation at 1 thread, 0.35 s at 4). 3. cross_validate fitted LightGBM with n_jobs = threads (16) on a few hundred rows: one CV repeat took 204 s at 16 OpenMP threads and 0.3 s at 1 on a shared node. 4. tu_block_bootstrap built a data frame per replicate, and scipy.stats.spearmanr/rankdata have a large per-call overhead (about 90,000 calls per run).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• _ElasticNetCV (a subclass) routes its inner-fold path through enet_path(check_input=False). _path_residuals has already validated X, y, Xy and the Gram matrix, so the skipped checks returned their inputs unchanged.
  • null_p runs model by model: LightGBM permutation refits on threads workers, then the elastic net's serially. They are not overlapped, because that causes a GIL convoy on a loaded node.
  • _repeated_oof fits every fold single-threaded. With threads > 1 the LightGBM fits run on a pool of threads workers and are collected in (repeat, fold) order. The elastic net stays serial.
  • tu_block_bootstrap gains a keyword-only columns= path. It calls stat_fn(*arrays) with the same draws and the same replicate rows. univariate uses it, with exact average ranks in place of rankdata/spearmanr (each rank is (i + j)/2 of integers, and np.corrcoef of the stacked ranks is what spearmanr computes).
  • New benchmark benchmarks/test_determinants_bench.py and two baseline entries.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text:
• Byte identity (before = origin/main d29a2ea5):
  • null_p (40 permutations) null R² arrays, p and b;
  • cross_validate r2/oof/ΔR² at threads 1, 4 and 16, and SHAP blocks;
  • univariate tables on the 500-kb replicate and sim50;
  • the three determinants tables of the 500-kb replicate (threads 16). _ranks/_rho equal rankdata/spearmanr bit for bit on 20,000 random inputs with ties and ±0. All determinants unit, property, integration and calibration tests pass. Among them, example 4 checks that threads 1 and 8 give byte-identical tables.
  • Determinants step on the 500-kb replicate (iron-13, threads 16): cross_validate 682 → 9.7 s, null_p about 1,000 → 305 s, univariate 44 → 8 s; total about 1,730 → 323 s.
  • Benchmarks (iron-13): determinants_univariate_b1000_n400 7.29 → 1.57 s; determinants_null_b50_n400 (4 threads) 33.74 → 11.09 s.
  • Fast suite (16 CPUs, barley, -p no:randomly, no coverage): 1,956 s (job 1879345) → 1,437 s with the first commit (job 1879720). The final run is listed in the commit and PR text.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• CvResult.boosters now hold LightGBM models fitted with n_jobs=1. Their predictions are identical, and SHAP is computed single-threaded per booster.
  • The elastic-net null is serial: about 0.2 s per permutation, which is the step's floor without processes. A process pool for it is a possible follow-up; it needs an ADR, because of its memory and CPU budget under R14.
  • Proposed baseline additions: determinants_univariate_b1000_n400, determinants_null_b50_n400 in benchmarks/baseline.json. No existing entry changes.

docs.title: ADR-0054: External artefacts of the A3 de novo arm (ADR-M10-B): conversion route, TDF-SDK licence, Cascadia weights host, Unimod table
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-24, in session: "go with your recommendation": Bruker TDF-SDK accepted for route B2; cascadia.ckpt allowed from the authors' Drive folder with its sha256 pinned; the ProteoWizard route not accepted)
  • Date: 2026-10-24
  • Spec sections: §15.1 (arm A3), §15.2 steps 6-7, §17, §3.2, §14.8 item 1; R5, R6, R9, R11, R14
  • Needs Khoa: yes (a new download source, drive.google.com, and a proprietary licence, Bruker's TDF-SDK agreement)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Arm A3 runs Cascadia 0.0.7 (Apache-2.0, PyPI) on the PXD078459 diaPASEF runs (docs/specs/M10-08-a3-feasibility.md). Three external artefacts are not covered by §3.2:

  1. Cascadia reads mzML only, so the Bruker .d runs need a .d → mzML conversion. Both candidate routes decode analysis.tdf_bin with Bruker's proprietary TDF-SDK (libtimsdata.so):
  2. B2: TIMSCONVERT 2.0.0 (GitHub tag v2.0.0, commit 3cb96aef35bc0a15ce1b6cfe547386acc26a8b8b, Apache-2.0) with pyTDFSDK at commit 4808da81d3e37f82da96f392dbb446c3733edacb (Apache-2.0), which bundles the TDF-SDK. One proprietary licence: Bruker's TDF-SDK agreement.
  3. B1: ProteoWizard msconvert from the Docker Hub image proteowizard/pwiz-skyline-i-agree-to-the-vendor-licenses@sha256:34ed787cd4c3182c2d81adcbf7514031e594609ca460abc5d3d114dc2334dae8, under Wine. Six vendor licences: Bruker's, and five more (Agilent, Sciex, Shimadzu, Thermo, Waters) for libraries this pilot never loads.
  4. The Cascadia weights (cascadia.ckpt, Apache-2.0 per the Nat Methods 2025 Code availability statement) are published only in the Google Drive folder that the Cascadia docs link, https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1UTrZIrCdUqYqscbqga_KdX8kc8ZjMMfr. Drive is not a §3.2 source, and no checksum is published.
  5. Cascadia 0.0.7 fetches http://www.unimod.org/xml/unimod_tables.xml (plain HTTP, a host outside §3.2) twice per run: at the start, when its tokenizer resolves named modifications (pyteomics proforma -> psims obo_cache.resolve(UNIMOD_OBO_URL) -> Unimod()), and at the end, through pyteomics mass.unimod.Unimod().

The TDF-SDK agreement (read from the copy in ProteoWizard's repository, since Bruker's own page is login-gated) allows use "on any of your computing devices" (§2.1), forbids redistribution (§3.2), is free of charge (§6.1) and binds the user only "after having accepted this Agreement".

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Route order: B2, then B1, then E1. B2 is the conversion route (workflow/envs/timsconvert.yml, scripts/slurm/mzml_pilot.sbatch). B1 is used only if B2 fails after R9 and Khoa accepts the five non-Bruker EULAs. If neither route is available, rule E1 (route_unavailable) fires and A3 moves to the Casanovo fallback (M10-11a).
  2. Licences. Khoa accepts Bruker's TDF-SDK licence agreement for route B2 (2026-10-24, "the Bruker TDF-SDK licence is accepted for route B2 (TIMSCONVERT + pyTDFSDK)"). GIAP reads the FarmShare allocation it runs under as "your computing devices" (§2.1; spec question Q7). Nothing from the env, the SDK or the converted data is redistributed or committed (R11). Khoa does not accept the ProteoWizard five-EULA route (2026-10-24): B1 stays unavailable, no image is pulled, and fetch_a3_assets.sbatch has no pull step.
  3. Weights host. drive.google.com (file downloads through drive.usercontent.google.com, HTTPS) is the source of cascadia.ckpt, Drive file 14b7Y2-5ZqLY807MYtggoNocSfELdfHy9 (Khoa, 2026-10-24: "cascadia.ckpt may be fetched from the authors' Drive folder linked in the Cascadia docs, with its sha256 recorded and pinned"). The first download (fetch_a3_assets.sbatch --resolve) is trust on first use; its sha256 and size go into validation/pilot/a3_assets.tsv, and every later fetch and run must match it (R6). A changed file is a new asset row, approved by the lead. Only cascadia.ckpt is used (spec Q11). The quay.io/protio/cascadia copy is not used (spec Q8).
  4. Unimod table. The unimod_tables.xml.gz that psims 1.4.0 (conda-forge, Apache-2.0) vendors is gunzipped from the built giap-cascadia env to $GIAP_DB_DIR/cascadia/unimod_tables.xml and pinned by sha256. Cascadia runs through scripts/pilot/cascadia_offline.py, which blocks both Unimod fetches before Cascadia is imported: it registers a psims resolver for the Unimod OBO URL that reads that file (start of run) and points pyteomics' _unimod_xml_download_url at it (end of run). It also refuses every Python-level socket connection, and cascadia.yml pins lxml>=5.4, which refuses network entities, so a missed call site fails instead of reaching unimod.org.

fetch_a3_assets.sbatch refuses to request the weights until this ADR is accepted (A3_WEIGHTS_HOST_OK=1, set by the lead once the status changes).

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text:
• Licence texts and sources: docs/specs/M10-08-a3-feasibility.md, "What the official sources say" (S1-S18) and "Licence findings".
  • Tests: tests/unit/test_m10_08_scripts.py (no request before acceptance, https only, sha256 mismatch leaves no file, 0444 files), tests/unit/test_m10_08_launcher.py (both Unimod call sites read the local table, set before Cascadia is imported; Python sockets are refused), tests/unit/test_m10_08_committed.py (no weights, SDK, image, mzML or Unimod copy is tracked).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Two pilot-only envs (giap-cascadia, giap-timsconvert; conda channel conda-forge only, pip requirements from PyPI, pinned) in giap.annotate.tools.PILOT_TOOLS; they never join TOOLS, required_tools or build_envs.sh all.
  • cascadia.ckpt is a pickle (torch.load, weights_only=False on torch 2.0), so loading it runs code. It is trusted on first use, pinned by sha256 and loaded only inside the GPU job.
  • The weights may disappear or change on Drive: a sha256 mismatch exits non-zero and the lead records a Blocked row; it is never evidence about timsTOF data.
  • If B2 fails after R9, A3 needs Khoa again (B1's five EULAs) or goes to E1 and M10-11a.

docs.title: ADR-0055: Operon discordance under abundance-dependent Δ noise (attack D-1)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-24, in session: "1. Go with (a)"): option (a), σ as a function of mean abundance, with attack D-1b gated before the claim
  • Date: 2026-10-24
  • Spec sections: §7.4.2 (within-operon distribution), §7.4.3 (discordance test), §8.1 row "Operon discordance", §8.4 suite discordance, §8.5, §13 gate M6
  • Needs Khoa: yes. Either the method changes (§7.4.2) or the claim is narrowed. A failing attack blocks the gate, and no threshold is widened (R3).

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
§7.4.2 fits one Student-t (μ, σ, ν) to Δ over all usable OP pairs, and §7.4.3 tests every both-detected OP pair against it. Real proteomics has more noise at low abundance, so the spread of Δ shrinks as the mean abundance of the pair grows. The PR #147 statistician review owed attack D-1 to M6-09. In D-1, Δ − μ is scaled by exp(−0.5 z), with z the standardised mean log2 abundance of the pair, on operon_null(1800). It is implemented in _noise_by_abundance in tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_operons.py.

M6-09 measured it through the merged step (Slurm 1884412 at 90a0e709, rerun as Slurm 1884493 at 24267fd3 with identical pooled numbers; R = 1,000 genomes). The bounds are the §8.4 level bounds; the quartile bound treats the pairs as independent.

check α = 0.01 0.05 0.10 pooled level (200 random tested pairs per genome) 0.0076 (≤ 0.0104) 0.0521 (≤ 0.0510) 0.1064 (≤ 0.1013) lowest-abundance quartile, cut on the planted z (123,766 pairs) 0.0273 (≤ 0.0106) 0.157 (≤ 0.0512) 0.277 (≤ 0.1017) same data, no D-1 (the gate null) 0.0098 0.0500 0.0998
  • The pooled level fails at α = 0.05 and 0.10, 4.2 % and 6.4 % above nominal, and the failure is confirmed in both blocks (ADR-0015).
  • The lowest quartile runs at about 3× nominal, as the PR #147 oracle found (2.4–3×).
  • The fast tier fails the same way: R = 100, pooled 0.110 against 0.104 at α = 0.10.
  • Mechanism: one σ for all pairs is too narrow for noisy low-abundance pairs and too wide for precise high-abundance pairs. Null calls therefore land on low-abundance pairs. BH over the family does not repair the per-pair error.

Both checks now form one strict xfail naming this ADR (test_attack_d1_level). This follows the ADR-0049 pattern for the M7 gate. The M6 discordance claim is not met until this ADR is decided.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
(a) Model σ as a function of mean abundance (method change, §7.4.2). - The model is σ_i = exp(log σ₀ + γ z_i), with z_i the standardised mean log2 abundance of pair i. Location and ν stay as now. The fit is maximum likelihood over (μ, log σ₀, γ, ν), using the same Nelder–Mead routine and ν bounds as fit_student_t. - The p-value is 2 · sf_t(|Δ − μ̂| / σ̂_i; ν̂). - γ = 0 recovers the current method. A likelihood-ratio test of γ = 0 can be reported, but it is not used to choose between the models (no selection step). - Statistician check (a scratch oracle fit outside the code, not reproducible from the repo, R = 150 genomes; the implementer PR must re-measure it through D-1 and D-1b at the gate's R):

data pooled level, α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 lowest quartile γ̂ D-1 data 0.0103 / 0.0510 / 0.1004 0.0085 / 0.047 / 0.095 mean −0.508 (true −0.5) the null (no D-1) 0.0100 / 0.0507 / 0.1008 0.011 / 0.054 / 0.105 mean −0.004

So it restores the level in the lowest quartile and costs nothing measurable under the null. - Caveat: the log-linear σ is the shape D-1 plants, so this is a correctly specified check. A misspecified shape (a step or a curve) has to be added as attack D-1b before the gate is claimed. - Effort: about 60 lines of implementation: - a fit_student_t_scaled(delta, z) in giap.stats.tdist; - wiring in giap.operons.discordance, plus effect in σ̂_i units, optional; - the methods note, about 40 lines; - about 150 test lines (unit tests, the γ = 0 reduction, D-1 and D-1b).

That is one implementer PR plus a statistician review, roughly one feature-loop cycle. The z of a pair uses only the two observed abundances, so the step needs no new inputs. - With fewer than 20 usable pairs, or with a non-converged fit, the current too_few_op_pairs rule still applies.

(b) Narrow the claim. - Discordance calls are claimed only under Δ noise that does not depend on abundance. - operons.tsv and operon_flags.tsv carry a flag such as homoscedastic_assumption, and the report says the calls are anti-conservative for low-abundance pairs when noise grows at low abundance. - The D-1 tests stay strict xfails, and the gate is claimed as narrowed. - Effort is small (a flag, a sentence, the methods note), but the per-pair claim is then false exactly where proteomics noise is largest, and nothing in a run can tell the user whether the assumption holds.

(c) Stratify the fit by abundance quartile (a variant of (a)). - Fit one t per quartile of pair-mean abundance, each with ≥ 20 pairs, otherwise falling back to the pooled fit, and test each pair against the fit of its own stratum. - No functional form is needed, but each fit uses about a quarter of the pairs: about 115 at 1,800 genes, close to the n ≈ 50 regime in which ν̂ sits on a bound (docs/methods/operons.md, PR #147 table). - Strata boundaries also create discontinuities: a pair on either side of a boundary gets a different null.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
(a), with (b)'s label as the interim until (a) merges: - (a) is the only option that restores the per-pair level where the failure is, at no measurable cost under the null. - It reduces exactly to the current method when γ̂ = 0. - It is also the remedy the PR #147 review listed: "σ modelled as a function of mean abundance".

Gate D-1b (a non-log-linear σ, for example a step at the median abundance) together with D-1 at the same R before the M6 discordance claim is made.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Pending Khoa.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Until the decision: the M6 gate (simulation half) is not met for discordance. The missed-operon half and §7.4.7 criteria 1–3 on the gate null pass (docs/methods/operons.md, "The M6 gate, simulation half").
  • With (a): an implementer issue on giap.stats.tdist and giap.operons.discordance. The D-1 xfails become plain gated tests (an XPASS of a strict xfail fails the run, which forces the swap), and D-1b is added. M6-05H's P(miss) takes its ratio sample from the scaled fit: standardised residuals mapped back at the partner's z.
  • With (b): the flag goes into the §9.3 enum (an interface change, ADR-0036 style), the report text changes, and the xfails stay with the narrowed claim recorded in the spec sign-off.

docs.title: Amendment 1: the claim covers smooth, monotone σ(abundance) (accepted-by-khoa, 2026-10-24)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-24, in session: "Yes and yes", answering "Do you accept the amendment (option 1)?")
  • Measured (statistician, R = 1,000, M6-13 spec): log-linear σ(abundance) passes D-1 (pooled 0.0505 at α 0.05; lowest quartile 0.0478), D-1b-floor and D-1c. It does not pass D-1b-step (a step change in noise at the median abundance): pooled 0.0518 against a bound of 0.0510; Q2 1.8×. No flexible model tried (quadratic, cubic, spline, variance floor) passed it.
  • Decision: the M6 discordance claim is "pooled level under smooth, monotone σ(abundance)". Per-quartile rates are recorded (up to 1.7×, against about 3× under the constant scale). D-1b-step stays a strict xfail naming this amendment (full tier; non-strict in the fast tier, where it cannot be detected). No bound, alpha or R changes (R3). A variance-floor σ model goes to the backlog (M6-13 follow-up).

docs.title: ADR-0056: P(miss) is reported without a q and stays out of the discordance BH family
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-24, in session: "Accept it", after the P(miss) interpretation was explained)
  • Date: 2026-10-24
  • Spec sections: §7.4.3 "One detected, one not" and "Multiple testing", §8.1 row "Operon discordance", §8.5, §9.3 pairs.tsv
  • Needs Khoa: yes. It departs from §7.4.3's "BH across all tested OP pairs (both kinds together)" and from the §8.1 row, which names the detection-limit model as part of the discordance family.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
§7.4.3 tests two kinds of OP pair. A pair with both genes detected gets a two-sided Student-t p-value against the within-operon Δ distribution. A pair with exactly one gene detected gets p = P(miss): the probability, under M6-02's detection-limit model, that the undetected partner u would be missed, given the detected partner's abundance a_v and the empirical within-operon ratios. The spec then puts both kinds into one BH family at q ≤ 0.1.

P(miss) is a model probability of an event that has already happened. It is computed only on the pairs where u was missed, so conditional on entering the family it is not super-uniform under any null. M6-index lead decision 1 and M6-02 lead decision 4 therefore reported P(miss) with no q and kept it out of the BH family, pending M6-09 attack C and an ADR. M6-05H (PR #311) implements that: a one_detected_pmiss row has p_value = P(miss), method = detection_limit, null_model = p_detect_model and q_value NA, and the BH family holds only the both_detected_t rows.

M6-09 recorded attack C with the oracle P(miss) (the generating model). This ADR adds attack C through the step, with the M6-02 model fitted (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_operons_pmiss.py).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. P(miss) stays in pairs.tsv p_value for test = one_detected_pmiss rows, as §7.4.3 and §9.3 name it, with method = detection_limit and null_model = p_detect_model. It gets no q and never enters the BH family; operon_flags.tsv makes no discordance call from it.
  2. The §8.1 discordance family is every both_detected_t row of the run, one BH family at stats.alpha.operon_flags.
  3. The report and the methods note describe P(miss) as "the model's probability that this partner would be missed if it were co-expressed", never as a significance level, and say that it is anti-conservative when detectability varies between proteins in ways the model does not see.
  4. A scored one_detected_pmiss row carries ci_unestimated, as the both_detected_t rows do. Its effect and CI stay NA (M6-05 item 4), and §8's "effect sizes with 95 % CIs accompany every p or q" is then met by the flag rather than silently.
  5. Pooling is revisited only with a method that makes the one-detected arm a valid p-value under protein-level detectability heterogeneity. For example, a model with a per-protein random effect, or a replicate-model P(miss) where runs identify that effect. Any such method must pass the gene_effect arms of attack C with the pooled family's any-call share within the §8.4 bound.

docs.title: Evidence (attack C through the step; fitted M6-02 model)
docs.text:
Setup: operon_null(1800) genomes (TU blocks and the OPERON_T within-TU walk). Detection is redrawn at peptide level, with logit = −11.5 + 0.5 a − 0.03 L + 0.8 GRAVY + o_g, and a gene is detected at ≥ 1 seen peptide (k_min = 1). C11 holds the seen peptides, and P(miss) comes from giap.steps.operons.detection_limit → discordance. Arms: - null: o_g = 0; - gene_effect: o_g ~ N(0, 1), a per-protein detectability the model does not see; - gene_effect_05: o_g ~ N(0, 0.5²); - block: o_g = −1.5 on the ADR-0018 prophage block of operon_attack_detection.

Full tier: Slurm 1884524, R = 300 genomes per arm, 2,331 s on rye-01. It ran at commit 65d9fedd on branch stat/m6-05h-attack-c: #311 round 1 (fb1410cf, u scored with u's TU model) merged into #310 (bbd6d4a4). The fast tier (R = 20) was rerun on #311's review round (4551ab61: v's TU, the k_min event) and reproduces the round-1 fast numbers to every printed digit. - On these simulations OP pairs never cross a TU boundary (pure UniOP classes), so the v-TU fix cannot move them. - At k_min = 1, "fewer than k_min observable peptides seen" is the simulated non-detection, so the event fix cannot move them either. - On real data, OP pairs that cross a C5 TU boundary can move.

Rates are at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10. The step's P(miss) matches an independent recomputation to ≤ 6·10⁻¹⁶ on every row.

arm mean P(miss) vs miss rate recalibration (intercept, slope) share of one-detected rows with P(miss) ≤ α rate over at-risk pairs (u missed and P(miss) ≤ α) pooled per-pair rate (t + P(miss)) any BH call at q ≤ 0.1: t family / pooled null 0.197 vs 0.196 (−0.03, 0.97) 0.0037 / 0.028 / 0.068 0.0007 / 0.0055 / 0.0134 0.0082 / 0.0430 / 0.0895 0.077 / 0.063 gene_effect_05 0.172 vs 0.209 (0.18, 0.83) 0.0114 / 0.061 / 0.125 0.0024 / 0.0128 / 0.0261 0.0104 / 0.0544 / 0.1091 0.050 / 0.093 gene_effect 0.119 vs 0.236 (0.40, 0.56) 0.067 / 0.198 / 0.317 0.0159 / 0.0467 / 0.0747 0.0318 / 0.107 / 0.183 0.067 / 0.717 block 0.216 vs 0.252 (0.24, 0.92) 0.0061 / 0.037 / 0.084 0.0015 / 0.0093 / 0.0211 0.0090 / 0.0431 / 0.0912 0.110 / 0.140
  • Pooled sizes: 65,738 to 79,281 one-detected rows and 260,456 to 347,647 at-risk orientations per arm.
  • In every arm the oracle (the true model with its offset, Δ from the generating t) is calibrated: recalibration slope 0.96 to 0.99, intercept within ±0.03.
  • The step's ratio sample (both-detected Δ only) costs nothing: with the true model it gives a mean P(miss) equal to the oracle's to 3 decimals. The departures are all in the fitted model.
  • The any-call bound for R = 300 is 0.1 + 2 SE + 1/R ≈ 0.138. Flags per genome at P(miss) ≤ 0.05 are 6.4 (null), 14.8 (SD 0.5), 52.3 (SD 1) and 8.1 (block).

Reading: - Correct model: P(miss) is a calibrated probability. As a discrete p-value of the event "u missed", it is conservative over the at-risk pairs. The share of flagged one-detected pairs is below α, and pooling would not break the family on this arm. - Protein-level detectability breaks it. With o_g ~ N(0, 1) the fitted P(miss) is roughly half the true miss rate. The conditional flag share is several times α, the per-pair rate of the pooled mixture exceeds α, and the pooled BH family makes a false call in most genomes; the shipped t family does not. - The mechanism is the conditional (Huggins) likelihood. It assumes that detectability is a function of the three features alone. Genes that were detected have high o_g, so the model over-predicts detection for the genes that were not. - Real proteomes have such heterogeneity: ionisation, digestion, membrane location and peptide sharing all vary beyond length and GRAVY. - Spatially clustered detectability (block) biases P(miss) downward more mildly (intercept +0.24). It already takes the pooled family's any-call share to 0.140, just over the bound. - With SD 0.5 the pooled family stays inside its any-call bound, but the per-pair mixture rate is already above α at 0.05 and 0.10.

The oracle arm of M6-09 (generating model, gene-level detection) stays as recorded there: 0 / 0.0127 / 0.0832 on operon_null and 0.0176 / 0.0649 / 0.1189 on the detection attack.

docs.title: Options considered
docs.text:
• (a) Pool, as §7.4.3 says. This is safe only when M6-02 is correctly specified. Under a per-protein detectability SD of 1 logit, the pooled family's FWER/FDR under the complete null is far above 0.1. Rejected.
  • (b) A separate BH family over the P(miss) rows. Conditional on entering the family, P(miss) is not super-uniform, so BH over the one-detected rows alone is not valid. The valid discrete family would have to count every at-risk pair, including those where u was detected (p = 1). It would still inherit (a)'s misspecification failure. Rejected.
  • (c) No q, outside the family, labelled a probability (this ADR). No claim is made that can fail, and the number is still reported for ranking and inspection.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The §8.1 discordance family is narrower than the spec's. The M6 discordance claim is about both-detected pairs only (and is itself pending ADR-0055).
  • One-detected pairs are never flagged as discordant. A user who thresholds p_value on one_detected_pmiss rows gets the false-flag shares in the table above. The report must say so.
  • docs/methods/operons.md "One detected (M6-05H)" and "Family" cite this ADR in place of "needs an ADR (pending M6-09 attack C)". The two Superseded notes in docs/specs/M6-02 and M6-05 point here.
  • When the #311 review round lands (u scored with v's TU model; the one-detected event = fewer than k_min observable peptides seen), attack C through the step is rerun and the table updated. On real data, pairs that cross a TU boundary can move.

docs.title: ADR-0057: the calibration merge honours the xfail mark of the test that owns a check
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-24, in session: "Yes and yes", to "should the merge step honour expected-failure marks?")
  • Date: 2026-10-24
  • Spec sections: §8.4 (calibration criteria, nightly suites), §12 (calibration job array), §14.6; ADR-0015 (two-block confirmation)
  • Needs Khoa: yes (it changes when the calibration gate's exit code is a failure). Decided.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
A calibration test may carry a strict pytest.mark.xfail(raises=AssertionError) naming a pending decision. ADR-0055 Amendment 1 (accepted on m6/gate-09) is the motivating case: test_attack_d1b_step[full] is measured to fail its pooled level at full R, and the claim is narrowed by the amendment, never by widening a bound (R3).

Unsharded, pytest applies the mark. A confirmed fail raises AssertionError in the test, which is reported XFAIL, and the task exits 0. A pass is a strict XPASS, and the task exits non-zero.

Sharded (--shard K/N), no shard has a verdict. Each shard logs its block and skips. The verdict comes from _criteria.py --merge, which until now knew nothing about the test that wrote a record. So a confirmed fail of a strict-xfail check exited MERGE_FAIL, and a pass exited 0. That is the opposite of the unsharded run, so the same suite passed or failed depending on how it was run.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Owner in the record. tests/calibration/conftest.py names the running test around every test call (pytest_runtest_call → _criteria.set_current_test). It does this with pytest's own evaluation of the xfail marks (_pytest.skipping.evaluate_xfail_marks, which handles conditions and xfail_strict). Every record that calibrate, calibrate_pooled and calibrate_fdr_counts write then carries test (the node ID) and xfail. xfail is {"strict", "reason"} when the mark would turn an AssertionError into XFAIL, and None otherwise: no mark, a false condition, run=False, or a raises that excludes AssertionError.

This mapping comes from the tests themselves, not from a hand-kept list. Records of one check that disagree on xfail, or an xfail check written by two tests, are a merge error (MERGE_ERROR, fail closed). Logs written before this ADR, which have no test / xfail fields, merge as before. 2. Per-test outcome, as pytest's. A test with an xfail mark failed if any of its checks is a confirmed fail (both blocks, ADR-0015), or if one of its direct assertions failed in shard 0. In the second case conftest writes an xfailed line to <suite>.outcomes.jsonl (_criteria.log_test_outcome). - If the test failed, every one of its checks gets outcome = "xfail". - If every check is pass / unconfirmed and the test did not fail, every check gets outcome = "xpass". - A vacuous check leaves the test's outcome unset. 3. Exit codes of --merge. - A confirmed fail with outcome = "xfail" is an expected failure. It does not make the exit MERGE_FAIL. - A strict XPASS exits MERGE_FAIL (1), and the merge prints XPASS(strict) <test>. - A non-strict xfail is reported (xfail / xpass in the summary's status column and in <suite>.merged.jsonl) but never changes the exit code. - Any other confirmed fail is MERGE_FAIL, as before. Merge errors are unchanged. 4. Unsharded task exit is pytest's own exit code and already honours the mark. The teeth test (tests/calibration/test_criteria_shard_equivalence.py) checks that the unsharded and the sharded exits agree in every case.

No bound, alpha, R, level, seed or gate condition changes. Every check is evaluated exactly as before (ADR-0015). The only change is how --merge turns a check's verdict into an exit code, which now matches what pytest does with the same test unsharded.

docs.title: Evidence (before → after: metrics, tests, simulations)
docs.text:
• tests/calibration/test_criteria_merge_xfail.py covers the four cases on sharded logs:
  • strict-xfail fail → exit 0, xfail;
  • strict-xfail pass → exit 1, xpass, XPASS(strict);
  • non-strict xfail → exit 0, reported only;
  • unmarked fail → exit 1.

It also checks: - the per-test verdict (one failing and one passing check → xfail); - a shard-0 direct failure → xfail; - disagreeing marks → MERGE_ERROR; - pre-ADR logs merge unchanged. - tests/calibration/test_criteria_shard_equivalence.py runs a fixture suite unsharded and as 3 shards + --merge, through _criteria.main as calibration_full.sbatch does. It finds the same verdicts, the same pooled rates and the same exit in the ok, xpass and fail scenarios. - Before: the same strict-xfail check exited 1 sharded and 0 unsharded (or 0 and 1 for a pass).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A strict xfail now works the same in the nightly array (unsharded tasks), in task 13 (sharded in the task) and with scripts/slurm/calibration_sharded.sh (N shard jobs + a merge job).
  • A test's xfail mark is the single source of truth. Removing the mark, for example once an ADR amendment narrows the claim, takes effect in sharded runs without touching the harness.
  • A check that is shared by two tests, one with a mark and one without, can no longer be merged. Give each test its own stream.
  • <suite>.outcomes.jsonl is a new file in the calibration log directory. It is read only by --merge.

docs.title: ADR-0058: The tolerant matcher may consume an annotated stop codon (option B of M7-16)
docs.text:
• Status: accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-24, in session: "B"). Read-through residue in makedb patches = X (the proposed default, taken with B). Item 6 accepted-by-khoa (2026-10-24, in session: "Yes to 2"; built in M7-16 PR 16c, after 16b). Amendment 1 (Khoa, 2026-10-24: "sure"): placement-kind labels, under Consequences › Interfaces.
  • Date: 2026-10-24
  • Spec sections: §7.2.1 (six-frame index, decoys), §7.2.4 (route 3, the cost table, G4 completeness), §7.2.5 (placement FDR, G3), §7.2.6 (locus classes), §7.5.1, §7.5.3 G8 stop_codon, §7.6.3, §7.9.2 (makedb --patch), §11.6 TE1/TE2; ADR-0013 (cterm_extension, readthrough_candidate)
  • Needs Khoa: yes. It changes Module 2's search space and therefore what the placement FDR controls. Answered for items 1–5 ("B") and item 6 ("Yes to 2"), both 2026-10-24.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Three accepted parts of the design assume a peptide can be placed across a genome stop codon: §7.5.3 G8 stop_codon ("the REF residue is a stop (e.g., Sec read through UGA)") and §7.5.1 ("Sec sites … appear as ALT calls"); ADR-0013 (cterm_extension evidence is "a peptide spanning the annotated stop", the readthrough_candidate label, and a patch row with a new end); and TE2's stop_codon exception (§11.6).

The merged matcher cannot do any of this. The index writes * at every stop (§7.2.1). The exact automaton never matches across one. The M3-06 DP says "No operation may consume a target *" (tolerant_dp._verify_core gates every move on t1 < 19), and the frameshift route and the M7-01 re-alignment (variants.align._residues raises on a genome *) do the same. So in v1 as built, stop_codon and cterm_extension calls are unreachable (M7-05 rule 6, M7-09 rule 4, M7-11b), and M7-18 lead decision 1 handed the Sec/Pyl ALT rule to this ADR.

M7-16 listed three options (A leave it, B annotated-stop substitution, C any-stop substitution). Khoa chose B.

What B reaches, checked on the Nissle recording (tests/data/recorded/bakta/1.12.2-full/nissle, Bakta 1.12.2, full DB; all four replicons circular; the review's mass numbers, job 1889319, came from a local run with linear replicons, local/recordings/bakta_full/nissle1917, and job 1889965 reproduces them on this recording). There are 4,692 CDS and sORF features. 4,689 end in a stop (TAA 2,943, TGA 1,401, TAG 345); the other 3 are partial genes at plasmid edges with no stop as their last codon (JMJJOG_04967, JMJJOG_04968, JMJJOG_04975), counted as not_a_stop (corrected 2026-10-24 by the 16a implementation). No two features share a stop codon, and none crosses an origin. The 4 TE1 misses (M3-22) are the selenocysteine peptides of the two fdnG copies (JMJJOG_02511 −, JMJJOG_04733 +): VUHGPTVASLAPTFGR, VUHGPTVASLAPTFGRGAMTNHWVDIK, SLGMLAVDNQARVUHGPTVASLAPTFGR and ALGMLAVDNQARVUHGPTVASLAPTFGR. Bakta annotates both copies as full-length selenoproteins (1,015 and 1,016 aa), with U at residue 196 over an internal TGA: [2578627, 2578630) − and [4825395, 4825398) +. That TGA is not the last codon of the feature. So the option-B rule as worded does not reach the fdnG peptides. It reaches C-terminal read-through (cterm_extension) and any residue read at an annotated terminal stop. Item 6 states what reaching fdnG would take.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Consumable stops. The tolerant DP (route 3, M3-06/M3-07) may consume a target * only at the annotated stop codon of a CDS or sORF. That is the last codon of the feature (Gene.interval, feature_type in {cds, sorf}), on the feature's strand, in the feature's frame. It may consume it only by a substitution (one query residue against the *), at cost 1, recorded as diff_types substitution with REF *. The rule does not depend on the codon (TAA, TAG and TGA alike). A match is never possible: no query code equals a stop. Swaps, blocks and near-blocks never consume a stop, consumable or not. Every other * and every X stays unconsumable. Pseudogenes are excluded. So is a feature whose last codon is not a stop (for example a partial gene at a contig edge); it is counted in an event. On circular replicons the codon is marked at every copy in the origin-extended frames, including a codon that crosses the origin.
  2. Decoys. Each decoy search carries the same rule at the mirrored positions. For a reverse decoy frame of n residues, target position p becomes n − 1 − p (mirror_aa). For a shuffle decoy it stays p, because stops keep their positions. Both decoys keep a * at the mirrored cell, so a target and its decoy expose the same number of consumable cells per frame. Decoy hits stay counted only, never placed.
  3. Routes. The exact route is unchanged. The frameshift route (M3-08) never consumes a stop in either side. Its precedence check ("a non-frameshift alignment at cost ≤ the split's overlaps the split locus") does see consumable-stop alignments, so a split never coexists with a cheaper or equal read-through alignment of the same locus. M7-01 re-alignment uses the same set and rule. The recomputed cost must still equal n_diff.
  4. Variants. A substitution op with REF * is an ALT site with flag stop_codon (G8; M7-05 rule 6 as written). The snv/multi_nt class comes from the codon (for example W over TGA → snv). U over TGA and O over TAG are the standard decodings (Sec, Pyl). Per §7.5.1 they are ALT calls with stop_codon, zero nucleotide changes, neither snv nor multi_nt, no VCF record (ALT codon = REF codon) and flag vcf_unrepresentable. This replaces the M7-18 rare skip for exactly those two cases. Every other U/O, and every B/J/X/Z, is skipped as M7-18 does today.
  5. makedb --patch residue: X. A patch CDS with Note=cterm_extension translates the annotated stop codon of its locus_tag gene as X. Search engines treat X as any residue, which covers Sec (U), Trp (W) and Gln/Tyr read-through. Any other internal stop in any patch CDS still raises, as M3-23 does.
  6. Accepted by Khoa (2026-10-24), built in 16c. The consumable set also includes annotated recoded codons: an internal in-frame codon of a CDS whose Bakta protein has U over TGA or O over TAG at that residue. That is 3 sites in Nissle (fdnG ×2, fdhF). Decoys would be mirrored as in item 2. This is what makes the fdnG TE1 misses placeable. Until 16c merges, the code builds only item 1's set.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
• Search-space growth (an approximation, not a bound). A window can consume a marked stop only if it contains it: L windows per stop, with the other L − 1 residues within m − 1 differences. The added chance-hit mass is approximately G·L·Σ_{j<m} C(L−1, j)(1−s)^j s^(L−1−j), against E(L, m) of §7.2.5. In closed form the ratio is approximately G/(N(1 − s)) at m = 1 and 2G/(N(1 − s)) at m = 2, independent of L. It scales with the gene density G/N. In the Appendix B setting (N = 10⁷ six-frame positions, s = 0.069, G = 5,000 consumable stops, so G/N = 5 × 10⁻⁴) that is about 0.054 % and 0.107 %:
L, m E(L, m) added by B (approx.) ratio (approx.) 10, 1 3.3 × 10⁻³ 1.8 × 10⁻⁶ 0.05 % 11, 1 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ 1.4 × 10⁻⁷ 0.05 % 12, 2 1.4 × 10⁻³ 1.5 × 10⁻⁶ 0.11 % 16, 2 5.8 × 10⁻⁸ 6.2 × 10⁻¹¹ 0.11 %

The formula counts all N positions, stops included, and spreads chance hits evenly; against the realised searchable mass both sides lose stop-containing windows. Measured realised shares (exact expected chance mass, statistician, Slurm jobs 1889319 and 1889320, local/stat/m7-16-review.md): 0.04–0.08 % of the target chance mass on Nissle (i.i.d. and tryptic laws, m = 1 and 2), and 0.05–0.20 % on three giapsim 1-Mb genomes (the top of the range under the tryptic law at m = 2). On another genome the share is approximately, not at most, the formula's value for its G/N.

Option C, with about 5 × 10⁵ stops in 10⁷ positions, would add about 100× this, and that mass would sit at every stop of every frame. - Symmetry. By construction (item 2), each decoy frame has exactly the target's number of consumable cells. Each such cell holds * and is mirrored one to one. The tests in M7-16 make this a property test. The reverse decoy is exact under any i.i.d. peptide law (measured D_rt/T_rt = 1 to 1e-16).
