The local context is mirrored, not kept (gene | * | flank becomes flank | * | gene), so under the tryptic law the per-genome read-through D_rt/T_rt was 0.52–1.89 (giapsim) and 0.81–1.15 (Nissle) for reverse, and 0.58–1.74 and 1.14–1.42 for shuffle. The measured net effect on the total, (D_rt − T_rt)/T_regular, was −9.4 × 10⁻⁴ in the worst giapsim replicate. D_rt/T_rt is not an FDR for the read-through subset and is never reported as one. - Calibration. Before/after numbers come from the re-runs that M7-16 requires (fast + full, TE1/TE2/TE8). Only the exercised suites are evidence for this rule: the run_chain suites test_placement_fdr_sim.py, test_denovo_precision_sim.py and attack 5, plus the M7-16 stressed arm (test_readthrough_stressed.py) and the statistician's attack (attacks/test_attack_readthrough_decoys.py). For each exercised suite this section records the per-replicate number of accepted target rows that consumed a cell. The regression-only suites (test_tolerant_recall.py, test_placement_fdr_genome.py, test_placement_fdr_lists.py, attacks/test_attack_placement_*) are byte-identical by construction (cells=None or no matcher) and are not cited as evidence. This section is filled in with the Slurm job IDs when 16a merges.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Module 2 search space. Route 3 grows by at most one consumable cell per annotated gene and search (≈ 4,700 on Nissle), adding approximately G/(N(1 − s)) (m = 1) to 2G/(N(1 − s)) (m = 2) of the chance-hit mass; measured 0.04–0.08 % on Nissle and up to 0.20 % on giapsim (above). Peptides of 7–9 aa never reach route 3 (min_len 10), so a stop-spanning peptide shorter than 10 aa is never placed. At 10–11 aa (k = 1) the stop is the only allowed difference. With no annotated genes the matcher is byte-identical to main.
  • Placement FDR (G3). The estimator, the strata, π̂ (m ≥ 1 → 1) and the ranking score E are unchanged. Read-through placements are tolerant hits at m ≥ 1, so same_db exact skipping never applies to them. Validity rests on item 2. No tolerance, bound, α or R changes (R3).
  • Re-calibration required. The M3-21 placement suites must re-run, fast and full, with no tolerance change. A failure stops the merge and goes to a new ADR, never to a tolerance change. Regression-only (byte-identical by construction): test_tolerant_recall.py, test_placement_fdr_genome.py, test_placement_fdr_lists.py, attacks/test_attack_placement_*. Exercised: test_placement_fdr_sim.py, test_denovo_precision_sim.py and attack 5. Even the exercised suites see few cells at 100 kb to 1 Mb, so M7-16 adds a required stressed arm (dense short annotated genes, ≥ 100 expected false target read-through rows per replicate, reverse and shuffle arms, a negative control without decoy cells that must fail), a decoy-balance check (se_multiplier, one-sided, may be vacuous) and the statistician's exact-mass attack, which 16a's merge waits for. TE8 (Nissle pooled FDR ≤ 0.01) re-runs weekly as usual.
  • TE1. Unchanged under items 1–5. The fdnG Sec site is internal, so the 4 misses stay unmapped. Under item 6 (16c) they become tolerant placements (cost 1) flagged sec_site. They are still not exact, so they stay TE1 exceptions, now labelled as Sec.
  • TE2 and G8. The stop_codon flag becomes reachable. TE2's second exception is exercised only when an annotated stop or (item 6) a recoded codon carries a placed peptide. On Nissle same-strain peptides, items 1–5 add no site. Item 6 would add two candidate U sites at the fdnG codons, one unique peptide each (the 16-mer and 27-mer are shared between the copies), and no high site.
  • cterm_extension. It is reachable through route 3: a peptide in frame with a CDS/sORF that crosses its annotated stop into the 3′ flank (M3-14 _cterm, unchanged). M7-09's class rule becomes live (a spanning peptide plus an in-frame continuation; readthrough_candidate). Under M7-11 decision 2 the class stays unestimated, so it is called only with ≥ 2 distinct peptides. M7-07 writes its patch row, and makedb --patch translates the old stop as X.
  • Interfaces. sixframe_index gains the genes input and writes index format 2, which carries the consumable cells for the target and each decoy type. No config key, no new column and no new diff type. Amendment 1 (Khoa, 2026-10-24) adds labels, not method:
  • the placement flag readthrough (16b), and sec_site/pyl_site (16c), in the §9.4 vocabulary through the schema;
  • the GFF3 attributes readthrough_codon and recoded_codon;
  • an optional sixframe input to loci;
  • placement-kind count rows in detection_summary.tsv (section qc).

The other flags (stop_codon, vcf_unrepresentable, readthrough_candidate) already exist. See the M7-16 spec, "Amendment: 16b reporting and the 16c labels". - Backlog. "M7-16: decide stop_codon and mass_equivalent for blocks and swaps whose REF contains *" closes: no block or swap ever consumes a stop.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
• A. Leave it. No cost. But G8 stop_codon, ADR-0013's evidence and patch row, and TE2's second exception stay dormant or vacuous, and PROGRESS.md must keep saying so. Rejected by Khoa.
  • C. Any-stop substitution. About 150 lines, but every stop in every frame becomes a cost-1 chance-hit site: roughly 100× the added mass above, concentrated next to stops. The §7.2.5 / Appendix B.2 chance-hit table and the placement-FDR calibration would need re-derivation. Every pseudogene and frame-shifted ORF would also become a "read-through". Rejected.

Install
docs.text:
GIAP has two parts:

  • the Python package, which provides the giap command;
  • the tools it runs as separate programs (Bakta, miniprot, geNOMAD, antiSMASH and others). Each tool runs from a pinned container image or a prebuilt micromamba environment.

giap preflight, giap convert, giap compare and giap report need only the Python package. giap makedb also needs the contaminant library from giap setup, unless you pass --no-contaminants. giap setup needs a Bakta and, with --antismash, an antiSMASH tool environment or image (see below), but not Nextflow. giap run needs Nextflow, every tool environment and image, and the databases.

Supported platform for giap run in 1.0

The full pipeline is supported on Stanford FarmShare, from a checkout of the repository. Its tool environments are built by the repository's scripts. Outside FarmShare, no supported way to build the conda-only tool environments exists yet; this is tracked as an open issue. See What giap run needs and Platforms.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Requirement Version Where it is pinned Python Python ≥ 3.11 requires-python = ">=3.11" in pyproject.toml Nextflow 26.10.0 (the pinned version) or newer scripts/bootstrap_farmshare.sh, ADR-0002 Java 17 or newer, which Nextflow needs; the bootstrap installs OpenJDK 21 scripts/bootstrap_farmshare.sh A container runtime or Conda Apptainer (tested), Conda/micromamba or Docker see Platforms

docs.title: The Python package
docs.text:
From PyPI, with pip or uv:

pip install giap            # into the active environment
uv tool install giap        # or: an isolated tool environment with uv
giap --version

The PyPI package is published with each release. The extra giap[docs] installs MkDocs Material for building this site.

Bioconda. The recipe is pending (M11-10). Once it is merged, the install command will be micromamba install -c conda-forge -c bioconda giap. Until then, use PyPI.

docs.title: Nextflow and Java
docs.text:
Install Nextflow and a Java runtime from conda-forge and bioconda (never the defaults channel):

micromamba create -n giap-nf --override-channels -c conda-forge -c bioconda nextflow=26.10.0 openjdk=21
micromamba activate giap-nf
nextflow -version

giap run exits with code 2 when nextflow is not on PATH.

docs.title: Execution profiles
docs.text:
giap run --profile takes one or more of these Nextflow profiles, joined by commas: farmshare, farmshare_local, apptainer, conda, docker, standard. The default is farmshare,apptainer.

Profile What it does Status apptainer runs the container-pinned tools (Bakta, TransTermHP, geNOMAD, antiSMASH, miniprot, BLAST+) from images pulled by digest tested (on FarmShare) conda lets Nextflow create each tool's environment from workflow/envs/*.yml; preflight still requires the prebuilt environments of the conda-only tools (below) not tested on its own; see Platforms docker the same images as apptainer, through Docker not tested; see Platforms farmshare Slurm executor on Stanford FarmShare, plus the prebuilt tool environments under $GIAP_ROOT tested farmshare_local the same environments, but all tasks run inside the current Slurm allocation tested standard Nextflow's local executor, with no container or Conda settings not tested

Some tools have no container image yet: UniOP, Promotech, Promoter Calculator, TerminatorNet, OSTIR, BacTermFinder (opt-in) and the R fgsea runner (used with function and --abundance). These are the conda-only tools. Platforms lists which profile combinations are tested.

docs.title: What giap run needs before preflight passes
docs.text:
In run mode, preflight checks that every tool the run will use is installed. A missing tool is an environment error: giap run exits with code 2 before Nextflow starts. The checks are in src/giap/preflight/environment.py (missing_tools).

  1. $GIAP_ROOT. Preflight looks for tool environments and images under $GIAP_ROOT. When it is not set, every tool that needs an environment or image is reported missing.
  2. The conda-only tool environments, under every profile. Each conda-only tool the run uses needs $GIAP_ROOT/micromamba/envs/giap-<tool>/. That directory must contain the marker file .giap-built, holding the SHA-256 of workflow/envs/<tool>.yml. scripts/build_envs.sh builds the environments and writes the markers. On FarmShare, run it as sbatch scripts/slurm/build_envs.sbatch from a repository checkout. It sources scripts/farmshare_env.sh and updates the lock files in workflow/envs/locks/. It is written for FarmShare: a supported way to build these environments elsewhere does not exist yet.
  3. The pinned images, under the apptainer profile. Each container-pinned tool (Bakta, TransTermHP, geNOMAD, antiSMASH, miniprot, BLAST+) needs its image file in $GIAP_ROOT/containers/. The file is named after the reference in workflow/conf/containers.config: the docker:// prefix is dropped, and / and : become -, followed by .img. Preflight reads only this directory. scripts/slurm/build_envs.sbatch pulls every pinned image into $NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR, which scripts/farmshare_env.sh sets to $GIAP_ROOT/containers. Under the docker and conda profiles, preflight does not check the pinned images: Nextflow resolves them itself.
  4. The databases, from giap setup (next section).

The antiSMASH image alone is about 9 GB (GIAP_SPEC.md §3.9).

docs.title: What giap setup needs
docs.text:
giap setup fetches most items itself over HTTPS. It does not need Nextflow. Two downloaders run inside a tool environment:

  • bakta_db download, which also runs amrfinder_update (for --bakta light or --bakta full);
  • antiSMASH's database downloader (for --antismash).

For each of these, giap setup looks for one of two things (src/giap/setupdb/run.py, ToolRunner):

  • a micromamba environment giap-bakta or giap-antismash under $MAMBA_ROOT_PREFIX/envs/ (default $GIAP_ROOT/micromamba);
  • the pinned image, already pulled into $NXF_APPTAINER_CACHEDIR (default $GIAP_ROOT/containers), which it runs with apptainer exec.

To find the image reference, it reads workflow/conf/containers.config from $GIAP_REPO. From an installed wheel, the default location is wrong (a known issue). Set GIAP_REPO to a checkout of the repository at the same version. When neither the environment nor the image is found, the item stays absent, its record in db_manifest.json names the missing tool, and giap setup exits with code 2. On FarmShare, the environments and images come from sbatch scripts/slurm/build_envs.sbatch bakta antismash.

docs.title: Databases
docs.text: The databases and models are downloaded once with giap setup. See Set up the databases.

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
giap --version
giap setup --db-dir /path/to/db --check          # verify what is installed, download nothing
giap preflight --genome genome.fna --proteins proteins.faa

The CLI reference lists every command and option.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
This page runs GIAP once, from start to finish, on public inputs: the E. coli K-12 MG1655 genome from NCBI and the K-12 reference proteome from UniProt. You need an installation (Install) and the databases (Set up the databases).

Where this runs

giap run passes preflight only when the tool environments and images are in place under $GIAP_ROOT (see Install › What giap run needs). In 1.0 this is supported on FarmShare from a repository checkout. Steps 1 and 2 work anywhere the Python package is installed.

Why a protein list

giap run needs evidence: --peptides, --proteins or both. A genome alone fails preflight with exit code 1 (inputs.evidence_present). GIAP ships no demo peptide table. This quickstart therefore uses the UniProt proteome as a protein list. That gives the protein_list detection tier, whose gene detection is unestimated (see Interpreting results). To use your own search results, convert them with giap convert and pass --peptides.

This run carries no biological signal. The whole reference proteome is given as the list of detected proteins, so every mapped gene comes out detected. There is no undetected class for the region, island or enrichment contrasts to compare against. Use it as a smoke test of the installation and to learn the output layout, not to interpret results. No run of exactly this command has been recorded yet.

docs.title: 1. Download the inputs
docs.text:
mkdir -p quickstart && cd quickstart
# genome: NCBI assembly GCA_000005845.2 (one circular chromosome, U00096.3)
curl -fLO https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCA/000/005/845/GCA_000005845.2_ASM584v2/GCA_000005845.2_ASM584v2_genomic.fna.gz
# proteins: UniProt reference proteome UP000000625 (E. coli K-12 MG1655)
curl -fL -o UP000000625.fasta \
  "https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/stream?format=fasta&query=%28proteome%3AUP000000625%29"

NCBI headers carry no topology tag, so preflight reports the chromosome as linear and adds an info row (genome.topology). This assembly is complete. You can mark its replicons circular in either of two ways:

  • add [topology=circular] to the header;
  • pass --set annotation.bakta.complete=true, as below.

See Inputs.

docs.title: 2. Check the inputs
docs.text:
giap preflight --genome GCA_000005845.2_ASM584v2_genomic.fna.gz \
  --proteins UP000000625.fasta --set annotation.bakta.complete=true --outdir preflight_check

Preflight takes seconds. It prints a table of checks (ok, info, warn, error) and writes preflight_check/preflight/preflight.json and preflight.md. Exit code 0 means you can go on. Any other code is explained in Running GIAP › Exit codes; for an input error (1), the table names the rule that failed.

docs.title: 3. Run
docs.text:
giap run --genome GCA_000005845.2_ASM584v2_genomic.fna.gz \
  --proteins UP000000625.fasta \
  --set annotation.bakta.complete=true \
  --db-dir /path/to/db \
  --threads 16 --memory 64.GB \
  --outdir out

--profile defaults to farmshare,apptainer. Off FarmShare, choose the profiles that fit your machine: see Install › Execution profiles and Platforms. If a run stops, rerun the same command with --resume. Measured runtimes: see Runtimes.

docs.title: 4. The output tree
docs.text:
out/
├── run_manifest.json      tool and database versions, parameters, input SHA-256, seeds, timings
├── resolved_config.yaml   the configuration the run used
├── preflight/             preflight.json, preflight.md
├── annotation/            genes.gff3, regions.tsv, regions.bed, promoters.bed, terminators.bed,
│                          operon_pairs.tsv, tus.tsv, tools/ (native tool outputs)
├── mapping/               peptide_hits.tsv, protein_hits.tsv, unmapped.tsv, mapping_fdr.tsv,
│                          mappings.bed, mappings.probed, mappings.gff3
├── tables/                genes.tsv (the master table), detection_summary.tsv, …
├── plots/                 Vnn_<name>.svg|png|pdf, data/Vnn_<name>.tsv, support/
├── report/report.html
├── schemas/datapackage.json
└── logs/                  events.jsonl, trace.tsv, timeline.html, nf_report.html, <step>.log

Outputs describes every directory. Each table is documented in the table reference.

docs.title: 5. Open the report
docs.text:
report/report.html is one self-contained file. Plotly.js, the CSS and the scripts are inlined, so the page loads nothing from the network. Open it in any browser:

xdg-open out/report/report.html      # Linux desktop
open out/report/report.html          # macOS

On a cluster, copy the file to your computer first, for example with scp or rsync. The report links to the full TSV tables by relative path, so copy the whole out/ directory if you want those links to work.

  • Tutorial: E. coli K-12.

docs.title: Set up the databases
docs.text: giap setup downloads the databases and models into one directory and records each item in DIR/db_manifest.json. Run it once per installation. Then pass the directory to giap run with --db-dir DIR, or set GIAP_DB_DIR=DIR.

docs.title: The command for the default modules
docs.text:
giap run runs all four modules by default: core, mobile (geNOMAD), bgc (antiSMASH) and function (COG, GO, KEGG). They need this setup:

giap setup --db-dir /path/to/db --antismash --go --kegg --cog --contaminants

Without the extra flags, giap setup installs the Bakta light database, the geNOMAD database and the Promotech models. antiSMASH, GO, KEGG, COG and the contaminant library are opt-in.

To use the Bakta full database, add --bakta full. Runs annotated with the light database carry the run flag bakta_db_light. With giap run --annotation bakta.json, Bakta is not run. Preflight still checks that a Bakta database is installed, though, so do not use --bakta skip for a run.

Before the first giap setup, read Install › What giap setup needs: the Bakta and antiSMASH downloaders run in a tool environment or image that giap setup does not install.

On a shared cluster, run giap setup as a batch job: --bakta full alone downloads about 84 GB.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Every flag is listed in the CLI reference.

Flag Default Installs Needed by --db-dir required the target directory every item --bakta light light, full or skip: Bakta DB v6.0 (Zenodo record 14916843; bakta_db download also runs amrfinder_update) annotation, unless --annotation bakta.json is given --genomad / --no-genomad on geNOMAD DB v1.9 (Zenodo record 14886553) module mobile --antismash / --no-antismash off antiSMASH 8.0.4 databases (skipped when the image already contains them) module bgc --promotech-models / --no-promotech-models on Promotech RF-HOT model promoter predictions (core) --go off go-basic.obo and goslim_generic.obo module function --kegg off KEGG KO-to-pathway links and pathway names module function --cog off COG 2020 category tables (cog-20.def.tab, fun-20.tab) cog_category in genes.tsv; module function --contaminants off the universal protein contaminant FASTA contaminant labels in mapping; giap makedb --check off nothing: only verifies what is installed —

The shared options --config, --set, --log-level and --version work as for every command.

docs.title: Layout and sizes
docs.text:
The paths are relative to --db-dir, from src/giap/data/db_sources.yaml. Approximate sizes on disk are from GIAP_SPEC.md §3.9. Where §3.9 gives no size, the table says "not recorded". In that case, measure the size after your first download.

Item Path Size on disk (approx.) Bakta light DB v6.0 bakta/db-light 3.9 GB unpacked (the 1.3 GB archive can be deleted) Bakta full DB v6.0 bakta/db about 84 GB unpacked geNOMAD DB v1.9 genomad_db about 0.8 GB; giap setup asks for 4 GiB of free space before downloading antiSMASH databases antismash not recorded Promotech RF-HOT promotech not recorded GO go/go-basic.obo, go/goslim_generic.obo not recorded KEGG kegg/ko_pathway.tsv, kegg/pathway_names.tsv not recorded COG 2020 cog/cog-20.def.tab, cog/fun-20.tab not recorded Contaminants contaminants/contaminants.fasta not recorded

The Apptainer images take a separate 15–25 GB in the image cache (§3.9).

docs.title: db_manifest.json
docs.text:
giap setup writes DIR/db_manifest.json, next to the items. Each item gets a record with its name, version, URL, checksum, size and retrieval date. The schema is src/giap/schemas/db_manifest.schema.json. giap run copies the database versions and checksums into the run's run_manifest.json. Preflight reads the manifest to check that the database each module needs is installed.

KEGG has no release version. For KEGG, the manifest records the retrieval date and the SHA-256 of the downloaded bytes (ADR-0017). The contaminant library is pinned: commit bddf6da9, with a fixed SHA-256 in db_sources.yaml.

docs.title: Failures
docs.text: giap setup exits with code 2 in two cases: a source cannot be reached, or a checksum does not match. The message names the host, and the item stays absent. GIAP never falls back to another source. Run the command again later; --check shows which items are present.

docs.title: What giap setup does not download
docs.text:
• RegulonDB. Users never download RegulonDB. GIAP's developers use RegulonDB v12 only to calibrate cut-offs on E. coli K-12, and GIAP does not redistribute it.
  • Search-engine software and spectra. GIAP never searches spectra. You run DIA-NN or a de novo tool yourself, under your own licence (see Licences).
  • Genomes. You provide the genome FASTA.

docs.title: Licences of the downloaded data
docs.text: geNOMAD is for non-commercial use only. KEGG is free for academic use; other users need a licence from KEGG. Read Licences before you install either.

docs.title: Gene-level abundance: iBAQ, Top3, protein-level route, missing values
docs.text: Implements giap.genetable.abundance (peptide_abundance, protein_abundance, resolve_c10_scale, impute, gene_abundance); GIAP_SPEC.md §2.1 decisions 2–3, §7.3.4, §7.2.6, §9.3–9.4, §5.2 abundance; issue M4-14 (docs/specs/M4-14-abundance.md, including lead decisions 1–6 on PR #82). The output is one point estimate per gene in one sample. This module runs no test, so it has no p-values, no test family (§8.1) and no CI. Uncertainty enters downstream through rank-based statistics, TU-block resampling and the basic/full sensitivity reruns (§8.6).

docs.title: What is estimated
docs.text: The aim is the relative molar amount of each gene's protein in a single sample, known only up to one common constant per run. Only ratios between genes and ranks carry meaning. Values are not absolute copy numbers. Values from different runs or inputs cannot be compared without normalisation, which GIAP does not do.

docs.title: Which route is used (and when abundance is NA)
docs.text:
Condition (checked in this order) source abundance_type abundance_scale some abundance_eligible accepted peptide has a non-NA intensity peptide_intensity abundance.method (ibaq default, or top3) molar otherwise, C10 (abundance.tsv) given protein_table abundance.type (declared; default unknown) molar iff type ∈ {ibaq, top3}, else relative neither none none NA; every abundance column NA, imputation_policy NA

The two routes are never mixed. When peptide intensities exist, C10 is ignored. One edge case follows from this: if every eligible intensity is exactly 0, the run takes the peptide route, every gene comes out missing, and C10 is still not used. A no_observed_abundance warning is logged.

Under the relative scale (maxlfq, intensity, unknown), Module 4 marks its abundance tests unestimated (relative_scale) and skips stoichiometry (§7.3.4). The default C10 type is unknown. A protein table therefore gives relative abundance unless the user declares --abundance-type ibaq or top3.

docs.title: Peptide route
docs.text:
Inputs: - The M4-11 accepted peptides with abundance_eligible. These are unique exact hits plus tolerant hits under related. multi_identical, shared, N- and C-terminal extension evidence are excluded. - A finite intensity > 0. An intensity of 0 or NA means the peptide is skipped, not counted as 0. - Each peptide's intensity is already summed over charges and modified forms within a run, then the median across runs is taken (§5.3, C9).

Estimates: - iBAQ (Schwanhäusser et al. 2011): iBAQ_g = Σ_quantified intensity / max(1, n_obs,g), where n_obs,g = n_observable_peptides. This count comes from M4-10: configured enzyme, 0 missed cleavages, length 7–30, counted on the strain gene sequence (on the partial sequence for partial genes). - The sum of observed peptide intensities scales with the gene's molar amount times the number of its peptides the instrument can see. Dividing by the number of theoretically observable peptides removes the length (peptide-count) factor. - Top3 (Silva et al. 2006): the arithmetic mean, on the linear scale, of the (up to) 3 largest intensities, then log2 (lead decision on spec question 1). - With 1–2 quantified peptides it is the mean of those, flagged top3_lt3. - top3_log2 is always reported on the peptide route. abundance_log2 follows abundance.method. - abundance_raw is the linear iBAQ (or Top3) value, and abundance_log2 = log2(abundance_raw). - Sums are taken over sorted values with math.fsum, so results do not depend on row order. - Multiplying every intensity by c > 0 shifts every observed abundance_log2 by exactly log2 c (a unit property test).

docs.title: Assumptions and when they fail (direction)
docs.text: Assumption Fails when Effect Peptide intensity ∝ molar amount × a peptide response factor independent of the gene response factors vary a lot (ionisation, sequence) noise only. Ranks degrade smoothly (Spearman with truth 0.98 → 0.91 as the log-SD of peptide noise goes 0.5 → 1.5; table below) Missing peptides are missing at random (MAR) low-abundance genes lose more peptides (MNAR, the usual case) iBAQ of low-abundance genes is pulled further down, because unseen observable peptides count as 0 in the numerator. The scale is stretched at the low end. Ranks are mostly kept because the distortion is monotone in abundance Numerator and denominator count the same peptides accepted peptides include missed-cleavage or out-of-range-length peptides that n_obs does not count. Overlapping missed-cleavage forms count the same sequence twice iBAQ is somewhat inflated for genes rich in missed cleavages. This matches MaxQuant's iBAQ convention and is not corrected n_obs reflects observability genes with n_obs = 0 that still have quantified peptides (e.g. only missed-cleavage peptides) the denominator is floored at 1. For these genes iBAQ is the raw sum, which is too high relative to other genes Top3: the 3 best-responding peptides are similar across proteins genes with many quantified peptides the mean of the top 3 of n order statistics grows with n. Top3 is biased upward for long, well-covered genes. iBAQ has no such bias, which is why it is the primary method Tolerant (related) hits measure the strain protein strain differences change ionisation small per-peptide noise. These hits are labelled strain_difference upstream

docs.title: Protein route (abundance.tsv, C10)
docs.text:
C10 values are joined to genes through the M4-12 protein → gene map (protein_id, gene, method).

Measurement scale (lead decision 1). The scale is the explicit abundance.scale if it is not auto, otherwise the preflight scale (M4Inputs.abundance_scale), otherwise a ValueError. Two details: - C10 normally has no scale column. If a scale column carries more than one value under auto, the run errors. - Preflight detects the scale as log2 if any value is negative or every value is ≤ 50, else linear (§5.3).

Transform. Linear values become log2. Values ≤ 0 and ±inf become missing, because log2 is undefined for them. On a log2 scale, finite values are kept, including negatives. abundance_raw keeps the input value on the input's own scale, so for a log2 input it is the log2 number.

Several proteins on one gene (§7.2.6). The gene takes the largest log2 value (NA values lose; ties go to the smallest protein_id), with flag two_proteins_one_gene. - Taking the maximum rather than summing is the spec's choice. Two input proteins on one locus are usually redundant entries (isoform or accession duplicates) quantified from overlapping peptides, so summing would double count. - The maximum is biased upward when the entries are independent noisy measurements of one protein. The flag lets users filter these genes.

Cross-strain proteins (lead decision 2). A protein mapped by protein_hit whose C12 hit row carries cross_strain_protein passes its value to the strain gene, and the gene gets the flag.

docs.title: Missing values and imputation (§2.1 decision 2; §7.0 "two kinds of missing")
docs.text:
Two kinds of missingness are kept apart: 1. Never identified (not detected): the gene is never imputed. It is a detection outcome, handled by the detection and detectability models (left-censored ranks in §7.3.5 islands, p_detect weighting in ORA). Imputing it would invent a quantity for a protein with no evidence and would double count the detection-limit information those models already use. 2. Identified but not quantified (detected, no value): for example, every peptide of the gene is multi_identical, an extension, or has NA intensity; or the gene has no C10 row. abundance.missing applies to these genes.

Fill statistic. It is computed on the observed abundance_log2 of detected, eligible (non-partial) genes, pooled over all replicons:

Policy Fill value Role median (default) median of observed log2 primary: the genes are detected, so a typical value is used mean mean of observed log2 accepted min minimum observed log2 sensitivity (basic): treats unquantified as near the limit of quantification zero minimum − 1 (half the minimum on the linear scale) accepted; "zero" cannot be represented on a log scale exclude none: stays NA, stays detected, leaves abundance statistics sensitivity (basic)

Rules: - Filled genes get abundance_imputed = true and flag imputed_abundance. abundance_raw stays NA. - imputation_policy records the policy on every row whenever the source is not none. - If no detected eligible gene has an observed value, nothing is filled, fill_value is None, and no_observed_abundance is logged at WARNING. - Detected partial genes with a missing value are filled (lead decision 5). They do not enter the fill statistic, because their n_obs and their quantified peptides cover only part of the protein. - Undetected genes that have an observed value keep it (spec question 3; e.g. single-peptide genes under two_peptide). This is reporting only. Abundance statistics use detected genes.

Direction of the default. Detected-but-unquantified genes are most likely low in abundance (MNAR). Filling them at the median pulls them toward the centre. This attenuates region and island shifts driven by such genes and adds a block of tied values at the median. The basic sensitivity reruns under min (the opposite direction) and exclude (no fill) bracket this effect, and tables/sensitivity.tsv reports the Jaccard overlap of flagged sets.

Two places react to imputed values: - Operon discordance excludes imputed pairs from its t fit (§7.4.2). - Preflight warns when more than 20 % of values are missing (abundance_missing_warn_frac).

The fill statistic is genome-wide, not per replicon. On a high-copy plasmid the imputed value is the chromosome-dominated median. Correction (M4-18 lead decision 2): this does not only affect within-plasmid comparisons. The plasmid replicon-level effect (regions_stats.tsv, hl_shift of a plasmid_* region) contrasts the plasmid's raw log2 abundance with the chromosome's, and imputed plasmid genes sit at the chromosome median, which pulls that contrast towards 0. Imputed genes (abundance_imputed = true) are therefore excluded from both sides of the plasmid HL; they still count as detected in O − E (docs/methods/region-tests.md, "Replicon-level effects").

docs.title: Simulation evidence
docs.text:
Two claims are registered in tests/calibration/test_abundance_calibration.py (suite regions, criterion fwer at 0.05 on per-replicate 0/1 indicators, ADR-0015 two-block confirmation): - abundance.spearman.{ibaq,top3}: the indicator 1{Spearman(estimate, truth) < 0.7} over detected genes with ≥ 3 quantified peptides. This is a sanity claim, not an error-rate claim. - abundance.ibaq_denominator: the indicator 1{the 5 % paired gene-bootstrap lower bound of ρ_iBAQ − ρ_rawsum ≤ 0}.

The generator is the test oracle (tests/helpers/abundance_oracle.py): - giapsim layout with 400 chromosome genes and M4-08 expression; - observable peptides quantified independently with probability p_obs = 0.6; - peptide noise: ln I = a·ln 2 + N(0, 0.5²).

Statistician check (Slurm job 1848760; exact nightly streams, replicates 0–1999 = both blocks of the full run; head 0fcc695):

Quantity min 1 % median max ρ iBAQ 0.969 0.974 0.984 0.993 ρ Top3 0.968 0.976 0.984 0.992 ρ raw sum 0.911 0.924 0.951 0.976 bootstrap lower bound of Δρ 0.0087 0.0136 0.024 0.049 genes per replicate (≥ 3 peptides) 186 194 216 248

Results: - 0 failing replicates of 2,000 for each of the three claims. The fast (R = 100) and full (R = 1,000) checks pass in both blocks. - The per-replicate failure rate is < 0.0015 (95 % upper bound). The checks' added confirmed false alarm on the nightly run is therefore ≈ 0, well inside the ≈ 0.04 family budget. - Teeth: the permuted-n_obs denominator check failed in 40/40 replicates (largest lower bound −0.042), and the shuffled-estimate Spearman check fails. Each teeth check needs ≥ 3/20 failures in both blocks. - Cost: about 0.6 s per replicate per claim, so about 30 CPU-min per nightly run for the three claims and about 3 CPU-min in the fast suite.

docs.title: Stress (outside the gate; R = 300 per cell, seed [777, i])
docs.text:
p_obs, peptide log-SD ρ iBAQ median (min) ρ Top3 median (min) ρ raw sum denominator indicator rate 0.6, 0.5 (oracle default) 0.983 (0.971) 0.984 (0.975) 0.949 0.000 0.6, 1.0 0.959 (0.931) 0.941 (0.904) 0.923 0.000 0.6, 1.5 0.909 (0.851) 0.877 (0.801) 0.873 0.003 0.3, 0.5 0.969 (0.946) 0.981 (0.965) 0.954 0.103 0.3, 1.0 0.933 (0.883) 0.929 (0.874) 0.916 0.270 0.3, 1.5 0.871 (0.788) 0.853 (0.761) 0.850 0.403

How to read the stress table: - The Spearman sanity claim never failed: the 0.7 threshold is far below every cell. - The claim also cannot tell iBAQ from the raw sum, the max, or Top3 (reviewer finding 4). It guards only against estimators that ignore the data. - iBAQ ranks better than Top3 once peptide noise is large, as expected: Top3 discards information and has the order-statistic bias. - The denominator claim measures a property of the generator, not of the code. At low peptide coverage (p_obs = 0.3), binomial sampling of the quantified peptides swamps the n_obs correction. The per-replicate indicator rate is then 0.10–0.40, which would be a confirmed nightly fail at R = 1,000 (bound 0.064).

Before swapping the generator to M4-09 (backlog; logistic peptide detectability, missed cleavages), re-measure this rate. If the M4-09 coverage is low, restate the claim as a pooled effect (for example, the mean Δρ over replicates > 0 with a replicate-level CI) rather than per-replicate power.

The bootstrap resamples genes rather than TUs. Here the estimation errors are independent per gene, but the true abundances are TU-correlated (M4-08 AR(1)). The gene bootstrap therefore somewhat understates the variance of Δρ, which makes the claim easier to pass, not harder. This is acceptable for a teeth-style check. It is not an inference reported to users, so §8.2 "resample TUs" does not bind here.

docs.title: Sign-off
docs.text:
Statistician (M4-14, PR #82, 2026-10-15): approved. The following match §7.3.4/§7.2.6 and the lead decisions: - the iBAQ and Top3 definitions; - the eligibility and zero/NA rules; - the protein-route scale resolution and the maximum rule; - the fill rule (statistic over non-partial detected genes, filling only detected genes, never undetected ones).

The two calibration claims are sound as sanity and teeth checks, with zero false-alarm cost on the current generator. Forwarded: 1. The denominator claim's fragility at low peptide coverage, to re-check with the M4-09 generator before swapping. Suggested attack: p_obs = 0.3. 2. The MNAR direction of median imputation, for the Module 4 methods notes. 3. Recording the abundance claims' fast-suite time in benchmarks/baseline.json.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Schwanhäusser B. et al. (2011) Global quantification of mammalian gene expression control. Nature 473:337–342 (iBAQ).
  • Silva J.C. et al. (2006) Absolute quantification of proteins by LCMS^E. Mol Cell Proteomics 5:144–156 (Top3).

docs.title: Autocorrelation of abundance along the replicon
docs.text:
Issue M5-01 adds the shared detrending helper and M5-02 the lag statistics, nulls and block length; the per-replicon autocorrelation tables are M5-05 (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.5(c), ADR-0020 with Amendment 1, ADR-0021).

giap.stats.autocorr provides morans_i, join_count, label_permutations, tu_blocks, tu_block_permutations, lag_test, choose_block_len and block_len_prime (issue M5-02, lead decisions 4–22; GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.5(d) step 5, §7.3.6, §8.3, Appendix B.4). Statistician sign-off for the statistics is at the end of this note.

docs.title: Detrending
docs.text:
giap.stats.smooth.loess_detrend(y, pos, frac, *, circular, period=None, min_points=3) and loess_matrix(...) (the n × n smoother H with loess_detrend(y, …).fit == H @ y). M5-05 detrends log2-abundance residuals along gene index and M5-06 detrends Blom scores along TU order, both with span 10 % and circular padding on circular replicons, so both use this one helper.

  • Estimator. Plain local-linear LOESS: at each point a weighted least-squares line over its k nearest neighbours by pos, tricube weights (1 − (d/radius)³)³ with radius the distance to the farthest neighbour, and no robustness iterations (it = 0, lead decision 2). Robust reweighting would treat an island as an outlier and keep it out of the trend, so the detrend would depend on the signal being tested and the calibration would have to cover that data-adaptive step. Plain LOESS is linear in y: one matrix per set of positions, so ADR-0020 can apply it to B permuted replicates. The implementation reproduces statsmodels.nonparametric.smoothers_lowess.lowess(y, pos, frac=k/N, it=0, delta=0) operation for operation (≤ 1e-10; neighbourhood ties keep the window on the left, fewer than two weights above 1e-12 give fit = y, weighted variance of x floored at 1e-12).
  • Span in points. k = min(n, max(3, ⌈frac·n − 1e-9⌉)) (the 1e-9 keeps 0.1·30 at 3). pos are gene indices or TU ordinals, never base pairs; gaps are allowed and respected by the neighbour search. ADR-0020 passes ordinals 0 … n − 1 among the genes with values.
  • Circular padding. On a circular replicon the last k points are copied in front at pos − period and the first k behind at pos + period; the fit at the original points is kept and the padded copies feed back into their original columns of H. This removes the end effect (a cosine over 100 points, span 10: max residual 0.0071 circular vs 0.0098 linear, the latter at the ends) and makes the fit equivariant under rotation of the origin.
  • Small n. n = 0 gives an empty fit (k = 0). For 1 ≤ n < 3 no local line exists and the fit is mean(y) (residuals centred, k = n).
  • The 3-point floor is degenerate (lead decision 4). With k = 3 the farthest neighbour sits at the radius and gets weight 0, and the line through the remaining two points (one is the point itself) returns y: fit = y and every residual is 0, for any strictly increasing positions. At the 10 % span this covers n ≤ 30 values. The detrended series does not exist there, so M5-05 and M5-06 report NA with flag few_values for any replicon whose k < 4 instead of computing statistics over zero residuals. Power by replicon size is recorded in M5-07.

docs.title: Index and lags
docs.text:
Each replicon is a series of genes in gene-index order. Gene i and gene j form a lag-k pair when:

  • circular replicon: j = (i + k) mod n, for i = 0 … n − 1. The lag must satisfy 1 ≤ k ≤ ⌊(n − 1)/2⌋. A larger k would count each pair twice (k and n − k give the same pairs) or pair a gene with itself.
  • linear contig: j = i + k, with i + k < n. The lag must satisfy 1 ≤ k ≤ n − 1.

A statistic at an invalid lag does not exist and is NaN.

docs.title: Moran's I at lag k
docs.text:
Only genes with a value count. With n such genes, x̄ is the mean of their values and z_i = x_i − x̄. W_k is the number of lag-k pairs in which both genes have a value.

I_k = ((1/W_k) Σ_{pairs} z_i z_j) / ((1/n) Σ_i z_i²)

I_k does not exist (NaN) when:

  • the lag is invalid;
  • n < 2;
  • W_k = 0;
  • Σ z² ≤ 1e-24 · max(1, max x²), meaning there is no variance up to rounding.

Example: the alternating series +1, −1, … gives I_1 = −1 and I_2 = +1 (Appendix B.4).

  • I_k is invariant to affine maps x → a·x + b with a ≠ 0.
  • I_k is not bounded by [−1, 1] in small samples: the numerator averages over W_k pairs while the denominator averages over n genes.

docs.title: Join count: raw value and Pearson residual test statistic
docs.text:
Raw count. d_i marks whether eligible gene i is detected. The raw count is BB_k, the number of lag-k pairs in which both genes are detected. The table reports it as value.

Test statistic. The test does not use BB_k, because detection clusters for reasons other than expression: §8.2 requires detection tests to adjust for detectability. The test uses the Pearson residual (ADR-0020 Amendment 1, lead decision 17):

r_i = (d_i − p_i) / √(p_i (1 − p_i)),       S_k = Σ_{lag-k pairs} r_i r_j
  • p is the cross-fitted p_detect, unclipped.
  • A gene with p ∈ {0, 1}, with p NaN, or with d missing counts as missing: it has no residual (r = 0), so it joins no pair.
  • A non-NaN p outside [0, 1] can only come from an upstream bug, so join_count and join_count_matrix raise ValueError rather than drop the gene silently (decision 21).
  • A valid lag with no pair left gives S_k = 0.
  • effect = S_k − its null mean.

Assumption. The test is valid when the d_i are independent Bernoulli(p_i) given a calibrated p. It is therefore conditional on the cross-fitted p_detect being calibrated (M3 calibration). If p_detect is biased in a region (e.g. too low in an island), r has a non-zero mean there, and the test reports that miscalibration as detection clustering. A rejection means "clustering beyond the detectability model" (decision 22).

Why the earlier statistic was replaced. ADR-0020 decision 3 first used the raw residual Σ (d_i − p_i)(d_j − p_j). Its variance is Σ v_i v_j with v = p(1 − p). The permutation null averages v over random pairs, so when low p_detect clusters along the replicon, the null is too narrow and the test rejects too often. The statistician's attack set this up on a circular replicon of 1,000 genes: 30-gene islands with p ~ U(0.01, 0.05) among genes with p ~ U(0.3, 0.9), α = 0.05 (Slurm 1861073, 1861078). Rejection rates under both nulls:

Island share 10 % 20 % 30 % 50 % raw residual 0.059 0.074 0.086 0.105

Pearson residual results. Dividing by √(p(1 − p)) gives every gene unit variance under the null. - Level is 0.045–0.056 in every scenario above and in the original ADR-0020 attacks. - Power costs about 10 %. - At very small p (0.001–0.005), α = 0.01 gives a rejection rate of 0.019. This is recorded, not gated. - A floor on p in the denominator was rejected because it brings the clustering failure back.

The engine attack file tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_autocorr_engine.py gates the low-p island arms. It also has an arm that must fail (raw residual, 50 % islands), which shows the gate can detect the failure.

docs.title: The two nulls (B permutations each)
docs.text:
Gene-label null (label_permutations) asks whether there is any structure. - Values are shuffled uniformly among the replicon's genes that have values (movable). Genes without a value stay where they are, so the pattern of missing values is fixed and W_k does not change. - For the join count, p moves together with d.

TU-block null (tu_block_permutations) asks whether there is structure beyond operons. - A block is a maximal run of consecutive genes with the same TU label. On a circular replicon, a run at the end and a run at the start with the same label form one block (a TU that crosses the origin). - A TU interrupted by another TU's gene forms several blocks. - Whole blocks are placed in a uniformly random order. Each block keeps its internal order and orientation; a wrapped block is emitted as its end part followed by its start part. - Values, gaps and p move with their TU. - Under this null, within-TU correlation is part of the null, so only structure between TUs counts as a signal.

docs.title: p-value, the constant-null rule and the null summaries
docs.text:
lag_test(obs, null) drops NaN null entries; n_valid counts the rest, including ±inf (decision 13).

p-value. p = perm_p(obs, null, "two-sided"). It is centred on the pooled mean of the observation and the null and uses the +1 rule, so it is exactly valid under exchangeability (docs/methods/permutation-and-shifts.md).

Constant-null rule (decisions 6 and 14). If the null is constant, p is NA and the row is flagged not_estimable. - "Constant" means the spread of a null of finite values is ≤ 1e-12 · max(1, max |v|), which is perm_p's tie scale. A null whose entries are all the same inf is also constant. - This applies even when the observation differs from the constant null. The observed arrangement is always in the permutation support (the identity, or a rotation for the circular statistics), so a constant sampled null with a different observation arises only by chance from a sparse null. The +1-rule p, 1/(B + 1), would then be valid, but GIAP reports NA (decisions 20 and 22). - The rule is conservative: it never adds a rejection. A p of 1 from a degenerate null would make BH more conservative, not inflate the FDR. Reporting NA avoids enlarging the BH family (m) without adding information. - Examples of degenerate nulls: - a replicon that is one TU (the TU-block null is the identity); - a circular replicon with two TU blocks (both block orders are rotations of each other, and both statistics are invariant to rotation); - all genes detected or none detected, with every p equal.

Null summaries. The table reports: - null_mean, the mean of the valid null; - null_lo and null_hi, its linear 2.5 % and 97.5 % quantiles.

For a constant null all three equal the constant. If the observation is NaN or no null value is valid, every field except value and n_valid is NaN.

V10 envelope. The envelope in V10 plots these quantiles. Two points about it: - It is pointwise: each lag has its own 95 % band, not a simultaneous band over the 20 lags. - It is on the statistic's scale: I_k for Moran's I and the Pearson statistic S_k for the join count, not the raw count BB_k.

Lag statistics get no confidence interval (ADR-0020 decision 4, flag ci_unestimated).

docs.title: Block length
docs.text:
choose_block_len implements ℓ̂ from §7.3.5(d) step 5: - The Moran's I of the TU scores is tested at lags k = 1 … min(20, max_lag) under B gene-label permutations. One permutation matrix is shared by all lags, so the draws depend only on B and n. - ℓ̂ is the first lag whose raw two-sided p is above 0.05 or NaN. This is a stopping rule, not a reported test, so the p is not BH-adjusted. - If every lag is significant, ℓ̂ = min(20, max_lag + 1, n). With n < 3, ℓ̂ = 1.

The block length that callers actually use is ℓ' = block_len_prime(ℓ̂, T) = min(20, 2ℓ̂ + 1, T) (ADR-0021); see docs/methods/bootstrap.md "Block length".

docs.title: Statistician sign-off
docs.text: Signed off by the statistician (PR #116 re-review). The review covered "Statistics and nulls" and the Pearson residual implementation, after ADR-0020 Amendment 1 and lead decisions 17–22.

docs.title: TU-block bootstrap, circular block bootstrap and the Hodges–Lehmann shift
docs.text: Implements giap.stats.bootstrap (tu_block_bootstrap, percentile_ci, circular_block_bootstrap) and giap.stats.robust.hodges_lehmann (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.5(a)–(b), §8.2, §8.3, decision 14; issue M4-04). Statistician sign-off: see the end of this note.

docs.title: Why the resampling unit is the TU
docs.text:
Genes in one transcription unit share a promoter, a transcript and most of their regulation, so their abundances, detection indicators and O − E contributions are positively correlated. With an intra-TU correlation ρ and TUs of size m, the variance of a gene-level mean is inflated by the design effect 1 + (m − 1)ρ relative to iid genes. A bootstrap that resamples genes treats them as independent and estimates the iid variance, so its CI is too narrow by √(1 + (m − 1)ρ). TUs, not genes, are the units that are (approximately) independent, so §8.2 rules "resample TUs, not genes".

tu_block_bootstrap(df, tu_col, stat_fn, B, rng, level, strata_col):

  • each replicate draws, uniformly with replacement, as many TU IDs as there are TUs, and concatenates the drawn TUs' rows whole (a TU drawn twice contributes all its rows twice; a TU is never split; row order inside a TU is kept). TU sizes vary, so the replicate gene count varies; stat_fn must therefore be a statistic of the rows (sum, mean, HL, O − E), not of a fixed n;
  • stratified two-group statistics (strata_col): TUs are drawn within each stratum, as many as the stratum has, so every replicate keeps the inside/outside TU counts. This is what §7.3.5(b) asks for the HL shift ("resample the region's TUs and, for the HL shift, the outside TUs too"): both groups carry sampling error, and pooling them would let the region's size drift. A TU's stratum is the stratum of its first row; callers must not let a TU straddle a region boundary (M4-17 must assign each TU wholly to one side before calling);
  • NaN replicate statistics are dropped; with fewer than B/2 valid replicates the CI is (NaN, NaN) and n_valid says why. stat_fn errors propagate.

Randomness: the caller passes the Generator from giap.rng.for_step (§6.6); draws are made per stratum in sorted stratum order, each a (B × n_s) block, so results are reproducible given the seed.

Assumption: TUs are independent (or weakly dependent). Long-range dependence along the replicon (gene dosage, replichore gradients) is handled by the circular shift null for p-values (see permutation-and-shifts.md) and by detrending; the bootstrap CI is for the effect size only.

docs.title: CI method: percentile
docs.text:
Spec §8.3 fixes the percentile CI: np.quantile(boot, [(1 − level)/2, (1 + level)/2], method="linear"). Not BCa, not basic. Properties:

  • transformation-respecting and always inside the range of the statistic (useful for bounded statistics such as fractions);

  • first-order accurate only; it inherits the bootstrap's small-sample bias. For a mean of n independent units the bootstrap variance is (n − 1)/n of the plug-in variance and the true pivot is t_{n−1}, not z, so the expected coverage is

    c(n) = P(|t_{n−1}| ≤ z_{0.975} √((n − 1)/n)): n = 5: 0.846 10: 0.904 12: 0.913 20: 0.929 30: 0.936 100: 0.948.

Percentile CIs from fewer than ~20 TUs under-cover. Downstream modules (M4-17 region tests) must report n_tu with every CI and flag CIs from < 10 TUs (ci_few_units); they are not to be read as 95 % intervals. BCa or a studentised bootstrap would reduce the deficit and is a later improvement (spec M4-04 lead question 1), not required for M4. - Monte Carlo error: with B = 1000 each endpoint rests on ~25 tail replicates; the endpoint's MC SD is about 0.085 bootstrap SDs, enough for reporting. --publication uses B = 10000 (§5.1, stats.bootstrap), cutting it by √10. B = 1000 is the default (decision 14).

docs.title: Recorded coverage (fixed seeds; tests/calibration)
docs.text:
Scenario TUs statistic coverage c(n) test_stats_bootstrap_calibration (gated) 100, 1–4 genes, TU effect + noise sum in band 0.948 attack few_large_tus (gated, R = 100) 30, 5–15 genes, ρ = 0.9 mean ≥ bound 0.936 same data, gene-level resampling (teeth) 300 genes mean 0.44 — attack hl_two_group (gated) 12 in + 80 out, 2–6 genes, ρ = 0.8 HL ≥ bound 0.913 exploratory, R = 400 12 in + 80 out, ρ = 0.8 HL 0.925 0.913 exploratory, R = 400 30 in + 80 out, ρ = 0.8 / ρ = 0 HL 0.945 / 0.945 0.936 recorded, R = 200 5 / 10 TUs, ρ = 0.9 mean 0.86 / 0.89 0.846 / 0.904

The TU-block CI tracks c(n); the gene-level bootstrap covers 44 % on the same data, which is why the TU is the resampling unit. The attacks gate coverage ≥ c(n) − 2√(c(n)(1 − c(n))/R) (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_bootstrap.py).

docs.title: Circular block bootstrap (Politis–Romano)
docs.text: circular_block_bootstrap(x, block_len, B, rng) returns a (B × n) array: per replicate, ⌈n/ℓ⌉ start positions uniform on [0, n), each block ℓ consecutive values wrapping modulo n, concatenated and truncated to n. Wrapping makes every position equally likely to be sampled (unlike the moving-block bootstrap, which under-samples the ends), which matches a circular replicon. For a linear contig the wrap joins the two ends; with ℓ ≪ n the induced artefact is O(ℓ/n) and is accepted (spec uses the same function for both).

docs.title: Block length
docs.text:
The caller chooses the block length; this function does not. The island circular block bootstrap (§7.3.5(d) step 5) and the ori–ter slope CI (§7.3.5(e)) use the same rule, from ADR-0021:

  1. ℓ̂ = giap.stats.autocorr.choose_block_len(z, circular, B, rng): the smallest lag at which the TU-level Moran's I is not significant (raw two-sided p > 0.05 under the gene-label null, bounded to [1, 20]). See docs/methods/autocorrelation.md "Block length".
  2. ℓ' = block_len_prime(ℓ̂, T) = min(20, 2ℓ̂ + 1, T), where T is the number of scored TUs. ℓ' is the block length actually used. An integer context.islands.block_len overrides it unchanged.

Why ℓ' and not ℓ̂. ℓ̂ marks where the correlation stops being detectable, not the block length that a window-sum maximum needs (ADR-0021). - With ℓ̂ as the block length, island FWER on a 4,500-gene chromosome is 0.205 / 0.26 / 0.27 at ρ 0.5 / 0.9 / 0.95, and the ori–ter CI covers only 0.88–0.93. - With ℓ', FWER is 0.003–0.040 and the ori–ter CI covers 0.943 at ρ 0.5 (R = 300, Slurm 1863166; the 0.96 first reported was an R = 50 fluctuation). Coverage runs 0.875–0.945 across cells and arms, so the interval is slightly narrow everywhere — see docs/methods/oriter.md.

Validity domain. ADR-0021 Amendment 1 supersedes the original "fewer than 1,000 scored TUs" rule and drops the uncalibrated flag: re-measurement at R = 1,000 showed the scored-TU count decides nothing on its own (400 TUs at ρ 0.5 give FWER 0.005; 1,000 TUs at ρ 0.9 give 0.095–0.208; 2,500 TUs at ρ 0.9 give 0.024). What matters is whether strong TU-level autocorrelation is resolved by Moran's I to a long enough lag: every breach has ℓ' ≤ 7, and censoring is what hides the correlation (the same ρ 0.9 replicon gives ℓ̂ = 9 and FWER 0.007 uncensored, ℓ̂ = 2 and 0.208 at 55 % detected). No per-replicon statistic certifies the domain, and selecting on one is adverse, so the run report carries ℓ̂, ℓ' and the lag-1 Moran's I per replicon instead of a flag. See docs/methods/islands.md, "The island step (M5-06)".

Joins between blocks. ℓ = 1 is the iid bootstrap. Blocks join independent stretches, so the bootstrap slightly under-represents dependence across block joins. With ℓ above the correlation length this bias is small; the M5 island calibration checks FWER with this null.

Signed off by the statistician (PR #116 re-review).

docs.title: Hodges–Lehmann shift
docs.text:
HL(x, y) = median{x_i − y_j : all i, j}, the two-sample location estimator paired with the Wilcoxon rank-sum test: it is the Δ that makes the rank-sum statistic of x − Δ vs y central. Robust (breakdown ~29 %), invariant under common shifts, HL(x + c, y) = HL(x, y) + c and HL(y, x) = −HL(x, y).

  • Ties: all m·n differences count with multiplicity; tied values give tied differences and need no correction for the point estimate. Even m·n: mean of the two middle order statistics.
  • Missing: NaN raises (callers drop undetected genes first, §7.3.5(b) uses detected genes only). Empty sample → NaN.
  • CI: no analytic (Moses/Wilcoxon-inversion) CI is used, because genes are not independent; the CI comes from the stratified TU-block bootstrap above.
  • Exact computation: direct enumeration (np.median(np.subtract.outer(x, y))) for m·n ≤ 5 × 10⁴; above, bisection on Δ counting pairs with x_i − y_j ≤ Δ by binary search on sorted y, then a partition of the few remaining candidates. Float subtraction is monotone, so the counts use the very same float differences as enumeration and the result is bit-identical to it. The spec's threshold is 10⁶; 5 × 10⁴ was verified by the statistician (below) and is ~6× faster at the M4-17 size (m = 200, n = 4500: 2.0 ms vs 12.4 ms).
  • Non-finite values (NaN, ±inf from log2(0)) raise ValueError on both paths. Differences that overflow float64 fall back to enumeration up to m·n = 2 × 10⁷, else raise.

docs.title: Statistician sign-off (M4-04, PR #31)
docs.text:
Verified on branch m4/bootstrap (commit 75d7a92; re-verified at 5850e09). APPROVED.

  1. Bisection HL vs np.median(np.subtract.outer) with the threshold forced to 0: 297 cases (sizes 1×1 … 1000×999; normal, integer ties, decimal ties, 70 % one-value ties, Cauchy × 10⁶, 1e-300 scale, ±0.0) — all bit-identical. At the 5 × 10⁴ boundary (200×250, 250×201, 1×50001, 50001×1, 2×25001, 224², 225×223) and 2000×3000, 200×4500: 66 cases, all identical. The 5 × 10⁴ deviation is acceptable; the spec text should read 5 × 10⁴.
  2. Defect (blocking): non-finite inputs on the bisection path. x containing +inf (300×600): bisection 2.0 → inf vs enumeration 1.5; x containing −inf: 2.0 vs 0.5; differences that overflow (|values| ~ 1e308) or inf on both sides: infinite loop (mid = NaN, lo/hi never move). The direct path is fine. Fix: raise ValueError on non-finite input (like NaN), and fall back to enumeration (or raise) when x.min() − y.max() or x.max() − y.min() is not finite; add a regression test above the threshold. Resolved in 5850e09: all four reproducers now raise or match enumeration (overflow 400×400 → 0.0 = enumeration; 2.5 × 10⁷ overflowing pairs → ValueError). Exactness re-run: 264 forced-bisection cases + 10 × (200×4500) all equal; 200×4500 takes 1.9 ms vs 12.2 ms by enumeration. Nit (not blocking): with only ±0.0 inputs the result can be −0.0 where np.median gives 0.0 (equal as numbers; "bit-identical" holds up to the sign of zero).
  3. TU blocks: never split, internal order kept, stratum counts preserved (code + property tests); circular blocks wrap modulo n; RNG only from the caller's Generator. Correct.
  4. Small-TU bias of the percentile CI: tracks c(n), documented above; callers flag < 10 TUs.

docs.title: Calibration harness: criteria, error rates, seeds
docs.text: Implements tests/calibration/_criteria.py and the nightly job array (GIAP_SPEC.md §8.4, §8.5, §11.2, §12; issue M4-05). Constants come only from the protected tests/calibration/tolerances.yaml (levels = {0.01, 0.05, 0.10}, se_multiplier k = 2, ks_min_p = 0.001, seeds.calibration_base, replicates_fast, replicates_full). Statistician sign-off: see the end of this note.

docs.title: What R means
docs.text: R is the number of independent null (or truth) replicates: replicate i of a stream is a fresh simulated data set with its own generator, and the method is run once on it. Each criterion is a statement about R i.i.d. Bernoulli or bounded variables, so the SE formulas below are valid only if replicates do not share draws (see Seeds). Units within a replicate (genes, regions) are not replicates: a suite that pools p-values from many regions of one genome must either keep one p per replicate or use a criterion that accounts for within-replicate dependence.

docs.title: The four criteria (all one-sided: conservative is allowed, anti-conservative is not)
docs.text:
Criterion Statistic Passes when SE Level r̂ = #{p ≤ α}/R r̂ ≤ α + k·√(α(1−α)/R) nominal binomial SE at the null rate α Uniformity KS p-value of the R p-values vs U(0, 1) KS p > 0.001 none (exact KS) FDR mean FDP over R mean ≤ q + k·sd(FDP; ddof 1)/√R sample SE of the mean FWER share of replicates with ≥ 1 false discovery share ≤ α + k·√(α(1−α)/R), α = 0.05 nominal binomial SE
  • Level uses p ≤ α (inclusive), which is the definition of a valid p-value (P(p ≤ α) ≤ α). The SE is evaluated at the nominal α, not at r̂, so a method that never rejects is not rewarded with a tighter bound.
  • Uniformity is for continuous p only. Discrete p (permutation p = (1 + #{T* ≥ T})/(B + 1), Besag–Clifford p) have atoms, and KS against U(0, 1) rejects them for large R even when they are exactly valid. The harness refuses check_uniform when more than 5 % of values are repeated (1 − #unique/R > 0.05) and such p-values use the level check only (§8.4). Permutation p with α(B + 1) an integer (B = 199: 2, 10, 20 for the three levels) hits α exactly, so their level checks sit on the boundary and have the full false-alarm rate below.
  • FDR uses the sample SD because FDP has no known variance. When every FDP is 0, SE = 0 and the bound is q itself (the run passes, correctly). FDP is skewed (an atom at 0 at small q), so the normal approximation behind "q + 2 SE" is rough at small R·q; the Bernoulli-FDP worst case is computed exactly below.
  • FWER reuses the level bound with α = 0.05 (the spec's "0.05 + 2 SE"; the nominal binomial SE).

Inputs (fail closed). Empty inputs raise. check_level, check_uniform, check_fwer and check_fdr raise ValueError on any non-finite value or value outside [0, 1]. check_fwer accepts only 0/1 outcomes, and check_fdr requires R ≥ 2, since SE(FDP) is undefined for R = 1.

docs.title: False-alarm rate of each check (procedure exactly at level)
docs.text:
Exact binomial P(fail) for a level/FWER check when the true rejection rate equals α, and power when it is 1.5 α (k = 2, bound floor-ed to an integer count):

R α = 0.01: false alarm / power α = 0.05 α = 0.10 20 0.017 / 0.04 0.076 / 0.19 0.043 / 0.17 50 0.089 / 0.17 0.038 / 0.17 0.025 / 0.21 100 0.079 / 0.19 0.028 / 0.22 0.021 / 0.33 300 0.033 / 0.17 0.029 / 0.49 0.025 / 0.76 500 0.031 / 0.22 0.030 / 0.69 0.025 / 0.93 1,000 0.026 / 0.34 0.028 / 0.92 0.028 / 0.998

The nominal one-sided normal rate of "mean > α + 2 SE" is 0.023; discreteness pushes it to 0.026–0.09. The worst cells are α = 0.01 at R = 50/100 (fail iff ≥ 2 resp. ≥ 3 rejections; 8–9 % false alarms, < 20 % power): the fast α = 0.01 check is mostly noise and should be read as a smoke test only.

FDR check, exact for Bernoulli FDP (global null, FDP ∈ {0, 1}, the most skewed case): false alarm 0.0001 / 0.003 / 0.009 at R = 50 and q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10, and 0.004 / 0.009 / 0.011 at R = 300. For realistic FDP (BH, m = 1,000, π₀ = 0.9, Beta(0.1, 1) alternatives, oracle level q/π₀ so FDR = q exactly) simulation gives 0.01–0.07 per q at R = 50–300.

Validity of the seeding (below) was checked empirically: 400 independent streams of R = 1,000 exact U(0, 1) p-values failed the level check at rates 0.018 / 0.013 / 0.025 (theory 0.026 / 0.028 / 0.028), and the pooled 400,000 draws pass KS (p = 0.83).

docs.title: Family-wise false-alarm rate per nightly run
docs.text:
A nightly run has roughly 46 checks once all suites exist (6 level suites × 3 α, regions and autocorrelation with several test types, 3 engine level streams, 5 FDR streams × 3 q, 1 FWER). If every method sat exactly at level and checks were independent, P(≥ 1 red) ≈ 1 − ∏(1 − fᵢ) ≈ 0.75. Checks of one stream at three α are positively correlated and most methods are conservative (BH has FDR = π₀q), so the real rate is lower, but permutation and shift tests are exact-level and alone contribute ≈ 20–40 %.

A single-block gate with these numbers would not be acceptable. Seeds are fixed, so an unchanged tree gives the same verdict every night. The false alarm appears when a PR changes how a method consumes randomness and a correct method lands in the 2–3 % tail. The attack stream regions.attack_harness_valid did exactly that: 122/1,000 U(0, 1) p ≤ 0.10, P = 0.013. Seed-shopping to make such a check green is forbidden.

docs.title: Two-block confirmation (ADR-0015, accepted)
docs.text:
calibrate() runs a check on replicates 0 … R − 1 (block 1). If the check fails there, it is re-run on the disjoint, deterministic block R … 2R − 1 of the same stream (block 2). The gate fails only if both blocks fail; a block-1 failure that block 2 does not repeat is logged unconfirmed (shown in the summary, not red). Records carry block and status (pass | unconfirmed | fail). The two blocks are independent, so:

  • per-check confirmed false alarm = f² ≤ 0.0081 (worst cell α = 0.01, R = 50), ≈ 0.0008 at R = 1,000;
  • confirmed family-wise false-alarm rate per nightly run ≈ 0.04 (46 checks all exactly at level, independence; lower in practice), against ≈ 0.75 for a single block;
  • power of a confirmed fail = (single-block power)²: against 1.5 α at R = 1,000 it is 0.85 (α = 0.05) and 0.996 (α = 0.10); against 1.5 q FDR with realistic BH FDP it is 0.36 (q = 0.01) / 1.0 at fast R = 50 and 1.0 at full R = 300;
  • unconfirmed occurs at rate ≈ f (≈ 3 % of checks, about one or two per nightly run) and is informative: a method with persistent unconfirmed checks on the same stream deserves a look.

Empirical check (attack test_two_block_confirmed_false_alarm_matches_theory): 200 streams × 3 α of exact U(0, 1) p at R = 1,000 gave 0 confirmed fail in 600 checks (expected 0.5) and 24 unconfirmed (5 / 8 / 11 at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10; expected ≈ 5–6 each, within the 99.9 % binomial band). Oracle BH at FDR = 1.5 q is a confirmed fail at every q, fast and full.

Sharded runs. --shard K/N (N up to 10) sets GIAP_CALIBRATION_REPLICATES=start:stop@K/N. calibrate() then runs shard_replicates(R, N, K) of every check's own R, so a check whose R is not the suite's R is sharded too. It runs that range of block 1 and logs a shard record with the per-replicate values; an empty range (R < N) logs nothing. --merge puts the full R back together (refusing gaps or conflicting duplicates), evaluates block 1, and runs block 2 itself for every failing check. It never reports fail from block 1 alone. The merged verdict, the deciding block and the pooled rate equal the unsharded ones. This is tested with Hypothesis for N ≤ 10, and end to end on a fixture suite with 3 shards + --merge (test_criteria_shard_equivalence.py). A shard audit of all 15 fast-tier suites found the same check set and the same records sharded and unsharded.

Tests in a shard: - A test logs its checks and skips (skip_without_verdict, SHARD_SKIP). - Its direct parts run where owns_direct_checks() holds, which is unsharded or shard 0 of block 1. Direct parts are assertions or records over every replicate, fixed fits, and recorded quartiles. - tests/calibration/conftest.py applies this to whole tests: - a test with no harness check and no replicate_range runs in shard 0 only; - a teeth test (teeth_log) runs in shard 0 only; - a test marked calibration_unshardable runs whole and unsharded in shard 0, and its full records reach --merge; - a direct test over replicate_range (G2, A6a) checks its own range in every shard. - An xfail test cannot XPASS on no-verdict records: the XPASS becomes a skip. - --merge judges each test with an xfail mark as pytest would (ADR-0057).

A suite without harness checks merges once every shard has logged its completion (<suite>.shards.jsonl). scripts/slurm/calibration_sharded.sh SUITE N [extra] submits the N shards and a dependent --merge job with one shared log directory.

Scope. ADR-0015 and sharding apply only to checks that go through calibrate(). Suites that still call run_replicates / check_* directly (today all suites, including the M4-05 engine tests) keep single-block semantics until they are migrated (M4-05 lead decision 7, backlog). Until then the nightly family-wise false-alarm rate of those checks is the single-block figure above.

docs.title: Power to detect a 1.5× FDR inflation
docs.text:
For the FDR check, power ≈ Φ(0.5·q·√R / sd(FDP) − 2). With FDP sd from simulation (BH, m = 1,000, π₀ = 0.9: sd 0.014 / 0.029 / 0.038 at q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10):

R q = 0.01 q = 0.05 q = 0.10 fast, 50 0.6 1.0 1.0 full, 300 1.0 1.0 1.0

For the Bernoulli-FDP worst case (global null) power is far lower: 0.001 / 0.03 / 0.12 at R = 50 and 0.04 / 0.32 / 0.65 at R = 300. A suite whose null replicates make few discoveries (FDP mostly 0 or 1) cannot see a 1.5× inflation at q = 0.01 even at full R; such suites should plant enough true discoveries that each replicate calls tens of features, or report the per-replicate FDP histogram.

The attack tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_calibration_harness.py demonstrates both sides: oracle BH at FDR = q exactly passes, and at FDR = 1.5 q is flagged at every q, fast and full; the level check flags p = U/1.5 at α = 0.10 at full R; and exact-level p fail across 200 streams at the binomial false-alarm rate, not more.

docs.title: Seeds and independence
docs.text:
suite_seed(stream, rep) = SeedSequence([calibration_base, crc32(stream), rep]).generate_state(1, uint64), and replicate rep draws from default_rng(suite_seed(stream, rep)).

  • Independence. SeedSequence hashes its whole entropy list, so distinct (stream, rep) triples give statistically independent streams (NumPy's guarantee for distinct entropy). Folding to one uint64 and re-seeding loses nothing that matters: the chance that any two of N replicate seeds collide is ≈ N²/2⁶⁵ (< 10⁻¹² for N = 10⁴).
  • crc32. A 32-bit hash of the stream name; two names collide with probability 2⁻³², and a collision would make two streams draw identical data (not merely correlated). With n names the chance of any collision is ≈ n²/2³³ (< 10⁻⁶ for n = 100). The 23 names in use today (13 suites plus gene_fdr.*, regions.* streams) have distinct crc32. Test streams must have distinct names; two tests sharing a stream name share draws.
  • Sharding. The seed depends only on (stream, rep), never on the shard, so replicate i is the same data whether run alone or in a block, and shard_replicates(R, n, k) partitions 0 … R − 1 into contiguous blocks (tested). Criteria are only valid on the merged R replicates (--merge, above).
  • Fixed seeds (§8.4): calibration_base lives in the protected file; tests are deterministic.

docs.title: Suites and tolerances.yaml
docs.text: Array task i runs the i-th key of replicates_full (13 suites → --array=0-12); --fast uses replicates_fast. Engine tests reuse gene_fdr (BH) and regions (permutation, circular shift, Besag–Clifford), per M4-index lead decision 6. Each calibration test belongs to exactly one suite. The suite comes from a @pytest.mark.calsuite("<suite>") marker or from SUITE_REGISTRY in tests/calibration/conftest.py (keyed by function, then file). A test then gets the keyword calsuite_<suite>, and a unit test checks that every calibration test lands in exactly one array task.

docs.title: Review findings (M4-05, statistician)
docs.text:
First review (PR #54, BLOCK), all resolved at head 6fba049:

  1. check_level failed open on NaN and p > 1. Fixed: all checks fail closed. The attack tests test_level_check_fails_closed_on_nan and ..._out_of_range_p pass.
  2. --shard was inert. Fixed: shards are honoured; --merge evaluates the union and runs the confirmation block.
  3. check_fdr accepted R = 1 and FDP outside [0, 1]. Fixed.
  4. Suite tagging by source regex. Fixed: explicit marker or registry.
  5. Family-wise false alarms ≈ 0.75. Resolved by ADR-0015 (≈ 0.04 confirmed).

Open follow-up (not blocking this PR): migrate the existing suites to calibrate() (lead decision 7). Until then ADR-0015 protects only new suites.

docs.title: Sign-off
docs.text: Statistician, 2026-10-14 (M4-05 re-review at 6fba049): signed. The criteria, SE formulas, one-sidedness, k, discrete-p rule, fail-closed inputs, seed derivation, shard partition and merge, and ADR-0015 confirmation match §8.4, ADR-0015 and the M4-05 spec with lead decisions 1–7. The false-alarm and power numbers above are exact binomial or simulated as stated. The confirmed nightly family-wise false-alarm rate is ≈ 0.04 once suites run through calibrate().

docs.title: giap compare: detection, abundance agreement and result stability
docs.text: Implements giap.compare.{detection,abundance,stability} and giap.io.compare_io (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.9.3, §8.2, §8.3; issue M9-22; layout ADR-0046). Statistician sign-off: block B1 fixed (decision 11), 2026-10-22.

docs.title: Inputs and checks
docs.text: Two or more OUT/ trees on the same genome (genome SHA-256 from run_manifest.json, else preflight/preflight.json) with identical locus-tag sets. Labels are --labels or the directory basenames (repeats suffixed _2, _3).

docs.title: Detection
docs.text: A gene x run matrix of detected / detection_status (genes in §6.5 order of the first run) and the exact intersections of the detected sets: a gene detected in exactly A1 and A3 counts in A1&A3 only, as an UpSet plot draws it; none holds the genes detected in no run.

docs.title: Abundance agreement
docs.text:
Per unordered pair, shared genes are those detected with a measured (abundance_imputed = false) log2 abundance in both runs.

  • Spearman ρ with average ranks for ties (equal to scipy.stats.spearmanr); NA for a constant side.
  • CI: the 95 % percentile CI of tu_block_bootstrap with B = stats.bootstrap resamples of the TUs of the pair's first run (a gene without a TU is its own unit), drawn from giap.rng.for_step("compare", seed). Genes of one TU share promoter and transcript, so their measurement errors in both runs are positively correlated; resampling genes would treat them as independent and give a CI too narrow by about the square root of the design effect (docs/methods/bootstrap.md). The calibration test's teeth arm (gene-level units) shows the under-coverage.
  • Bland–Altman on log2: bias = mean(a − b), limits = bias ± 1.96 SD(a − b), ddof = 1.

Flags: too_few_shared (< 3 shared genes: every statistic NA), ci_few_units (fewer than 10 resampling units, reported in n_units: the CI is kept from 2 units but is not a 95 % interval; below 2 it is NA), ci_unestimated (fewer than B/2 finite replicates), scale_differs (abundance_type or abundance_scale differ: the bias is not interpretable but is written), missing_in:<label> (a run without abundance: the row is NA).

docs.title: Stability
docs.text: Jaccard |A ∩ B| / |A ∪ B| of five sets per run: genes of islands with p_value ≤ stats.alpha.context; (gene_a, gene_b) of operon_flags with q_value ≤ stats.alpha.operon_flags; (table, collection, term, direction) of enrichment_detection and enrichment_gsea rows with q_value ≤ stats.alpha.enrichment (GSEA direction = sign of NES); called novel ORFs; (contig, codon_start, strand, alt_aa) of variants rows with call = ALT. Two empty sets give NA with both_empty; an absent table (or the function module off) gives NA with missing_in:<label>. Jaccard is descriptive: no test, no CI.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text: tests/calibration/test_compare_rho_ci.py (suite compare, R = 100 / 1,000 per ADR-0042): coverage of the ρ CI on simulated TU-correlated pairs (gated, anti-conservative side), recorded coverage, width and bias, and the gene-level teeth arm.

docs.title: The context tables: autocorrelation.tsv, islands.tsv and the genes.tsv context group
docs.text: Issue M5-09 (docs/specs/M5-09-context-tables-step.md, lead decisions 1–5). Spec sections §6.2 (the context_stats step), §9.2 (table conventions and test columns), §9.3 (the two column dictionaries), §9.4 (the flag vocabulary), §9.5 (Frictionless resources), §6.5 (coordinates) and §6.6 / R7 (determinism).

docs.title: Where each row comes from
docs.text:
Table Rows Producer tables/autocorrelation.tsv Moran's I and join counts per replicon, lag and null giap.context.autocorrelation.autocorrelation_rows (M5-05) the pooled / right / left ori–ter slopes per circular chromosome giap.context.oriter.oriter_rows (M5-08) tables/islands.tsv one row per merged significant window giap.context.islands.islands_frame (M5-06) work/context/gene_context.parquet island_id, replichore, replichore_position per gene gene_island_map + gene_replichores work/context/island_diagnostics.parquet l-hat, l′ and the lag-1 Moran's I per replicon giap.context.diagnostics.island_diagnostics

giap.context.tables only concatenates and sorts: autocorrelation by contig (C1 order), statistic and null_model in §9.3 enum order, lag (NA last) and stat; islands by contig, start, end and the ISL_<n> number. Both sorts are stable, so rows that tie keep the order their producer gave them, and no island is renumbered.

giap.context.oriter emits lag as the schema's nullable Int64 rather than float64, so the concatenation of the two row sources keeps integer lags (1, not 1.0) in the written table.

docs.title: stat is a name, in all three tables
docs.text: §9.2 defines the test column stat as an enum of statistic names (enum{o_minus_e, hl_shift} for regions_stats), and autocorrelation follows it (morans_i, join_count_bb, oriter_slope_pooled, …). M5-06 originally shipped islands' stat as a float equal to scan_s, which both broke the convention and duplicated a column the same row already carries; M5-09 lead decision 6 fixed it, so islands' stat is the string "scan_max" (giap.context.islands.STAT) and scan_s keeps the value. A generic reader of the three test tables can therefore treat stat as a string everywhere.

docs.title: Random streams (§6.6)
docs.text: context_stats.autocorrelation, context_stats.islands and context_stats.oriter, each from giap.rng.for_step(..., cfg.seed). The island stream is shared by scan_replicons and then islands_frame, in that order. The M4 parts keep their own streams, so changing an M5-only knob (the detrend span, the block length, the presence of an oriC) leaves regions_stats.tsv and detection_summary.tsv byte-identical.

docs.title: Writer conventions
docs.text:
giap.io.context_tsv hands cells to M1-04 write_tsv by value: %.6g for floats, integers as integers, NA for missing (including a row with no flag), ; for the flags and genes lists. Nothing is coerced to its schema type on the way out, so a frame that violates the schema is written as it stands and caught by frictionless validate rather than silently rewritten. Only start is converted, to 1-based; end is unchanged, because a half-open 0-based end equals a closed 1-based end, and an island that crosses the origin therefore keeps end > length (§6.5). An empty frame writes the header line only.

The readers are the inverses and type each column from the shipped schema: integer → pandas nullable Int64, number → float64, string → object of str, and the list cells → tuples of str.

flags is checked against giap.context.vocab.CONTEXT_FLAGS (§9.4 is closed) and an unknown flag raises ValueError naming it. Note that pandas.Series.flags shadows the flags column: a writer reaching for row.flags on an iterrows row gets a Flags object, so every access is by name or by position.

docs.title: The island diagnostics, and why 0 is not a value
docs.text:
