ADR-0021 Amendment 1 (decision 2a) and M5-06 decision 48 dropped the uncalibrated flag: no per-replicon statistic certifies the validity domain, so a flag would be false reassurance. Instead the run must report, per replicon, the block-length estimate l-hat, the bootstrap block length l′ and the lag-1 Moran's I of the detrended TU scores. IslandScan carries them, but it dies with the step, so context_stats persists them as work/context/island_diagnostics.parquet; the §9.4 run report will consume that file rather than recompute (lead decision 1).

IslandScan.l_hat is 0 in two different situations — the replicon was not scanned, and context.islands.block_len fixed the block length so l-hat was never estimated — and IslandScan.block_len is 0 when the replicon was not scanned. Printed as a number, l-hat = 0 reads "no autocorrelation", which is precisely the false reassurance Amendment 1 refuses. The persisted table therefore carries NA, never 0, render_l_hat prints a sentence that never contains the character 0, and block_rule keeps the two reasons apart:

block_rule l-hat l′ lag-1 Moran's I flags calibration auto ≥ 1 ≥ 1 finite none applies fixed NA the configured value finite none does not apply not_scanned NA NA NaN few_values does not apply

calibration_applies is True only for auto: Amendment 1's FWER evidence is conditional on ADR-0021 decision 1's rule l′ = min(20, 2·l-hat + 1, T), so a run with an overridden block_len is outside the regime the calibration covers — as the M5-09 island fixture deliberately is (lead decision 5).

docs.title: genes.tsv
docs.text: context_stats writes tables/genes.tsv with gene_context left-joined on locus_tag (lead decision 3): it is the last M4/M5 step and the only one holding both the gene table and the three context columns, so one write with the join already applied beats writing the file early and patching it. A run that skips context_stats (no C7/C8) therefore produces no genes.tsv; that is recorded in docs/backlog.md and resolved when §6.2's finalize step takes the file over.

docs.title: M7-17 G4-k3 flag gate, full tier: statistician's verdict (PR #291, ebfdd065)
docs.text: Verdict (b): a test-and-generator defect, not a method failure. The flag follows its rule on every reached row. The two unflagged "intergenic" rows are not false intergenic ORFs. They are planted true antisense ORFs whose stop the injector reused. The pooled 300 records can be rescored. No rerun is needed.

docs.title: What failed
docs.text: _check(True) failed at its last line, per_class["intergenic"]["flagged"] == ["reached"], with 467 of 469. summarise bins rows by the injected class. Rule 4, and the test's own violation check, use the row's TSV (observed) class.

docs.title: Class confusion in the 300 records (Slurm 1881039 for replicates 0–187, 1886178–87 for 188–299)
docs.text:
• Rows at injected keys, by injected → observed class:
  • intergenic → intergenic: 5,972;
  • intergenic → antisense: 20;
  • intergenic → cds_outframe: 6;
  • cds_outframe and antisense: 6,000 each, all matched.
  • Of the 469 reached intergenic-injected rows, 443 are observed as intergenic, and all 443 are flagged. The other 26 are observed as antisense (20) or cds_outframe (6). 24 of them have no RBS support and are flagged. 2 have RBS support, so they are exempt (replicate 13, NOVEL_chr1_165770_m; replicate 253, NOVEL_chr1_791521_m).
  • Violations of the rule, both ways: 0 of 18,448 reached rows.

docs.title: Cause (diagnostics: Slurm 1886794, 1886826, 1886919; census: 1886842)
docs.text:
• Stop collision with a planted ORF: 25 of 26 rows, including both exempt rows.
  • inject_false_orfs takes stop-closed segments from the non-coding pool. The pool masks the codons of planted ORFs, but a segment upstream of a planted ORF's start, in its frame, ends at that ORF's stop. Its key is then the planted ORF's key.
  • Example, replicate 13: the row is truth NOVEL_0578 (antisense, 165770–165982 −). It has 8 peptides, all of them background reads of the true ORF.
  • Example, replicate 253: the row is truth NOVEL_0649 (antisense, stop 791521). The injected exact read LANMFWYK is placed intergenic at 791803–791826, upstream of the true start, and joins that ORF.
  • Census over all 300 replicates (simulation and injection only): 97 of 18,000 injected keys are planted truth keys. By injected class: intergenic 50 (25 at a true intergenic key, 19 at a true antisense key, 6 at a true cds_outframe key), cds_outframe 11, antisense 36. The per-replicate counts explain all 6 cds_outframe rows and 19 of the 20 antisense rows.
  • null_segments in the same harness already excludes truth keys and planted spans; inject_false_orfs does not.
  • Background wrong read joins the ORF: 1 of 26 (replicate 130, NOVEL_chr1_567837_p). A chance de novo read (PSSSLTK, score −4.05) is placed antisense over GSIM_02660 and shares the injected segment's stop. The row has no RBS support and is flagged.
  • Reclassification is correct behaviour. An ORF is every placement to one stop (§7.6.2, "Grouping"). Its class is the highest-priority member class (§7.2.6; CLASS_PRIORITY), and antisense and cds_outframe rank above intergenic. GIAP cannot see what was injected.

docs.title: Q1: injected or observed class?
docs.text:
• The spec defines the observed class:
  • rule 4 reads "the class";
  • the edge-case row class_mismatch says the flag reads "its TSV class";
  • criterion 6 exempts "a cds_outframe or antisense row".
  • "For intergenic this is every such row" follows from these only if the injected class equals the observed class. A stop collision breaks that assumption.
  • The test's docstring also uses the TSV class ("unless its TSV class is …"). Only the last assertion bins by injected class.

docs.title: Fix that keeps the gate's intent
docs.text:
1. Required. The last assertion counts rows whose observed class is intergenic, and requires all of them to be flagged.
  2. Why this is not a widening:
    • every reached row is still checked against rule 4 both ways, with zero tolerance;
    • R, q ≤ 0.05, the RBS threshold and the rule are unchanged;
    • the intergenic statement still has to hold exactly on every row GIAP calls intergenic.
  3. What it gives up: exempting an injected-intergenic row that GIAP calls antisense with chance RBS support. That is the antisense chance-RBS escape the methods note already documents ("intergenic and nterm_extension are never exempt" refers to the TSV class), and it stays recorded.
  4. The diagnostics should also record the injected → observed table above.
  5. Backlog; needs a rerun, not this PR. inject_false_orfs should skip segments at a planted truth key, as null_segments does, so that every injected key is a false ORF.
  6. This makes G4-k3 stricter, not looser: today 0.54 % of injections land on true ORFs and add no false ORF. It does not change the ADR-0050 conclusions.
  7. It changes the G4-k3 stream (rng draws), so the lead should list it for Khoa's batch.
  8. Do not exclude every segment whose span overlaps a CDS. That would narrow the intergenic attack territory, and the replicate-130 path is correct GIAP behaviour.

docs.title: Rescored, observed class, R = 300 (from the existing records; no rerun)
docs.text:
Class Reached Flagged Exempt Escape share intergenic 443 443 0 0 cds_outframe 5,993 5,667 326 0.054 antisense 6,012 5,637 375 0.062
  • With fix 1, the gate passes on the pooled records. The records store class, so rescoring is exact.
  • The escape shares stay below the 0.2 line of lead decision 1.
  • Under the injected class, the recorded escape shares are: intergenic 2/469 = 0.004, cds_outframe 326/5,987 = 0.054, antisense 373/5,992 = 0.062.
  • Scripts and logs: local/stat/m717-gate/ (diag2.py, census.py, census_*.jsonl, *.out).

docs.title: De novo precision, estimated from the genome
docs.text:
Implements giap.mapping.denovo_precision (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.2.5 "De novo precision, estimated from the genome" and step 4, §8.1, §8.4, §9.3, §9.4; issue M3-11; ADR-0010).

Status: signed off by the statistician (M3-11 review, 2026-10-14; see Sign-off).

docs.title: Estimand (ADR-0019 decision 5)
docs.text:
Status: signed off by the statistician (M3-25 review of #124, 2026-10-20; ADR-0019 decisions 1–5).

prec_b estimates the correct share among the distinct de novo peptides of GIAP score bin b. Two consequences of "distinct" and "GIAP's bins":

  • the unit is the distinct peptide string, after §5.3 collapses the rows of a peptide (score = max over its rows), not the spectrum or the read; a peptide is correct when its string (I = L) equals the true_peptide of at least one of the reads it was collapsed from;
  • the bins are GIAP's own score deciles over those aggregated scores (see Bins), not the bins or the design parameters of whatever produced the input.

Calibration therefore gates against that realised share, computed per bin from the truth table. giapsim's truth/denovo_precision.tsv is the per-read design precision of the error model — a different quantity, over another unit and other bins — and is not the target of these gates. The two drift apart whenever correct and wrong reads collapse into peptides at different rates (a correct peptide is usually read several times; a wrong one once), which is the ordinary case.

docs.title: Estimator
docs.text:
De novo peptides that enter mapping are split into score bins b and length classes l (M3-10 labels 7, 8, 9, 10-11, 12-14, 15-19, 20-40). Per bin and class:

  • m_bl: share matching the six-frame target translation exactly (I = L);
  • r_bl: share matching the shuffled decoy exactly;
  • c_l: share of reference peptides (--reference-peptides, targets with q ≤ 0.01) matching the target exactly. Without reference peptides c_l = 0.99 and every row carries c_assumed (also a run flag). With reference peptides, a class that has none gets c_l = NA.

A peptide is correct with probability p_bl; a correct one matches the target with probability c_l, a wrong one with the decoy-match probability r_bl. So m_bl = p c_l + (1 − p) r_bl, and

prec_b = Σ_l w_bl (m_bl − r_bl) / (c_l − r_bl),   clipped to [0, 1],

with w_bl the share of bin-b peptides in class l.

docs.title: Bins
docs.text: Deciles of score: edges np.quantile(scores, [0.1, …, 0.9]), right-closed; coinciding edges merge bins (tied scores share a bin). Peptides without a score get bin −1 and no row.

docs.title: Reportability
docs.text: The estimator is unstable when c_l − r_bl is small. A class with c_l − r_bl < 0.05 (or c_l = NA) is dropped from that bin and the remaining weights renormalised (c − r = 0.05 is kept). A bin with no class left has precision NA and flag unreported. c_value = Σ_l w_bl c_l over the classes used.

docs.title: Bootstrap
docs.text:
1,000 resamples of the bin's peptides with replacement (drawn as one multinomial over the class × target-match × decoy-match cells, which is the same distribution and is invariant to row order), c_l held fixed; the same reportability rule is applied to each resample. CI = 2.5 % and 97.5 % percentiles. RNG: giap.rng.for_step("placement", seed). A bin with n = 1 yields a degenerate CI and is reported (n is visible).

Equivalence. The estimator depends on a bin's rows only through the 4k cell counts (k classes), so one Multinomial(n, cell shares) draw has exactly the distribution of the cell counts of n rows drawn with replacement; the two bootstraps are identical, not approximately so. The class weights w_bl are resampled too (the bin's class mix is treated as random), which is right for a bin whose peptides were not stratified by class.

What it ignores (and the direction): - c_l's sampling error (held fixed). Matters only when a class has few reference peptides; an underestimate of c_l is anti-conservative (see Calibration and attacks, hard_reference). - Dependence between rows: nested or overlapping de novo peptides of one locus, or several candidates from one spectrum, share correctness and match status. Rows are treated as independent, so the CI is too narrow (per-bin lower-bound coverage ≈ 0.70–0.84 with runs of 5 dependent rows). - The bin edges are data-dependent quantiles and are held fixed. - Resamples that become unreportable (every class c_l − r_bl < 0.05) are dropped, so ci_low is taken over the reportable resamples only. Near the 0.05 boundary this conditions on a small denominator; counting such resamples as precision 0 would be the conservative choice (follow-up, not observed in calibration). - The percentile interval at the clip: when every row in a small bin matches the target, the point estimate is clipped to 1 and the bootstrap distribution is degenerate at 1, so ci_low = 1 and π̂ = 0. Per-bin coverage of the lower bound is therefore poor in small high-precision bins (P(1 − ci_low ≥ π) ≈ 0.75 / 0.64 at p = 0.98 / 0.99 with 50 peptides per bin, ≈ 0.5 with 20, versus 0.95–1.0 with 400).

docs.title: π̂ for M3-10
docs.text:
π̂_wrong (m = 0, de novo) = 1 − ci_low of the peptide's bin: the conservative bound (ADR-0010; a point-estimate π̂ that is too small breaks placement FDR). Unreported bins, bins without a row and unscored peptides get π̂ = 1.

Why the per-bin lower bound is enough. ADR-0010 needs W_m(e) = Σ π̂_j over decoy hits not to underestimate the expected number of wrong target hits. A per-bin undercoverage in a small, high-precision bin costs at most π_b per decoy hit from that bin (≤ 0.02 here), and the + c term (c = max π̂ over searched peptides, ≈ 1 whenever any bin has low precision or is unreported) adds a whole false hit; small lists accept nothing at q = 0.01. The attacks below confirm the placement FDR holds with 5 peptides per bin.

docs.title: Calibration and attacks
docs.text:
tests/calibration/test_denovo_precision_calibration.py: known p_b per bin, two classes; per-bin |bias| ≤ denovo_precision_max_abs_bias (0.05), 95 % CI coverage, and P(π̂ ≥ π) ≥ 0.975 within a binomial band. Genome-level validation with giapsim de novo errors is M3-21.

tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_denovo_precision.py (§8.5) feeds π̂ = 1 − ci_low into the ADR-0010 rule written out directly, FDR(e) = (Σ π̂ over decoy hits with E ≤ e + max π̂) / T(e), with the precision estimated from the same exact-match calls the placement uses. Ten bins with p = 0.30 … 0.99, chance rate r = 0.1. Mean FDP at q = .01 / .05 / .10, R = 300 (SE ≤ .0015):

Scenario FDP Gate oracle π (reference) .0098 / .032 / .032 – base, N = 4000 .0083 / .032 / .032 at level small_bins, 20 per bin .0033 / .025 / .032 at level tiny_bins, 5 per bin .0000 / .013 / .027 at level chance_by_bin (r 0.25 → 0.05 with p) .0084 / .043 / .064 at level clustered (runs of 5 dependent rows) .0085 / .033 / .033 at level easy_reference (c_ref .99 > c_true .90) .0064 / .033 / .035 at level (conservative) c_true_one (c_assumed .99, true 1.0) .0086 / .032 / .032 at level hard_reference (c_ref .85 < c_true .99) .0124 / .032 / .032 direction: anti-conservative near_correct_wrong (wrong hit target 2r) .0186 / .062 / .062 direction: fails with oracle π too (.0195 / .062)

Directions to remember: - Reference peptides easier than the de novo peptides (c_ref > c_true) bias precision DOWN and π̂ UP: conservative. The dangerous direction is reference peptides harder than correct de novo peptides (c_ref < c_true: the reference search covers variant or contaminant peptides, or a class has only a handful of reference peptides): precision is biased up by (c_true − r)/(c_ref − r) and π̂ is too low. A shortfall of 0.04 in c (.95 vs .99) stayed at level (.0094); 0.14 did not. - Wrong de novo peptides that match the target more often than the shuffled decoy (near-correct errors that hit a paralog or the true locus exactly) inflate m − r and break the placement FDR even with the true π: a decoy-model violation owned by M3-09/M3-10 and measured in M3-21.

docs.title: Assumptions and limits
docs.text:
• c_l from reference peptides transfers to de novo peptides of the same length class.
  • Wrong de novo peptides match the target no more often than the shuffled decoy (r_bl unbiased for the wrong-peptide target-match rate).
  • c_l's own sampling error is ignored in the CI (small with hundreds of reference peptides).
  • Rows are independent within a bin (see Bootstrap: dependence narrows the CI).

docs.title: Sign-off
docs.text: Statistician (M3-11 review, 2026-10-14): approved for giap.mapping.denovo_precision as implemented: the estimator is §7.2.5's (a de novo peptide counts as matching only on an exact target hit, I = L; r_bl from exact shuffled-decoy hits; c_l per class from q ≤ 0.01 target reference peptides, entering only the denominator), the multinomial bootstrap is exactly the row bootstrap, and π̂ = 1 − ci_low keeps the ADR-0010 placement FDR at level in every at-level attack, including 5-peptide bins. Forwarded to M3-21 (genome-level, giapsim): measure c_ref − c_true and the wrong-peptide target-vs-decoy match ratio, the two directions that make π̂ anti-conservative; consider a minimum reference count per class (or resampling c_l) and counting unreportable resamples as precision 0.

docs.title: Detectability model (cross-fitted p_detect)
docs.text:
Implements giap.genetable.detectability (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.3, §8.2 "Adjust for detectability", §8.4 row "Detectability", §8.5 attack 2; G5; issue M4-13, docs/specs/M4-13-detectability.md).

Status: signed off by the statistician (M4-13 review, 2026-10-15; see Sign-off).

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
Response: detected of the eligible genes (non-partial protein-coding rows; others get NaN). Covariates are physicochemical only: log1p(n_observable_peptides), log(length_aa), GRAVY, pI, tm_segments. Expression determinants and tested categories are never covariates (an included category would have O − E = 0 by construction). NaN or infinite values take the median of the transformed column; a zero-variance column is dropped and reported (dropped_zero_variance).

Per covariate a cubic SplineTransformer(n_knots=5, knots="quantile", extrapolation="linear") (tm_segments enters raw when it has fewer distinct values than knots), then an L2 logistic regression (l1_ratio=0, lbfgs, tol=1e-6). Rows are processed in locus_tag order, so the result does not depend on the input row order.

docs.title: Cross-fitting and the choice of C
docs.text:
• Outer folds: the sorted unique TU IDs are permuted with giap.rng.for_step("detectability", seed); fold = position mod 5. Every gene's p_detect comes from the model fitted without its TU (genes without a TU are their own TU).
  • Inner search, per outer fold, on its training TUs only: 3 TU folds from the same generator, C ∈ {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10} by the mean per-fold held-out log loss; ties go to the smaller C.
  • Fewer than 50 detected or 50 undetected eligible genes, or fewer TUs than folds: p_detect = the overall rate, flag detectability_constant (too_few_tus is reported and logged too).

Why TU folds. Genes of one TU share abundance and therefore detection; a gene-level fold would let the model learn a TU's detection state from its neighbours. With physicochemical covariates only this leakage is small and cannot be detected statistically (gene folds gave the same slope as TU folds in the review simulations); it is guarded structurally by unit tests (example 4; oracle checks of the chosen C and of p_detect to 2e-3).

docs.title: Calibration diagnostics (detection_summary.tsv, section detectability)
docs.text:
• 10 equal-count bins of p̂ (stable rank order): mean p̂, observed rate, n.
  • Brier score.
  • Recalibration fit d ~ a + b·logit(clip(p̂, 1e-6)) by unpenalised Newton–Raphson; ci_low / ci_high are Wald 95 % intervals from the inverse observed information X'WX at the MLE. Other rows carry no CI. If the data are (quasi-)completely separated in either direction (every detected gene's logit ≥ every undetected one's, or every one ≤) the MLE does not exist: intercept, slope and CIs are NaN and the recalibration_separated row is 1 (0 otherwise; spec M4-13 decision 17). These are descriptive: there is no p-value and no test family (§8.1 has no detectability claim).

Do not test b = 1 with this Wald interval on cross-fitted p̂: cross-fitted predictions are shrunk by estimation error, so b ≈ 0.97 ± 0.02 at n = 2,000 even when the model is right, while the interval half-width is ≈ 0.11. The interval is a statement about the realised p̂, not about the true model.

docs.title: Calibration evidence
docs.text:
Slurm jobs 1848615 (pre-code, spec simulation) and 1848717 (this implementation). Generator: the M4-07 layout with M4-08 covariates_only detection (logistic truth in log length, log1p n_obs, GRAVY), unless stated.

Check (suite detectability) Result on the implementation D1 (§8.4 gate, mean cross-fitted slope ∈ [0.8, 1.2]) slope 0.972 ± 0.019 per replicate at n = 2,000 (200 reps), 0.981 ± 0.011 at 4,500; gate replicates 0–19: mean 0.974. False alarm ≈ 0. Median fit time 4.7 s / 6.9 s single-threaded D2 (bins χ²₁₀, slope, intercept at known p; Bonferroni × 3) rejection 0.008 / 0.043 / 0.086 at α 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 (4,000 reps); components 0.049 / 0.045 / 0.052 at 0.05 Wald CI coverage (known a, b; n 200–5,000; b ∈ {0.7, 1, 1.3}) 0.944–0.960 for slope and intercept (2,000 reps per cell) Attack 2 subgroup gate, correct model, prophage O − E z mean −0.35, SD 0.89; rejection 0.005 / 0.039 / 0.089 (1,000 reps) same, shortest-length decile mean −0.66, SD 0.69; rejection 0.002 / 0.026 / 0.087 Teeth: model without length and n_obs, prophage z mean −3.60, SD 0.75; rejection at 0.05 is 0.99; gate blocks 20/20 and 20/20 Implementation vs the statistician's independent sklearn simulation of the spec (8 replicates, same data and generator) same C in 39 of 40 folds; mean

False-alarm budget of the suite (probability that some detectability check is a confirmed fail under a correct implementation, two-block rule, levels 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 evaluated together): fast (R = 20) 0.0066 (D2 0.0035, prophage 0.0023, short decile 0.0008, teeth and D1 ≈ 0); full (R = 100) 0.0029. The pre-review design (separate D2–D4) spent ≈ 0.023.

docs.title: Power and what the gates do not see
docs.text:
• D1 catches gross mis-specification: C fixed at 0.01 (slope 2.5) and logit scaling by 0.7 or 1.4. It misses in-sample prediction (slope 1.03–1.05), gene folds, and dropping the size covariates (0.93): its marginal slope is blind to subgroup miscalibration.
  • The subgroup gate (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_detectability.py) covers the §8.5 attack 2 confounding for p_detect itself: dropping the size covariates is a confirmed fail.
  • Short genes are over-predicted a little even by the correct model (decile z −0.66; prophage −0.35): the penalised spline flattens at the low-length edge. The gate holds because the subgroup z is under-dispersed, not because the bias is zero. Region tests and ORA (M4 region tests, M7) must run their own attack-2 gate on this p_detect; a region made only of very short genes will show a small negative O − E.

docs.title: Sign-off
docs.text: Statistician (M4-13 review, 2026-10-15): approved for giap.genetable.detectability as implemented. Cross-fitting, the inner C search and the recalibration match an independent simulation of the spec; D1 and the merged D2 hold their level; the Wald intervals cover at the nominal rate; the attack-2 subgroup gate is at level for the correct model and fails the model without size covariates; the suite's false-alarm budget is ≈ 0.007 per run. Forwarded: the short-gene over-prediction to the region-test and ORA attack-2 suites.

docs.title: Detection-limit model (P(detect | abundance) and P(miss))
docs.text:
Implements giap.operons.detection_limit (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.4.3 "One detected, one not", §7.3.3 conventions, §8.7; issue M6-02, docs/specs/M6-02-detection-limit-model.md). Consumer: M6-05H.

Status: method reviewed by the statistician before implementation (2026-10-21). The estimator below replaces the naive logistic fit that the spec's wording suggests; the model, its features, its training rows and its outputs are the spec's.

docs.title: Why the naive fit is wrong
docs.text:
Both training sets in §7.4.3 are selected on the response:

  • the peptide model is trained on the observable peptides of detected genes, and a gene is detected exactly when at least k_min of those peptides were seen;
  • the replicate model is trained on genes seen in some but not all runs, i.e. with 1 ≤ S ≤ R − 1 per-run detections out of R.

An ordinary logistic regression on such rows estimates P(seen | features, gene selected), not P(seen | features). At low abundance a detected gene has, almost by definition, one peptide seen out of several, so the per-peptide rate looks flat in abundance: the abundance coefficient is attenuated and the intercept is pushed up. The fitted P_det is then too high at the low end, which is exactly where the undetected partner lives, so P(miss) is too small (anti-conservative).

At R = 2 the replicate training set is degenerate: every retained gene has S = 1 of 2, the response is 1/2 for every gene whatever its abundance, and the logistic MLE is the constant 1/2 (slope exactly 0). No estimator can recover the slope from those rows: P(S = 1 | 1 ≤ S ≤ 1) = 1.

docs.title: Estimator: conditional (truncated) likelihood
docs.text:
Same model, same rows, the likelihood conditioned on the selection event (the conditional likelihood of capture–recapture with covariates; Huggins 1989, Biometrika 76:133–140).

Peptide model. For a training gene g with observable peptides j, linear predictor η_gj = β₀ + β_a·a_g + β_L·L_j + β_G·GRAVY_j, p_gj = σ(η_gj), and P_det,g = P(X_g ≥ k_min) the Poisson-binomial survival over g's peptides (the quantity p_detect already returns):

ℓ_c(β) = Σ_g [ Σ_j ( o_gj·η_gj − log(1 + e^η_gj) ) − log P_det,g(β) ]

Score: Σ_g Σ_j ( o_gj − P(O_gj = 1 | X_g ≥ k_min) )·x_gj, with P(O_gj = 1 | X_g ≥ k) = p_gj · P(X_g,−j ≥ k − 1) / P(X_g ≥ k); for k_min = 1 this is p_gj / P_det,g.

  • The conditioning event must be the event P_det models: training genes = genes with finite abundance_log2 and at least k_min distinct observable peptides seen in C11 (any route, any uniqueness, Q2). A detected gene whose evidence lies only outside the observable set (missed cleavages, length outside 7–30) contradicts the conditioning and is not a training gene; count it in the detection summary. For the detected genes of the spec that satisfy the event this is the spec's training set.
  • Genes with exactly k_min observable peptides contribute 0 (all seen given detection); they are still counted in n_fit, which stays "rows of the training genes".
  • Fit unpenalised (Newton or BFGS with the analytic score; centre and scale the features for the optimiser, report coef on the raw scale). Do not use a cross-validated ridge on the naive log loss: shrinking β_a towards 0 is the anti-conservative direction. If the optimiser fails to converge or the data are separated, usable = False (spec degenerate row "separated logistic"). A fixed, negligible ridge purely for numerical safety is acceptable only if the calibration criteria below still pass.
  • Cross-fitting, folds and model_for_tu are unchanged (GroupKFold by TU, folds from giap.rng.for_step("operons.detection_limit", seed)).

Replicate model. Per-run detection probability q_g = σ(γ·z_g) on the gene's mean abundance_log2 plus detectability.covariates; S_g of R runs. Training genes as in the spec (1 ≤ S_g ≤ R − 1); the likelihood is the doubly truncated binomial

ℓ_c(γ) = Σ_g [ S_g log q_g + (R − S_g) log(1 − q_g) − log(1 − (1 − q_g)^R − q_g^R) ]

(the binomial coefficient is constant). It is identified for R ≥ 3. At R = 2 the replicate model is not fitted and usable = False with reason replicate_two_runs: under the spec's training set its MLE is the constant model, which spec item 6 already declares unusable; the code must decide this from R, not from a numerically small slope. When runs differ per gene (a run in which the gene could not be quantified), R is the gene's own number of runs.

p_detect for the replicate model is the per-run probability q (spec item 4). The partner is undetected in the pooled table, i.e. in all R runs, so 1 − q overstates P(miss) relative to (1 − q)^R under run independence: the spec-literal choice is conservative. Changing it is an ADR (see Open decisions).

docs.title: Evidence (statistician simulation, 2026-10-21, Slurm job 1864733)
docs.text:
Calibration design of tests/calibration/test_detection_limit_calibration.py (truth logit = −10 + 0.5a − 0.03L + 0.8·GRAVY, a ~ N(15, 2.5), 5–20 observable peptides per gene), R = 100 replicates per row, scored on an independent 4,000-gene genome. CITL = calibration in the large, the intercept of d ~ offset(logit p̂) + c.

genes k_min fit β_a (0.5) β₀ (−10) slope intercept CITL mean p̂ − mean d 600 1 naive 0.349 −7.15 1.067 −0.951 −0.889 +0.138 600 1 conditional 0.501 −10.01 1.000 +0.024 +0.026 −0.004 600 2 naive 0.316 −6.40 1.141 −1.463 −1.358 +0.194 600 2 conditional 0.499 −9.98 1.005 +0.002 +0.005 +0.000 1500 1 naive 0.351 −7.20 1.065 −0.960 −0.899 +0.139 1500 1 conditional 0.502 −10.04 1.001 +0.009 +0.011 −0.002 1500 2 naive 0.320 −6.47 1.134 −1.447 −1.348 +0.191 1500 2 conditional 0.504 −10.08 0.993 +0.017 +0.024 −0.002

The true coefficients give slope 1.00 and |CITL| ≤ 0.01 on average. The naive fit passes the slope gate [0.8, 1.2] in every row while over-predicting detection by 14–19 points.

Replicate model, truth per-run logit = −8 + 0.5a, a ~ N(16, 2), 600 genes, R = 100:

runs naive slope (0.5) doubly truncated, mixed genes zero-truncated, all seen genes 2 0.000 (exactly) not identified 0.498 3 0.149 0.515 0.502 4 0.245 0.500 0.498 6 0.361 0.501 0.499 8 0.417 0.501 0.502

Propagation to P(miss) under the operon null (900 OP pairs, a_u = a_v + Δ, Δ ~ N(0, σ²), the r sample = oriented Δ of both-detected pairs; opportunities = (v detected, u) ordered pairs):

σ k_min fit mean P(miss) observed undetected share P(miss) ≤ 0.05 among one-detected P(miss) ≤ 0.10 among one-detected 0.6 1 true β 0.301 0.300 0.013 0.035 0.6 1 naive 0.199 0.300 0.036 0.097 0.6 1 conditional 0.302 0.300 0.014 0.035 1.5 1 true β 0.304 0.310 0.018 0.047 1.5 1 naive 0.206 0.310 0.046 0.119 1.5 1 conditional 0.304 0.310 0.019 0.048

The naive fit shrinks P(miss) by a third and multiplies the rate of small P(miss) under the null by 2.5–3. The selection of the r sample on both-detected pairs was negligible in this design (sd of the r sample 0.60 / 1.48 against 0.6 / 1.5). Scripts and raw output: $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m6-02/ (sim_pep.py, sim_rep.py, sim_pmiss.py, out/).

docs.title: Calibration criteria
docs.text: The slope alone has no teeth here: unlike M4-13 (trained on the population it scores, so a logistic MLE with an intercept is calibrated in the large by its score equation), this model is trained on a selected subset and scored on everyone. Proposed for DL1 (Khoa's decision; the tolerance file is protected): mean CITL over R within ±0.2 in addition to the slope in [0.8, 1.2]. The conditional fit gives |mean CITL| ≤ 0.03; the naive fit −0.89 to −1.36. Until a key exists, DL1 records the CITL.

docs.title: P(miss) is a probability, not a p-value
docs.text: M6-index decision 1: no q-value, no BH family. For a pair whose detected partner has abundance a_v, P(u undetected | a_v, H0) = P(miss); so P(P(miss) ≤ α and u undetected) ≤ α per opportunity if P(miss) is correctly estimated — the level is valid over opportunities, not conditionally on the pair being in the one-detected arm. An underestimated P(miss) breaks this: a pair with true P(miss) 0.2 estimated at 0.04 contributes 0.2 to the level at α = 0.05.

docs.title: Owed to M6-09 (attack C)
docs.text:
• Report the level with both denominators: per opportunity (v detected) and per one-detected pair. Only the first is a validity property; a 2 × α trigger on the second can fire under a correct model (or stay silent under a biased one, as above at σ = 0.6).
  • Record the calibration in the large of P(miss): mean P(miss) over opportunities against the observed undetected share (the conditional fit matches to 0.01; the naive fit is 0.10 low).
  • Run the arm with k_min = 2 (two_peptide) and with a replicate-only input at R = 3 and R = 2 (the latter must give no_detection_limit_model).
  • Measurement error with selection in abundance_log2 of low-abundance detected genes (estimated from one or two observed peptides, biased upwards) is not in these simulations; it pushes the same direction and needs an M6-03 generator in which abundance is estimated, not given.

docs.title: Open decisions (ADRs for Khoa)
docs.text:
1. Replicate model at R = 2: accept usable = False (inside the spec), or widen the training set to every gene seen in at least one run with the zero-truncated binomial likelihood, which is identified at R = 2 (slope 0.498 above). The second changes the spec's training set.
  2. Replicate p_detect: per-run q (spec, conservative) or pooled 1 − (1 − q)^R (correct under run independence, anti-conservative if detections are over-dispersed across runs).
  3. The DL1 CITL tolerance (above).

docs.title: Statistical review of the implementation (PR #157, head cf164a5, 2026-10-21)
docs.text:
Simulations ran the code under review: Slurm jobs 1865238 and 1865261. The scripts and output are in $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m6-02/review/ (review_sim.py, review_sel.py, out/). R = 100 replicates per arm, 60 for the selection arm. The values below are means, with the Monte Carlo SE in brackets.

Verdict: blocked on one item (B1). Everything else matches this note.

docs.title: Matches the note
docs.text:
• Likelihoods. The peptide conditional likelihood and its score are correct, including the leave-one-out factor P(X_−j ≥ k − 1) for k_min = 2. The same holds for the doubly truncated binomial and its score. Since cf164a5, _newton returns only at a stationary point with −H positive definite.
  • Peptide model on the operon null. 900 OP pairs, opportunities = (v detected, u). The level is per opportunity.
σ k_min β_a (0.5) gene slope CITL mean P(miss) undetected share level α=0.05 level α=0.10 0.6 1 0.502 (0.002) 0.998 +0.006 (0.008) 0.302 0.304 0.004 0.011 0.6 2 0.504 (0.002) 0.992 +0.015 (0.014) 0.434 0.443 0.003 0.009 1.5 1 0.503 (0.002) 1.000 +0.012 (0.009) 0.305 0.313 0.006 0.016 1.5 2 0.504 (0.002) 0.999 +0.017 (0.014) 0.420 0.459 0.005 0.014

At σ = 1.5 with k_min = 2, P(miss) falls 0.04 below the observed share. This gap comes from the r sample, which is selected on both-detected pairs; the model itself has CITL +0.017. It belongs to M6-09 attack C, not to M6-02. - Cross-fitting is honest. The folds are a seeded partition of the training TUs. fold_coef[j] never saw fold j, and a TU that trained nothing gets the full model, which never saw it either. An undetected partner is never a training gene in either model. M6-05H must call model_for_tu with the TU of the detected partner v. That is the only gene of the pair that can have trained. - Replicate model at R ≥ 3. The slope is 0.504 (0.004) at R = 3 and 0.499 (0.003) at R = 4, against a truth of 0.5. At R = 2 the model is decided from the run count. With the per-run q, P(miss) is very conservative: mean 0.45 against an observed undetected share of 0.15, and level 0 at every α. This is as the note predicted. - Calibration tests. The DL1 slope gate has no teeth against the naive fit. The teeth are elsewhere: - DL2 (halved slopes); - the every-commit β_a recovery test (±0.08; the naive fit gives 0.35); - the slow unit CITL test (|CITL| ≤ 0.1 on an independent genome; the naive fit gives −0.89); - the k_min = 2 recovery test (±0.04; the k = 1 score gives 0.44).

These tests are adequate for the failure this note predicted. They cannot detect B1, because in simulate_peptides detected is exactly X_obs ≥ k_min.

docs.title: B1 (blocking): the training genes are selected on detected, not on the conditioning event
docs.text:
fit_peptide_model keeps called & finite(abundance) and then sum(o) >= k. The likelihood conditions on X_obs ≥ k_min. In the mayu and decoy_picked tiers, detected is a gene-level q ≤ α. That is a strict subset of the conditioning event: single-hit genes fail it at random. Genes that fail are missing from the training set, yet the likelihood treats them as possible. Because they are low-abundance genes with few peptides, the bias that this note's estimator was chosen to remove comes back, in the same direction (anti-conservative).

Attack arm (review_sel.py): the pair design above with σ = 0.6. Every gene with ≥ 2 peptides seen is called, and a gene with one peptide seen is called with probability π₁.

π₁ X ≥ 1 genes not called fit β_a CITL vs X ≥ 1 level α=0.05 (event: u not called) level α=0.10 0.5 22 % code (detected) 0.447 −0.40 (0.01) 0.022 0.049 0.5 22 % training = X ≥ 1 0.503 +0.01 (0.01) 0.014 0.033 0.2 36 % code (detected) 0.400 −0.75 (0.01) 0.046 0.092 0.2 36 % training = X ≥ 1 0.503 +0.01 (0.01) 0.023 0.050

The fix is in the implementation and the tests, which are not mine to edit:

  • Training genes = finite abundance_log2 and ≥ k_min distinct observable peptides seen in C11, whatever detected says. This is decision 5's wording and this note's; spec item 2's "detected" is the special case. M4-11 gives finite abundances to undetected genes that have accepted peptides.
  • The test-author adds a case in which a gene with ≥ k_min observable peptides seen but detected = False contributes its rows to n_fit, and a recovery test with π₁ < 1.

If the lead reads spec item 2 as binding, this needs a Khoa ADR. Until one exists, it stays blocking.

B1 re-check (bac9046, Slurm 1865546, R = 60). B1 is fixed and the block is lifted. The selection arm against bac9046 reproduces the "training = X ≥ 1" rows to every printed digit:

π₁ β_a CITL vs X ≥ 1 level at α = 0.05 (event: u not called) level at α = 0.10 0.5 0.503 +0.011 0.014 0.033 0.2 0.503 +0.011 0.023 0.050

The two fits, with detected as called and with detected = X ≥ 1, are identical in both arms. N1 (now spec decision 9) stands for M6-05H.

docs.title: Non-blocking
docs.text:
• N1: the event P(miss) models. Even with B1 fixed, P_det models X_obs ≥ k_min, not detected. Against the event "u not called", P(miss) is too small in the large: CITL −0.84 (π₁ = 0.5) and −1.39 (π₁ = 0.2). The per-opportunity level still held in these arms: at most 0.023 at α = 0.05 and 0.050 at α = 0.10. M6-05H must define the one-detected arm by u having < k_min observable peptides seen, or ADR the gap. This is owed to Khoa (M6-05H) and to M6-09 attack C.
  • N2: stray run label. With 5 % of the run labels dropped to "":
  • 2 real runs give R = 3 and the replicate model is fitted instead of replicate_two_runs;
  • with 3 real runs the slope is 0.473 (0.003) against 0.5.

P(miss) stays conservative under the per-run q: level 0. A C16 validation item, not blocking. - N3: unstored covariate median. At scoring, a NaN covariate gives NaN, so the pair is not tested. This costs power, not validity. Store the median. If M6-05H passes cov=None, every replicate P(miss) is NaN, so M6-05H must pass the M4-10 covariates. - N4: replicate model under two_peptide. A run counts as seen with ≥ 1 peptide, while detection needs ≥ 2 distinct peptides pooled. P(miss) is then 0.41 against an observed share of 0.46 (R = 3, 1–4 peptides per gene), still level ≤ 0.003 at α = 0.10 because 1 − q is so conservative. Record it in the summary; it only matters if the pooled 1 − (1 − q)^R ADR is accepted. - N5: imputed abundances. A detected gene with an imputed abundance_log2 (no intensity) trains with a fill value. Excluding abundance_imputed rows from training would be cleaner; the current behaviour is measurement error in the direction this note already lists. - N6: the DL1 docstring still describes the naive oracle as "recorded, not gated" with intercept −0.97. It should describe the conditional fit. - The other backlog nits are numerical or test gaps, not statistical issues: NaN tu_id pooled into one fold group, rng consumption order, I/L, a constant feature giving a singular H.

docs.title: ADRs owed to Khoa
docs.text:
1. The DL1 CITL tolerance of ±0.2 (tolerances.yaml is protected). The measured |CITL| is ≤ 0.02 at k_min = 1 and 2. A conditional-fit CITL record should also be added at k_min = 2 (DL1 runs only k_min = 1).
  2. If B1's fix is read as a change to spec item 2: the training set is the conditioning event, not detected.
  3. The one-detected event for M6-05H (N1).
  4. The two existing open decisions above: R = 2 zero-truncation, and the pooled replicate p_detect.

docs.title: References
docs.text: Huggins RM (1989). On the statistical analysis of capture experiments. Biometrika 76:133–140.

docs.title: Basic detection summary (O − E) and QC rows
docs.text: Implements giap.context.summary (basic_rows, qc_rows, detection_summary) and giap.io.summary_tsv.write_detection_summary (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.5(a), §8.2, §9.3; issue M4-16). Statistician sign-off: see the end of this note (approved after the review fixes, 2026-10-15).

docs.title: O − E against Σ p_detect
docs.text: For a group G of eligible genes (detection_status != partial_excluded; single-peptide genes are eligible and undetected in the primary analysis), O = Σ d_g and E = Σ p_g with the cross-fitted p_detect of M4-13, so E[O − E] = 0 when the detectability model is calibrated (§8.2: never against raw counts). Reported: n_genes, n_detected, pct_detected (0–100), expected, o_minus_e, o_over_e (NA when E = 0) and n_tu; n = n_genes on every row.

docs.title: TU-block CI
docs.text:
O − E = Σ_TU s_t with s_t = Σ_{g ∈ G ∩ t} (d_g − p_g): only the group's genes inside a drawn TU count. The 95 % percentile CI comes from tu_block_bootstrap (docs/methods/bootstrap.md) over the group's TU sums, B = stats.bootstrap (1000). Groups are processed in sorted (group_type, group) order from one for_step("context_stats", seed) generator, so the draws for a group depend only on the TU counts of the groups before it, not on gene labels outside it. A group carries the flag ci_few_units (on the o_minus_e row only) when it has fewer than 10 TUs or when min(E, n_genes − E) < 10 (lead decision 4); a single-TU group has a degenerate CI equal to the estimate. Calibration: tests/calibration/test_detection_summary_calibration.py (coverage of 0 under a TU-comonotone null, where gene-level resampling under-covers).

What the CI does and does not cover: it is the sampling variability of Σ (d − p) over the group's TUs given p_detect; the estimation error of the cross-fitted model is not propagated. For a group that is (nearly) the whole eligible set (the main chromosome, cog_category none without function annotation) Σ (d − p̂) ≈ 0 by construction (the logistic intercept fits calibration in the large, up to cross-fitting noise), so its O − E is a sanity check, not a finding.

docs.title: Recorded coverage (review of PR M4-16; R = 2000 unless noted, B = 1000)
docs.text:
Null group TUs non-coverage (SE) TU-comonotone, giapsim 400 genes, p = p_detect_true replicon chr1 (gated) 223 0.046 (0.005) same feature_class cds / hypothetical 219 / 84 0.054 / 0.060 same, gene-level resampling (teeth) chr1 400 genes 0.166 independent detection within TU chr1 223 0.054 comonotone, p / 10 (rare detection) chr1 223 0.080 comonotone, k random TUs of chr1 chr1 3 / 5 / 8 / 10 / 15 / 20 / 40 0.25 / 0.15 / 0.11 / 0.094 / 0.089 / 0.085 / 0.064 same feature_class sorf / pseudogene ≈ 8 / ≈ 4 0.90 / 0.40 single-gene TUs, independent (R = 1000) 50 TUs, E = 1 50 0.37 same E = 5 (50 / 100 TUs) 50 / 100 0.065 / 0.11 same E = 10 / 20 / 50 100–200 / 200–400 / 100 0.07–0.08 / 0.04–0.07 / 0.04 2-gene comonotone TUs E = 2 / 10 / 20 50 / 50–100 / 100–200 0.36 / 0.05–0.12 / 0.07

Gate cost (ADR-0015): at the measured rate 0.046 the fast gate (R = 100, ≤ 9 misses) fails a block with probability 0.017 and the full gate (R = 1000, ≤ 63) 0.006; two-block false alarms 3 × 10⁻⁴ and 3 × 10⁻⁵ per night, negligible against the ≈ 0.04 nightly budget. Power against gene-level resampling (0.166): 0.96 (fast), 1.0 (full).

The TU count alone does not govern accuracy. The percentile CI of a sum of residuals d − p fails when few TUs carry the minority outcome (few detections when p is small, few non-detections when p is near 1): with no detection in the group every TU sum is negative and the CI excludes 0 whatever the TU count. sORF and pseudogene groups (low p) and small COG letters are exactly this case. A CI should be read as 95 % only when ≥ 10 TUs and ≥ 10 expected minority events (min(E, n_genes − E) ≥ 10); below, coverage is 0.63–0.95 (table). CIs from 10–19 TUs cover ≈ 0.91 (c(n) of bootstrap.md), so ci_few_units at < 10 is a lenient threshold.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text: replicon (each contig), feature_class (cds, sorf, pseudogene, and hypothetical = any feature type with hypothetical = true), cog_category: a gene is counted once in every letter of its cog_category (COG convention; KT counts in K and in T), genes without a category in none. Groups without eligible genes are omitted.

docs.title: QC rows (section = qc, run/all)
docs.text:
• id_mixups (§7.5.1: same-database ALT sites without start_codon/stop_codon): NA with flag requires_variants until the variant module (M7) exists (lead decision 6).
  • engine_protein_mismatch_rate: distinct C11 peptides flagged engine_protein_mismatch over distinct placed (C11) peptides; n = that denominator; NA without C11 rows. A QC proxy reported under its own name, not id_mixups.
  • genome_inconsistent_rate (§7.5.1): among distinct C9 target, non-contaminant peptides with search_db = other, the share without an exact C11 placement (absent, or tolerant only); n = that denominator; NA without such peptides (e.g. all search_db = same) (lead decision 5). §7.5.1 defines it under --genome-relation same; under related tolerant placements are expected and the rate is not a mismatch signal (it is still computed; read it accordingly).
  • contaminant_peptides, contaminant_proteins, unmapped_peptides, unmapped_proteins: C13 rows by label and kind; NA without C13.

docs.title: Table
docs.text: Sections in order tier, basic, detectability, qc, then group_type, group, metric. Parts without n/flags (M4-12, M4-13 rows) get NA / empty. Floats are written with round-trip precision (shortest repr) rather than %.6g, so CIs read back exactly (writer tests require 1e-9).

docs.text:
The E rule counts expected detections in genes; under within-TU dependence the effective count is the number of TUs that carry a detection (≈ E / TU size when detections are comonotone). Unflagged groups (≥ 10 TUs and min(E, n − E) ≥ 10) at the boundary:

TUs × genes per TU, p E non-coverage (SE) flagged 300 × 1, 0.034 10.2 0.069 (0.008) 0 % 100 × 2, 0.05 / 200 × 2, 0.026 10 / 10.4 0.112 / 0.119 (0.010) 0 % 100 × 3, 0.04 12 0.089 (0.009) 0 % 50 × 4, 0.05 / 40 × 5, 0.05 10 0.089 / 0.113 (0.009–0.010) 0 % 20 × 10, 0.05 10 0.356 (0.015) 0 % 100 × 3, 0.10 30 0.059 (0.007) 0 %

For realistic operon sizes (2–5 genes) the unflagged boundary covers 0.88–0.93, the same order as the accepted 10–19-TU regime (≈ 0.91), and coverage recovers once E is a few multiples of 10 (0.059 at E = 30). Only long, uniformly low-p TUs (20 × 10 genes) fall far below; that is not a realistic group. Recommendation (non-blocking, backlog): flag in TU units as well, e.g. fewer than 10 TUs with an observed detection (or non-detection) in the group.

docs.title: Statistician sign-off (M4-16)
docs.text:
Re-review at 338f49f (2026-10-15): APPROVED. Lead decisions 4–9 are implemented and tested: the E rule and flag only on o_minus_e (4, 9); genome_inconsistent_rate over search_db = other non-contaminant targets (5); id_mixups NA + requires_variants and engine_protein_mismatch_rate (6; the 3/5 example of 338f49f is the correct distinct-peptide count); ValueError naming genes with NaN p_detect or no tu_id (7); COG -/blank → none, non-boolean detected raises (8); group-order mutant killed (9). Unit + integration tests 80/80 pass locally; implementer's calibration with the low-E attack (job 1849314) passed: the sORF E = 1, E = 2 (operons) and n − E = 1 attacks are flagged in every replicate and their unflagged miss rate is a confirmed fail. No p- or q-values, so §8.1 families do not apply; every CI is a TU-block CI (§8.2). Non-blocking: the TU-unit flag above; the genome_relation caveat of genome_inconsistent_rate; hypothetical still uses astype(bool) (a string "false" would read as True; the same fail-closed check as detected would cover it).

Earlier review at db7dae0 (history):

Reviewed on branch m4/detection-summary at db7dae0. CHANGES REQUESTED (see the PR comment):

  1. Flag rule: extend the CI flag to rare outcomes (min(E, n_genes − E) < 10, or fewer than 10 TUs with a detection / a non-detection), not only < 10 TUs (table above); add a gated attack null for a low-E group.
  2. genome_inconsistent_rate uses the wrong peptide subset: §7.5.1 defines it for peptides searched against another strain (search_db = other, --genome-relation same); for search_db = same it is ≈ 0 by construction. Exclude is_contaminant peptides from the denominator. id_mixups (§7.5.1: same-db ALT sites without start_codon/stop_codon) is approximated by engine_protein_mismatch peptides until M5 lands; this needs an ADR or a renamed metric.
  3. Fail closed: an eligible gene with NaN p_detect gives expected = NaN but a finite CI (pandas groupby skips NaN); an NA tu_id is dropped from the bootstrap (pandas 3 keeps NaN through astype(str)). Both should raise.

Verified correct: O − E and O/E, eligibility, multi-letter COG counting, TU sums restricted to the group's genes, sorted-group draws, writer round trip; 13 / 15 manual mutants killed.

docs.title: Detection tiers and gene-level FDR (M4-12)
docs.text: Status: M4-24 shared ranking key approved by the statistician 2026-10-23 (PR #238). Earlier: statistician re-review 2026-10-15 (PR #92, after f297600): PEP-only path approved; changes requested on the contaminant-decoy rule (lead decision 11), see Sign-off. Code: src/giap/genetable/detection.py. Spec: GIAP_SPEC.md §2.1 decision 4, §7.3, §7.3.2, §9.3; ADR-0009; docs/specs/M4-12-detection-tiers.md.

docs.title: Tier choice (once per run, from the input)
docs.text:
1. decoy_picked: at least one C9 decoy row with protein_ids passes q <= input.q_value_max (NA q passes), and the paired share f = paired / (paired + unpaired) is at least max(mapping.proteins.min_identity, mapping.proteins.min_coverage) (0.80 by default), and the paired decoys share at least one ranking column with the targets (M4-24, see "Shared ranking key"). Decoys above q_value_max are neither paired nor unpaired; that filter applies only when some C9 target row carries q (ADR-0047).
  2. mayu: decoys exist but f is below the cut-off (warning decoy_pairing_low), or an accepted target carries a q-value or a PEP.
  3. two_peptide: C11 has rows but no accepted q or PEP.
  4. protein_list: no peptides at all.

docs.title: Protein to gene map
docs.text: Priority: (1) the ID is a C2 locus_tag; (2) the gene of its C12 rank-1 hits (one gene only); (3) peptide vote: among accepted unique target peptides whose C9 protein_ids contain the ID, the gene with the most distinct peptides (a tie leaves the ID unmapped). Protein groups A;B are split; contaminant-prefixed IDs are never mapped.

docs.title: Decoy pairing
docs.text: The longest matching input.decoy_prefixes entry is stripped from every member of the decoy's protein_ids. A decoy with any stripped member carrying an input.contaminant_prefixes prefix is a contaminant decoy and is neither paired nor unpaired (lead decisions 6, 11). Otherwise the decoy pairs when every member maps, and all map to the same gene.

docs.title: PEP-only input (lead decision 5)
docs.text:
When every accepted q-value is missing and PEPs are given, peptide q is the running mean of the sorted distinct accepted PEPs (q_i = mean of the PEPs <= PEP_i), and MAYU uses those q for the thresholds and sum PEP for F(t). Mixed input keeps the given q (decision 11).

Asymmetry (lead question 1). Decoys pass the same q <= q_value_max filter as targets, but targets must also be placed on a gene and decoys cannot be. False targets that do not place are lost while their decoys stay, so D is too large and the picked estimate errs conservative. In giapsim every false target places (false_source = random_gene), which is the least favourable case for this asymmetry.

What 1/f assumes (ADR-0009). Decoys are lost at random with respect to score while their target counterparts stay. When loss is symmetric (a reference protein absent from the strain loses its false targets and its decoy alike, as in cross-strain searches), 1/f over-corrects and the estimate is conservative. Loss that depends on score is not corrected. Stress run below: losing the best-scoring 10 % / 20 % of passing decoys gives FDP 1.5x / 2x q at q = 0.01, and the 80 % guard does not catch it. Nothing in the input should make pairing depend on score. If an engine ever does that, a KS check of paired against unpaired decoy scores would be the diagnostic (backlog).

docs.title: Picked gene-level FDR (Savitski 2015, ADR-0009)
docs.text: Per eligible (non-partial) gene: best accepted target and best paired decoy by the key (q ascending, PEP ascending, score descending; NA last), dense-ranked over the union (no -log10 0). The better one is kept; a tie goes to the decoy. With f the paired share, FDR(t) = (D(t)/f + 1) / T(t), made monotone. Decoy winners and genes without accepted peptides get q NA (not_detected). detection_summary.tsv reports f (decoy_paired_share) and 1/f (decoy_win_weight). It also reports q_floor = 1/T, where T is the number of eligible genes won by a target. It is a lower bound on every picked q, from the +1 that finite-sample control needs: q = running min of (D/f + 1)/k ≥ 1/T, whatever f is. It is reached only when no decoy win scores at or above the weakest target win. When q_floor > stats.alpha.identification, i.e. fewer than 1/alpha genes are won by a target, no gene can be detected at that alpha. The run then warns q_floor_above_alpha, and q-values and detection calls are reported unchanged (Khoa, 2026-10-22). The row is NA outside the picked tier: MAYU has no +1 term (its q → 0 as the expected false-peptide count → 0), and the two_peptide and protein_list tiers have no gene q.

docs.title: Shared ranking key (M4-24)
docs.text: A target and a decoy can only be compared on a column both of them carry. The picked tier therefore ranks on S, the shared key. Let C_T be the key columns (q, PEP, score) that at least one accepted target carries. S is the part of C_T that has a value on every paired decoy, kept in key order with the same directions. Columns outside S are ignored on both sides. Before M4-24 a column that the decoys lacked was NA on the decoy side, so every decoy ranked last, D(t) = 0 and every target-won gene got q = 1/T. That was a no-decoy estimate labelled decoy_picked. 1. S = C_T: unchanged, no warning. DIA-NN input (q and PEP on both sides) is in this case. 2. ∅ ≠ S ⊊ C_T: decoy_picked on S, with warning decoy_unscored. One NA value in a decoy column takes that column out of S for every row. No decoy row is dropped, because dropping decoys that lack a value is loss that depends on the input, and 1/f does not correct it. A target with NA in a column of S still ranks last and loses to its decoy. That costs power and is conservative. Shorter keys give more ties, and ties go to the decoy (also conservative). The spec's examples 3–5 show this case: with S = {score}, a decoy that outscores its target wins even though it has no q. 3. S = ∅: the decoys cannot compete. They are treated as absent for the tier choice, with decoy_unscored. The no-decoy chain applies (mayu when an accepted target has q or PEP, else two_peptide or protein_list). The gene table equals that of the same input without its decoy rows. The tier rows still report the decoy counts and f. Two inputs reach this case: decoys with no ranking value at all (giapsim M3-19), and targets with none. 4. q filter (ADR-0047). Decoys with q above q_value_max leave the competition only when some C9 target row carries q. Without that, filtering only the decoys would remove weak decoys whose targets all stay. When q ∈ S and q is monotone in the ranking, the filter changes no target's gene q. It changes f, the 80 % guard and the counts. Why ranking on S still controls the gene FDR: the competition needs decoys that are a null for the ranked column on the side that was selected. Targets are accepted on q, but decoys whose q is NA are not filtered. Selection can only remove false targets, so in expectation D(t)/f over the unselected decoys is at least the false-target count above t, and the estimate errs conservative when the score and q disagree (table below, score + noise). The one input this does not cover is accepted targets whose q is NA while their decoys have a q and are filtered (see Sign-off of M4-24, note 1).

docs.title: MAYU tier
docs.text: giap.stats.mayu.mayu_gene_fdr (see mayu-gene-fdr.md) on eligible genes, with sizes n_observable_peptides, P(t) = distinct accepted peptides, F = sum of PEP when every accepted peptide has one. Otherwise F = t |P(t)|, with warning pep_partial when only some have one. fdr_2pep is reported under its own name and is not the gene FDR. Warning unspecific_search: more than 50 % of distinct accepted peptides (placements ending at the gene's C-terminus excepted) do not end in K/R.

docs.title: Unestimated tiers
docs.text: two_peptide: >= detection.min_peptides_sequences_only distinct accepted peptides -> detected; exactly one -> single_peptide_unestimated (not detected in the primary analysis). protein_list: a C12 rank-1 hit with a gene -> detected. Both carry no gene q. Contaminant evidence counts toward detection in every tier (lead decision 2).

docs.title: Statistician replication (Slurm job 1849140; R = 1,000 at 2,000 genes, R = 300 at 4,500 genes)
docs.text:
The pipeline is the suite's own (detection_tiers_calsim: M4-07 -> M4-08 -> M4-09 -> M4-10/11 -> detect). Seeds are SeedSequence([20261015, 1000 pi, n_genes, rep]), independent of the harness streams. The script is local/scratch/review-m4-12/exp.py. The table gives mean FDP +- SE at q = 0.01, and in brackets the ratio of mean FDP to the mean estimated FDR of the last gene detected.

claim 2,000 genes, pi 0.01 2,000, pi 0.05 4,500, pi 0.01 4,500, pi 0.05 picked 0.00979 +- 0.00013 0.00926 +- 0.00013 0.00970 +- 0.00016 0.00949 +- 0.00015 MAYU (PEP = no PEP) 0.00996 +- 0.00009 [1.08] 0.00979 +- 0.00009 [1.04] 0.01004 +- 0.00011 [1.04] 0.00979 +- 0.00011 [1.01] picked, q from TDA D/T 0.01013 +- 0.00013 0.00960 +- 0.00013 MAYU PEP, q from TDA 0.00963 +- 0.00009 0.00947 +- 0.00009 MAYU no PEP, q from TDA 0.01010 +- 0.00011 0.00993 +- 0.00011 picked, 10 % / 20 % random loss 0.00980 / 0.00985 0.00932 / 0.00947 same, without 1/f (pre-ADR mutant) 0.01073 / 0.01216 0.01030 / 0.01168 picked, best-scoring 10 % / 20 % lost 0.0148 / 0.0197 0.0145 / 0.0193

At q = 0.05 every row except the mutant lies within 0.0475-0.0500. The pre-ADR mutant at 20 % loss reaches 0.0526 / 0.0522 (z ~ +11-15). At q = 0.10 every row equals its q = 0.05 FDP (saturation).

Reading: 1. MAYU at q = 0.01 is at level, with no margin. The implementer's 0.0104 +- 0.0004 was a +1 SE block. With 3x-6x the replicates the mean is 0.0100 (pi 0.01) and 0.0098 (pi 0.05). The estimate itself runs 4-8 % low (ratio > 1, as in mayu-gene-fdr.md: noisy a_g, bin averaging). The step between gene q values absorbs this, so the realised mean lands on q. This is noise around an unbiased-at-q procedure, not material anti-conservatism. Nightly false-alarm cost (normal approximation, two-block rule): MAYU pi 0.01 at q = 0.01 and R = 300 fails one block with probability ~0.05 and both with ~0.0024. Every other gene_fdr claim, the attack included, is below 1e-3. The suite adds ~0.003 to the ~0.04 nightly budget of ADR-0015. 2. PEP against no PEP. In giapsim q is the running mean of PEP, so sum PEP equals t |P(t)| and the two gated claims are one claim. The M4-09 simulator is the one already in use, so it does not separate them on its own. Once q comes from target-decoy competition (D/T over the emitted decoys), the two differ (0.0096 against 0.0101 at pi 0.01) and both stay at level. An EvidenceConfig mode with an engine-like q is needed before the two can be counted as independent evidence (backlog). 3. Decoy-loss attack (ADR-0009). With 1/f, random loss of 10 % or 20 % keeps the level. Without 1/f, 20 % loss inflates FDP by 1.2-1.25x. The attack catches that mutant with probability ~0.4-0.5 per level in the fast suite (both blocks must fail) and ~1.0 in the full suite. At 10 % loss its power is low: ~0.004 fast and ~0.04 full at q = 0.01. With floor(0.3 n) decoys lost, f = 0.70 < 0.80 holds in every replicate, so the "30 %" claim always runs MAYU. It tests the guard, not 1/f. 4. Levels 0.05 and 0.10 are weak and vacuous. Peptides are capped at q <= 0.01, so the loosest gene FDR reachable is ~0.053 and the q = 0.10 claims sit ~200 SE below the bound. Giving them teeth needs a suite variant with input.q_value_max = 0.10 (backlog). 5. Null structure: false targets and decoys land on genes in proportion to n_observable (§8.4), which is MAYU's own model. Departures from it are covered by the M4-02 attacks (mayu-gene-fdr.md). TU blocks and autocorrelation do not enter gene detection. One test family per run (all eligible genes), as in §8.1. Effect size: the gene q is reported next to M4-11's n_accepted and coverage_frac. The FDR curve rows carry no CI (ci_low/ci_high NA). They are estimates of an expectation, as in mayu-gene-fdr.md.
