docs.text:
Script local/scratch/review-92/exp.py; seeds SeedSequence([20261015, 92, 1000 pi, n_genes, rep]). Mean FDP +- SE.

PEP-only input (decoys dropped, C9 q_value and C11 best_q_input NA, PEP kept; tier mayu in every replicate). Every target peptide passes the q filter, so q = 0.05 / 0.10 are reachable:

n genes, pi q = 0.01 q = 0.05 q = 0.10 2,000, 0.01 0.00973 +- 0.00009 0.04886 +- 0.00018 0.05514 +- 0.00018 2,000, 0.05 0.00965 +- 0.00009 0.04926 +- 0.00021 0.09831 +- 0.00028 4,500, 0.01 0.00983 +- 0.00010 0.04940 +- 0.00022 0.05538 +- 0.00020 4,500, 0.05 0.00995 +- 0.00011 0.04945 +- 0.00025 0.09871 +- 0.00035

At q <= 0.05 it equals the mayu_pep claim (giapsim q is the running mean of PEP, so the derived q reproduces it on the accepted prefix). At q = 0.10 and pi 0.05 it is the first gene-FDR claim of M4-12 that is informative at 0.10 (FDP 0.098, at level). Approved.

Contaminant-shared groups (attack; picked input, a share X of the genes has CON__<g> / rev_CON__<g> appended to target / decoy protein_ids; targets still place by sequence):

n genes, pi X = 0.2, q = 0.01 X = 0.4, q = 0.01 X = 0.4, q = 0.05 2,000, 0.01 0.01184 +- 0.00015 0.01597 +- 0.00019 0.05302 +- 0.00018 2,000, 0.05 0.01176 +- 0.00015 0.01575 +- 0.00019 0.05316 +- 0.00020 4,500, 0.01 0.01199 +- 0.00017 0.01621 +- 0.00021 0.05348 +- 0.00020 4,500, 0.05 0.01232 +- 0.00019 0.01657 +- 0.00024 0.05334 +- 0.00024

The tier is decoy_picked in every replicate: the mixed decoys leave both counts, so f stays ~1 while D loses a share X of the gene decoys and FDP ~ q / (1 - X). The rule rewards the input with the higher tier exactly when its decoy side is depleted, and nothing bounds X (an organism whose proteins overlap the contaminant FASTA, or a contaminant FASTA that carries organism proteins). Gated as tests/calibration/attacks/test_detection_tiers_attack_inputs.py (X = 0.3): fast run (job 1850411) is a confirmed fail at q = 0.01 (0.0143 / 0.0138 against bound 0.0115) and at q = 0.05; the pep_only claim of the same file passes at all three levels.

docs.title: Sign-off
docs.text:
Re-review (2026-10-15, after f297600 and lead decision 11): changes requested. 1. Decision 5 (PEP-only q) is implemented and calibrated (table above); approved. 2. Decision 11 as implemented ("ANY stripped ID is a contaminant -> out of both counts") is anti-conservative for decoys of mixed groups rev_P;rev_CON__X: their targets P;CON__X still place on P's gene by sequence, so dropping only the decoy is unaccounted decoy loss. Required: a decoy is a contaminant decoy only when ALL its stripped members carry a contaminant prefix; for mixed decoys drop the contaminant members and pair on the rest (or, at least, count them as unpaired so 1/f and the 80 % guard see them). The attack file above must pass. 3. Decisions 7-9 verified (longest prefix, Detection.protein_gene_map, mutant tests).

Statistician (M4-12 review, 2026-10-15): the gene-level FDR claims (picked with ADR-0009's 1/f, and MAYU) are approved as calibrated on the evidence above. Sign-off of the module is conditional on two code fixes, listed in the PR #92 review: (a) PEP-only input reaches the mayu tier but detects no gene, because the gene thresholds come from q alone; (b) decoys of contaminant proteins count as unpaired and lower f.

docs.title: M4-24 statistician review (PR #238; Slurm jobs 1871621, 1871625, 1871630)
docs.text:
Script local/scratch/stat238/exp.py and exp2.py, detection_tiers_calsim picked input, 2,000 genes, pi 0.05, R = 300 (200 for the last block), seeds SeedSequence([20261023, 238, 50, rep]). Mean FDP +- SE.

decoy input q = 0.01 q = 0.05 tier / warning all columns (baseline) 0.00959 +- 0.00025 0.04762 +- 0.00044 decoy_picked score only (S = {score}) 0.00959 +- 0.00025 0.04762 +- 0.00044 decoy_picked + decoy_unscored PEP only (S = {pep}) same as baseline same decoy_picked + decoy_unscored q NA on 5 % of decoys (S = {pep, score}) same as baseline same decoy_picked + decoy_unscored score only, score + N(0, 1) on both sides 0.00729 +- 0.00021 0.02838 +- 0.00031 decoy_picked + decoy_unscored score only, score + N(0, 2^2) on both sides 0.00418 +- 0.00014 0.01881 +- 0.00025 decoy_picked + decoy_unscored targets: q NA on 50 % of rows, decoys complete 0.00460 +- 0.00014 0.05302 +- 0.00290 (p90 0.135) decoy_picked same, decoy q filter off when a target q is NA (mutant) 0.00423 +- 0.00018 0.02234 +- 0.00039 decoy_picked

Reading: in giapsim, q and PEP are monotone in the score, so any non-empty S gives the same ordering and the same FDP as the baseline. When the ranked score disagrees with the q that accepted the targets (noise rows), the estimate is conservative, as argued above. The targeted calibration files (attacks unscored, decoy_loss, inputs, and test_gene_fdr_real_mapping) pass on the branch (job 1871621). The MAYU change through libm exp / pow is bit-identical to numpy on an AVX2 node (EPYC 7742, 22,000 random (w, F) pairs, plus 0^0 and empty shapes).

docs.title: Sign-off (M4-24, 2026-10-23)
docs.text: Approved: rules 1-6 and the S = ∅ fallback. Notes, none blocking: 1. Existing before M4-24, unchanged by it: accepted targets whose q is NA (NA passes the filter) compete only with the decoys that pass q <= q_value_max. Their null peptides above the cut-off stay, but the matching decoys are filtered out. All NA-q targets tie at the bottom rank, so the whole block enters together or not at all. With 50 % of target q NA the FDP at q = 0.05 is bimodal (mean 0.053 +- 0.003, p90 0.135). Switching the decoy filter off whenever some C9 target q is NA restores the margin (0.022). Rule 6 calls the sparse target column "conservative". That holds for the ranking, not for the ranking combined with the filter. Backlog: extend ADR-0047's symmetry from "some target carries q" to "every target carries q". 2. The calibration attack decoys_score_only has teeth against the defect (D = 0). In giapsim it cannot tell S = {score} from S = {q}, because the columns are monotone in each other. A variant with an engine-like q that is not monotone in the score (M4-12 replication, Reading 2) would separate them. 3. libm exp / pow are the same on nodes that share a glibc build and the FMA code path. A node without FMA would take another glibc variant (correctly rounded in practice, but not guaranteed). Every FarmShare node with AVX2 has FMA.

docs.title: Determinants: what explains abundance
docs.text: Module 8 track R (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.8). Issues M8-07 onward; this note grows with each.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Issue M8-07, module giap.determinants.features (pure). feature_frame builds tables/determinants_features.tsv; model_matrix encodes it for M8-08.

Rows. One per eligible gene (§7.3: not partial, finite p_detect), in §6.5 order (C1 contig order, start, end, strand, locus tag). Ribosomal-protein genes, the CAI reference set, stay in the table with ribosomal_protein = true; M8-08 excludes them from fitting and from univariate CAI statistics. ribosomal_protein is the C2 column when the gene table carries it, otherwise the §7.1.2 product / gene-name rule or the cai_reference gene flag.

Columns. Identity (locus_tag, tu_id, detected, abundance_log2, abundance_imputed, ribosomal_protein), then the 31 features of §7.8.1 in table order. Name map (feature ← source):

Feature Source promotech_max, promotech_tu gene table promoter_score, promoter_score_tu n_promoters_tu_to_gene C6 n_promoter_windows_tu (windows ≥ promotech_yes, lead decision 1) mw gene table mw_da replichore_position M5-09 context/gene_context.parquet (NA without it or without an oriC) in_prophage, in_bgc C8 region_genes with C7 region_type prophage / bgc; NA without C7/C8 dist_to_tu_start_bp computed: bp from the TU's first start codon to this gene's, in the direction of transcription, modulo the length on circular replicons; NA for a gene in no TU nterm_residue computed from C2 aa (the Met rule below) every other feature the gene-table column of the same name

The Met rule (decision 19). nterm_residue is residue 2 when residue 1 is M and residue 2 ∈ {A, C, G, P, S, T, V} (methionine aminopeptidase removes the initiator Met before small residues), else residue 1; NA for proteins shorter than 2 aa or with an empty aa (pseudogenes). It is a covariate only: nothing in mapping or annotation uses it (§16 excludes a recoding catalogue).

Transforms. None in the TSV (raw values). In model_matrix: tir_ostir and length_aa → natural log (lead decision 1; values ≤ 0 → NaN); start_codon one-hot over {ATG, GTG, TTG, other}, replicon_type over {chromosome, plasmid, unknown}, nterm_residue over the 20 residues (every level kept), named <feature>_<level>, an NA value giving NaN in every level; booleans 0/1. A feature that is NA on every row (a missing layer) stays in the TSV and is dropped from the matrix with all its encoded columns; the returned column → block map omits it, and a block left without columns is absent. Run flags (layer_missing:<layer>) are the step's (M8-10).

docs.title: Null and attribution
docs.text: Issue M8-09, modules giap.determinants.null and giap.determinants.attribution (pure). Outputs: one NullResult per model and tables/determinants_attribution.tsv (§9.3).

docs.title: The null
docs.text:
• Statistic: the observed mean CV R² over the 5 repeats (cv_r2_mean); one p per model, no BH (§8.1 "Determinant model"). p = (1 + b)/(1 + B), b = #{null R² ≥ observed} (perm_p, alternative="greater"); B = determinants.permutations (10,000 with --publication).
  • Permutation unit: TUs are grouped by their number of model rows (detected, non-imputed, non-ribosomal genes). Within a group of ≥ 2 TUs, whole TU response vectors move among the TUs, gene order inside a TU kept. A TU whose size is unique stays put (conservative).
  • Degenerate: if every TU size is unique, every permutation is the identity: no refit, b = B, p = 1, flag null_degenerate.
  • Refit: each permutation refits one CV repeat on the fixed repeat-1 folds (decision Q1). The folds depend only on the TUs, not on y, so conditioning on them is sound and the permutation test of the repeat-1 R² is exact.
  • Seeds: permutation b uses child b of SeedSequence([seed, crc32("determinants.null")]).spawn(B), so permutation b is the same for any B, and results are identical for any thread count.

docs.title: Conservativeness of the 5-repeat statistic
docs.text:
The 5-repeat observed mean against a 1-repeat null is not exact, but it is conservative in practice. Statistician runs (Slurm 1867304, 1867334, 1867348, 1867349; B = 99, 50 trees, 400 genes, R = 200 replicates), rejection at α 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 (binomial bound α + 2 SE: 0.024 / 0.081 / 0.142):

World LightGBM Elastic net clustered 0.010 / 0.040 / 0.105 0.000 / 0.005 / 0.020 (mean p 0.55) size 0.000 / 0.020 / 0.075 0.005 / 0.025 / 0.045 clustered, exact (observed = repeat-1 R²) 0.010 / 0.060 / 0.115 0.015 / 0.060 / 0.140
  • LightGBM is at nominal level; the elastic net is clearly conservative (0.005 against 0.060 for the exact version at α 0.05).
  • Swapping the observed statistic for the repeat-1 R² would restore power; this is an option, not a requirement.
  • The §8.4 gate tier (R = 20) is not a level claim: 0 of 20 rejections happens 36 % of the time for a level-0.05 test.

docs.title: Pass-1 limit (ADR-0034, accepted by Khoa)
docs.text:
The p is valid only when TU response blocks are exchangeable within size groups. It fails the statistician's attacks (R = 100, same jobs; bound at α 0.05: 0.094):

Attack LightGBM at α 0.05 Elastic net at α 0.05 inter-TU AR(1) abundance (ρ 0.9) with an independent AR(1) gc_local_dev 0.12 0.12 + replichore_position 0.95 0.41 detection selection (y ⊥ X; detection depends on y and length) 0.53 0.83
  • Why: permuting TUs destroys the response's autocorrelation, so the null is too narrow; scattered TU folds let a positional feature interpolate a gene's response from its neighbours; detection is a collider of abundance and the detectability covariates in the protein block.
  • Consequence: every NullResult carries null_uncalibrated (M8-10 copies it onto the null_p row). The p is not a discovery claim.
  • Committed arms: tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_determinants_null.py; they gate the level unless every result of an arm carries null_uncalibrated (the ADR-0032 pattern).

docs.title: Hardening owed (pass 2)
docs.text:
• Spatially contiguous CV folds (chunks of consecutive TUs) for both the observed CV and the null. In the statistician's probe this brings the AR(1) attack to level (EN 0.06, LightGBM 0.02 at α 0.05) with unchanged planted power; circular shifts within size groups did not.
  • A decision on positional features (replichore_position): exclude them from the null claim, or use a spatial null. Contiguous folds alone leave LightGBM at 0.70.
  • A detection-selection model. Stratifying the permutation by TU-mean detectability still fails (EN 0.46 at α 0.05).
  • Fresh folds per permutation stay a sensitivity option (decision Q1).

docs.title: SHAP attribution
docs.text:
• Scope: LightGBM only (pred_contrib=True, no shap package); the elastic net has no SHAP. The primary attribution is the elastic-net ΔR² (ADR-0033); SHAP describes the LightGBM fit only.
  • Per gene: in each repeat, the fold model that held the gene out gives its contribution vector; the vectors are averaged over the 5 repeats and summed by block into shap_transcription, shap_translation, shap_codon, shap_protein, shap_context (NA for a block with no column).
  • Additivity (§7.8.3): Σ block SHAP + mean expected value = the OOF LightGBM prediction, per gene. A guard raises if any row misses by more than 10⁻⁶ (the rows of X are not in fitted order); the unit tests hold the identity to 10⁻⁹.
  • Dominant block: for top-decile genes (model rows with abundance_log2 ≥ the linear 90th percentile), the block with the largest positive SHAP sum; NA when none is positive; ties by block order.

docs.title: Ribosomal rows
docs.text:
• Ribosomal-protein genes are the CAI reference, so their CAI is self-referential and lies outside the training range. They are excluded from fitting.
  • Detected, non-imputed ribosomal genes get rows predicted by the mean of all repeat × fold models (none saw them), with SHAP likewise averaged; additivity holds for the average.
  • These predictions are extrapolations (trees cannot extrapolate), labelled cai_reference. The rows are kept out of the residual SD and the top decile and are never residual-flagged.
  • Undetected ribosomal genes get no rows in pass 1.

docs.title: Residual flag
docs.text:
• residual = observed − predicted_log2 (the mean OOF LightGBM prediction).
  • |residual| > 2 SD (ddof 1, over model rows; two-sided, decision Q2) adds abundance_not_explained_by_sequence; SD exactly 0 sets no flag.
  • A descriptive screen, not a claim: about 4.6 % of genes are flagged under any model (statistician review of #173).
  • Fewer than 100 model rows: no SHAP and no null; rows have NA predictions and too_few_rows.

docs.title: Simulator worlds for the M8-15 gate (giapsim, M8-14)
docs.text: giapsim.scenarios.determinants_null / determinants_planted (issue M8-14, PR #251; §7.8.3, §11.3). Response: abundance_log2_true = mu + TU effect (SD 1, iid across TUs, ρ 0) + gene noise (noise_sd) + Σ_j β_j z_j, with z_j the ddof-0 z-score of the planted promoter (σ70 box score, one value per TU), RBS (Shine-Dalgarno score per gene) and CAI features. Detection is Bernoulli(p_true) on the M4-09 covariates, independent of the features and of the response. - True R² = Σβ² / (Σβ² + 1 + noise_sd²): the population R² of the three features, valid because the features are mutually uncorrelated and uncorrelated with the TU effect and with detection. Statistician probe (10 worlds of 3,000 genes): feature cross-correlations within ±0.07 and correlation of CAI and promoter with detection within ±0.04; OLS R² on the three features 0.206 (all genes) and 0.198 (detected genes) for a true 0.200. The arm determinants_true_r2_is_recovered_among_detected_genes gates this at true R² 0.2 and 0.5. - Null: the TU blocks are iid, so the M8-09 within-size-group TU permutation is exact here; the generator does not exercise the ADR-0034 attacks (AR(1) between TUs, positional features, detection selection), which stay in test_attack_determinants_null.py. - Dominant block truth (truth/determinants_genes.tsv) is argmax_j |β_j z_j|. M8-09's dominant block is the largest positive SHAP block sum in the top decile, so a recovery check should compare against argmax_j β_j z_j (signed) on the top-decile genes. - Feature names: the planted features are promoter, rbs and cai; the M8-07 feature frame reads promoter_score / promoter_score_tu, tir_ostir and cai from the gene table, so the M8-15 recovery run must write them into those columns.

docs.title: fgsea port (G15; GIAP_SPEC.md §7.7.4) — superseded by ADR-0038
docs.text:
Superseded. Since M8-17b, enrichment_gsea.tsv comes from R fgsea 1.36.2 (fgsea::fgseaMultilevel), run as a separate process (ADR-0038; docs/methods/function-gsea.md). The port below no longer produces any pipeline output. This note is kept as the history of M8-02 and as a reference: its function map names the fgsea 1.36.2 source behind each column of the recorded R calls that ReplayEngine replays (tests/helpers/fgsea_switch_data.py), and it documents SIMPLE_ENGINE, the in-process stand-in that unit tests inject in place of R. The hardening pass removes giap.stats.fgsea and its kernels unless Khoa keeps a no-R fallback (ADR-0038 item 6). Its 1/(1 + modeFraction) floor and the evidence below describe the port only, not the shipped engine.

GIAP's former preranked GSEA engine is a Python/numba port of fgsea 1.36.2 (MIT, © 2016-2019 Alexey Sergushichev; licence text in NOTICE.md), the version the golden environment runs (M8-12).

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
• Bioconductor 3.22 source tarball fgsea_1.36.2.tar.gz, sha256 d6996ff50410d363b717b634baab22e91d1ee88c70355d71ffcb9f075a525f5a; DESCRIPTION: git_url https://git.bioconductor.org/packages/fgsea, git_branch RELEASE_3_22, git_last_commit b7862b7 (2026-01-05).
  • Only scoreType std and gseaParam 1 are ported (M8-02 lead decision 2). No fgsea file is committed to GIAP.

docs.title: Function map (part I, M8-02)
docs.text: GIAP fgsea 1.36.2 giap.stats.fgsea.prepare R/fgsea.R preparePathwaysAndStats (finite check, sort(decreasing = TRUE), abs) and R/util.R preparePathways (minSize >= 1, maxSize <= N - 1, unique(na.omit(fmatch(...))), duplicate-name check) giap.stats.fgsea.gsea_es, _fgsea_kernels.es_walk R/fgsea.R calcGseaStat (std, returnLeadingEdge = TRUE) _fgsea_kernels.random_es_prefixes src/fastGSEA.cpp calcGseaStatCumulative (std; statEps weighting of zero stats) _fgsea_kernels.random_es_batch + the count loop of fgsea_simple src/fastGSEA.cpp calcGseaStatCumulativeBatch giap.stats.fgsea.fgsea_simple (NES, p, nMoreExtreme) R/fgsea.R fgseaSimpleImpl fgsea_simple (modeFraction, NaN rule, simple log2err, needs_multilevel) R/fgseaMultilevel.R fgseaMultilevel up to the split into dtSimpleFgsea / dtMultilevel, and multilevelError

docs.title: Behaviours reproduced and deviations
docs.text:
• No integer scaling. 1.36.2 computes ES on float |stats| (the 2³⁰/Σ rounding exists only on later masters; M8-02 lead decision 5).
  • Stable decreasing order: ties keep input order, and ES depends on it (fgsea warns about ties).
  • The ES = 0 tie (maxP == -minP) gives ES 0 and an empty leading edge; a negative ES's edge is rev(S[which.min(bottoms) .. m]); the positive edge stops at the first maximum.
  • Random ES of exactly 0 count in both leZero and geZero.
  • An even sampleSize is raised by one, as fgseaMultilevel does; sample_size < 3 raises instead of being silently raised to 3.
  • Prefix walk instead of the convex hull. fgsea's C++ finds each prefix's extremes with a block convex hull; GIAP walks every prefix directly (O(K²) per sample) with calcGseaStat's arithmetic, so a random ES of size k equals gsea_es on the same ranks. R's random stream is not reproduced: each chunk of 100 permutations draws from a child of rng.spawn (Generator.choice(N, K, replace = FALSE), random order like fgsea's shuffled combination).
  • Owed to M8-13: R accumulates some sums in long double, so near-ties may be decided differently in rare cases; the statEps weighting of zero stats in the random kernel is not pinned by tests.

docs.title: Statistical review (M8-02, statistician, 2026-10-21)
docs.text:
Checked against the official 1.36.2 tarball (sha256 above): R/fgsea.R lines 666–695 (counts, NES, p, nMoreExtreme) and R/fgseaMultilevel.R lines 100–200 (modeFraction, the < 10 rule, the Beta borders, multilevelError, the simple log2err). The port matches them line for line.

  • Validity of the simple p. Under fgsea's null (the tested set is a uniform random set of its size), the observed ES and the n_perm random ES are exchangeable, and the observed and random ES both go through es_walk. Conditional on the sign of ES, (1 + nMoreExtreme)/(1 + modeFraction) is therefore a +1 permutation p among the same-signed draws, and the min in fgsea's formula always picks that side: for ES > 0 the le-side ratio is ≥ 1, and ES = 0 gives p = 1. Marginally, the p is a mixture of two conditionally valid p-values, so it is valid too. Dropping sets with modeFraction < 10 depends only on the sign of ES and on the reference, so the sets that are kept stay conditionally valid, and BH over them (fgsea's p.adjust on non-NA) is not biased.
  • Evidence (seeded simulations, not committed; scripts in $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m802/): N = 2,500 iid stats, 40 random sets per replicate, 500 replicates, n_perm 1,000, set sizes 10/15/50/200/500, under six nulls (normal, centred lognormal, uncentred lognormal, half-integer ties, 40 % zeros, t₂). All 30 cells are at level, with the rejection rate ≤ 0.0117 / 0.0521 / 0.1046 at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 (20,000 p-values per cell). Exact ES = 0 ties: 0 in 36,000 random prefixes with k ≥ 10, except when every |stat| is equal. With equal |stats|, float rounding hides most exact ties, so the port gives ±x where exact arithmetic would give 0. That changes parity with R, not validity, because the observed and random ES share one rule.
  • The 1/(1 + modeFraction) floor. With m tests per BH family, the floor (≈ 1/501 for balanced stats) is above the BH cut for one rejection, 0.05/m, once m ≳ 25. Pass 1 (simple stage only) can therefore reject only when several sets sit at the floor together. With 200 sets and 20 shifted ones, power was 0 at shift 0.3 and 0.23 at shift 0.6 (mean FDP 0.019). Pass-1 GSEA is valid but has little power on large collections until M8-11 lands.
  • log2err is fgsea's Beta(k + 1, n − k) posterior SD of log2 of the unconditional tail probability (it uses n = n_perm, not modeFraction). For the conditional p it understates the error slightly. It is ported as is, as a precision label.
  • Known structure that this null does not keep (owed to M8-05/M8-15, not this port): (a) positional autocorrelation between TUs together with genomically clustered sets inflates the set-permutation p. With AR(1) φ = 0.5 TU scores and sets made of 5 clusters of 3 adjacent TUs, the rejection rate is 0.14 at α = 0.05; with one contiguous run of 15 TUs it is 0.22, and with φ = 0.8 it is 0.44. Scattered sets stay at level. (b) Stable tie order by TU ID (M8-05 rule 2) inflates level when many TUs tie at an extreme score, as with abundance.missing = min: with 30 % of TUs tied at the 2nd percentile and contiguous 15-TU sets, the rate is 0.165 at α = 0.05. A seeded random input order restores 0.053. Ties at the centre (median imputation after centring) do not bite (0.048).
  • RNG. rng.spawn children have distinct spawn keys and come from the SeedSequence, not from the parent's state. Draws made before the call therefore do not change the samples, and a second call on the same generator gets fresh children. Sampling without replacement is uniform (pair χ² p = 0.27 on N = 6, K = 3).

docs.title: Free entrapment: the FDP of A1's identifications
docs.text: Implements validation/pilot/entrapment.py (GIAP_SPEC.md §15.5 metric 8, §8.7; issue M10-07, docs/specs/M10-07-free-entrapment.md with its binding statistician decisions). Validation only: metric 8 gates nothing (§15.6) and is in no §8.1 testing family.

docs.title: Source
docs.text:
Wen B, Freestone J, Riffle M, MacCoss MJ, Noble WS, Keich U. "Assessment of false discovery rate control in tandem mass spectrometry analysis using entrapment." Nature Methods 22 (2025), doi:10.1038/s41592-025-02719-x (open access, CC BY 4.0). N_T and N_E are the numbers of original target and entrapment discoveries, and r is "the effective ratio of the entrapment to original target database size".

  • Equation (1), the combined method. FDP̂(T ∪ E) = N_E (1 + 1/r) / (N_T + N_E). Under an assumption analogous to the equal-chance assumption of target–decoy competition, the paper proves (Supplementary Note 2.2) that it is "an estimated upper bound, that is, on average it overestimates the true FDP". This is fdp_combined, §15.5's formula unchanged.
  • Equation (2), the lower bound. N_E / (N_T + N_E). If every entrapment discovery is false, it is a lower bound on the FDP (Supplementary Note 2.1). This is fdp_lower.
  • Why the sample method (3) is not used. N_E (1/r) / N_T estimates the FDP among the original targets only; the paper calls it "inherently flawed", so it is not computed.
  • The paired method needs one shuffled partner per target peptide (r = 1). A free entrapment has no such pairs, so it does not apply.

The statement about (1) is about expectation: a single estimate can fall below the realised FDP. The report therefore says "estimated upper bound", never "upper bound".

docs.title: Mapping onto the pilot
docs.text: A1 searched UniProt K-12 plus contaminants. Against Nissle spectra its peptides split into the original targets T, the K-12 peptides present in Nissle's translation (shared), and the entrapment E, the K-12-only peptides (k12_only). The entrapment is free: it is already in A1's database, and DIA-NN competed and filtered T and E together without knowing which is which. (It does use protein information in its precursor q-values, which breaks the symmetry in a known direction; see Bias.) So the combined method's quantity is the FDP of A1's accepted set after removing contaminant-sequence and not_in_universe discoveries. r is computed in silico: r = |k12_only| / |shared|.

docs.title: The universe and "present"
docs.text:
• Digest. D(F) = the distinct trypsin_p products of 7–30 aa with ≤ 1 missed cleavage (initiator M kept, giap.mapping.digest), I → L, with every product holding a residue outside the 20 standard letters dropped (non_standard). The universe is D(K-12) \ D(contaminants): a peptide a contaminant also yields could be a true contaminant identification, so it is removed on both sides.
  • Present. One function, applied unchanged to the in-silico universe and to the discoveries, with one index. Rule 1 (exact): an exact match in Nissle's six-frame translation (match_exact; I → L, both strands, the origin overlap of circular replicons), or (strain_db) a substring of a Bakta protein after I → L, which covers N-terminal products of non-ATG starts. Rule 2 (mass_equivalent): a tolerant target row (match_tolerant, GIAP's mapping.tolerant defaults, ≥ 10 aa) whose diff_types is non-empty and only block, the exact-composition exchanges of §7.2.4. near_block, swap, substitution and frameshift rows do not make a peptide present. Using one function on both sides keeps every asymmetry of the rules (for example that 7–9-aa peptides can only be present through rule 1) the same in r and in N_T, N_E.
  • Distinctness. I/L-collapsed on both sides and at both levels. Two K-12 library entries that differ only by I/L give one collapsed element two chances of a false match; this is rare.

docs.title: The searchable space
docs.text: Precursors carry carbamidomethyl on every C and 0 or 1 oxidised M (each oxidised position its own form), at charge 1–4 with 300 ≤ m/z ≤ 1800, m/z = (M + z · 1.007276) / z and M the residue masses plus 18.010565. At peptide level these bounds remove nothing: a 7–30-aa peptide weighs between 7 G + H₂O and 30 W + H₂O, carbamidomethyl-C and oxidised M lie inside the G–W residue range, and charges 1 and 4 together already cover that whole mass range. The bounds are still applied (they are parameters), and at precursor level they decide how many charge states a peptide has. r_prec = Σ_{k12_only} n_prec / Σ_shared n_prec is taken from these configured bounds, not from DIA-NN's library.

docs.title: Levels and the assessment rule
docs.text:
q_value is DIA-NN's experiment-wide precursor Global.Q.Value, so the set of distinct accepted precursors (norm(modified_peptide), charge), pooled over the wild-type runs, is the only unit whose FDR the search claims to control at α = 0.01.

What DIA-NN 2.3.1 has already filtered. The DIA-NN documentation for 2.3.1 (README at 2fb4df2, "GUI settings reference" and "Main output reference") says that the precursor FDR setting (--qvalue) is "the precursor q-value filtering to be applied to the main output report", and, of the recommended main-report filters, only "Q.Value at 0.01" is "done by DIA-NN automatically"; the global, library and protein-group q-values (Global.Q.Value, Lib.Q.Value, PG.Q.Value, Global.PG.Q.Value, Lib.PG.Q.Value) are listed as filters for the user to apply, because "the main report is designed to be filtered". The matrices, which the pilot does not use, are filtered at 1 % with global protein-group q-values. A1 sets --qvalue 0.01 and no flag that changes these defaults (validation/pilot/diann_A1.cfg). The accepted set is therefore the precursors with run-level Q.Value ≤ 0.01 (DIA-NN) and Global.Q.Value ≤ 0.01 (GIAP, Q_ACCEPT). No FDR claim attaches to that intersection itself: a subset of an FDR-controlled list is not FDR-controlled in general. The run-level filter removes only rows that are low-scoring in their run, so in practice it lowers the false share, and the pooled set stays the closest unit to one with a stated FDR. This is why α is the reference there and only there. No protein-level filter is applied by either. A1 also runs without --no-refine-q, so the precursor q-values use protein information (see Bias and the next paragraph).

The assessment is issued only at precursor level:

  • evidence_of_failure if fdp_lower > α (checked first);
  • consistent_with_control if fdp_combined ≤ α (inclusive);
  • inconclusive otherwise; not_evaluable when there are no discoveries or no shared peptides.

Both comparisons are exact rationals (fractions.Fraction, α = 1/100): fdp_combined is computed as N_E (k + s) / (k (N_T + N_E)) with k = |k12_only| and s = |shared|, which equals equation (1) because 1 + 1/r = (k + s)/k. These are the paper's three readings (Fig. 1b).

What the labels do and do not say. The labels are readings of point estimates, not tests, and carry no error rate:

  • consistent_with_control. It does not mean that the FDP is at most α at any stated confidence. In the attack's equal-chance scenario A, with a mean true FDP of 1.6 % (above α), about 15 % of lists read consistent_with_control, because fdp_combined is noisy. In scenario F, a search whose true FDR is about 0.5 α, about 11 % of lists read inconclusive. ucb95 ≤ α is the stronger reading, and holds only under its model.
  • The A1 settings. The upper-bound property behind this label needs equal chance. DIA-NN's documentation calls --no-refine-q "essential" for validating its precursor q-values with classic entrapment, and A1 runs without it. So for A1, consistent_with_control has less support than the paper's reading.
  • evidence_of_failure. It needs only that every entrapment discovery is false. It is therefore unaffected by equal-chance violations, but not by the genome and contamination caveats.

The peptide level is §15.5's number but is not assessed (not_assessed): DIA-NN claims no FDR for the distinct peptides derived from its precursor list, and false precursors spread over distinct peptides while true ones cluster, so a peptide-level FDP above α is not evidence that the search failed. Per-run blocks are descriptive and not assessed either, because the rows were selected by the global q-value together with the run-level one, and no FDR claim attaches to a run's intersection. Estimates are reported unclipped and flagged above_one when equation (1) exceeds 1, which small counts allow.

docs.title: Uncertainty
docs.text:
• fdp_lower is a realised bound, not an estimate. If every entrapment discovery is false, the realised FDP of this list is at least fdp_lower, with no sampling error. The condition is that the genome is complete and is the sample's strain, and that no K-12 material is in the sample. The report calls it a realised lower bound, conditional on these caveats.
  • ucb95, a one-sided 95 % upper confidence bound for the FDP. Model: the equal chance assumption in its plainest form, with independent false matches. Given M false discoveries among N = N_T + N_E, N_E ~ Binomial(M, π) with π = k/(k + s) = r/(1 + r); then N_E/π estimates M without bias, and fdp_combined = N_E/(π N). The bound inverts the exact one-sided test: M_max = max{M ∈ {N_E, …, N} : BinomCDF(N_E; M, π) > 0.05} and ucb95 = M_max / N. It bounds the realised FDP M/N, which lies on the grid {0, 1/N, …, 1}, so it is at most 1 and can sit below an unclipped fdp_combined (above one, or π close to 1); it is never below min(fdp_combined, 1) by a full grid step 1/N. It is not valid under clustered (protein-level) errors, and no two-sided interval is given. At precursor level π comes from the precursor sums.
  • A protein-block bootstrap was rejected: the discoveries are one realised list, and the resampling unit for false matches is not the protein of the discovered peptides.

docs.title: Bias
docs.text:
Source Direction Near-homolog entrapment: every K-12-only peptide near a Nissle variant has its neighbour's signal in the sample, so neighbour-driven errors concentrate on E (§15.5 "errs high") high 7–9-aa variant peptides are not tolerantly matched, so they stay in E high The tolerant route reports only minimal-cost loci; a block-only locus behind a cheaper non-block locus is not seen high, negligible An incomplete genome, a different strain, or K-12 material in the sample (carryover, lab contamination) makes some K-12-only discoveries true; the lower bound then stops being a bound high Six-frame chance hits move short K-12-only peptides into shared lower N_E (a more conservative lower bound); negligible for equation (1) E and T differ in length and charge composition, so equal chance per precursor mis-weights the peptide-level r (sensitivity.r_prec_weighted) either False matches attracted to T, e.g. interference from abundant co-eluting shared proteins (equal-chance violation in the low direction) low, unquantified A protein-level filter (PG.Q.Value) would remove K-12-only proteins first; neither DIA-NN's main report nor GIAP applies one (DIA-NN 2.3.1 docs, above), and adding one is a lead finding low DIA-NN's precursor q-values use protein information unless --no-refine-q is set, which the docs call "essential if the goal is validation of DIA-NN's precursor-level q-values using classic entrapment"; A1 does not set it. False matches are favoured on proteins with many true identifications. In A1's database those are mostly K-12 proteins with an expressed Nissle ortholog, whose peptides are mostly shared and whose few K-12-only peptides are the variant peptides. K-12-specific proteins, almost all E, and unexpressed proteins are penalised. The E share among favoured elements is below π, so false matches go to T more often than equal chance assumes (the attack's scenario D shows this direction). This is an equal-chance violation; fdp_lower is unaffected low, unquantified K-12-derived constructs in engineered strains excluded: only wild-type runs are accepted

Sensitivities, pre-registered and descriptive (no assessment): present_broad widens rule 2 to rows of block, swap and near_block only; r_prec_weighted uses r_prec in equation (1); far restricts E to K-12-only peptides of ≥ 10 aa with no tolerant target row of any type, and T to shared peptides of ≥ 10 aa, and reports the split of k12_only and N_E into lt10, near_homolog and far.

docs.title: Simulation evidence
docs.text:
tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_free_entrapment.py (statistician; seed seeds.calibration_base + 707) simulates a protein-grouped universe with r = 0.25 and checks: the mean of fdp_combined is at least the mean true FDP under equal chance (edge and uniform), and with whole-protein clustered errors; the excess grows with homolog attraction λ ∈ {1, 2, 4}; attraction to T biases low; fdp_lower never exceeds the true FDP; no list with true FDP ≤ α is labelled evidence_of_failure; and ucb95 covers at ≥ 95 % under equal chance. Two teeth checks show the tests can fail: fdp_lower used as an estimate fails the mean check, and a median bound fails the coverage check.

Recorded, not gated (R = 2,000):

  • ucb95 coverage. About 0.72 under whole-protein clustered errors (E) and about 0.75 under attraction to T (D). This is why its assumes string excludes them.
  • Labels in scenario A (mean true FDP 1.6 %): 15 % of lists read consistent_with_control.
  • Labels in scenario F (true FDR about 0.5 α): 89 % read consistent_with_control, 11 % inconclusive, and none evidence_of_failure.

docs.title: Function collections (M8-03)
docs.text: Gene sets for ORA (§7.7.3) and GSEA (§7.7.4) are built by giap.function.collections.build_collections. The installed resources are read by giap.io.function_resources.read_resources.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Who can be a member: only genes eligible for detection-aware testing (giap.genetable.eligible: not partial, and a finite p_detect). Empty sets are left out.
  • Coverage: the share of eligible genes in at least one set. It is NaN when no gene is eligible.

docs.title: GO (go_bp, go_mf, go_cc)
docs.text:
• Annotations: gene-table go_terms IDs are mapped to their primary term through go-basic alt_id. Obsolete or absent IDs are dropped and counted in n_unknown_ids, once per (eligible gene, ID).
  • Propagation: annotations are propagated to every ancestor over is_a and part_of, as GO.db and topGO do; goatools' default would be is_a only. The three namespace roots are then removed.
  • Namespaces: go-basic has no cross-namespace edges, which was checked on release 2026-05-19.
  • Parents: parents holds each term's direct non-root parents in the same namespace. GO elim uses it.

docs.title: GO slim (go_slim)
docs.text:
• Membership: a gene belongs to a slim term when the term is in the gene's full propagated ancestor set.
  • Testing: the collection mixes namespaces and is tested with classic tests only.

docs.title: KEGG
docs.text:
• Sets: one per mapNNNNN, built from the path:map rows of link/pathway/ko.
  • Excluded: the global and overview maps (ADR-0023).
  • Unknown KOs: a KO absent from the link table counts as unknown. That includes valid KOs that have no pathway.

docs.title: COG
docs.text: One set per COG 2020 functional-category letter from the gene table's cog_category, with names from fun-20.tab. - is not a category.

docs.title: Run flags
docs.text:
• layer_missing:go drops all four GO collections. A missing slim alone drops only go_slim.
  • layer_missing:kegg and layer_missing:cog are raised when those resources are absent.
  • bakta_db_light is raised when the annotation came from the Bakta light database.

docs.title: Abundance GSEA (M8-05, engine M8-17b)
docs.text: giap.function.gsea.gsea_table tests whether a gene set's genes rank high or low by protein abundance (§7.7.4). It ranks TUs, not genes, and hands the ranking to R fgsea 1.36.2 (fgsea::fgseaMultilevel), run as a separate process (ADR-0038, M8-17). The Python/numba port of M8-02 (docs/methods/fgsea-port.md) is superseded; it survives only as SIMPLE_ENGINE, the in-process stand-in that unit tests inject.

docs.title: Engine (ADR-0038)
docs.text:
• Environment. workflow/envs/fgsea.yml (giap-fgsea): r-base 4.5.3, bioconductor-fgsea 1.36.2 and r-data.table 1.18.6.1 from conda-forge and bioconda, installed from the explicit lock workflow/envs/locks/fgsea.explicit.txt. No Bioconductor data package is needed, so nothing is fetched from bioconductor.org. fgsea is conda-only under every profile for now (M8-17 lead decision 9).
  • Call. workflow/bin/giap_fgsea.R runs under Rscript --vanilla and calls fgseaMultilevel(sampleSize = 101, eps = 0, nPermSimple = 1000, minSize, maxSize, scoreType = "std", nproc = 1) with the function.gsea defaults. eps = 0 means the multilevel stage estimates p with no lower bound, so there is no 1/(1 + nPermSimple) floor. The engine's method is fgsea_multilevel.
  • Seed. gsea_table keeps one generator, for_step("function.gsea", seed). It draws the tie order (perm = rng.permutation(n)) and then one integer r_seed = rng.integers(1, 2**31 - 1). R runs set.seed(r_seed) before every job, and nproc = 1 (SerialParam) makes a rerun byte-identical (acceptance A2, Slurm 1868835).
  • At most two R calls per step. The main call holds one job per collection with an in-range set (main:<collection>). The second call holds every GO redundancy re-test of every GO collection (retest:<collection>:<term>) with the same ranking and the same r_seed; it is made only when at least one re-test exists. With no job at all, R is not called and the table is header-only.
  • Shared seed. The re-test's Monte Carlo draws are common random numbers with the main call's. Each p is still a valid marginal estimate, and p_re only enters its own collection's BH vector, whose main p values already share one permutation set inside fgsea; so the shared seed adds only dependence of the kind BH already faces (statistician, PR #214). BH never crosses collections.
  • Failure. Any R error fails the function step with exit 4 and writes no partial GSEA table (M8-17 lead decision 5). R's warnings (for example fgsea's ties warning) go into the function.gsea_engine event, never into errors.
  • Licence. fgsea is MIT (NOTICE.md); R is GPL-2. Both run only as a separate program started by the step; nothing under src/ imports or links them (R5; scripts/ci/check_imports.py, check_no_rscript.py).

docs.title: Ranking unit: TUs
docs.text:
• Scoring genes: detected, not partial, with a finite p_detect and an abundance (abundance_log2 not NA). Imputed abundances count (ADR-0028); the §8.6 sensitivity reruns vary the imputation.
  • TU score: the mean abundance_log2 of the TU's scoring genes. Only TUs with at least one scoring gene are ranked.
  • Centring: scores are centred on their median over ranked TUs (ADR-0028). Raw log2 abundances are all positive, so scoreType = std would make the test effectively one-sided. Centring changes the weights only, so validity under exchangeability is unchanged.
  • Ties: ties enter fgsea in one seeded random order per run, drawn from the function.gsea stream: stats.tsv lists the TUs in that order, and fgsea's stable sort keeps it. Re-tests share that order.
  • Membership: a TU is in a set when any of its scoring genes is. A detected gene without an abundance gives its TU no membership; §7.7.4's "detected genes" is read as scoring genes.
  • Size: set sizes are counted in TUs, and the function.gsea_size filter applies to them. R's reported size must equal Python's count, or the call fails.
  • A set covering every ranked TU has no complement: its running sum has no miss step, and every permutation gives the same set, so ES and its null are degenerate. It is never sent to R. When its size is within function.gsea_size and its collection has a job, it gets an NA row flagged unestimated; a collection with no job adds no row, and no job anywhere gives a header-only table (M8-17 lead decision 6a). This mirrors the ORA whole-universe rule.

docs.title: Family and multiple testing
docs.text:
• BH family: BH runs per collection over the size-filtered sets, with both ES signs in one family (§8.1). Unestimated sets (NaN p, including the whole-ranking row) are left out of m. R must return a row for every set it was sent (read_results), so it cannot silently shrink m.
  • p-values: fgsea multilevel p with eps = 0, so small p go below 1/1001 (minimum 1.2e-4 in the R = 300 null run) and BH can reject single sets in large collections. This is the engine §7.7.4 and §8.1 ask for.
  • unestimated: fgsea's unbalanced-signs case returns NA p and NES; the row keeps its ES, and its q is NA.
  • log2err: fgsea's Monte Carlo precision label for p. When the multilevel stage cannot estimate it (isCpGeHalf FALSE), fgsea sets log2err to NA and warns that the p is likely overestimated. GIAP keeps that p in BH, which is level-safe because the p is conservative, and flags the row log2err_unestimated. The flag excludes unestimated (an NA p implies an NA log2err) and sits where unestimated would in the flag order.

docs.title: GO redundancy
docs.text:
• The re-test: a significant GO set with at least one significant descendant is re-tested without the genes of all its significant descendants. TU membership is rebuilt, so a TU stays when another of its scoring genes is still in the reduced set. The re-test uses min_size 1.
  • Deciding redundant: the re-test p replaces the set's main p in a copy of the collection's p vector, and redundant is true when that substituted BH q is above α.
  • Reported q: q_value stays the main-run BH q.
  • Degenerate re-tests: a 0-TU re-test gives redundant = true plus size_filtered. A NaN re-test p gives redundant = NA.
  • parent_group: the most general significant ancestor, meaning the one with the shortest path (in parents steps) to a term without parents, ties broken by ID. A set with no significant ancestor is its own group.

docs.title: What a row claims (restricted claim)
docs.text:
• p-values are valid under TU exchangeability.
  • There is no level claim for genomically clustered sets under positional autocorrelation (ADR-0025).
  • Results are conditional on detection, with no p_detect adjustment (ADR-0026).
  • NES has no CI; every row carries ci_unestimated (ADR-0027, a deviation from §8.2).
  • "Significant and non-redundant" is not an FDR-controlled list.
  • "No significant set" never means "no enrichment": power is limited by set sizes in TUs, by the number of ranked TUs and by detection, and the result is conditional on detection (above).

The two position flags below mark the rows where the last two limits are most likely to matter. An unflagged row is not a guarantee (see Limits).

docs.title: Position flags (M8-05b; spec decision 9, ADR-0025, ADR-0026)
docs.text:
Both flags are computed for every main-run row, are pure and use no RNG. Redundancy re-tests compute no flags; a re-tested parent keeps the flags of its main run. They follow the existing flags in the order ci_unestimated, unestimated, size_filtered, genomic_cluster, detection_confounded.

  • genomic_cluster (δ ≥ τ = 0.15). δ estimates how much the set's member TUs inflate the variance of its mean score, relative to the TU-label permutation null, if TU scores were AR(1) with φ₀ = 0.5 along the genome.
  • Order: ranked TUs are split by replicon (contig) and kept in natural TU-ID order (genome order, from build_tus); unranked TUs are skipped, so members with only unranked TUs between them are adjacent. On a circular replicon (C1 topology == "circular") d = min(|i − j|, n_r − |i − j|); every other topology is linear. Members on different replicons are never paired.
  • Statistic: with w(d) = 0.5^d for 1 ≤ d ≤ 10 (else 0), k member TUs and n ranked TUs, C = (2/k) Σ_{member pairs} w(d), E[C] = 2(k − 1) P_w / (n(n − 1)) with P_w = Σ w(d) over all pairs of ranked TUs, and δ = (C − E[C]) / (1 − k/n); δ = 0 when k < 2 or k ≥ n. δ is centred at 0 for randomly placed sets of any size.
  • detection_confounded (|z| ≥ z₀ = 1 with the sign that produces the observed ES). Counted in genes over the eligible universe (non-partial, finite p_detect): M eligible genes, N scoring genes, n eligible genes of the gene-level set (undetected members included), x of them scoring. With f = N/M and v = n f (1 − f)(M − n)/(M − 1), z = (x − n f)/√v (z = 0 when v = 0). The row is flagged when ES is finite and ≠ 0 (unestimated rows included, since their ES is a real statistic) and z · ES < 0 with |z| ≥ 1; when ES = 0, when |z| ≥ 1. A NaN ES (the whole-ranking row) is treated as 0.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• genomic_cluster is calibrated only for φ ≤ 0.5: the kernel fixes φ₀ = 0.5, and at φ = 0.7 unflagged rows are anti-conservative at α = 0.01 (0.0165 against 0.0143). It uses ranked-TU order, not bp distance. The claim is per-row level, not FDR among unflagged rows.
  • detection_confounded is a screen, not a guarantee. In mixed-confounding worlds (s ~ U(0, 1.5), β ∈ {1, 2}) unflagged rows reject at about 1.3α / 1.15α / 1.07α at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 (pooled R ≈ 12,600: 0.0128 / 0.0567 / 0.1073), above the §8.4 bound; unscreened rows in the same worlds reject at about 0.25 at α = 0.05. Under an unconfounded null, unflagged rows reject at about 1.1α (0.0551 / 0.1088 at 0.05 / 0.10), because flagged null rows are conservative. Rows with |z| < 1 keep a small bias that no detected-fraction threshold can screen out. It reacts to observed detection, so a real effect with an opposite-sign detection difference is flagged too; about 13–16 % of rows are flagged under an unconfounded null.
  • q values of unflagged rows come from a BH family that includes flagged rows. A flagged row whose p is anti-conservative acts like a signal in BH and lowers the cut for every row of the collection, so unflagged null rows can be rejected more often. The only measurement (10 flagged sets among 40: FWER of unflagged null rows 0.004–0.02 without them, 0.022–0.057 with them; Slurm 1867330) was made on the port, whose 1/500 floor kept BH from rejecting, so it does not carry over to the R engine. Open (statistician): the spillover limit is not re-justified for the R engine and has to be re-measured on R; until then no FWER or FDR claim is made for unflagged rows in a collection with flagged rows.
  • The detection-screen figures above and the genomic_cluster φ = 0.7 figure were measured on the port engine. The flag screens themselves use no RNG and do not depend on the engine, but their at-level numbers must be re-measured on R before the hardening pass removes the port (statistician, PR #214 N4).
  • The hardening ADRs (a rotation null; censored or p_detect-weighted ranks) remove both limits.

docs.title: R engine (shipped)
docs.text: Rates are rejection rates at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 with the §8.4 bounds from tolerances.yaml. The R-engine arms run on Slurm only (slow, requires_r), in the weekly gsea task of the full-calibration array (calsuite gsea); that task needs the giap-fgsea env built. In every arm the fast tier (R = 50) reuses replicates 0..49 of the full arm's stream, so the fast arm is a prefix of the full arm and not independent evidence. - Single-set level (Slurm 1868835, tests/calibration/test_gsea_r_engine_calibration.py, R = 300, all pass): - null: 0.017 / 0.057 / 0.127 (bounds 0.021 / 0.075 / 0.135); KS against U(0, 1) p = 0.78, so the slight excess over nominal is Monte Carlo noise, not a shape problem; - attack 3, operon-packed sets after the TU collapse: 0.003 / 0.020 / 0.047 (KS p = 0.08, slightly conservative); - ties (40 % of TUs tied at the minimum score, as with abundance.missing = min; contiguous 15-TU sets) in the seeded order: 0.007 / 0.030 / 0.093 (KS p = 0.19). - Reproducibility: two step runs with one seed are byte-identical (A2, Slurm 1868835). - BH per collection, without the floor (statistician's attacks, Slurm 1869053, tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_gsea_r_engine.py, code at e3c4614; 12 passed; R = 300, records in $GIAP_ROOT/logs/calibration/pr214/gsea.jsonl). GO-like nested collection: 1,000 TUs (E. coli operon lengths, ρ 0.8), 10 parents each the union of 3 children of 10–25 TUs, 20 standalone sets of 10–60 TUs. - complete null, FWER (= FDR here) at q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10: 0.007 / 0.050 / 0.123 (bounds 0.021 / 0.075 / 0.135); - first child of 3 parents shifted by +1.5, mean FDP: 0.006 / 0.037 / 0.073 (bounds 0.015 / 0.062 / 0.115). Here parents and children are significant together, so the second R call (the GO re-test with the shared seed) runs live; the test asserts that it ran. - Structure arms on R (same job, R = 300, all at level): - median imputation: 0.007 / 0.043 / 0.087; - size-biased membership: 0.000 / 0.017 / 0.067; - scattered between-TU AR(1) (φ 0.5): 0.010 / 0.050 / 0.120. - Teeth on R (same job): attack 3 ranked at gene level (R = 50) and ties sent to R in TU-ID order (R = 300) are both confirmed fails through calibrate, so the R arms above can fail. Teeth log to a private directory, so their rates are not in the record file. The port's teeth stay in tests/calibration/test_gsea_tu_calibration.py.

docs.title: Port (superseded, history only)
docs.text: These were measured on fgsea_simple, whose 1/500 floor kept BH from rejecting; they do not carry over to the R engine. - Single-set level at R = 4,000 (statistician, Slurm 1867122): rejection 0.0508 at α = 0.05 under the null. Attack 3, the ties, median imputation and scattered AR(1) are all at level. - Family probe (GO-like nested sets, R = 2,000): FWER 0.0015 at q 0.05 under the complete null. With shifted children, FDR is 0.017 at q 0.05 and 0.053 at q 0.10 (shift +1.5), and 0.0035 / 0.024 (shift +0.8). - Committed arms: tests/calibration/test_gsea_tu_calibration.py (which also holds the port's attack 3 and ties teeth) and tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_gsea_structure.py (Slurm 1867070: 14 passed, 2 strict xfails). - Position flags (statistician, #174): full tier R = 300 (Slurm 1867323: 33 passed, 2 strict xfails); R = 4,000 per arm (Slurm 1867332; cluster φ 0.5 mix at level, detection as in Limits); BH-family spillover (Slurm 1867330). Committed arms: tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_gsea_flags.py (detection arms gated at ≤ 1.5α).

docs.title: Function module: detection enrichment primitives
docs.text:
Implements giap.stats.wallenius and giap.function.elim (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.7.3, §7.7.5, §8.1 row "Category detection", §8.2, §8.3; issue M8-01, docs/specs/M8-01-stats-wallenius-elim.md, lead decisions 1–4; M8-index lead decision 5). The families, the effect size and parent_group are M8-04's: see "Detection enrichment" below, which replaces the Wallenius p with the TU-counted conditional Poisson-binomial (ADR-0029). The ora suite and attack 2 are M8-15's.

Status: statistician review of #153 (2026-10-21). The primitives are approved as implemented. The method is not yet approved as a calibrated test: the mean-odds Wallenius null fails the §8.4 ORA null and attack 2 (see "Calibration evidence"). See Sign-off.

docs.title: Quantities
docs.text:
Per category C over the eligible universe U that the caller passes:

  • M = |U|, n = |C ∩ U|, N = the number detected, k = the number detected in C;
  • the odds ω = mean(p_detect in C) / mean(p_detect outside C). This is goseq's weighting with p_detect as the PWF. Algebraically it equals avg_w·(M − n)/(Σp − n·avg_w), and a unit test pins the identity.

ω is NaN when C or its complement is empty, or when the outside mean is 0. Those categories are not tested; M8-04 writes them unestimated. ω = 0 is allowed and is exact: X = lo almost surely. ω = 1 uses the central hypergeometric pmf.

docs.title: Tails: direct sums of the pmf
docs.text:
p_over = Σ_{j=k}^{hi} pmf(j) and p_under = Σ_{j=lo}^{k} pmf(j), with lo = max(0, N − (M − n)) and hi = min(n, N). Both are math.fsum sums (correctly rounded) of scipy's nchypergeom_wallenius.pmf, clipped to [0, 1].

These are the same quantities as the spec's .sf(k − 1) / .cdf(k). The sums are used because scipy computes sf as 1 − cdf, which cancels to 0.0 below about 1e-16 (M8-01 example 1: true 3.2e-14, sf returns 0). p_over and p_under are each a valid one-sided p under the urn model: they include the observed k, so p_over + p_under − pmf(k) = 1.

docs.title: Fail-closed range (lead decision 4)
docs.text:
Outside ω ∈ [1e-6, 1e6] scipy's pmf turns NaN, and near 1e±300 it aborts the process. A pmf that is non-finite or does not sum to 1 ± 1e-6 also raises ValueError. M8-04 reports such a category unestimated, flag odds_out_of_range.

Is the range statistically acceptable for pass 1? Yes. - Upper bound. ω ≤ 1/mean(p outside C). With a size cap of 500, the outside mean is close to the run's detection rate (about 0.3–0.7), so ω > 1e6 cannot occur. With fewer than 50 detected genes, detectability_constant sets ω = 1. - Lower bound. ω < 1e-6 needs every member of C to have p_detect below 1e-6 × the outside mean. - Simulation. I used 300 giapsim genomes (M ≈ 4,450, M4-13 cross-fitted p̂). The smallest p̂ was 2.7e-4. The worst possible size-5 category (the five smallest p̂) had ω ≥ 1.1e-3, with a median of 1.1e-2. - Accuracy inside the range. Against an exact forward urn DP, the tails at ω ∈ {1e-6, 1e-4, 1e-2, 1e2, 1e4, 1e6} are within 5e-11 relative error, for M up to 4,500 and tails ≥ 1e-8. - No spurious failures. Over 400 random (M ≤ 12,000, n ≤ 500, ω ∈ [1e-3, 1e3]) cases, the pmf-sum check never raised.

So the fail-closed path is a safety net, not an expected outcome. It is R4-honest because the category is labelled unestimated, never given a p. - Elim caveat. elim recomputes ω on a reduced set, which can be a single gene; a single gene with p̂ < 1e-6 × the outside mean would also fail closed. This is not seen in the simulations.

docs.title: Far-tail precision of scipy's pmf (lead decision 2)
docs.text:
Compared against the exact urn DP over 60 random (M ≤ 1,500) urns and every k (15,585 tails), the maximum relative error per tail magnitude was:

true tail max relative error ≥ 1e-4 5e-10 1e-8 – 1e-4 3e-7 1e-11 – 1e-8 2e-4 1e-13 – 1e-11 0.04 < ~1e-14 up to 1 (scipy's pmf returns exactly 0.0, so p = 0)

Decisions at BH q ≤ 0.1 and at the elim cut are unaffected. - BH. BH q is a continuous, coordinatewise-monotone function of the p vector. A relative error ε in each p moves each q by at most ε relative. A q near 0.1 in a family of m ≤ ~3,000 terms needs p ≥ 0.1/m ≈ 3e-5, where ε ≤ 5e-10. - elim. The elim cut at 0.01 sees ε ≤ 1e-11. - Deep tails. Tails below 1e-11 have q below about 1e-7, far below any threshold. A deep tail returned as 0 is still below every threshold, and ties at 0 do not change which terms pass.

What it does affect: - Reported precision. p_value = 0 can appear in enrichment_detection.tsv for true values around 1e-14 and below. That precision is not real. - M8-13 golden. The relative-1e-6 comparison with goseq cannot hold for p below about 1e-9 unless both sides are exact there.

Both are pass-2 items: a log-space or exact pmf, an ADR if needed, and never a tolerance change.

docs.title: The approximation and the attack it implies
docs.text:
Mean-odds Wallenius is exact only for its own model. That model is sequential weighted sampling of N genes without replacement, with weight ∝ p_detect and a single weight inside C and another outside. The fast calibration test (tests/calibration/test_wallenius_calibration.py) draws exactly that urn, so it checks the code, not the method.

The §8.4 ORA null is a different model. There, detection depends only on p_detect: each gene is detected independently with probability p_i. Given N, that law is the multivariate Fisher non-central hypergeometric distribution with odds p_i/(1 − p_i), not a Wallenius urn with weights p_i. Mean-odds Wallenius departs from it in two ways: 1. Saturation. With N/M ≈ 0.5, as in proteomics, the urn's mean of k is pulled toward the central value. Example: p = 0.9 in C and 0.5 outside, n = 60, M = 4,000, ω = 1.8. Wallenius gives E[k | N] ≈ 43, but the truth is 54. So |log ω| is effectively too small. A low-p_detect category then looks under-detected, and a high-p_detect one over-detected. The two approximations agree only when p_detect ≪ 1, which is goseq's DE setting. 2. Heterogeneity within C (Jensen). A category that mixes p = 0.02 and p = 0.9 genes is not one urn colour. A hazard-weight variant (ω from mean −log(1 − p)) fixes 1 but not 2: it stays at level for homogeneous categories, yet rejects 52 % at α = 0.01 for the mixed one.

The exact test under the §8.4 null is the conditional Poisson-binomial ("conditional Bernoulli"):

P(k | N) = PB_C(k) · PB_{U∖C}(N − k) / PB_U(N),

where PB_A is the Poisson-binomial pmf of the p_i in A. The DP costs O(n² + (M − n)·N) per category: tens of milliseconds vectorised at M = 4,500, and the poisson_binomial_sf primitive of §8.3 already exists. Multiplying every p_i/(1 − p_i) by a constant does not change it, so a global intercept miscalibration of p_detect cancels. This is the Poisson-binomial fallback the issue asks the note to name. Swapping it in is an ADR for Khoa (see Sign-off).

TU dependence (new ORA attack, §8.5 "new attacks"). - What it is. Detection really depends on abundance, which TUs share. p_detect uses physicochemical covariates only. So detection is positively correlated within a TU beyond p_detect, and a category packed into few operons has an over-dispersed k. - Who fails. Every gene-independent null fails this attack, the exact conditional Poisson-binomial included. It is the ORA analogue of attack 3, and §8.2 "resample TUs, not genes" applies. - Candidate fixes. A TU-level count (TUs as units, as in the GSEA collapse), or a design-effect variance from the within-TU correlation of d − p_detect. M8-15 must calibrate either.

docs.title: Effect size
docs.text: OraResult.odds is the weighting ω, not an effect. §8.2 requires an effect with a 95 % CI on every p or q. M8-04 reports O − E = k − Σ_C p_detect with the CI NA in pass 1; that CI is owed. A test-consistent effect would be the conditional MLE of a log-odds shift δ for members of C (the odds p_i/(1 − p_i) multiplied by e^δ), with an exact CI by inverting the CPB test. The TU-block bootstrap CI of O − E (M4-16 construction) is the TU-aware alternative.

docs.title: Algorithm
docs.text:
Terms are visited deepest first: level = the longest path to a root, ties broken by term ID. Each term is tested on its genes minus those removed for it. A term whose elim p is strictly below 0.01 (topGO's < cutOff) removes the genes it was tested on from every ancestor (the transitive closure). M and N stay fixed. M8-04 recomputes ω on the reduced set.

p_classic is the test on the full set. An empty remainder gives NaN, and M8-04 writes it unestimated. Cycles raise before any test runs. M8-04 runs elim for the over direction of go_bp, go_mf and go_cc only; every other family uses p_value = p_classic.

docs.title: Validity of BH on elim p (§8.1 family = (collection, direction))
docs.text:
The elim p is conditional on the removal steps, which depend on the same data. Alexa et al. (2006) and the topGO documentation present elim p as conditional scores and do not derive multiplicity control for them. BH on elim p is not covered by the BH theorem: its dependence is neither independent nor PRDS by any argument I know. In the direction it is run, the selection bias is conservative: - removal takes out genes of a significantly over-detected descendant; - this leaves the ancestor's remainder depleted, while N still counts the removed genes; - conditioning on non-significant descendants also biases their genes downwards.

Applying the over removals to an under test would be anti-conservative. M8-04 avoids this: under is never elim'd.

Simulation. I built a synthetic GO-like DAG: 2,000 genes; 200 leaves of 5–30 genes; 60 mid-level terms, each the union of 2–6 leaves plus 5 own genes; 15 top terms; the true-path rule; multiple parents; size filter [5, 500]. p = 0.5 everywhere, so the central hypergeometric is the exact conditional null. "Planted" leaves get p_plant. BH ran at 0.05 within the one family, with R = 1,000 per row.

setting FWER, complete-null terms (classic / elim) mean FDP, terms with no planted gene (classic / elim) FDP counting inherited ancestors as false (classic / elim) complete null 0.016 / 0.012 0.016 / 0.012 same 5 planted, p 0.95 0.006 / 0.005 0.0015 / 0.0015 0.155 / 0.013 5 planted, p 0.75 0.004 / 0.002 0.0023 / 0.0013 0.056 / 0.018 20 planted, p 0.95 0.004 / 0.002 0.0002 / 0.0001 0.309 / 0.020 20 planted, p 0.75 0 / 0 0 / 0 0.173 / 0.023 20 planted, p 0.65 0.001 / 0.001 0.001 / 0.001 0.065 / 0.024

Under a correct per-term null, BH on elim p is conservative for both readings of a false discovery: - the strict one: a term with no signal genes at all; - the elim one: an ancestor whose only signal is inherited from planted descendants.

elim keeps 81–98 % of the classic true positives (lowest with 20 weak plants, p 0.75).

Residual risk. A truly enriched child that misses p < 0.01 leaves its signal in its ancestors, which can then be called. The rate here is ≤ 0.024 FDP at q = 0.05.

Verdict. The elim p are acceptable for the (collection, direction) BH families under R4 as long as the report and this note say: - the q-values are BH on elim p; - the claim is "over-detected after removing the genes of its elim-significant descendants"; - FDR control for that claim is empirical (simulation), not a theorem.

M8-04's labels (p_classic kept, p_value = elim) meet this. The per-term null must itself be valid, and with mean-odds Wallenius it is not (above). elim does not repair that.

docs.title: Sign-off
docs.text:
Statistician (#153 review, 2026-10-21).

Approved: the M8-01 primitives (category_odds, wallenius_tails, wallenius_ora, elim). They compute what the spec defines: - the direct tail sums are exact to 5e-10 relative for every decision-relevant p; - the fail-closed range is never reached by realistic p̂; - elim matches topGO's elim with a strict cut, and BH on elim p is empirically conservative.

Not approved: mean-odds Wallenius as the calibrated ORA claim of §8.1. - It fails the §8.4 ORA null (independent detection with p_detect) and the §7.7.5/§8.5 attack 2, both in synthetic urns and in giapsim with cross-fitted p̂. - Every gene-level null, the exact one included, fails the new TU-packing attack.

Forwarded: - M8-15: - the Bernoulli generator for the ora gate (the urn-model test is a code check only); - attack 2 on the prophage short-gene layout; - the TU-packed attack with abundance-driven detection. - M8-04: the O − E CI, or the CPB log-odds CI. - M8-13: the far-tail precision and p = 0 below ~1e-14. - Khoa, by ADR: replace the ORA p with the conditional Poisson-binomial; make ORA TU-aware.

docs.title: Detection enrichment
docs.text:
Implements giap.function.ora, giap.function.summary and tilt_pair(comp=) in giap.stats.poisson_binomial (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.7.2, §7.7.3, §8.1 row "Category detection", §8.2; issue M8-04, docs/specs/M8-04-category-summary-ora.md, lead decisions 1–13; ADR-0029, ADR-0035). Outputs: the rows of enrichment_detection.tsv and category_summary.tsv (§9.3).

Status: PR #179. The statistician's review blocked it (B1–B6); decision 13 answers each point, and the re-check lifted the block. Statistician sign-off: given (#179 re-check of 2026-10-22, after edits M1–M6). Every ORA row carries ora_uncalibrated (see "Pass-1 limit").

docs.title: The unit: TUs
docs.text:
• Eligible genes are the non-partial genes. Only they count, for q and for detection.
  • Universe U: the TUs with ≥ 1 eligible gene, in natural TU-ID order. Results do not depend on the input row order.
  • Detection: TU t is detected (d_t = 1) when any of its eligible genes is detected.
  • Membership rule (decision 1): TU t is in category C when any of its eligible genes is in C. The rule runs over all eligible genes, never over the detected ones, so membership cannot depend on the response.
  • Partial membership dilutes. A TU with one member gene counts as one unit of C, and it may be detected through a gene outside C. This costs power, not level. Its power (spec arm 7) is owed.
  • Size filter (decision 6): n = |C| counted in TUs must lie in function.ora_size ([5, 500], both ends included). A term outside it writes no row and does not enter elim. Under elim the filter applies to the full TU set; a term reduced below 5 TUs is still tested.
  • Count columns are in TUs: n_universe, n_in_set, n_detected, k_detected_in_set. n_in_set_genes and k_detected_in_set_genes are the gene counts behind p_classic.
  • Fail closed (decision 13): an eligible gene with a NaN p_detect, a p_detect outside [0, 1], or no tu_id raises ValueError naming the locus tags. So does a TU missing from a non-empty folds mapping.

docs.title: The statistic and the null
docs.text:
• Statistic: k = the detected TUs in C (stat).
  • Null: the TUs are independent, and TU t is detected with probability q_t. The test is the law of K = Σ_{t∈C} d_t given S = Σ_{t∈U} d_t = N (the conditional Bernoulli law):

P(K = j | N) = PB_C(j) · PB_Ū(N − j) / Σ_i PB_C(i) · PB_Ū(N − i),

where PB_A is the Poisson-binomial pmf of the q_t in A and Ū = U ∖ C. - Tails: p_over = Σ_{j ≥ k} P(K = j | N) and p_under = Σ_{j ≤ k} P(K = j | N). Both include k and both are sums of non-negative terms, never 1 − cdf.

Computation (exact; no approximation, no Monte Carlo). 1. Truncated DP. The convex-combination recurrence \(\mathrm{pmf}[j] \leftarrow \mathrm{pmf}[j](1 - q) + \mathrm{pmf}[j - 1]\, q\), numba-compiled and stopped at the highest index read. PB_C runs to min(|C|, N); PB_Ū is computed only on the band that the support reads. 2. Tilt, once per run. tilt_pair(q, N, comp=) multiplies every TU odds q/(1 − q) by one factor e^θ, with θ solving Σ_t expit(logit q_t + θ) = N. The solver is Newton with a bisection guard; it targets |Σ − N| ≤ 1e-13 N, inside the spec contract of 1e-9 N. - The logit is log q − log comp, and the tilted complement is expit(−(logit q + θ)). Neither is ever re-derived as 1 − q, so a TU with q that rounds to 1.0 keeps its complement (decision 11). - q = 0 and comp = 0 stay exact. Every open entry stays ≥ the smallest normal double, so an open TU is never treated as certain. - The tilt is numerics only. It puts the mass of PB_Ū near the indices that are read, so no weight underflows. The conditional law is invariant to a common odds factor, so the tilt does not change the p. - Conditioning on N cancels only a common TU-level odds factor (ADR-0035). A mis-scaling of q that varies with TU size, with q itself or with the category does not cancel. That is why q is recalibrated (next subsection). 3. Support-sum normalisation. The weights PB_C(j) · PB_Ū(N − j) are normalised by their sum over the support, not by a separate PB_U(N). This saves a DP and makes the tails sum to 1 by construction. A zero or non-finite sum raises ValueError. 4. p domain (decision 13, review B1). The numerator and the support sum can round apart by one ulp, which gave p = 1 + 2⁻⁵² and aborted BH: 663 of 4,000 strongly under-detected categories, and 120 of 3,000 replicates of 4b at c = 3.5. Both tails are now clamped to [0, 1], in the primitive and again before BH (test: tests/unit/function/test_ora_pvalue_domain.py).

Precision contract (tests/unit/stats/test_conditional_poisson_binomial.py: enumeration for T ≤ 14 units, a Fraction DP for T ≤ 60):

input tails ≥ 1e-300, and the mean smaller tails untilted q relative 1e-12 of the exact rational value the float underflow: ≥ 0, never NaN tilt_pair output with its complements relative 1e-11 of the untilted exact law, including q within 1e-15 of 1 and θ > 0 the same

A tail of 0.0 is reachable only below about 1e-300, far below the ~1e-14 floor of scipy's Wallenius pmf ("Far-tail precision" above).

docs.title: TU detection probability
docs.text:
Clipping (decision 12). For the null only, p̂ is clipped to [1e-12, 1 − 1e-12]. Exact 0 and 1 from M4-13 are therefore never treated as certain. - The run, and every row whose full TU set holds a TU with a moved gene, gets p_detect_clipped. - expected in category_summary and the Wallenius odds_weight / p_classic use the unclipped p̂. The difference is ≤ 1e-12 per gene (statistician, #179 review).

Raw q. Per TU, log_comp = Σ log1p(−p̂) over its eligible genes and q_raw = −expm1(log_comp) = 1 − ∏(1 − p̂) (ADR-0029). - q_raw assumes that the genes of a TU are detected independently given p̂. - Shared abundance makes co-detection positive, so q_raw overstates q for multi-gene TUs, and more so for larger TUs. - The ADR-0035 attack gave p̂ as the exact gene marginal over a shared TU effect of strength c. Before recalibration, the rejection rates were (3,000 p per cell; bounds 0.0136 / 0.058; Slurm 1867453, 1867454):

scenario categories tail α 0.01 α 0.05 c 1.5 large TUs under 0.107 0.248 c 1.5 single-gene TUs over 0.019 0.079 c 2.5 large TUs under 0.278 0.490 c 2.5 single-gene TUs over 0.044 0.143 c 0, gene-level p̂ intercept +0.5 large TUs under 0.0137 0.067

Recalibration (ADR-0035, decision 12). - Model: d_t ~ Bernoulli(expit(β₀ + β₁ logit q_raw,t + β₂ log n_t)), where n_t is the number of eligible genes in TU t. The log n term is dropped when every training TU has the same size. - Cross-fitting: for each of M4-13's TU folds (fold_of_tu), the model is fitted on the TUs of the other folds and predicts the held-out fold. A TU's own detection never enters its q. - Output: η = x·β̂, then q = expit(η) and comp = expit(−η), each computed directly. These pairs are what the tilt and the conditional law receive. - Leakage left: cross-fitting does not remove own-category leakage when a category is a large share of a covariate stratum. In the statistician's worlds this was only conservative (a power loss).

Fit (decision 13, review B4). - An unpenalised logistic MLE by Newton, started at (0, 1, 0), the identity on logit q. - Damped: each step is halved until the log-likelihood does not decrease beyond rounding noise (relative 1e3 · ε), up to 60 halvings. - Converged when the full Newton step is below 1e-10 in every coordinate, within 50 iterations. - The noise slack cannot fake convergence. Convergence is tested on the full Newton step H⁻¹g at the current iterate, which is a stationarity test. A concave log-likelihood has exactly one stationary point, the MLE. The slack can only let a near-optimal step through, or use up iterations and end in a skipped fit; it cannot stop the fit away from the MLE. - Checked against scipy (statistician re-check at c1e3ca0, $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m804b/recheck/ newton_check.py, newton_summary.txt): 9 worlds × 40 seeds × 5 folds = 1,800 fits against scipy trust-exact plus Newton polishing. 0 fits failed. Max |Δβ| was 5.3e-15, and the max gradient at the returned β was 9.7e-13. The slack branch was taken in 74 folds, and every one ended at the reference MLE. Complete separation, quasi-separation and a collinear design return no fit, so the fit is skipped (newton_adversarial.py). - Before decision 13 the full-step Newton diverged where the MLE exists: 2,898 of 3,000 replicates of the 4b + 4c world (c = 2.5, a = +0.5, b = 0.8). Each fell back to the raw q, where large-TU under rejected 0.49 at α 0.01. - Tests: tests/unit/function/test_ora_recal_convergence.py (the divergent case) and test_ora_recal_oracle.py (an independent scipy fit per fold, to 1e-8 relative, including a case where the size term matters).

Skipped fit (tu_recal_skipped). The fit is skipped, and q = q_raw with comp = exp(log_comp), when any of these holds: - folds is None or empty. folds is a required keyword, so this is the caller's explicit choice (it is the path of M4-13's constant model); - a fold's training TUs have fewer than 10 detected or fewer than 10 undetected TUs; - the Hessian is singular or a step is non-finite; - 60 halvings find no increase, or 50 iterations do not converge.

The run flag and every row get tu_recal_skipped (review B3). - How often: at c1e3ca0, 0 of 2,000 replicates skip in any tested world, deep coverage included (Slurm 1867941, 1867942). - Why the flag matters: a raw-q fallback over-rejects. At 3f82e0f the undamped Newton diverged in 417 of 3,000 deep-coverage replicates (eta0 = +1.5, about 75 % of genes detected) and fell back to the raw q. There, large-TU under rejected 0.45 at α 0.01, and the ~200-TU categories 0.98 (raw q, 3f82e0f). The statistician's first review attributed those skips to MIN_CLASS; the re-check corrected this. - A skipped run keeps ora_uncalibrated even after the pass-1 flag is lifted.

docs.title: Tests per term: directions, elim and BH
docs.text:
Every tested term gives one row per direction, over and under.

column what it is unit elim enters BH p_value CPB tail of the tested TU set (elim-reduced for GO over, else the full set) TUs GO over only yes p_noelim CPB tail of the full TU set TUs no no p_classic M8-01 mean-odds Wallenius tail on the full gene set genes no no

elim over TU sets (decision 2). - Scope: go_bp, go_mf and go_cc, direction over only. Everywhere else (under, cog, kegg, go_slim) p_value = p_noelim. - Walk: M8-01's walker, fed TU index sets. A term is tested on its remaining TUs against U ∖ remaining, with the run's N and tilt. - Removal: a term whose elim p_over is strictly below 0.01 removes the TUs it was tested on from every ancestor that passed the size filter. - Why TUs, not genes: removing genes would leave a shared TU in the ancestor and count the same detection event twice (spec example 7). - Empty remainder: p_value NA, flags unestimated;elim_empty; p_noelim and p_classic are kept. - Evidence (statistician, $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m804b/probe_elim.py and elim.log, 12,000 parents, R = 600): the elim test, with N fixed, is conservative relative to the exact law that also conditions on the removed child's count. Rates at α 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10:

world elim p_value p_noelim bound global null 0.0048 / 0.031 / 0.070 0.0065 / 0.036 / 0.076 0.0118 / 0.054 / 0.1055 one planted child per parent (logit +3, child power 0.67) 0.0008 / 0.0073 / 0.019 0.0093 / 0.056 / 0.117 same
  • R4 label: "BH on elim p; conditional on removing elim-significant descendants; FDR control is empirical."

BH (decision 5). One family per (collection, direction), on p_value, with giap.stats.bh. - A NaN p stays out of its family and the row gets unestimated. - p_classic and p_noelim are never adjusted.

parent_group (GO only). For a row with q_value ≤ stats.alpha.enrichment it is the most general significant ancestor in the same direction and namespace (by depth, ties by ID), or the term's own ID if it has none. Otherwise it is NA.

Why Wallenius stays only as p_classic (ADR-0029). - Mean-odds Wallenius fails the §8.4 ORA null and attack 2 ("The approximation and the attack it implies" above). - It is kept, on genes, for goseq parity (M8-13). - If it fails closed, p_classic is NA with odds_out_of_range; the CPB columns stand.

docs.title: Effect size
docs.text:
• effect = k − E[K | N] for the tested TU set (the full set, or the elim-reduced one), in TUs. It is the mean of the same conditional law as the p.
  • A positive effect means more detected TUs than expected given N.
  • ci_low and ci_high are NA and every row carries ci_unestimated (decision 6, the accepted Q6 pass-1 waiver).
  • It is not the gene-level O − E of category_summary.

docs.title: Degenerate cases
