docs.title: Pass-1 limit (decision 13; ADR-0035 decision 3)
docs.text:
• Every ORA row carries ora_uncalibrated (CALIBRATION_FLAGS).
  • Why: arm 4b (c = 2.5, large TUs, under) fails at R = 1,000 in both blocks (0.0140 and 0.0130 against 0.0120 at α 0.01). Its close variants 4d–4f fail by more, and so does the size-dependent co-detection world. These are routine category kinds within [5, 500]: high-q operons (ribosome-like), and categories of 100–200 multi-gene TUs.
  • What holds: the conditional law is exact for the q it is given (oracle-q cells at level; precision contract). 4c and the random whole-TU and random-gene categories are at level.
  • What fails: q itself, through the misfit of the 3-parameter recalibration (re-check table B′). It is anti-conservative for:
  • under-detection of large or high-q TU sets;
  • under-detection of low-q TU sets at deep coverage (loq_any, 0.024 at α 0.01);
  • over-detection of large multi-gene categories (big_multi over, 0.016 to 0.026 at α 0.01);
  • high-q categories in a small genome (800 genes).

Any category selected on TU size or on q is at risk. Only the random whole-TU and single-gene categories were at level in every world. The conditional law itself is still sound: the oracle q is at level in every cell. - Consequence: the p and q are not discovery claims. ora.py writes no "calibrated" claim (ADR-0029). A skipped fit (tu_recal_skipped) is a second, independent reason for the flag.

docs.title: Hardening owed (pass 2)
docs.text:
• Flexible recalibration. Adopt the statistician's comparator model (C above), or another that passes. It needs an ADR-0035 amendment from Khoa.
  • Lifting the flag. Only on a pass at R = 1,000 in both blocks of every cell of 4b–4f, with rates logged; the fast tier is a smoke test. Skipped runs keep the flag regardless. The fallback in the attack files cannot trigger on its own, because the flag is a constant (backlog N10).
  • Comp underflow (backlog N1). comp = exp(log_comp) underflows to 0 once log_comp < about −745: about 27 genes at the clip 1 − 1e-12 in one TU, or a very large TU. On the fitted path, expit(−η) underflows once η > about 745. An undetected TU with comp = 0 makes the whole run null_degenerate. Fix: carry log_comp into the tilt instead of comp.
  • Clip semantics (backlog N3). State which rows count as affected. The clip also moves p̂ in (0, 1e-12) and (1 − 1e-12, 1).
  • The CI on effect. Candidates: a TU-block bootstrap of k − E, or the conditional MLE of a log-odds shift δ for C's TUs with an exact CI by inverting the CPB test.
  • The category_summary CI for small categories (below).
  • Power of partial membership (spec arm 7): owed.
  • The 4b + 4c combination fails with the damped fit (large under 0.0168 / 0.0750 / 0.1336 and 0.0206 / 0.0776 / 0.1381 in the two blocks; large_hiq under 0.081 / 0.218 / 0.321 pooled). The pass-2 model must pass it, together with every other failing cell of B′, in both blocks at R ≥ 1,000.

docs.title: category_summary
docs.text:
• Scope: collections cog, kegg and go_slim. It is descriptive: no test, and every category is reported whatever its size. It is gene-level, as §9.3 names it.
  • Columns, per category:
  • n_genes (eligible members) and n_detected;
  • expected = Σ p̂ over members (unclipped);
  • o_minus_e = n_detected − expected, with a 95 % CI;
  • median_abundance_log2 over detected members with a finite abundance (imputed values included);
  • the collection's coverage.
  • CI: a percentile TU block bootstrap (giap.stats.tu_block_bootstrap, M4-16 basic_rows construction). Per-TU sums of d − p̂ over the category's members are resampled as whole TUs and summed. B is the caller's (stats.bootstrap), and the draws come from the step's rng in row order.
  • Few units: below 10 TUs (CI_MIN_UNITS) the CI is NA with ci_few_units.
  • Coverage is low for small categories (statistician, $GIAP_ROOT/stat/m804b/probe_boot.py and boot.log; B = 999, 1,200 CIs per cell, true O − E = 0):
category coverage, c = 0 coverage, c = 2.5 10 TUs 0.886 0.887 15 TUs 0.908 0.898 30 TUs 0.922 0.933 100 TUs 0.963 0.932 40 random genes 0.933 0.942
  • Nominal 95 % CIs covered 0.89 to 0.93 at 10 to 30 TUs (Monte Carlo SE about 0.009).
  • Under TU-packed detection (c = 2.5) they covered 0.93 even at 100 TUs.
  • The misses are mostly intervals wholly below the truth (hi < 0), because the sum is skewed: 8.5 % at 10 TUs against 2.5 % nominal (0.085 at c = 0, 0.087 at c = 2.5; lo > 0: 0.029 and 0.025).
  • So an apparent under-detection (a CI entirely below 0) in a category of 30 TUs or fewer is weaker evidence than its nominal level.

Raising CI_MIN_UNITS to about 30, or a BCa or studentized bootstrap, is owed (backlog).

docs.title: Simulator worlds for the M8-15 gate (giapsim, M8-14)
docs.text: tests/sim/giapsim/function_sim.py and the giapsim.scenarios function pairs (issue M8-14, PR

docs.title: 251; GIAP_SPEC.md §8.4, §8.5 attacks 2 and 3, §11.3). Statistician review of PR #251
docs.text:
(2026-10-23); the attack arms are in tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_sim_function.py.

Annotations. A random GO-shaped DAG in the reserved range GO:9000000–GO:9999998 (three namespaces, is_a and part_of), 35–55 % of genes annotated directly, COG letters on synthetic COG<n> IDs, 2–20 synthetic KEGG maps (K9xxxx, map9xxxx). Annotations are drawn from their own stream, independently of every covariate, of abundance and of detection. world.sets keeps sets of 10–500 TUs (the GSEA filter), so the 5–9-TU sets the ORA filter (function.ora_size [5, 500]) would test are absent there; an ORA gate should build its sets through M8-03 from world.obo and world.layout.xrefs.

ORA null (ora_null). Detection is redrawn as Bernoulli(p_true), with p_true the M4-09 covariate logistic (length, observable peptides, GRAVY). Membership is independent of detection given p_true, so the conditional Poisson-binomial law holds exactly with q from p_true. With the fitted M4-13 p_detect the null is the M8-04 claim itself (arm ora_null.fitted).

Attack 2 (ora_attack_confounded). One random GO set covering 8–20 % of genes; the confounding is carried by n_obs (CONFOUND_COVARIATE, M8-14 lead decision 6). Each member with an aa and n_obs > 0 has its K/R residues moved, with their codons, so that its recomputed observable-peptide count gives the logit shift nearest member_shift. Composition is preserved, so GRAVY and length are unchanged. Short sORFs that cannot lose a peptide keep shift 0. The mean shift over movable members is −1.44 to −1.50 at −1.5; about [−2, +0.5] is reachable, and a draw whose mean misses member_shift by more than SHIFT_TOL = 0.15 raises (M8-14 decision 9). - Visibility: over 200 worlds, GIAP's covariates() recomputed n_observable_peptides equal to n_obs_true for every gene, and GRAVY was unchanged exactly. A side effect: 66 % of members change tm_segments (+1.56 on average) and pI moves by up to 0.22. These are not in the truth logit. - Results at −1.5: the oracle arm is at level and the unweighted test rejects at 1.0. The fitted M4-13 arm is at level and strongly conservative: 0.00 / 0.01 / 0.01 at R = 100 (Slurm 1873380). The default five-covariate fit, recomputed from aa, gives 0 / 0 / 0.005 at R = 200. - Why it is conservative: 99 % of members sit at or below the non-members' 5th n_obs percentile, so the cross-fit learns the members' own rate. Their O − Σp̂ has SD 0.30 in units of √Σp̂(1−p̂). This comes from the plug-in variance (q̂ treated as known) and shrinks with overlap: SD 0.67 at −0.5, 0.55 at −0.75, 0.43 at −1.0. - Power: the same plug-in costs power against a real category effect beyond the covariates. For an extra −0.5 logit, the fitted arm detects it in 0.19 of worlds and the oracle in 0.68 at shift −0.5; at −1.5 the figures are 0.01 and 0.33 (statistician probes, Slurm 1874044 and 1874094). - M8-15: gate −1.5 as a separation check and −0.75 as an overlap arm (unweighted 0.95 at 0.05).

GSEA null (gsea_null). The M4-08 model (AR(1) TU levels with ρ 0.5 and SD 2, stoichiometry 0.7, gene noise 0.5) with position_decay_log2 = 0. Gene-level abundance is independent of membership for any decay. The TU score (mean of the scoring genes) falls with TU size under decay, and any-gene membership favours large TUs, so decay is a potential TU-level confounder. It is not one at the M4-08 default: with decay 0.2, the pooled rate over every in-range set (about 268 per world, R = 80, SIMPLE_ENGINE) was 0.0084 / 0.047 / 0.096, against 0.0087 / 0.045 / 0.094 at decay 0; at 0.5 it was 0.011 / 0.060 / 0.115 (pooled over dependent sets, so indicative only). The arm gsea_null.decay0.2 gates one random set per world at the default decay.

Attack 3 (gsea_attack_operon_packed). Each set is 1–3 packed chr1 operons of 10–30 genes plus PACKED_SINGLES = 40 single-gene TUs (at least 9 on small layouts), whole TUs only, so every set is inside function.gsea_size [10, 500]. Packed TUs draw their level like every other TU; the shared TU level, moving 10–30 genes together, is the attack. - The packed TUs are exchangeable with the other chr1 TUs: Fligner test 0 / 0.02 / 0.08. - The TU-collapsed GSEA is at level: 0 / 0.04 / 0.10 at R = 50. - Gene-level ranking with gene-label permutation is a confirmed fail (Slurm 1872913, 1873380).

docs.title: Islands: expression islands along the replicon
docs.text: Issues M5-01 (scores, detrending) and M5-03 (scan engine) add the engine helpers; the island step itself is M5-06 (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.5(d)). Each section records its own statistician sign-off; the block-bootstrap null and its calibration are signed off with M5-06/M5-07.

docs.title: Report text (M9-16)
docs.text:
The block below is copied into the run report's methods section by scripts/dev/sync_report_snippets.py (plain paragraphs and lists only).

Islands are runs of adjacent transcription units whose detrended abundance scores are jointly high or low along a replicon. Each window sum is compared with the maximum of a TU-block bootstrap of the same scores, taken over every scanned replicon, so one family-wise error rate covers the whole run; a window is reported when its p-value is at most stats.alpha.context.

The FWER is claimed for a dependence regime, not for a replicon size. The calibration supports it for TU-level autocorrelation up to rho = 0.5 at every replicon size measured, and up to rho = 0.9 at 4,500 genes; there is no evidence beyond that (rho above 0.95, or dependence longer than the 20-TU bootstrap block cap). It is not claimed where strong TU-level autocorrelation is resolved by Moran's I only to a short lag (block length 7 or less): a high Moran's I with block_len 7 or less is outside the claimed domain. No per-replicon statistic certifies the domain, so nothing is flagged; instead the report lists, per replicon:

  • the estimated correlation length (l-hat), or why it was not estimated;
  • the bootstrap block length used (block_len);
  • the lag-1 Moran's I of the detrended TU scores.

docs.title: Gene scores: left-censored Blom
docs.text:
giap.stats.scores.blom_scores(x, censored_mask) (§7.3.5(d) step 1, §8.3). Within a replicon the eligible genes are ranked by log2 abundance. Undetected genes are left-censored: they lie below the detection limit, so their order among themselves is unknown, but their position (below every detected gene) is known. All n₀ of them therefore share the average of ranks 1 … n₀, r = (n₀ + 1)/2, and a detected gene gets n₀ + its average rank among the detected values; a detected gene with a very low abundance still ranks above every undetected one (censoring is "at the lowest rank", not "at its own value"). Ties among detected values and the censored block are averaged separately. The score is the Blom normal score Φ⁻¹((r − 3/8)/(n + 1/4)) (scipy.special.ndtri).

Properties: scores are invariant under strictly increasing transforms of the values and equivariant under permutation; without ties or censoring the scores of ranks r and n + 1 − r sum to 0; a fully censored replicon scores exactly 0 everywhere (r = (n + 1)/2 maps to Φ⁻¹(0.5)). An uncensored NaN or ±inf raises ValueError: the caller decides who is scored.

The scores are detrended with the shared LOESS helper (docs/methods/autocorrelation.md, "Detrending") along TU order, span 10 % of TUs.

docs.title: Scan and maximum statistic (M5-03)
docs.text:
giap.stats.scan (§7.3.5(d) steps 4–6, §8.3). Windows are lengths w = wmin … min(wmax, cap) with cap = n − 1 on circular replicons (no window covers the whole circle; after detrending such a window has S ≈ 0) and n on linear ones. Circular windows start at every position and wrap. They are ordered by length, then start. S_w = Σ_{t∈w} z_t / √n_w comes from prefix sums. The observed series and the null rows use the same kernel, so a null row equal to the observed series reproduces its maximum exactly.

Family and FWER. One family is all windows of one replicon, both signs. The statistic is M = max_w |S_w|, and p_w = (1 + #{M_b ≥ |S_w|})/(1 + B) (single-step maxT, Westfall–Young), so high and low islands share one α. Ties within 1e-12·max(1, |S|) count as exceedances (conservative). If the null rows are exchangeable with the observed series under the complete null, P(min_w p_w ≤ α) ≤ α exactly. The excess over α is discreteness only, at most 1/(B + 1). With true islands present, the signal is spread into the null rows (permutation or block bootstrap), which raises M_b. The procedure is then conservative: in simulation with planted high islands of 5–60 TUs the false-island rate was 0–0.033 at α = 0.05 (PR #118 review). A planted low (silenced) island, which the step cannot detect, is not conservative in this sense: it is a low-variance stretch at the censored atom, not extra variability spread into the null rows. It gives 0.034–0.036 at R = 500, against 0.020 on the complete null ("Calibration and power" below), which is within α. Being single-step, it is also conservative for secondary islands. The engine is only as valid as the exchangeability of its null rows: iid permutations are not valid under autocorrelation. The production null is the circular block bootstrap with ℓ′ (ADR-0021), calibrated in M5-06/M5-07. Which family applies where (M5-06 decision 46): the engine used alone, one call per replicon against that replicon's own M_b, controls the FWER per replicon, and across k replicons the genome-wide rate is then up to 1 − (1 − α)^k. The M5-06 island step does not use it that way — it pools one genome-wide M_b over every scanned replicon, so one FWER covers the run ("The null and the genome-wide family" below). A replicon with no window (n < wmin) has max_abs NaN and p NaN, which is never significant. A non-finite |S| gives NaN; a negative finite |S| is a caller error and raises (decision 22).

Why S/√n_w is not standardised for TU size. z_t is the mean of the gene scores of TU t, so Var z_t falls with the TU's gene count. S_w/√n_w has unit variance only when every TU has unit variance. Windows of single-gene TUs have the largest variance and dominate M_b. Windows over large operons then need a larger true shift to exceed the same threshold, so power is lower in operon-dense regions. This is a power cost, not a size cost, as long as the null rows keep the positional mix of TU sizes (the block bootstrap does; iid permutation does not). TU-size-standardised scores were evaluated and rejected (ADR-0021: FWER 0.18 at ρ = 0).

Merging and the representative. Significant windows of the same direction that share ≥ 1 TU (cyclically on circular replicons) are linked. Islands are the connected components; touching windows stay separate. A window with S = 0 has no direction and is dropped (it cannot be significant, because M_b ≥ 0 gives p = 1). The best window has the largest |S|, then fewer TUs, then the smaller start. Island-level guarantee: a false island (no window overlapping a true island) contains a falsely rejected window, so P(any false island) ≤ the window FWER. Not controlled: the island's extent. Boundary-straddling windows are non-null and significant, so the union of a cluster usually extends past the true island (27–100 % of replicates in simulation). The reported span is therefore the best window's span (≤ wmax = 20 TUs), not the union. An island longer than 20 TUs is represented by a best window of ≤ 20 TUs and can split into two islands; M5-10's Jaccard inherits both effects. S and the effect of the best window are selected (winner's curse; see ADR-0021 on the effect CI).

Signed off by the statistician (PR #118 review).

docs.title: The island step (M5-06)
docs.text: giap.context.islands (§7.3.5(d) steps 1–10, §8.1 row "Islands", §9.3 tables/islands.tsv). This section is the claim the island table makes; the two sections above are the pieces it is built from.

docs.title: Scores, TU series, detrending
docs.text:
Per replicon: the eligible genes (not partial, p_detect present) are Blom-scored with the undetected ones left-censored ("Gene scores" above); z_t is the mean score of the scored genes of TU t; the series is detrended by LOESS over TU ordinals (not base pairs) with span k = ⌈0.1·T⌉ points and circular padding on circular replicons.

  • Missing-value policy (decision 22). A detected gene whose abundance is NaN — possible only under abundance.missing = exclude — is not scored: it is detected, so censoring it at the bottom would be a lie, and its rank is unknown. It therefore leaves the ranking entirely, which changes every other gene's Blom score slightly; a TU with no scored gene left is dropped from the series. Under abundance.missing = min the same gene is scored at the imputed minimum. The two policies are the §8.6 basic sensitivity axis, so the island membership must not move with the policy for its own reasons — see "What is reported, and what the gene list is" below.
  • The detrend attenuates the signal it is scanning for. A boxcar island of w TUs keeps about 1 − 1.7·w/k of its amplitude while w ≲ k/3 and far less beyond. Measured retained amplitude (circular LOESS, span 10 %):
T (scored TUs) k w = 2 w = 5 w = 10 w = 20 2,500 250 0.99 0.97 0.93 0.86 1,000 100 0.97 0.91 0.83 0.66 400 40 0.91 0.79 0.58 0.32 200 20 0.83 0.58 0.32 0.16

Since w ≤ max_tus = 20, this is a few per cent on a chromosome and a near-total loss of the long windows on a replicon of a few hundred TUs: on small replicons the step effectively scans only its short windows. It is a power cost, not a level cost — the null rows are detrended by the same linear smoother.

docs.title: The null and the genome-wide family
docs.text:
Each scanned replicon is resampled by circular_block_bootstrap(detrended, ℓ′, B, rng) with ℓ′ = min(20, 2ℓ̂ + 1, T) per replicon (ADR-0021 decision 1; the rule, the evidence for ℓ′ over ℓ̂ and the join bias live in docs/methods/bootstrap.md "Block length"). The null keeps what the data have: whole TU scores move together, so the TU-size mix and the detectability pattern travel with the scores, and blocks of ℓ′ consecutive TUs keep the local autocorrelation. It is a stationary null: it does not keep variation of the local scale along the replicon, which is the source of both breaches recorded below.

One family, genome-wide (decisions 21 and 46). For replicate b, M_b is the maximum of |S_w| over the windows of every scanned replicon, taken element-wise across replicons at the same b; the replicons are resampled independently, which is the complete null (replicons are independent under it), and the pairing at index b is arbitrary but valid. p_w = (1 + #{M_b ≥ |S_w|})/(1 + B) and a window is reported when p_w ≤ stats.alpha.context. So one FWER of 0.05 covers the whole run, matching the single §8.1 row, instead of 1 − (1 − α)^k over k replicons. The price is paid by the smaller replicons: a 60-TU plasmid raises the common threshold a little and loses power to the chromosome's maximum, which is the correct direction for a run-level claim. A replicon that is not scanned (below) contributes nothing to M_b, consumes no draws and cannot carry an island.

docs.title: Validity domain (ADR-0021 Amendment 1)
docs.text:
The FWER is claimed for a dependence regime, not for a replicon size. It is claimed for giapsim ar1_background at ρ ≤ 0.5 at every size measured (557 / 1,001 / 2,501 scored TUs: 0.020 / 0.031 / 0.037 at α = 0.05, R = 1,000, bound 0.0638), for the 4,500-gene chromosome at ρ = 0.9 (0.024, where ℓ̂ ≈ 8 makes ℓ′ = 17 span the 20-TU windows) and for the §8.5 attacks that stay in that regime.

It is not claimed where strong TU-level autocorrelation is resolved by Moran's I only to a short lag (ℓ′ ≤ 7): ρ = 0.9 gives 0.113 at 557 TUs and 0.095 at 1,001 TUs, and 1,000 single-gene TUs give 0.068 / 0.110 / 0.208 / 0.327 at ρ = 0.7 / 0.8 / 0.9 / 0.95. The scored-TU count decides nothing on its own (400 TUs at ρ 0.5: 0.005; 1,000 TUs at ρ 0.9: 0.095–0.208; 2,500 TUs at ρ 0.9: 0.024); it enters only through the power of the ℓ̂ test, together with ρ, the TU-size distribution and the censored share — the same ρ = 0.9 replicon gives ℓ̂ = 9 and 0.007 uncensored, ℓ̂ = 2 and 0.208 at 55 % detected.

Two mechanisms, both measured at 1,000 TUs and ρ = 0.9 with the block forced:

  1. Autocovariance beyond the block. Uncensored, Î₁ = 0.78: FWER 0.576 at block 5 against 0.016 at block 19. The bootstrap breaks the dependence at every join, so a block shorter than the correlation length makes the null rows too tame and M_b too small.
  2. Local-scale heterogeneity at matched variance. With 45 % censored the overall variance ratio is ≈ 1.0 and the FWER is still 0.158 at block 5; the block-SD ratio q90/q10 is 1.73 at ρ = 0.9 against 1.24 at ρ = 0. A stationary null gives every window the same scale, so the windows that sit in a locally noisy stretch are tested against too narrow a null. This is the same mechanism as the ori–ter gradient attack (decision 49): left censoring compresses the low half of the Blom scores against the censored atom while the high half spreads, so a gradient makes the detrended series heteroscedastic (local-SD ratio 1.74 against 1.35 without it) and removing censoring removes the inflation (0.066 → 0.011).

A long block fixes both and costs all the power, which ADR-0021 decision 1 rejected. Local standardisation (dividing by a LOESS fit of |residual|) was measured and rejected: it reduces the inflation (ρ 0.8: 0.106 → 0.032; ρ 0.9: 0.188 → 0.084, still a breach) and absorbs the signal (power on a 20-TU × +2 SD island at ρ 0.5: 0.103 → 0.003). A scale-aware null is on the backlog.

No flag, and why not (decision 48). Nothing is flagged uncalibrated: no per-replicon statistic certifies the domain, and selecting on one is adverse. ℓ̂, ℓ′, the lag-1 Moran's I, a Bartlett variance ratio of the window sums and a local-scale ratio all fail as keep/flag rules — at ρ = 0.9 and 557 TUs the overall rate is 0.113 but 0.220 among the replicates that look calmest (ℓ̂ ≤ 1, flat local scale), because a small ℓ̂ is exactly what makes the block too short, and the same rule flags 94 % of the perfectly calibrated 2,501-TU ρ = 0.5 cell. Instead the §9.4 run report carries ℓ̂, ℓ′ (block_len) and the lag-1 Moran's I of the detrended TU scores per replicon, so a reader can see where their data sit against the paragraphs above. Reading them: ℓ̂ is reported as 0 when it was not estimated — the replicon was not scanned, or context.islands.block_len fixed it — and block_len is 0 only for a replicon that was not scanned. ℓ̂ = 0 is a sentinel, never a measurement: the estimator is bounded to [1, 20], so a report must render it as "not estimated" and never as the number 0, which would read as "no autocorrelation" — the false reassurance the amendment refuses. The lag-1 Moran's I is computed from the data either way, so a fixed block does not blind the reader. With block_len fixed the calibration above does not apply at all: it is evidence about ℓ′, and the FWER claim is conditional on the default rule.

docs.title: The low direction is a structural zero at normal detection rates
docs.text:
Left censoring is not symmetric (decisions 47 and 50). Every undetected gene shares the censored Blom score c = Φ⁻¹(q/2) with q the undetected share, so a fully silenced window of w TUs cannot go below −√w·|c|: about 3.4 at q = 0.45 and w = 20, against a genome-wide critical value of about 4.1–4.9 across the settings measured. low_direction_ceiling(q, w) returns this bound. Measured on a ρ = 0.5 null with 10 / 20 / 40 consecutive TUs silenced entirely: ceiling 3.42 / 3.38 / 3.35, M_b 95th percentile 4.92 / 4.57 / 4.49, best low p = 1.000, no low island at any α. The high direction has no such cap — the top Blom score is about +3.3 at these sizes — which is why planted low islands are missed on giapsim at the default detection rate while high ones are found.

The bound is exact for the raw TU scores; the detrended statistic differs from it by √w times the window's mean trend, so it can sit slightly below the ceiling when the window lies on a locally high trend (measured −2.77 detrended against −2.42 raw at 10 silenced TUs) — far below the critical value either way. The procedure is two-sided and costs the high direction almost nothing, but a null result in the low direction is not evidence of no silenced island unless the censored share is small (roughly below a quarter undetected). M5-07 records low-island power separately and labels it a structural zero with the ceiling and the critical value printed beside it; the run report prints the ceiling against the 95th percentile of M_b per replicon.

docs.title: What is reported, and what the gene list is
docs.text:
Each cluster of merged significant same-direction windows is reported by its best window, never by the union (decision 42, "Merging and the representative" above): tu_first/tu_last, n_tus, unwrapped start/end (end > length when the window crosses the origin), scan_s, block_len, p_value (FWER), q_value NA, method = scan_max_stat, null_model = circular_block_bootstrap.

genes, n_genes and detected_frac cover all eligible genes of the window's TUs, including a detected gene that was dropped from the scores for want of an abundance. The asymmetry with the scoring is deliberate: the statistic is an inference about the scored series, while the gene list is a description of the locus, and it is the gene list that the §8.6 sensitivity Jaccard compares across abundance.missing ∈ {min, exclude}. If membership followed the scored set, that comparison would mostly measure the missing-value policy instead of the island's extent, and detected_frac would stop being comparable to the replicon-level detected fraction and to the §7.3.5(c) region tests, which also count detection over eligible genes. Two consequences to keep in mind: detected_frac·n_genes can exceed the number of genes behind mean_abundance_log2 (which averages only detected genes that have a value), and a TU with no scored gene at all is absent from the series, so the span start … end can contain eligible genes that genes does not list.

docs.title: The effect and its CI: a selected interval
docs.text:
effect is the mean detrended score of the best window's TUs — identically scan_s/√n_tus, the test statistic on a per-TU scale — with a 95 % percentile tu_block_bootstrap CI over that window's TUs (decision 26). Read it as a descriptive size, not as a test. Four caveats, all in the anti-conservative direction:

  • Winner's curse. The window was chosen as the genome-wide maximum of |S|, so both the point estimate and the interval are conditional on that selection: effect is biased away from zero, the CI under-covers the underlying island mean, and it essentially never contains zero — so it carries no independent evidence that the island is real. The p_value is the only test. On a 600-gene null with the threshold opened to α = 0.9, the three reported windows have effects +2.35, +2.33, +1.67 with CIs [1.88, 2.83], [1.70, 2.96], [1.44, 1.99] — every one excluding zero — at p = 0.70, 0.86, 0.13.
  • Within-window dependence is ignored. The CI resamples TUs independently inside the window; with positive autocorrelation that understates the variance and the interval is too narrow.
  • Scale. The units are detrended Blom scores, not log2 fold change, and the detrend has already attenuated the island by the factor tabulated above.
  • Few units. Windows of 2–9 TUs carry the M4-16 flag ci_few_units: a percentile bootstrap over so few units is coarse (at 2 TUs the interval is essentially the two values).

The realised coverage of this CI is not yet measured (backlog).

docs.title: Degenerate cases
docs.text: Situation Behaviour LOESS span gives k < 4 points (≈ T ≤ 30 at the 10 % span), or T < 2·min_tus not scanned: run flag few_values, no table row, no draws, out of both maxima (decisions 40–41) no replicon scanned empty table, every island_id NA, null_max empty all genes undetected every Blom score 0 → S = 0 → p = 1 → no island no valid M_b p NaN; p <= alpha is false, so NaN never reports an island low island with no detected gene mean_abundance_log2 NA, detected_frac 0, still reported context.islands.block_len > T bounded to T; ℓ̂ reported as 0 (not estimated) max_tus ≥ T on a circular replicon windows capped at T − 1 by the engine

docs.title: Calibration evidence
docs.text:
Fast tier (tests/calibration/test_islands_calibration.py, R = 50, B = 199, bounds 0.0381 / 0.1116 / 0.1849 at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10): 1,000-gene null at ρ = 0 → 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.04, at ρ = 0.5 → 0.00 / 0.02 / 0.06; chromosome + 60-gene plasmid in one family → 0.00 / 0.02 / 0.04. Teeth: the bare ℓ̂ as the block length is a confirmed fail at ρ = 0.9 (0.62 and 0.72 in the two ADR-0015 blocks against 0.1116). Attacks (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_islands.py, §8.5): the ori–ter gradient at a realistic 2 log2 (0.003 / 0.042 / 0.094) and the same with detection driven by abundance (0.000 / 0.017 / 0.057) are gated, as are large TUs, a draft assembly of 133 short contigs and a chromosome with three plasmids; the 4-log2 gradient (0.009 / 0.062 / 0.136) and ρ = 0.9 at three sizes are recorded, not gated, as the known breaches of the domain above. M5-07 carries the full-size gate and the power table.

Signed off by the statistician (PR #131 review).

docs.title: Calibration and power (M5-07)
docs.text:
The M5 gate (§8.4 row "Islands"; tests/calibration/test_island_fwer.py). Each replicate draws giapsim ar1_background with no island planted; the indicator is "at least one island reported". Settings: stats.bootstrap = stats.permutations = 1000, default context.islands, criterion fwer with the ADR-0015 two-block confirmation. Levels and bounds come from tests/calibration/tolerances.yaml (0.05 + 2 SE: 0.0189 / 0.0695 / 0.1268 at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10, R = 500). The layout is a circular 4,500-gene chromosome (median 2,501 scored TUs) plus a circular 60-gene plasmid, in one genome-wide family. Branch run: Slurm 1868005 (commit fdbfc77). Main run: Slurm 1868687 (commit ed129c4, barley-01, 1 h 10 min), rates identical to the branch run. Every cell passed on block 1. Rates carry Wilson 95 % intervals.

Cell (R = 500) α = 0.01 α = 0.05 α = 0.10 ρ = 0 0.004 0.022 [0.012, 0.039] 0.050 [0.034, 0.073] ρ = 0.5 0.006 0.020 [0.011, 0.036] 0.068 [0.049, 0.094] ρ = 0.9 0.000 0.024 [0.014, 0.041] 0.096 [0.073, 0.125] attack (a): ρ = 0.95 0.002 0.026 [0.015, 0.044] 0.094 [0.071, 0.123] attack (b): ori–ter cosine 2 log2, ρ = 0.5 0.006 0.048 [0.032, 0.070] 0.114 [0.089, 0.145] attack (c): tu_null, mean TU size 3 0.006 0.022 [0.012, 0.039] 0.030 [0.018, 0.049] attack (d): ρ = 0.5, detection from abundance 0.000 0.010 [0.004, 0.023] 0.070 [0.051, 0.096] attack (e): tu_null(1800), short genes in the prophage 0.000 0.010 [0.004, 0.023] 0.022 [0.012, 0.039]

Attacks (a)–(d) use 4,500 genes and no plasmid (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_islands_scenarios.py, §8.5 attack 1, gated). Arm (b) has the least margin at both levels. It is the local-scale mechanism of "Validity domain" item 2, whose 4-log2 version is the recorded breach. Recorded, not gated (ADR-0021 Amendment 1): ρ = 0.9 gives 0.096 [0.073, 0.125] at 1,000 genes (557 TUs) and 0.130 [0.103, 0.162] at 1,800 genes (999 TUs), at α = 0.05 against 0.0695. Both are breaches outside the claimed domain. Fast tier: 1,000 genes, ρ = 0.5, R = 50, 13.6 s (benchmarks/baseline.json). Teeth: the iid bootstrap (block_len = 1) on the fast cell is a confirmed fail (0.23 at R = 100 in the statistician's probe, against 0.1116). A fixed block of 3 on the full ρ = 0.9 cell gives 0.765 (R = 200).

Block lengths observed (chromosome, R = 500 per cell):

Cell ℓ̂ median [10 %, 90 %] ℓ′ counts ρ 0, 4,500 genes 1 [1, 1] 3: 459, 5: 40, 7: 1 ρ 0.5, 4,500 2 [2, 3] 3: 26, 5: 309, 7: 147, 9: 18 ρ 0.9, 4,500 8 [6, 11] 7: 2, 9: 12, 11: 27, 13: 65, 15: 87, 17: 89, 19: 85, 20: 133 ρ 0.95, 4,500 (attack a) 11 5: 2, 7: 2, 9: 8, 11: 13, 13: 24, 15: 31, 17: 36, 19: 64, 20: 320 ρ 0.9, 1,800 (recorded) 3 [1, 5] 3: 96, 5: 135, 7: 127, 9: 77, 11: 40, 13: 14, 15: 9, 17: 2 ρ 0.9, 1,000 (recorded) 1 [1, 2] 3: 352, 5: 111, 7: 28, 9: 7, 11: 2

ℓ′ = min(20, 2ℓ̂ + 1, T) reaches the cap whenever ℓ̂ ≥ 10: in 133 of 500 replicates at ρ 0.9 and 320 of 500 at ρ 0.95. The cap does not show in the rate. Capped replicates: 0/133 and 2/320 at α = 0.05 (9/133 and 26/320 at 0.10); the rest: 12/367 and 11/180. The excess sits where ℓ̂ is small for the dependence (uncapped ρ 0.95: 0.061 at α = 0.05, R = 180), the adverse selection of decision 48, not where the cap binds. This comes from the statistician's probe for PR #188, which reran ℓ′ per replicate and joined it to the gate indicators. Limitation: the blocks underrepresent dependence at the joins (docs/methods/bootstrap.md, "Block length"). At 4,500 genes ℓ′ spans the dependence well enough for 20-TU windows; the evidence does not extend to correlation lengths beyond the cap (ρ > 0.95, or longer-range structure).

The plasmid is not always scanned. The 60-gene plasmid has 21–46 scored TUs (median 34). With T ≤ 30 the LOESS span ⌈0.1·T⌉ is below 4 points, so the replicon is not scanned (few_values, decision 40). That happened in 93 / 89 / 98 of 500 replicates at ρ = 0 / 0.5 / 0.9, about 19 %. The two-replicon family was therefore exercised in 402–411 replicates per cell, with FWER 7/407, 9/411 and 11/402 at α = 0.05. An unscanned plasmid cannot carry an island and adds nothing to M_b; the genome-wide-family claim rests on the 81 % of replicates where it was scanned.

Power (recorded, not gated; §7.3.6). scripts/dev/island_power.py, Slurm 1868246 (commit 20e5273), R = 100 per cell. Layout: the 4,500-gene island_power scenario at ρ = 0.5, island starting at chromosome TU 625, stats.bootstrap = stats.permutations = 1000, α = 0.05. The layout carries no regions: the scenario has no region effect and the island step reads no region, so this changes the random stream, not the distribution of anything the step sees. Power is the share of replicates with a same-direction island sharing at least one TU with the planted island; J is the TU Jaccard of the best such island's best window with the planted TUs, averaged over hits (unstable below 5 hits); false is the share of replicates with an island that shares no TU with the planted one (an island counts as false when its best window misses the planted TUs, even if its cluster touches them, which biases this rate upward). Null FWER of this layout: 0.020 [0.011, 0.036] (gate cell ρ = 0.5).

High direction: power [Wilson 95 %] / J / false.

TUs × SD covariates_only detection from abundance 5 × 1 0.00 [0.00, 0.04] / – / 0.02 0.00 [0.00, 0.04] / – / 0.04 5 × 1.5 0.01 [0.00, 0.05] / 0.62 / 0.02 0.00 [0.00, 0.04] / – / 0.01 5 × 2 0.00 [0.00, 0.04] / – / 0.01 0.01 [0.00, 0.05] / 0.28 / 0.01 10 × 1 0.01 [0.00, 0.05] / 0.67 / 0.03 0.00 [0.00, 0.04] / – / 0.03 10 × 1.5 0.02 [0.01, 0.07] / 0.65 / 0.01 0.05 [0.02, 0.11] / 0.76 / 0.02 10 × 2 0.05 [0.02, 0.11] / 0.84 / 0.03 0.11 [0.06, 0.19] / 0.83 / 0.00 20 × 1 0.02 [0.01, 0.07] / 0.55 / 0.01 0.04 [0.02, 0.10] / 0.83 / 0.02 20 × 1.5 0.10 [0.06, 0.17] / 0.63 / 0.04 0.30 [0.22, 0.40] / 0.78 / 0.03 20 × 2 0.20 [0.13, 0.29] / 0.59 / 0.01 0.65 [0.55, 0.74] / 0.86 / 0.00

The low direction is a structural zero: power is 0/100 in all 18 low cells in both detection modes (upper Wilson bound 0.04). The ceiling √w·|Φ⁻¹(q/2)| at q ≈ 0.45 is 1.68 / 2.38 / 3.37 for w = 5 / 10 / 20, while the genome-wide critical value (the 95th percentile of M_b) has median 4.40–4.58 and minimum 3.71; across 1,200 probe replicates the ceiling was never at or above it. False-island rates in the low cells (R = 100), covariates_only, 5 / 10 / 20 TUs × 1 / 1.5 / 2 SD: 0.04, 0.05, 0.05 / 0.03, 0.00, 0.01 / 0.06, 0.05, 0.07; detection from abundance: 0.02, 0.05, 0.05 / 0.04, 0.03, 0.00 / 0.00, 0.03, 0.02.

The planning target of ≥ 0.8 is not met under giapsim defaults: 0.20 at 20 TUs × 2 SD. When detection follows abundance (0.65), a high island also raises detection, and the left-censored Blom score turns that into larger scores. Pooled false-island rates with a planted island: high cells 18/900 = 0.020 (covariates_only) and 16/900 = 0.018 (abundance); low cells 36/900 = 0.040 and 24/900 = 0.027. At R = 500 the low 20-TU cells give 0.034 (−1 SD) and 0.036 (−2 SD): within α but above the complete-null 0.020. All of these are high-direction islands, mostly more than 300 TUs from the planted one (see "Scan and maximum statistic").

Several strong islands mask each other (MVP-04 gate 13, Slurm 1872831, 1872881). The block bootstrap resamples the observed series, planted islands included, so the null maxima M_b contain copies of the islands. When the islands are few and short relative to ℓ′, the copies are often intact and M_b sits at the islands' own S. On the K-12 evidence layout (RegulonDB TUs, ρ = 0.5, q ≈ 0.38) three 8-TU high islands at +3 SD have median S 4.7–6.7 (range 3.5–7.3), raise ℓ̂ from a median of 4 to 5 (ℓ′ 7–19, at least 9 in 21 of 22 runs, longer than an 8-TU island), and lift the 95th percentile of M_b from 5.0–5.7 (no islands) to 6.3–7.4. They were recovered in 3 of 33 island-seeds with truth detection (Wilson [0.03, 0.24]; 1 of 33 with GIAP-like detection). A single 20-TU island at +3 SD also raises the 95th percentile of M_b (6.3–9.5), but its S of 7.5–10.3 stays above it: it was recovered in 21 of 22 seeds ([0.78, 0.99]). The one miss had ℓ̂ = 12, ℓ′ = 20, so an intact copy fits in a block. The three 8-TU low islands of the same layout had S −1.6 to −3.3 against a ceiling of 2.2–2.5 and were never recovered (0/330 across all variants, [0, 0.012]). This is the structural zero above. The FWER is unaffected: no spurious island appeared in 220 runs ([0, 0.017]). The effect is a power loss specific to the stationary maxT null, and it is conservative. A missing call among several similar islands is therefore not evidence that they are absent. MVP-04 gates one 20-TU high island for this reason and reports its low islands as exempt with their ceiling. A null that masks the top windows before estimating ℓ̂ is on the backlog.

Signed off by the statistician (PR #188 review).

docs.title: MAYU-style gene-level FDR (closed form)
docs.text: Implements giap.stats.mayu.mayu_gene_fdr (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.2 "MAYU-style closed form (G7)", §8.3, Appendix B.3; issue M4-02). Used by the mayu detection tier (M4-12): when the input has no pairable decoy rows, or when more than 20 % of decoys are unpaired (ADR-0009 keeps this as an upper guard; below it the picked tier rescales decoy wins by 1/f).

docs.title: What is estimated
docs.text: Peptide-level q-values do not control gene-level error (§8.7): false peptides pile up on genes that have no true peptide, and each such hit creates a whole false gene. Given F expected false peptides among the accepted ones, MAYU (Reiter et al. 2009) estimates how many of the genes with ≥ 1 accepted peptide owe their detection to false peptides alone.

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
1. Where false peptides land. Each false peptide independently picks one eligible gene, gene g with probability a_g / Σ_h a_h, where a_g = n_observable_peptides (floored at 1). This is "false peptides spread uniformly over the database's observable peptides": a random match is equally likely to be any observable peptide, so a gene with twice the observable peptides takes twice the wrong hits.
  2. Size bins. Genes are split into mayu_size_bins equal-count bins by rank of a_g (ties broken by input order; fewer bins when there are fewer genes). Within bin b every gene gets the bin's mean share w_b = mean(a_g ∈ b) / Σ_h a_h, so Σ_b N_b w_b = 1. Rank bins are deterministic and always non-empty; with many ties (e.g. all sizes equal) they give equal w_b and the one-bin answer.
  3. Per-gene hit probability. With F independent false peptides, a given gene in bin b is missed by all of them with probability (1 − w_b)^F, so p_b = 1 − (1 − w_b)^F (binomial, sampling with replacement). F is an expectation and need not be an integer; the power is evaluated directly so w_b = 1, F = 0 gives p_b = 0.

  4. Fixed point. False genes can only arise among genes with no true peptide. Let M_b be that number in bin b. Then E[false genes] = M_b p_b and E[undetected genes] = N_b − n_b = M_b (1 − p_b). Eliminating M_b: FP_b = (N_b − n_b + FP_b) p_b, i.e.

    FP_b(t) = (N_b − n_b(t)) · p_b / (1 − p_b), FDR(t) = Σ_b FP_b(t) / Σ_b n_b(t)

(FP_b = N_b − n_b when p_b = 1; FDR clipped to 1; NaN when no gene passes). Under the model this is a ratio of unbiased estimates: E[FP_b] equals the expected number of false genes given M_b. 5. F(t). P(t) = accepted peptides with q ≤ t. With PEPs, F(t) = Σ_{P(t)} PEP (the expected number of false peptides if PEPs are calibrated). Without PEPs, F(t) = t·|P(t)|, the q-value's bound on the false count. When q is the running mean of sorted PEPs the two agree at every threshold (the no_pep attack below is numerically identical to the PEP run). PEPs are used for all peptides or none: all-NaN means "no PEPs"; partly-NaN raises (the tier decides once per run). 6. Gene q. Thresholds are the distinct finite best-peptide q values; q_g = min over t ≥ best_q_g of FDR(t) (monotone_q from giap.stats.tda). Detected at q_g ≤ 0.01. This is one test family per run (all eligible genes), matching §8.1's "Gene detected" row. 7. ≥ 2-peptide variant. The chance that a gene gets ≥ 2 false peptides is approximated by Poisson(λ = F·w_b): p_b⁽²⁾ = 1 − e^(−λ)(1 + λ), plugged into the same FP formula with the same n_b, N_b. Reported as fdr_2pep in the curve and in detection_summary.tsv only; it is not a valid FDR for the set of ≥ 2-peptide genes (n_b still counts ≥ 1-peptide genes), only an indication of how much of the error a two-peptide rule would remove.

docs.title: Approximations
docs.text:
• Binomial vs hypergeometric. Reiter's MAYU draws false protein IDs from the database without replacement (hypergeometric within a size bin). Here false peptides choose genes with replacement; several false peptides on one gene are allowed and count once. For F ≪ N_b the two coincide; for large F the binomial form is the exact one for independent random matches.
  • Bin averaging. p_g = 1 − (1 − w_g)^F is concave in w_g, so within a bin the mean of p_g is ≤ p(mean w). The bins also mix genes whose absence probabilities differ (short genes are more often absent). Both effects are small with 10 rank bins (simulation below: estimated / realised loose-threshold FDR within ±3.5 % for log-SD 0.6–1.2 sizes); a single bin overstates FDR by ≈ 22 % when absent genes are shorter than average (one bin: est. 0.0323 vs realised 0.0264).
  • Expectation, not a bound. FDR(t) estimates E[false]/n; it carries no +1 and no finite-sample guarantee. Its calibration rests on the model and on F being right.

docs.title: Assumptions and when they fail (direction)
docs.text:
Assumption Fails when Direction False hits ∝ a_g wrong hits concentrate on long genes beyond a_g (e.g. ∝ a_g²; long, well-covered proteins attract more near-miss matches) conservative (realised / est. ≈ 0.78): more false peptides land on genes that are present anyway wrong hits spread more evenly than a_g (∝ a_g^0.5 or uniform; e.g. semi-specific or unspecific search while a_g counts tryptic peptides) anti-conservative: uniform hits give realised / est. ≈ 1.24 and FDP 0.0122 at q = 0.01; a_g^0.5 ≈ 1.14 (R = 100) a_g is the right weight a_g is a noisy proxy of the true hit weight (hits ∝ length, a_g = Poisson(length/25), zeros floored) mildly anti-conservative (≈ 1.05; FDP 0.0102 at q = 0.01, R = 300): genes with a_g overstated by noise are more often detected, so the undetected pool is under-weighted a_g ≥ 1 floor genes with no observable peptide conservative (they cannot really be hit) F is right PEPs miscalibrated (too optimistic), or q-values anti-conservative upstream (Wen 2025, §8.7) FDR scales roughly linearly with F; an underestimated F is the main real-world risk and is not detectable here (validation: entrapment, §15.5) Independent hits false peptides cluster (several wrong peptides from one homologous or contaminant protein onto one gene) conservative: fewer distinct false genes than the independent model predicts "No true peptide" = undetected present genes whose true peptides were all rejected get hit by a false peptide counted as false by the estimator, as true by an entrapment truth: conservative Many single-peptide genes (one-hit wonders) not a violation: n_b counts genes with ≥ 1 peptide and the model is per gene at level (attack one_hit_wonders); the share of single-peptide genes is what fdr_2pep speaks to

The anti-conservative cases need a hit distribution flatter than the weights. n_observable_peptides comes from the configured enzyme (§7.3.3); when the input search was semi-specific or unspecific the tier should say so in the manifest (recommendation for M4-12: warn and report fdr with weights a_g ∝ length as a sensitivity row).

docs.title: Relation to the picked tier and ADR-0009
docs.text: Picked target–decoy (Savitski 2015) estimates gene FDR from decoy wins, with a +1 and a finite-sample argument; MAYU estimates it from a hit model and F. Picked is preferred whenever decoys are available. ADR-0009 rescales picked decoy wins by 1/f for unpaired decoys and keeps the > 20 % unpaired fallback to MAYU as an upper guard: beyond that share the paired decoys may no longer be a random sample of all decoys, and MAYU's model-based estimate is the safer one. MAYU's own weak spot (hit distribution flatter than a_g) is independent of the decoy-loss problem, so the fallback does not compound errors. M4-12's gene_fdr suite calibrates both tiers (± PEP) and the decoy-loss cases.

docs.title: Simulation evidence
docs.text: tests/calibration/test_mayu_calibration.py (test-author): under the exact model (two size groups aligned with bins), FP is unbiased, the pooled hit rate matches p_b, and mean FDP ≤ mean FDR + 2 SE.

docs.title: Attack nulls (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_mayu.py)
docs.text:
G = 3,000 genes, lengths log-normal (median 300 aa), a_g = round(length/25) ≥ 1, presence logistic in log a_g (absent genes are short), Poisson(0.3·a_g) true peptides per present gene, calibrated PEPs (each peptide false with probability PEP), accepted at peptide q ≤ 0.01, 10 bins. Criterion §8.4: mean FDP ≤ q + 2 SE. Seed 20261014. Mean FDP at gene q ≤ 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 (the loosest estimated FDR is ≈ 0.026–0.033, so 0.05 and 0.10 accept every gene):

Attack R = 50 R = 300 realised / est. (R = 300) detectability_bias (base) 0.0095 / 0.0267 / 0.0267 0.0098 / 0.0266 / 0.0266 1.005 heavy_tail (log-SD 1.2) 0.0092 / 0.0318 / 0.0318 0.0095 / 0.0321 / 0.0321 0.982 one_hit_wonders 0.0053 / 0.0053 / 0.0053 0.0053 / 0.0053 / 0.0053 0.997 long_gene_concentration (∝ a_g²) 0.0076 / 0.0202 / 0.0202 0.0076 / 0.0206 / 0.0206 0.782 no_pep (F = t·|P|) as base as base 1.005

All stay at level (SE ≤ 0.0004 at q = 0.01, 0.0007 at the looser levels). Note the base case sits at 0.0098 for q = 0.01: the estimator is essentially unbiased, with no conservative margin.

Violations (direction tests, not level gates): uniform_hits realised / est. 1.24 (FDP 0.0122 at q = 0.01), noisy_size 1.05 (FDP 0.0102 at q = 0.01; at the 2-SE edge).

docs.title: Numerical notes
docs.text:
• 1 − (1 − w)^F loses relative precision only for w ≲ 1e-9 (relative error ~1e-7 at w = 1e-9, F = 0.01); real genomes have w ≥ 1/Σa ≈ 1e-6. -expm1(F·log1p(−w)) with a w = 1 guard would be exact; not needed.
  • p⁽²⁾ is clipped to ≤ p (always true mathematically: Poisson P(≥ 2) ≤ Poisson P(≥ 1) ≤ binomial P(≥ 1)).
  • Not validated by the function: PEPs outside [0, 1] (a negative PEP lowers F silently), non-finite sizes (NaN sizes give an all-NaN q), non-integer n_bins. Callers (M4-12) build these from validated tables; input validation would be cheap and is recommended.
  • No effect size or CI: gene q is an error-rate estimate, not a test of an effect. The curve's fp and n_genes (the estimated false and total detected genes) are what detection_summary.tsv should report next to the q threshold; no CI is available for a plug-in model estimate, which is why the calibration suites carry the evidence.

docs.title: Sign-off
docs.text: Statistician (M4-02 review, 2026-10-14): approved for mayu_gene_fdr as implemented in src/giap/stats/mayu.py: formula matches §7.3.2 and B.3, bins and monotone q are correct, at level under the model and the attacks above. Forwarded to M4-12: the flat-hit-distribution direction (semi-/unspecific searches), the base case's zero margin at q = 0.01, and input validation of PEPs and sizes.

docs.title: Multiple testing: Benjamini–Hochberg
docs.text: Implements giap.stats.multitest.bh (GIAP_SPEC.md §8.2, §8.3, Appendix B.1; issue M4-01). Statistician sign-off: see the end of this note.

docs.title: Definition
docs.text:
For the m non-missing p-values sorted ascending, p₍₁₎ ≤ … ≤ p₍ₘ₎,

q₍ᵢ₎ = min( 1, min_{j ≥ i} m · p₍ⱼ₎ / j ).

Rejecting every hypothesis with q ≤ α is the Benjamini–Hochberg (1995) step-up procedure at level α. q is returned in input order (never sorted).

  • Monotone. The running minimum from the largest p makes q non-decreasing in p, so the q ≤ α set is exactly the BH rejection set.
  • Ties. Tied p-values get equal q (the running minimum assigns each tie group the value at its largest rank). The result does not depend on input order.
  • Missing values. NaN p-values stay NaN and are not counted in m. A NaN means "no test was possible" (for example, no permutation was run), not "p = 1". Callers who want such units to dilute the family must pass 1.0 explicitly.
  • Range. Any non-NaN p outside [0, 1] (including ±inf) raises ValueError; clipping upstream is the caller's job, because silent clipping hides bugs.
  • Empty input returns an empty array.

docs.title: What is and is not controlled
docs.text:
• BH controls FDR ≤ π₀·α ≤ α for independent p-values and under positive regression dependence (PRDS; Benjamini & Yekutieli 2001), which covers one-sided tests on positively correlated Gaussian statistics. It does not guarantee FDR under arbitrary dependence (BY would be needed); GIAP's families are chosen so that PRDS is plausible or so that resampling respects the dependence (TU blocks, circular shifts).
  • No π₀ estimation is done (no Storey adjustment): BH is conservative by the factor π₀.
  • Discrete p-values (permutation p = (1 + b)/(1 + B), rounded p) keep control; BH is conservative for them.
  • BH guarantees nothing across families. Error control is per family (§8.1), so a reader scanning several families should expect roughly α × (number of discoveries) false ones per family.

docs.title: Families (§8.1, pre-declared)
docs.text:
BH is applied within each family and never across them:

Family BH unit Level Region effect region, within region type 0.05 Autocorrelation lag, across lags 0.05 Operon discordance pair 0.1 Category detection (ORA) category, per ontology × direction 0.05 GSEA gene set, per collection 0.05

The family keys are fixed in the calling modules (M4-17/18, M5, M6, M8), which must cite this table. Islands use FWER (maximum statistic) and identification/placement use target–decoy q-values (see target-decoy.md), not BH. All p and q values are reported, whether or not they pass.

docs.title: Simulation evidence
docs.text:
Generator (tests/calibration/test_stats_fdr_calibration.py): N = 2000 tests, π₀ = 0.8, null p ~ U(0, 1), alternative p ~ Beta(0.1, 8). Criterion (§8.4): mean FDP ≤ q + 2 SE. Seed calibration_base = 20261014.

R q = 0.01 q = 0.05 q = 0.10 mean discoveries (q = 0.05) 50 (CI) 0.0094 ± 0.0010 0.0428 ± 0.0016 0.0790 ± 0.0017 331 300 0.0081 ± 0.0003 0.0406 ± 0.0006 0.0800 ± 0.0008 331

Observed FDP ≈ π₀·q, as theory predicts.

Attack (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_fdr_engine.py, bh_equicorrelated_ties): N = 1000, one-sided z with pairwise correlation 0.5 and p rounded to three decimals (heavy ties), R = 300: FDP 0.0049 ± 0.0015, 0.0281 ± 0.0046, 0.0592 ± 0.0073 at q = 0.01, 0.05, 0.10 — at level.

Exactness: agrees with statsmodels.stats.multitest.multipletests(method="fdr_bh") to rel. 1e-12 (tests/property) and reproduces Appendix B.1.

docs.text: Statistician (M4-01 review, 2026-10-14): approved for bh as implemented in src/giap/stats/multitest.py.

docs.title: Novel ORFs (M7)
docs.text: Status: §"Class FDR" written for the statistician's round-2 review of PR #237 (M7-11). Code: src/giap/novel/fdr.py (pure); the novel_orfs step wiring (M7-11b, PR #256) is src/giap/novel/class_call.py and §"Wiring in the novel_orfs step". Spec: GIAP_SPEC.md §7.6.4, §7.9.2, §8.1, §8.2; ADR-0009, ADR-0010; docs/specs/M7-11-novel-class-fdr.md, lead decisions 1–14; docs/specs/M7-11b-class-fdr-wiring.md, lead decisions 1–7.

docs.title: Class FDR
docs.text: Novel peptides have a lower prior than annotated ones, so the global search FDR understates their error (§7.6.4). GIAP therefore estimates the error of a novel-ORF call within its class (intergenic, cds_outframe, antisense, nterm_extension), with stats.alpha.novel_orfs (0.01) as the call threshold.

docs.title: Regimes (rule 1, decision 1)
docs.text:
The regime is chosen per ORF from the source of its peptides, database first.

  • picked_decoy: the run has decoy rows whose stripped protein IDs (longest input.decoy_prefixes match removed) are class-tagged makedb IDs GIAPORF_{class}_{contig}_{start1}_{end1}_{p|m}, and the ORF has at least one database (non-denovo) peptide.
  • denovo_subgroup: otherwise, when the ORF has a de novo peptide.
  • unestimated: everything else, for example decoys from a Bakta-protein search (rev_<locus_tag>). The pass-1 rule (≥ 2 distinct peptides) applies, and class_fdr = unestimated.

Database and de novo q-values are never pooled into one list. Their decoys answer different questions (a search-engine competition and a genome placement), so a pooled list would have no single decoy model.

docs.title: Picked class FDR (rule 2; ADR-0009)
docs.text:
Matching. Each target ORF is matched to the makedb six-frame ORF with the same (contig, strand, stop). A makedb ORF is stop to stop, so the codon position just past its 3′ end identifies it: the entry's 0-based end on the plus strand, and 3 nt below the entry's start on the minus strand. For an ORF closed by a stop codon, that position is where Orf.stop (the stop's lowest coordinate) lies. A 3′-open ORF (linear contig end or an X codon) has no closing stop: Orf.stop is its last whole codon, and makedb ends the segment at that codon's end. Its key is therefore Orf.stop + 3 on the plus strand and Orf.stop − 3 on the minus strand (decision 13). When replicon lengths are given, both keys are wrapped modulo the length, so origin-crossing entries match (decisions 8 and 14). Without lengths, an ORF whose entry crosses the origin is unestimated. An nterm_extension ORF with no stop match is paired by locus tag. Its makedb entry covers the upstream part plus the first 30 codons, so its stop lies inside the gene.

The pairing rules have these consequences: - When the ORF's class and the entry's tag differ, the entry tag wins, because pairing and the class list follow the entry. The ORF is flagged class_mismatch (decision 9). - An ORF whose own class is untagged (pseudogene, sorf, cterm_extension) is unestimated (untagged_class, decisions 2 and 10). - A tagged ORF with no entry is unestimated (no_makedb_pair, decision 7).

Scores. The score of an entry's target side is its matched ORF's best peptide. Only non-de-novo peptides count, because makedb decoys mimic database-search targets only; adding de novo target evidence with no decoy counterpart would be anti-conservative (decision 10). The score of its decoy side is the best decoy row whose stripped ID is the entry. Within each entry class, picked_fdr keeps the better side per entry, and ties go to the decoy. Entries hit only by their decoy count as decoy wins.

Unscored rows (decision 11, as M4-24). C9 allows a missing q_value and a missing score. Mapping a missing q to +∞ would rank an unscored decoy below every target and silently give D = 0. In the statistician's all-null attack, 400 of 400 null ORFs then reached q ≤ 0.05. GIAP therefore ranks a class only on a key that every target and decoy row of that class carries: - (q ascending, then score descending) when every q is finite; - otherwise score alone, when every score is finite; - otherwise the class is unestimated with reason decoys_unscored.

Paired share and rescaling. f is the share of the class's distinct stripped decoy IDs that are makedb entries. The decoy's class is the tag in its ID. Unpaired decoys never enter the list, and each decoy win counts 1/f:

FDR(t) = (D(t)/f + 1) / T(t), made monotone (ADR-0009, via stats.tda.picked_fdr_rescaled).

The unit is distinct IDs because decoy wins are counted per entry: the share of lost entries is what the correction needs, while a row count would weight entries by their number of peptides. An entry missing from id_map also loses its target (no_makedb_pair). That loss is symmetric, so 1/f is conservative there. 1/f matters when a decoy is lost but its target stays.

80 % guard (decision 4). A class with f < 0.80 falls back to unestimated (paired_share_low), by analogy with the §7.3.2 tier guard; changing the guard needs an ADR. Below the guard the cost is power (the ≥ 2-peptide rule), not validity. In the decoy-loss attack (10 % and 20 % of decoy rows re-pointed to unmapped tagged IDs), FDP stays at level.

A class with targets and no decoys gets q = 1/T, so it needs ≥ 100 target wins before any ORF reaches 0.01 (the B.6 logic).

docs.title: De novo subgroup FDR (rule 3; ADR-0010)
docs.text:
Decoy hits come from the mapping work tables (search = decoy). Each peptide is taken at its best decoy cost (minimum n_diff). Each hit takes the M3-14 LocusClassifier class of its mirrored target interval, and is counted once per (peptide, class) at its minimum E (decision 10). A target peptide enters the list of its ORF's class with its E. Per class, peptides are ordered by E:

FDR_class(e) = (W_class(e) + c) / T_class(e), monotone q (stratum_qvalues),

where W sums the decoys' own π̂ (a missing π̂ counts as 1), and c is the largest π̂ over the searched peptides, those with a target or decoy hit (decision 5), with a missing π̂ again counting as 1. A class with no decoy hit gets q = c/T. A hit with no E (e_target or e_decoy NaN) raises ValueError naming the peptide (decision 11). Dropping such a decoy would shrink W and be anti-conservative: with 30 % of decoy E missing, FDP was 0.0133 / 0.069 / 0.104 against bounds of 0.0115 / 0.053 / 0.103.

docs.title: Why the classes are never pooled
docs.text: The false share differs strongly between classes. intergenic ORFs are mostly false, while cds_outframe calls next to expressed genes are mostly true. A pooled list lends the clean class's target wins to the noisy class. In the statistician's attack (intergenic 3 % true next to cds_outframe 80 % true, FDP measured inside intergenic), the per-class estimate is at level. A pooled list gives FDP 0.068 / 0.29 / 0.46 at q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10. The de novo attack (80 % of chance hits intergenic, correct peptides 5 % intergenic) is also at level per class.

docs.title: ORF q = minimum peptide q (decision 3): anti-conservative
docs.text:
For de novo ORFs, the ORF class q is the minimum of its peptides' subgroup q. That is the best-evidence statistic, but it is anti-conservative at ORF level: a false ORF with k wrong peptides gets k chances to draw a small q. In the review's generator, ORF FDP at q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 was:

Wrong peptides per false ORF ORF FDP q + 2 SE 1–5 0.0185 / 0.078 / 0.113 0.0117 / 0.053 / 0.103 1–10 0.030 / 0.097 / 0.131 —

The 1–5 case failed in both confirmation blocks. That generator is a worst case: in real data, chance hits of wrong de novo peptides rarely fall in one ORF. The cases that matter are systematic de novo errors that cluster, such as reversed stretches (§8.5 attack 5) in intergenic space. M7-13 G4 must measure ORF-level FDP per class with false ORFs carrying ≥ 3 peptides, including attack 5. If it fails, an ADR chooses between a picked ORF-level competition on the genome decoy and a per-ORF Bonferroni over peptides (decision 3). A strict xfail in tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_novel_class_fdr.py flags any change to decision 3.

docs.title: Wiring in the novel_orfs step (M7-11b)
docs.text:
Code: src/giap/novel/class_call.py, giap.novel.evidence.class_rules and _call, src/giap/steps/novel.py. Spec: docs/specs/M7-11b-class-fdr-wiring.md, lead decisions 1–7.

Inputs. The step reads the C9 peptides (picked regime), and for the de novo regime it reads placement_costs, hits_exact and hits_tolerant. All are optional. Without peptides, every ORF is unestimated (no_decoys), which is the pass-1 output byte for byte. One regime is assigned per ORF, with no cascade: a picked-regime ORF whose picked result is unestimated never falls back to its de novo peptides (Q6). Each (regime, class) list is one §8.1 "Novel ORF" family, and α is stats.alpha.novel_orfs everywhere.

Call rule (rule 6). - Numeric class_fdr = q: called = class rule ∧ q ≤ α. q is compared as the unformatted float. The TSV shows %.6g, and q is never parsed back from the cell. There is no peptide minimum (§7.6.4), but the cds_outframe and antisense class rules still require 2 peptides. - class_fdr = unestimated: called = class rule ∧ n_peptides ≥ min_peptides_without_decoys (§7.6.4 "Neither"), with the flag class_fdr_unestimated. - lost_pick (Q1): the class is estimated, but the ORF's own decoy beat it or tied it. The cell is 1 and the ORF is never called. - Why it must not fall back to the ≥ 2-peptide rule: losing the pick is the competition's evidence that the target looks like chance. Falling back would call exactly the ORFs that the competition rejected. - In the statistician's attack (cds_outframe ORFs of 2–3 peptides, 25 % true, exchangeable false targets and decoys; tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_class_call_wiring.py), the fallback reading gives FDP 0.98 / 0.31 / 0.35 of called at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10. The wired rule gives 0.0015 / 0.043 / 0.096, against bounds of 0.012 / 0.058 / 0.112 (R = 50). - Why 1 and not "the q at the decoy's rank": the target never enters the picked list, so it has no q. 1 is the conservative bound, and it keeps the cell numeric. - The FDR claim covers the set {q ≤ α}. The class rule then keeps a subset of it. This preserves control as long as the rule does not prefer false ORFs. The rules (start codon, length, RBS support, ≥ 2 peptides) favour real ORFs. M7-13 G4 measures the called set itself, class_rule_met ∧ q ≤ a, from the side table. - Fallback calls in a makedb run carry no error control. These are the no_makedb_pair, no_target_score and untagged-class ORFs. They are labelled unestimated (§8: never silently trusted), and G4's prediction set ("class q ≤ q") excludes them. M7-13 should therefore also report how many calls in each class came through the fallback.

Class q floor (rule 8). - No picked q can fall below 1/T_wins, where T_wins is the class's entries won by their target. At any threshold, FDR = (D/f + 1)/T ≥ 1/T ≥ 1/T_wins, and the monotone q is a minimum of these values. - No de novo q can fall below c/T, where T is the class's target peptides, because W ≥ 0. - When the floor is strictly above α, nothing in the class can be called. The run then logs the WARNING novel_orfs.class_q_floor_above_alpha: a class with fewer than about 1/α candidates cannot be called at α. q and α are unchanged (Khoa, 2026-10-22). - T_wins = 100 at α = 0.01 gives a floor equal to α. That raises no warning, because the best ORF can still be called. - A class with no target win (picked) or no target (de novo), and an unestimated class, has no floor and raises no warning. - The warning goes to the manifest warnings list (--strict exits 3), not to a run-flag token (Q4). It mirrors the gene-level q_floor_above_alpha. - The picked floor counts entries won. The warning text quotes n_targets, the ORFs entering the list. When several ORFs share one entry, or many targets lose the pick, the two differ: read q_floor in the event data, not the target count.

Paired share in v1 (rule 2, Q5). - No run input carries makedb's db_id_map.tsv. makedb_id_map therefore builds the map from every class-tagged ID in protein_ids (targets, and decoys with their prefix stripped). The nterm_extension locus tags come from nterm_entries on the run's own gene model. - So every tagged decoy is an entry, the paired share is f = 1, and the 80 % guard cannot fire from the pipeline (backlog). - This is not anti-conservative. The guard and the 1/f rescaling exist because an unpaired decoy is dropped from the list while targets stay, so D is undercounted. In v1 no tagged decoy is dropped: a decoy whose entry has no target ORF competes alone, and so counts as a decoy win. - In the re-pointed-decoys attack (20 % and 50 % of decoy rows moved to tagged IDs with no target, through makedb_id_map), FDP is 0.0081 / 0.044 / 0.089 at 20 % and 0.0062 / 0.034 / 0.071 at 50 %, against bounds of about 0.012 / 0.053 / 0.104. FDP falls as the loss grows. - Pairing can still be lost on the target side. - A nterm_extension ORF pairs through the locus tag of the run's own nterm_entries, and the other classes pair through the (contig, strand, stop) key. If the run's annotation or genome differs from the one makedb used, the ORF is no_makedb_pair. - Its decoy stays in the list, so the rest of the class becomes more conservative. The ORF itself, however, drops to the uncontrolled fallback above. - A real db_id_map.tsv would not change this, because f counts observed decoys. - No share detects decoy rows that are missing from the input altogether, for example an engine that exports only some of its decoys. On the calibration generator, halving the tagged decoy rows gives FDP 0.017 / 0.096 / 0.20. Input decoys are assumed complete, as for the gene-level picked tier.

De novo inputs (rule 3, Q11). - denovo_inputs keeps only source = denovo rows of placement_costs: - targets: ORF peptides with a finite e_target; - decoys: those peptides' decoy hit rows at their best decoy cost, carrying e_decoy; - weights: π̂ from pi_denovo; - c: the largest π̂ over the de novo peptides with a target or decoy hit. - Database peptides' decoy hits and their π̂ (NaN, which would count as 1) never enter a de novo list. This is valid, because the list estimates the chance hits of wrong de novo peptides. - The target E is the peptide's best target E over the genome, as M7-11 assumed. The step does not restrict it to the ORF's interval. candidate_rows keeps only peptides with a single novel locus and no hit in an excluding class, so the two usually coincide. They are not guaranteed to. - Decoys of de novo peptides that are not in a de novo ORF still count (for example, banned, multi-locus or picked-regime ORF peptides). That is conservative.

Calibration of the wired path. tests/calibration/test_class_call_calibration.py runs class_fdr, with its own makedb_id_map and denovo_inputs, plus class_fdr_cell. - In the statistician's mutation probe (PR #256), these mutations fail the criterion: - de novo decoys restricted to ORF peptides (0.0175 / 0.084 / 0.116 against 0.012 / 0.053 / 0.103); - decoy weights halved; - c = 0 (at α = 0.01); - half of the picked decoy rows dropped. - Two mutations pass: - dropping the picked +1, whose effect is too small with T in the hundreds; - pooling the classes, because the generator gives every class the same prior. The M7-11 low_prior_class attack covers that case. - The suite measures numeric cells only. test_attack_class_call_wiring.py adds the called column.

Diagnostics. novel/novel_class_fdr.parquet has one row per novel_orfs.tsv row, in the same order. - Columns: orf_id, class, fdr_class, regime, q (float, NaN unless estimated and won), class_fdr (the TSV cell), reason, class_mismatch, class_rule_met and called. - G4 calls at level a with class_rule_met ∧ q ≤ a. A lost_pick row has q NaN, so it is never in the set. - One novel_orfs.class_fdr INFO event per (regime, class) list carries the counts, f, c, the floor and n_called. The manifest novel_orfs.classes block holds the same data.

Statistician (PR #256, M7-11b review, 2026-10-23): wiring, call rule and floor rule reviewed. Verdict recorded on the PR.

docs.title: Exact systematic de novo errors (ADR-0050)
docs.text: The class FDR treats wrong peptides as decoy hits treat them: a wrong read lands on the genome by chance, so a reversed or shuffled genome decoy is as likely to receive it. A de novo read that is wrong but exactly equals the translation of a non-coding six-frame segment breaks that assumption. It places with zero cost, like a true peptide, and no decoy can match it except by chance, so no decoy-based estimate counts it. When several such reads fall in one segment, the ORF also gets several chances at a small q (decision 3). In M7-13 G4-k3 (a stress design: 20 injected false ORFs per class, 3–5 wrong reads each; R = 300) the ORF-level FDP was 0.072–0.075 for cds_outframe and antisense at both q = 0.01 and 0.05, and 0.015–0.017 for intergenic at 0.01. The exact reads account for the excess; error-bearing reads alone leave only a small excess at q = 0.01. The size of the excess scales with how many such errors a run contains, so it is not a prediction for real data. GIAP therefore does not claim class-FDR control against exact systematic de novo errors. q values and calls are unchanged. Calls that this limitation can affect carry denovo_only_unsupported unless chance RBS support exempts them (below): every peptide is de novo, none is a database PSM, and there is no RBS support beyond what the class rule already requires. RBS support at the 0.10 quantile is weak evidence: in M7-13 G4-k3, the chosen start of an injected false ORF that reached q ≤ 0.05 passed it in 12 of 199 cds_outframe rows (0.060) and 15 of 199 antisense rows (0.075) (Slurm 1879351, fast tier, R = 10), so those calls escape the flag; intergenic and nterm_extension are never exempt. The flag is therefore a pointer to an evidence gap, not a second error estimate: flagged calls are not estimated to be false, and unflagged de novo-only calls are not estimated to be correct. In a run with only de novo input nearly every call carries it. Users who need such calls should confirm them by a database search against the giap makedb six-frame database, or by independent evidence.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• c over hit peptides only. ADR-0010 reads "the peptides … searched"; c here is the largest π̂ over peptides with a target or decoy hit (decision 5). This is anti-conservative only when the highest-π̂ peptides have no hit at all: negligible at N in the thousands, visible in B.6-sized lists.
  • Class asymmetry. A de novo target takes its ORF's class (the highest-priority member class), while its decoy analogue takes its own interval's class. A wrong peptide that joins an ORF of another class moves T toward that class, and no D moves with it. The effect is small; M7-13 G4 reports FDP per class, not only per regime.
  • Target E. A target peptide's E is its best E over all its target hits, not its hit inside the ORF. The M7-11b step does not restrict it, and documents this under "De novo inputs" above.
  • regime() of a mixed set of ORFs returns the first of picked / de novo / unestimated held. The M7-11b step uses orf_regimes per ORF. The regime of each ORF is in the side table, and the per-class events hold the list counts. No separate regime-count event is logged.

docs.title: C-terminal extensions (M7-16 rule 12, ADR-0058)
docs.text: A cterm_extension ORF is called when some peptide interval strictly contains the gene's annotated terminal stop codon and extends past it on the 3′ side (spans_annotated_stop); its label is readthrough_candidate. The class is untagged, so its class FDR is unestimated and the call needs ≥ 2 distinct peptides (M7-11 decision 2). A window that ends on the stop codon classifies as cds_inframe and is no extension evidence; it shows up as a stop_codon ALT site instead. A called row is written to annotation_patch.gff3 as the gene from its start to the ORF's stop (Note=cterm_extension, partial=true when the ORF is open at a linear 3′ end), and makedb --patch translates the old stop codon as X.

docs.title: Operons: the within-operon distribution and the missed-operon decoy FDR
docs.text: Issue M6-01 (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.4.2–§7.4.4, §8.1–§8.3), modules giap.stats.tdist and giap.stats.decoy_fdr, with the lead decisions of docs/specs/M6-01-lead-decisions.md. The pair table is M6-04, the discordance tests M6-05, the missed-operon step M6-06 and the operon-level calibration gate M6-09. This note covers the engine and the discordance step (M6-05); the other step sections come later.

docs.title: The within-operon distribution
docs.text:
Model. Δ = log2 abundance(downstream) − log2 abundance(upstream) over OP pairs whose two genes are both detected (imputed abundances are excluded by the caller) is modelled as a Student-t with free location μ, scale σ and degrees of freedom ν ∈ [2, 50] (fit_student_t, default df_bounds = (2, 50)). μ is free because operon polarity makes the downstream gene systematically lower; a heavy tail is allowed because operon partners legitimately differ 1–10-fold (§7.4).

Fit. Maximum likelihood, Nelder–Mead on (μ, log σ, ν) from μ₀ = median, σ₀ = 1.4826 · MAD (floored at 10⁻⁶), ν₀ = 8, maxiter 2,000. The ν bound is passed to scipy's bounded Nelder–Mead rather than through the logit reparameterisation the issue text names; the two have the same optimum. A simplex pressed against a bound stops just short of it (ν = 49.9997), so after the fit both bounds are scored at the fitted (μ, σ) and the best of the three ν is kept (_snap_to_bound). That step can only lower the negative log-likelihood, so it cannot move the fit away from the optimum; a ν on a bound is a legitimate optimum and is returned with converged = True. converged is otherwise scipy's own flag (False when the optimiser stops on iterations); M6-05 marks the tests unestimated when it is False.

Two-sided p. p = 2 · min(F, 1 − F), F = F_t((Δ − μ)/σ; ν) (student_t_two_sided): exactly 1 at Δ = μ, asymmetric about 0 whenever μ ≠ 0, NaN in → NaN out, all-NaN under an unestimated fit.

Abundance-dependent scale (M6-13, ADR-0055 option (a)). Proteomics noise grows at low abundance. One σ for every OP pair is therefore too narrow for low-abundance pairs and too wide for high-abundance ones. Attack D-1 measured the consequence through the step: the pooled level failed at α = 0.05 and 0.10, and the lowest-abundance quartile ran at about 3× nominal (Slurm 1884493). The scale is therefore modelled as σ_i = σ₀ · exp(γ z_i), where z_i is the pair's mean log2 abundance, standardised over the fit pairs (fit_student_t_scaled). - μ, σ₀, γ and ν are fitted jointly by maximum likelihood, by Nelder–Mead from the constant fit, with ν ∈ [2, 50] and γ ∈ [−2, 2]. - γ = 0 is the constant model above, and the p of a pair is 2 · sf_t(|Δ − μ̂| / σ̂_i; ν̂) (scaled_t_two_sided). It applies from the same 20 usable pairs as the constant model. At n = 20–50 it was measured at level, and more conservative than the constant fit (statistician, M6-13 S-5). - The fitted σ̂_i does not depend on how z is centred or scaled. γ is reported per SD of pair-mean log2 abundance, and per log2 unit.

Tested pairs outside the fit's abundance range (imputed pairs) are evaluated at the nearest end of that range, not extrapolated.

The constant model is used instead, and the run log says why, when: - the pair means vary by less than 0.1 log2 (SD). This is a relevance guard, not an identifiability one: over so narrow a range no noise curve changes σ appreciably; - the four-parameter fit fails to converge, collapses, or fits worse than the constant one.

There is no model-selection step: when the four-parameter fit is available it is used. The likelihood ratio against γ = 0 is reported, not acted on.

γ̂ describes the spread of Δ among pairs whose two genes were both detected, given their observed mean abundance. It is not the instrument's noise curve, for two reasons. - Detection truncation can narrow the spread at low abundance (in the simulator the effect is not measurable: γ̂ is 0.001 under the null). - m carries the same measurement noise as Δ, which attenuates γ̂.

The conditional spread is the right null for the test, which is conditional on detection.

What the level claim covers. The claim is the pooled per-pair level. m = a + Δ/2 contains the response, so even under homoscedastic noise the pairs in the outer quartiles of m are enriched for large |Δ − μ| (1.05–1.17× nominal at α = 0.01, for the constant and the log-linear model alike). Within quartiles of an abundance that is independent of Δ (the upstream gene's), the null is at level.

The one-detected P(miss) still averages over the raw within-operon ratios. Under abundance-dependent noise that sample is too narrow for a low-abundance partner (open, M6-13 Q1).

The log-linear form is an assumption. Attack D-1b checks a step and a variance floor, and D-1c checks per-gene measurement noise.

The record (full tier, Slurm 1886733 task 6, commit fd701591, R = 1,000; records in local/logs/calibration/m6-13-fd701591-full/). Rates are at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10. Pooled rates use 200 random tested pairs per replicate, with bounds 0.0104 / 0.0510 / 0.1013.

arm pooled level worst quartile (cut, × nominal) γ̂ per SD (SD over replicates) mean LR gate null, operon_null(1800) 0.00982 / 0.04991 / 0.09983, pass upstream a: 1.06× (Q3, α = 0.01); pair mean m: 1.14× (Q4) −0.0014 (0.042) 1.11 D-1, σ ∝ e^(−z/2) 0.00979 / 0.05016 / 0.09930, pass planted z, Q1: 0.00929 / 0.0478 / 0.0969, pass (bounds 0.0106 / 0.0512 / 0.1017); Q4 1.06× −0.513 (0.041); planted −0.5 140.2 D-1b-floor 0.00986 / 0.05013 / 0.09934, pass planted z, Q4: 1.22× / 1.15× / 1.11× −0.430 (0.042) 105.0 D-1b-step 0.00954 / 0.05168 / 0.10212, confirmed fail (block 2: 0.05173 / 0.10312) planted z, Q2: 1.81× / 1.82× / 1.66×; Q3: 0.22× / 0.35× / 0.43× −0.286 (0.042) 45.7 D-1c, per-gene noise 0.01012 / 0.04794 / 0.09688, pass true upstream a, Q4: 1.68× / 1.25× / 1.14× −0.229 (0.040) 42.0
  • No quartile in any arm reaches the 2α escalation. The highest is D-1b-step Q2, at 1.82×.
  • The constant model under the same null gives a worst upstream-a quartile of 1.04× and a worst m quartile of 1.14×. On m, the log-linear model is no worse than the constant one.
  • Every one of the 1,000 fits in every arm is loglinear:None. No arm fell back to the constant model.
  • γ̂ per log2 unit: null −0.0005, D-1 −0.220, floor −0.185, step −0.124, D-1c −0.098.
