What the attacks show:

  • FDR control holds in every tested arm that makes calls. All of those arms use one configuration: convergent-only decoys and 100 planted pairs at 10⁻³ SD. The arms cover AR(1) at ρ = 0.5 and 0.9, detection confounded with distance, and an abundance mix that differs between NO pairs and decoys. A′ at ρ = 0.9 is 0.046, well below the 0.15 escalation threshold.
  • With the shipped decoys, A, A′ and B make no call, so they test nothing beyond "no false call".
  • Other decoy configurations, and planted spreads where calls are rarer, are not covered.
  • M-1 made no call in any arm: shipped decoys (median min q 0.95), convergent-only (0.31) and 6,000 genes (0.85). So M-1 is untested here. This is a no-call result, not evidence of robustness.
  • In the shipped arm, the SW-sparse bins hold every q high.
  • The convergent-only arm has no SW decoys, and the reason it stays above q 0.1 has not been analysed.
  • The PR #148 failure (balanced classes, ~2,000 NO pairs) is not reproduced, and the risk stays open. The ADR question, whether to exclude imputed pairs, is unchanged.
  • C (the one-detected arm, oracle P(miss)). With the generating detection model, the share of one-detected pairs with P(miss) ≤ α is at most 1.8 α. That is below the 2 α revisit threshold, so the M6-05 Q3 decision (P(miss) with no q, outside the BH family) stands.
  • This is the oracle P(miss); the M6-02 fitted model is not used here.
  • The step's arm (M6-05H) is not merged, and test_attack_c_through_the_step skips until it is.
  • D-1 fails the pooled level. It is confirmed at α = 0.05 and 0.10, where the rate is 4.2 % and 6.4 % above nominal (0.0521 and 0.1064); within the lowest quartile it is about 3× nominal. One t for all pairs puts null calls on noisy, low-abundance pairs.
  • D-1 stays gated: test_attack_d1_level checks the pooled level and the quartile, as a strict xfail naming ADR-0055 (proposed), in the ADR-0049 pattern.
  • A sharded discordance task followed by --merge exits 1 on it until ADR-0055 is decided. That is intended.
  • In an oracle check (scratch only, not reproducible from the repo; the implementer PR re-measures it through D-1 and D-1b, R = 150), a heteroscedastic t with σ_i = σ₀ e^(γ z_i) restores the level: pooled 0.0103 / 0.0510 / 0.1004, lowest quartile 0.0085 / 0.047 / 0.095. Under the gate null it changes nothing.
  • Khoa decides ADR-0055: (a) that method, recommended, or (b) a narrowed and labelled claim.
  • D-2 (TU-chained Δ) is built into every scenario. D-3 is the M6-05 review table above.

Verdict (simulation half). §7.4.7 criteria 1–3 pass at full R: - criterion 1, the gate with the shipped decoys, is a recorded vacuous pass (Khoa, 2026-10-22). The extra convergent-only arm also passes, non-vacuously; - criterion 2 is attack A (ρ = 0.5). It too is vacuous with the shipped decoys, and passes non-vacuously only in the extra convergent-only arm. Attack B behaves the same way; - criterion 3 is the KS test and the pooled level.

Attacks A, B and M-2 pass; A and B with the shipped decoys are vacuous. A′ and C are recorded below their thresholds.

  • missed_operons: MET (vacuous with the shipped decoys; extra arm FDP 0.033). It is not power evidence, and FDR evidence comes only from the convergent-only arm.
  • Discordance gate: NOT MET (D-1), pending Khoa (ADR-0055). The §15.4 half of the gate (M6-11/M6-12, RegulonDB) is separate.

Verdict after M6-13 (Slurm 1886733, fd701591). ADR-0055 option (a) is in place. - Discordance gate: MET for the claim of ADR-0055 and its Amendment 1: the pooled per-pair level under smooth, monotone σ(abundance). - D-1, D-1b-floor and D-1c pass the pooled level at R = 1,000, and D-1's lowest quartile passes its bound. - The gate null is unchanged: level, KS and BH all pass. - The log-linear σ is non-inferior in power. - D-1b-step is a confirmed fail, as pre-registered. It is outside the claim and stays a strict xfail. - Recorded limits: - top-quartile excess up to 1.68× at α = 0.01 under D-1c, and 1.22× under the floor (below 2α); - the pair-mean-m quartiles are not a level check; - one-detected P(miss) under abundance-dependent noise is still open (M6-13 Q1).

docs.title: Sign-off
docs.text:
Statistician (PR #140 review, 2026-10-21): FDR control and the KDE evaluation approved; the zero-MAD / dominant-tie fit (σ → 0 reported as converged) must be fixed before merge; the power limitation above is a property of the specified method and is reported, not a merge blocker.

Statistician (PR #148 review, 2026-10-21): the missed-operon step is at level under every continuous null tried, including an abundance mix that differs between NO and decoy pairs. Pairs with both genes imputed share a fill value, so their Δ = 0 is a point mass that can produce wholesale false calls when it is more common among NO pairs. The imputed state must travel with the pair rows now, and exclusion on both sides is an ADR for Khoa. Relative-scale rows need unestimated (§7.3.4), and scored rows need ci_unestimated. Statistician (PR #147 review, 2026-10-21): the discordance test is at level with the double use included, and BH over the both-detected t p-values is the specified family. The flag on tested rows must say that the CI, not the claim, is unestimated. Power is near zero at realistic effects; that is reported here, not a merge blocker. Attack D-1 is owed to M6-09.

Statistician (M6-12 PR-A design review, 2026-10-23): blocked on B1 (the refit diverges on K-12 from the spec's start; fixed by the separation check, the (logit ȳ, 0) start and step-halving) and B2 (the TerminatorNet "lower bound" ignores coincidental matches; fixed by the offset-preserving coincidence null and the corrected bound). Both fixes are specified in "K-12 cut-off calibration (M6-12)"; once the lead accepts them the design is approved. Directon resampling, the stable rule, the fixed-t CIs with the selection statement, and the degenerate rules are sound.

Statistician (M6-09, 2026-10-24; Slurm 1884493, rerun of 1884412): - missed_operons: MET (vacuous with the shipped decoys; extra arm FDP 0.033). - §7.4.7 criteria 1–2 and attacks A and B are vacuous with the shipped decoys. They are non-vacuous only in the extra convergent-only arm, and M-2 likewise. - Criterion 3 passes on the gate null. Discordance gate: NOT MET (D-1), pending Khoa: attack D-1 is a confirmed failure of the discordance level, gated as strict xfails naming ADR-0055 (proposed).

Statistician (M6-13 design review, 2026-10-24; scratch oracles at R = 1,000, Slurm 1885387, 1885388, 1885429, 1885466 and 1885467; local/logs/calibration/m6_13_statreview{,_a}/): approved with edits. - The log-linear σ restores D-1 (pooled 0.0101 / 0.0505 / 0.1002; lowest quartile 0.0093 / 0.0478 / 0.0969) at no cost under the null. - It is at level from 20 pairs, so there is no separate 50-pair gate. - D-1b-step fails the pooled level (0.0518 / 0.1024), which confirms the spec-writer's prediction. No smooth σ(z) fixes it, so it is a strict xfail under an ADR-0055 amendment. - The variance floor and per-gene measurement noise (new D-1c) pass the pooled level. Their top quartile runs at up to 1.7× nominal at α = 0.01: recorded, with a 2α escalation. - Quartiles of the pair mean m are not a valid level check. m contains Δ/2, and the shipped constant method fails them under the gate null. Quartiles of the upstream gene's abundance are at level. - Power non-inferiority uses an absolute margin of 0.02. The measured difference is −0.006 at α = 0.05. - Decisions S-1 to S-11 and the Q1–Q8 rulings are in docs/specs/M6-13-discordance-abundance-sigma.md.

Statistician (M6-13 full-tier record, 2026-10-24; Slurm 1886733 task 6 at fd701591, R = 1,000; local/logs/calibration/m6-13-fd701591-full/): signed off. - D-1 under the log-linear σ is at level: pooled 0.00979 / 0.05016 / 0.09930, and the lowest planted-z quartile is 0.00929 / 0.0478 / 0.0969, both within their bounds. γ̂ = −0.513 against a planted −0.5. - D-1b-floor and D-1c pass the pooled level. Their worst quartiles (1.22× and 1.68× at α = 0.01) are below the 2α escalation. - D-1b-step is a confirmed fail in both blocks at α = 0.05 and 0.10, as pre-registered. It is a strict xfail under ADR-0055 Amendment 1. - The null is unchanged: level, KS p = 0.511 and BH. γ̂ = −0.0014, and every fit stays log-linear. - Power non-inferiority passes, with d = −0.0059 (SE 0.0011) at α = 0.05. - The fast tier at f9c06a4c (27 passed, 1 xpassed) agrees. - No bound, tolerance or R changed (R3). - Condition: the text of ADR-0055 Amendment 1 is not in docs/adr/ on this branch. It must be committed before merge so that the strict xfail's reason resolves to a document.

docs.title: Origin-to-terminus gradient
docs.text: Issue M5-08 (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.5(e), §9.3), module giap.context.oriter. The step plumbing that writes the rows into autocorrelation.tsv and the two genes.tsv columns is M5-09.

docs.title: Why the regression is descriptive
docs.text:
Replication from a single origin makes gene dosage decrease from oriC to the terminus during exponential growth, and highly expressed transcription and translation genes sit near oriC because of it. The ori–ter gradient of protein abundance is therefore an evolved property of the gene order, not a deviation from an exchangeable null: no permutation of the genes (or of the values) reproduces "the same genome without a gradient", because the placement of the genes is the effect we would be testing. GIAP consequently reports the slope and an interval, never a p-value: every row carries p_value = NA, q_value = NA and the flag descriptive (§7.3.5(e)). The interval answers "how precisely is this genome's gradient measured", not "could it have arisen by chance".

The rows therefore enter no §8.1 multiple-testing family. §8.1 lists no ori–ter claim; the autocorrelation BH family is keyed on (contig, statistic, null_model) over lags with a p-value, and these rows carry statistic = oriter_slope, null_model = bootstrap and a NA p, so they can only form a family of their own with nothing in it. M5-09 must keep it that way: p_value NA ⇒ q_value NA, and no ori–ter row is counted in any BH denominator.

docs.title: Replichore geometry
docs.text:
The oriC midpoint o comes from Bakta (C15 features, type = oric); the terminus is taken as o + L/2. For a point at coordinate m on a circular replicon of length L, with d = (m − o) mod L:

condition label position right replichore d ≤ L/2 right d / (L/2) left replichore d > L/2 left (L − d) / (L/2)

Positions lie in [0, 1]: 0 at the origin, 1 at the terminus. right is the arm of increasing coordinate from the oriC (lead decision 32); the labels are directions on the circle, not Bakta-annotated leading/lagging strands. The geometry is intrinsic to the circle: rotating every coordinate and the oriC by the same offset leaves both columns unchanged, mirror images across the oriC share a position on opposite arms, and the strand never enters. Midpoints are taken modulo L, so an origin-crossing interval written unwrapped (end > L, §6.5) lands where it belongs.

Only circular chromosomes are analysed (lead decision 33): the geometry above assumes a circle with one origin, so linear replicons, unknown-kind contigs and plasmids get no row and NA gene columns. Plasmid oriV/oriT calls are not origins of chromosomal replication and are ignored.

docs.title: Several oriC calls
docs.text:
Bakta can call more than one oriC (the recorded K-12 MG1655 annotation has two, 42 kb apart). The calls are summarised by their circular mean (the angle of the mean of the unit vectors 2π·mᵢ/L), which handles calls either side of coordinate 0, but only when every pair lies within 0.05·L circular distance; farther apart the module refuses to guess and the replicon is no_oric (lead decision 31). Requiring the maximum pairwise circular distance to be ≤ 0.05·L (not the spread about the mean) is what makes the mean well defined: with 0.05·L < L/3 the calls then necessarily lie inside one arc of that length, so the circular mean is inside the arc and no antipodal cancellation is possible. Both branches log the event context_stats.oriter.multiple_oric with the midpoints, the spread and the decision, so a questionable origin is visible in logs/events.jsonl. For K-12 the two calls differ by 0.009 of a replichore, far below the resolution of a descriptive slope. Without any call — or without a features table at all — the replicon yields one row with value NA and the flags descriptive;no_oric, and its genes get NA ori–ter columns.

An oriC that is wrong by δ bp shifts every x by 2δ/L and swaps arms for the genes in between. The slope is not invariant to that (only the geometry is), so a genome whose oriC call is doubtful is better read from the multiple_oric event than from the slope.

docs.title: Points and fits
docs.text:
The regression is at TU level, so that an operon counts once rather than once per gene: y_t is the mean abundance_log2 of the TU's detected eligible genes with a value (censoring is ignored — the quantity regressed is the observed abundance of what was detected, lead decision 34), and x_t is the replichore position of the TU midpoint. TUs without a value are dropped. Three OLS fits are reported per replicon: the TUs of the right arm, of the left arm and pooled. The slope b is in log2 per replichore, i.e. the fitted terminus minus the fitted origin, and is written to both value and effect. A fit with fewer than three TUs, or with no variance in x, does not exist: its row is NA with descriptive;not_estimable.

Each arm is a subset of the pooled points, so a non-estimable pooled fit forces both arms to be non-estimable: with fewer than three pooled TUs neither arm can have three, and if the pooled x has no variance then neither subset has any. That is why ℓ̂ is only ever estimated when the pooled fit exists, and the arms can still use it. The invariant is about subsets, not about the circle, so a future change to the per-fit minimum would have to re-check it; block_len_prime raises on ℓ̂ < 1, so a violation fails loudly rather than quietly resampling with block 1.

The pooled fit regresses on |position|, not on a signed coordinate, so it is the gradient averaged over the two arms, weighted by their TU counts. Read the two arm rows before the pooled one when the arms disagree; a single pooled slope hides an asymmetric origin call or a genuine asymmetry.

docs.title: The interval and its block length
docs.text:
Neighbouring TUs are correlated (operons, local expression domains), so an iid bootstrap of the TUs would be too narrow — measurably so: resampling single TUs instead of blocks on the calibration cell below gives mean width 0.78 against 1.11 and coverage 0.785 against 0.943 (R = 200/300). The CI comes from the circular block bootstrap (docs/methods/bootstrap.md) of each fit's own TU sequence — the pooled fit in genome order, an arm ordered from oriC to terminus — resampling index blocks of (x, y) pairs and refitting; the reported interval is the 95 % percentile interval of the stats.bootstrap refitted slopes. Replicates whose resampled x has no variance give a NaN slope and are dropped; n_perm counts the valid ones, and fewer than B/2 of them leaves the CI NA with not_estimable added (B ≥ 1 is assumed, as everywhere else in giap.stats.bootstrap).

Resampling pairs in blocks, rather than residuals, is deliberate. A TU's y is the mean of however many of its genes were detected, so Var y_t falls with that count and unweighted OLS is heteroscedastic; the pairs bootstrap carries each TU's own noise level with it, so the interval does not assume equal variances even though the point estimate ignores them. The resample also keeps the realised detection pattern: it never re-draws which genes were detected, so the interval is conditional on the detected set (see the caveats).

The block length follows ADR-0021 decision 1, shared with the island null: ℓ′ = min(20, 2ℓ̂ + 1, T), with ℓ̂ the first lag at which Moran's I of the pooled fit's residuals is no longer significant (choose_block_len, stats.permutations gene-label permutations). ℓ̂ is estimated once per replicon; the clamp to T is applied per fit with that fit's own TU count, because an arm may hold far fewer TUs than the pooled sequence the length was estimated from. An integer context.islands.block_len overrides the rule (clamped to T as well). Those residuals still carry whatever the straight line failed to absorb of the true (cosine-shaped) dosage curve, but that does not drive ℓ̂ in practice: on the calibration cell ℓ̂ averages 3.91 with a 2-log2 cosine planted and 3.87 with no gradient at all, so the AR(1) background, not the leftover curvature, sets the block.

On an arm the circular wrap joins the TU nearest the terminus to the TU nearest the origin, which are not neighbours on the chromosome; ℓ′/T of the blocks straddle that join (≈ 1 % at 20 TUs and 2,000). The pooled sequence wraps at coordinate 0 between genuine neighbours.

docs.title: What is measured
docs.text:
Coverage of the 95 % pooled interval for the OLS slope of the planted curve, on scenarios.oriter_gradient (4,500 genes, ≈ 1,720 TUs with a value, B = 199, the real giap.context.oriter.oriter_rows). The estimand is the OLS slope of the planted cosine over the TUs that enter the fit, which the closed form puts at −12a/π² = −2.432 for a = 2 log2 under a uniform design; the estimator is unbiased for it (mean −2.424 against mean estimand −2.432 at R = 300). Statistician re-measurement for this review, Slurm 1863166 (local/scratch/stat-132-work/); the implementer's recorded run (Slurm 1863081) is the first 50 replicates of the first row and reproduces exactly.

cell (ρ, amplitude) ℓ̂ ℓ′ R pooled right left width ρ 0.5, 2 log2 (the gate cell) 3.9 8.8 300 0.943 (SE 0.013) 0.920 0.930 1.11 ρ 0, 2 log2 1.1 3.2 200 0.925 (0.019) 0.930 0.945 0.69 ρ 0.9, 2 log2 17.9 20 200 0.900 (0.021) 0.890 0.875 4.41 ρ 0.5, no gradient 3.9 8.7 300 0.917 (0.016) 0.923 0.937 1.09 ρ 0.5, 2 log2, abundance-driven detection 4.0 9.0 200 0.940 (0.017) 0.945 0.920 1.11 ρ 0.5, 2 log2, 1,000 genes (381 TUs) 3.1 7.1 200 0.905 (0.021) 0.905 0.905 2.29 ρ 0.5, 2 log2, blocks off (block_len = 1) — 1 200 0.785 (0.029) 0.775 0.815 0.78

Validity domain. The interval is nominal to within a few points over the whole range measured: 0.90–0.94 against a nominal 0.95, never grossly wrong, and never conservative. What is claimed is coverage ≥ 0.90 everywhere in the table above, and ≈ 0.94 for giapsim ar1_background at ρ ≤ 0.5 on a ≈ 4,500-gene chromosome (the gate cell); the gate's numeric bound below is the finite-R form of the first claim, not a second one. Unlike the island FWER (ADR-0021 Amendment 1) there is no regime here in which the procedure breaks down — at ρ 0.9 the cap ℓ′ = 20 binds and the interval becomes nearly vacuous instead (width 4.4 for an effect of −2.4), which is a loss of precision, not of validity. No ori–ter row carries uncalibrated (Amendment 1 dropped the flag).

The shortfall is systematic, not noise: it is the percentile interval's own skewness and the blocks' under-representation of dependence across joins. ℓ′ is shared with the island scan only because ADR-0021 made it so, and the island scan's power trade-off (which is what kept ℓ′ short) does not apply to a slope CI; a longer block, a studentised interval or BCa would likely recover the missing 1–3 points. That is hardening-pass work (backlog), not a merge condition for a descriptive statistic.

docs.title: Caveats a reader must apply
docs.text:
The island effect CI is conditional on a selected window (winner's curse). Nothing is selected here — three fixed fits per replicon, no scan, no maximum — so that caveat does not carry over. These do:

  1. The interval is not a test. With no gradient planted at all, the 95 % interval misses the true slope 0 in 8.3 % of replicates (R = 300, above). Reading "the CI excludes 0" as a 5 % test of "this genome has no ori–ter gradient" is wrong twice over: the error rate is not 5 %, and §7.3.5(e) refuses that test on purpose, because gene placement is the effect, not the null.
  2. Conditional on what was detected. y is observed abundance among detected proteins. The bootstrap never re-draws detection, so the interval is for the gradient of the observed abundances of this detected set, not for the complete-data gradient. Under giapsim's abundance-driven detection the coverage of the planted curve is unchanged (0.940, above), but that is a statement about the simulator's selection strength, not a licence: if detectability covaries with position — ribosomal and transcription genes near oriC are short, abundant and easy — the slope is confounded with it and no interval repairs that.
  3. Conditional on the design. The estimand is the OLS slope over the realised TU positions. Slopes are comparable across genomes only to the extent that the oriC call, the TU density and the detected share are; the dosage curve is not a straight line (the planted one is a cosine), so b is a linear summary whose value depends on how the TUs are spread over [0, 1].
  4. No simultaneity. The three rows of a replicon, and the rows of different replicons, are each 95 % intervals, not a 95 % simultaneous set; the pooled row and its two arms use the same TUs and are strongly dependent.
  5. The arms are the weaker rows. They carry half the TUs, 40 % wider intervals and 1–2 points less coverage than the pooled row at every cell measured (0.875–0.945). Only the pooled row is gated.

docs.title: Statistician sign-off
docs.text:
Signed off by the statistician (PR #132 review). The review covered the estimand and its closed form, the per-fit block clamp, the percentile interval, the degenerate rules and the measurements above, and settled M5-08 lead decision 8:

Example 7 is promoted to a gate, on the full (nightly) arm only. The claim is the non-coverage rate of the pooled interval on the gate cell, R = replicates_full.islands = 500, bounded by the house rule level_bound(0.07, R) = 0.0929, i.e. coverage ≥ 0.907, with a non-estimable CI counted as a miss (fail closed) and ADR-0015 two-block confirmation. At the measured 0.943 that gate fails 0.1 % of blocks and ~1e-6 of confirmed nightlies, and catches a regression to 0.88 — what the spec's ℓ̂ produced before ADR-0021 — with probability 0.98. The tolerated non-coverage is 0.07 and not the nominal 0.05 because the measured coverage is 0.943 ± 0.013, not 0.95: a 0.05 tolerance (bound 0.9305) would fail 12–20 % of blocks and 1.6–3.8 % of confirmed nightlies. The fast arm (R = 50) stays recorded: at that R no bound has both a confirmed false-failure rate below 1 % and any power (bound 0.90: 0.4 % false failures, power 0.32 against 0.88). The two arm rows and every other cell of the table stay recorded.

docs.title: Permutation p-values, circular shifts and Besag–Clifford
docs.text: Implements giap.stats.permutation (perm_p, circular_shifts, apply_shift, choose_shifts, besag_clifford; GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.5(b), §8.2, §8.3, decision 14, Appendix B.4; issue M4-03). Statistician sign-off: see the end of this note.

docs.title: The +1 rule
docs.text:
For an observed statistic T₀ and B null statistics T₁ … T_B,

p = (1 + b) / (1 + B),     b = #{ i ≥ 1 : T_i is at least as extreme as T₀ }.

If T₀, T₁, …, T_B are exchangeable under H₀, the rank of T₀ among the B + 1 values is uniform, so P(p ≤ α) ≤ α for every α, exactly and for any B (Phipson & Smyth 2010). Consequences:

  • p is never 0 and never exceeds 1: 1/(B + 1) ≤ p ≤ 1. The floor 1/(B + 1) is why many-test families use Besag–Clifford, Wallenius or fgsea multilevel instead (§8.2, decision 14).
  • p is discrete on the grid {1, …, B + 1}/(B + 1). Under H₀ with a continuous statistic, P(p ≤ α) = ⌊α(B + 1)⌋/(B + 1) ≤ α; it is uniform on the grid, not on (0, 1). The calibration suite therefore uses the level check only, never KS (§8.4).
  • Ties count as exceedances, so ties only make p larger (conservative).
  • Dropping the "+1" (p = b/B) gives p = 0 and is anti-conservative; it is never used.

docs.title: Two-sided p: centring
docs.text:
Two-sided p counts null values whose distance from a centre c is at least the observed one: b = #{ |T_i − c| ≥ |T₀ − c| }. The spec (§7.3.5(b), §8.3) centres on "the null mean". Exactness requires the statistic |T − c| to treat T₀ and the T_i symmetrically, i.e. c must be a symmetric function of all B + 1 values:

c = (T₀ + T₁ + … + T_B) / (B + 1)      (mean of the randomization distribution, identity included).

For exhaustive shifts this is the mean over all n placements of the region (the shift k = 0 is a member of the null orbit), which is what "the null mean" of a randomization distribution means. Centring on the mean of T₁ … T_B only (the first implementation) makes T₀ look more extreme by the factor (B + 1)/B and is anti-conservative when B is small:

iid N(0, 1), 4 × 10⁵ replicates α null-only centre pooled centre (exact) B = 9 0.10 0.141 0.099 B = 19 0.05 0.062 0.050 B = 19 0.10 0.118 0.100 B = 99 0.05 0.053 0.051 B = 999 0.05 0.048 0.048

Small K is routine in GIAP: plasmids with 10–20 genes (K = n − 1) and short linear contigs (K = n − span). The attack nulls tiny_circular_n10, tiny_circular_n20 and tiny_linear_n12 (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_permutation.py) fail with null-only centring (rates 0.14, 0.064 and 0.126 against bounds 0.109, 0.056, 0.109) and pass with pooled centring (0.104, 0.052, 0.091). Implemented (5e80944): perm_p two-sided centres on the pooled mean of the finite values among T₀, T₁ … T_B; ±inf null values are kept in B and always count as extreme (an infinite T₀ is left out of the centre). M4-03 example 1 is now perm_p(5.5, [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]) = 2/6 (pooled centre 3.417; |1 − 3.417| = 2.417 > |5.5 − 3.417| = 2.083); examples 2 and 4 and B.4 are unchanged. Centring is translation-equivariant either way, so the "invariant to adding a constant" property still holds.

Besag–Clifford has no pooled set to centre on; for two-sided use the caller must centre on a value known a priori (e.g. 0 for a difference in means under label permutation, whose permutation mean is exactly 0), never on a running estimate.

docs.title: Float ties
docs.text:
Exhaustive shifts sum equal multisets in different orders, so exact ties can differ by rounding. perm_p counts T_i as an exceedance when it is within tol of the threshold:

one-sided:  tol = 1e-12 · max(1, |T₀|)
two-sided:  tol = 1e-12 · max(1, |T₀ − c|, |c|)

The implementer added |c| to the two-sided scale (a deviation from the spec text 1e-12 · max(1, |x|)). Assessment: correct and needed. |T_i − c| is computed after subtracting c, so its rounding error scales with |c|, not with the deviation; without |c| a large centre (log₂ intensities ≈ 20–30 summed over a region) would leave ties unresolved. The tolerance only ever adds exceedances, so it can only make p larger (valid, at worst slightly less powerful).

Limitation (non-blocking): the rounding error of a sum scales with the summands, not with the sum. With large summands that cancel (terms ±1000.1, width 50; or ±100000.1, width 200) a true tie can be missed: in a probe, 1/300 and 7/300 replicates had float p below the exact rational p (one tie missed; effect ≤ 1/(B + 1)). For GIAP's region statistics (z-scores or log intensities, widths ≤ a few hundred genes) the error stays far below 1e-12·scale; the attack test_tie_tolerance_never_lowers_p (heavy ties on log₂-like decimals, width 50, exhaustive shifts) checks float p ≥ exact p. If a caller ever sums large cancelling terms, it should pass rounded statistics or a scale.

docs.title: Circular shifts (§7.3.5(b), §8.1 "region effect")
docs.text:
A region is a set I of gene indices on a replicon of N genes. The null statistics are the same statistic on I + k (mod N) for k = 1 … N − 1 (circular_shifts(n, idx, circular=True); apply_shift). B.4: N = 100 gives K = 99, and an observation more extreme than all 99 gives p = 1/100.

What the shift null preserves. Region size, the gaps between its genes (non-contiguous AMR sets move as a block), and the joint distribution of abundance along the replicon, in particular its autocorrelation: each shifted set sees a stretch of the same autocorrelated series, so the null variance of a region sum includes the positive covariances between neighbours, exactly as the observed one does. What it breaks: only the region's position. H₀ is "the region's position is unrelated to abundance", formalised as the abundance series being stationary on the circle (rotation-invariant in distribution); then T₀ and the shifted T_k are exchangeable and the +1 rule is exact.

Why gene permutation is wrong here. Permuting gene labels draws the null region from scattered genes, whose sum has variance ≈ w·σ²; the observed contiguous region has variance ≈ w·σ²·(1 + ρ)/(1 − ρ) under AR(1). The test is then anti-conservative. Attack test_naive_permutation_is_anticonservative (circular-stationary AR(1), ρ = 0.9, w = 20, N = 1000) confirms the attack has teeth: label permutation rejects far above 0.05, while the shift null on the same data stays at level (table below).

Caveats the callers own (M5): stationarity fails near replication-origin/terminus gradients (gene dosage) — shifts then compare a region with regions at other dosage; GIAP mitigates this by detrending (§7.3.5) and by reporting plasmids as replicon-level effects (§8.5 attack 4).

Linear replicons. On a linear contig a wrapped set is not a region, so only translations that keep I inside [0, N) are used: k with max(I) + k < N (right) or min(I) + k ≥ N (left by N − k). With span = max(I) − min(I) + 1 this gives K = N − span shifts, and with the identity the N − span + 1 placements of the block; the set of placements is the same from every placement, so the exhaustive linear null is exact under translation-stationarity. K = 0 (the region spans the contig) → no test; callers report p_value = NA.

Exhaustive vs sampled. Exhaustive (all K shifts) while N ≤ context.exhaustive_shift_max_genes (default 20,000), otherwise B random shifts drawn without replacement from the valid set (all of them when B ≥ K). Sampling a uniformly random subset of the other placements keeps T₀ exchangeable with the chosen ones, so the +1 rule stays exact (Hemerik & Goeman 2018); without replacement avoids duplicated null draws and is never worse. Determinism: the shifts depend only on the Generator state (from giap.rng.for_step) and are returned sorted.

docs.title: Besag–Clifford sequential p (§8.2, decision 14)
docs.text: Draw null statistics one at a time; stop at the h-th draw ≥ T₀ (h = 10 by default). If that is draw L, p = h/L; if max_B draws give b < h exceedances, p = (b + 1)/(max_B + 1). This is the sequential Monte Carlo p-value of Besag & Clifford (1991, Biometrika 78:301): it is exactly valid, P(p ≤ α) ≤ α under exchangeable draws, with ties counted as exceedances. It spends few draws on clearly null tests (L ≈ h/p) and up to max_B on small p, so its floor is 1/(max_B + 1) rather than 1/(B + 1) for the fixed B, at a fraction of the cost. h < 1 or max_B < h is rejected.

docs.title: Missing and infinite values
docs.text: NaN null values are dropped (B counts the rest); NaN T₀ or B = 0 gives NaN. ±inf null values are kept in B and count as extreme in their direction (+inf for "greater", −inf for "less", both for "two-sided"), so perm_p(5, [1, 2, inf], "greater") = 2/4. The first implementation dropped them, which lowered p; fixed in 5e80944 (lead decision). choose_shifts reports exhaustive=True whenever every valid shift is used, including n > n_max with B ≥ K.

docs.title: Sign-off
docs.text: First review (2bee83c): BLOCK on null-only centring. Re-review of 5e80944: APPROVE. All 24 permutation calibration and attack tests pass (fast and full), and 144 unit/property tests pass. An independent level check of two-sided perm_p (R = 20,000 per cell, iid normal and lognormal B + 1 values) gives rates at α = 0.05 / 0.10 of 0.047–0.051 / 0.097–0.102 for B = 19, 0.099–0.102 at α = 0.10 for B = 9, and 0.0089–0.0098 / 0.049–0.051 / 0.096–0.102 at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 for B = 99. All are within bounds. Approved: the +1 rule, one-sided and pooled two-sided p, tie handling including the |c| scale, ±inf handling, circular and linear shift sets, sampling without replacement, Besag–Clifford, and determinism. The tie-tolerance limitation above stays open and is non-blocking.

docs.title: Placement FDR: genome decoys, chance hits and per-stratum q-values
docs.text:
Implements the genome side of GIAP_SPEC.md §7.2.1 (decoy translations), §7.2.5 (placement FDR, G3), §8.1 rows "Peptide placed at a locus", §8.2 "decoys mimic targets", §8.5 attack 5 and Appendix B.2/B.6. Issues: M3-03 (decoys, this section), M3-09 (chance hits), M3-10 (strata and q-values), M3-21 (genome-level calibration). Engine for the q-values: docs/methods/target-decoy.md.

Sections: Genome decoys (M3-03, signed off below); Chance hits and the ranking score (M3-09, signed off below); π̂_wrong in the stratum FDR (M3-10, rule signed off below); Strata and ranking, π̂_wrong sources, Same-strain input, Calibration (M3-10, signed below; implementation approved at 031378c after two same-strain fixes, see "Implementation review (M3-10)"). Genome-level calibration with tolerant hits and de novo errors, and attack 5, are M3-21.

docs.title: What the decoy has to estimate
docs.text:
A placement is wrong when a wrong peptide (a misidentified spectrum or a de novo error) happens to occur in the six-frame translation. For one wrong peptide the number of such chance hits depends only on the search space: the set of distinct stop- and X-free L-mers of the six frames (each peptide counts once at its best cost, §7.2.5 step 1, so multiplicity of a word does not matter), and the peptide law. The decoy search space must give a wrong peptide the same hit probability as the target space, while giving a correct peptide (which is in the target by construction) only that same chance probability. Then D (peptides with a decoy hit at cost m) estimates the number of wrong peptides with a chance target hit at cost m, and π̂_wrong (D + 1)/T is the stratum FDR (M3-10).

Formally, for a peptide law Q and a space with distinct words W, P(hit) = Σ_{w ∈ W} Q(w) (exact search; for ≤ m differences replace W by its m-neighbourhood). The decoy is valid for Q when Σ_{W_D} Q = Σ_{W_T} Q.

docs.title: The two constructions
docs.text:
Both act on the I→L-folded uint8 frames of build_sixframe, frame by frame, and return frames of the same contig, strand, offset and length (build_decoys).

reverse (database input) shuffle (de novo input) Operation frame string reversed inside each stop-free segment, non-X residues cut into consecutive windows of 50 from the segment start (last window shorter); each window permuted uniformly (Fisher–Yates), seeded for_step("sixframe_index", seed) * and X mirrored (position n−1−i) fixed in place Frame composition identical identical Per-window composition identical (mirrored windows) identical (exactly, per 50-aa window) Stop-free segment lengths and X positions same multiset, mirrored identical Number of L-mer positions without */X identical identical Local order kept, reversed (dipeptide xy → yx) destroyed below 50 aa; composition gradient above 50 aa kept Repeats / low-complexity runs kept (a repeat stays a repeat) homopolymer runs kept; periodic repeats and multi-copy elements destroyed Mirror map (§7.6.4, mirror_aa) [n − end, n − start) identity

Same search-space size. The decoy frames have the same frames, the same length, the same * and X geometry (identical or mirrored) and therefore exactly the same number of candidate L-mer positions for every L (verified for L = 7, 8 in every replicate of the attack suite). The I→L fold is applied before decoying, so neither space can match I/L differently. The circular extension (first 120 nt appended, §7.2.1) is decoyed with its frame: for reverse the duplicated words stay duplicated, so distinct-word counts agree exactly; for shuffle the extension is shuffled independently of the origin region, which adds at most 40 distinct decoy words per frame per circular replicon (≈ 2 × 10⁻⁵ of a 5-Mb space, conservative, negligible).

docs.title: Why reverse for database input
docs.text:
• Exact under any i.i.d. peptide law. If Q(w) = Π Q₁(wⱼ) then Q(rev w) = Q(w), and W_D = rev(W_T) word for word, so Σ_{W_D} Q = Σ_{W_T} Q exactly — for every genome, including repeat-rich and low-complexity genomes, and for every difference budget (the m-neighbourhood of rev w is the reverse of the m-neighbourhood of w for substitutions; adjacent swaps and the mass-equivalence operations are closed under reversal because the operation tables list both orders). Positional laws that are not reversal-symmetric (tryptic C-terminal K/R) still agree in expectation when the genome's L-mers are reversal-exchangeable; the attack suite confirms it on giapsim genomes.
  • It keeps everything structural. Composition per window, repeats, low-complexity runs and the stop geometry are kept, so the decoy reproduces the de-duplication that repeats impose on the target (see the low-complexity results below: shuffle over-counts by 40–70 % there, reverse is exact).
  • Deterministic and seed-free, and its own inverse (mirror_aa is an involution).
  • It is also the standard choice of proteomic search engines, so database peptides are not systematically "close to" reversed sequence (input decoy rows are never mapped, M3-17).

docs.title: Why shuffle for de novo input (§8.5 attack 5)
docs.text:
De novo errors frequently reverse a short stretch of a correct peptide (b/y-ion ambiguity). A peptide with a reversed internal stretch, or a fully reversed one, matches the reversed frame near the true locus far more often than chance, so a reversed decoy would inflate D with correct-locus peptides and make the de novo FDR uselessly conservative and the de novo precision estimator (§7.2.5, r_bℓ) biased. A window shuffle breaks all order below 50 aa, so such peptides hit the decoy only at chance rate, while the 50-aa windows keep local composition (codon bias, hydrophobic stretches, AT-rich non-coding frames), which is what per-position match probability depends on.

Window size. 50 aa is a compromise: windows must be much longer than the longest tolerant peptide window that matters for chance hits (≤ 40 aa) so that a peptide-length stretch is a near-random draw from its window, and short enough to keep composition gradients (genes vs. intergenic, GC skew, transmembrane segments). Windows restart at each stop and skip X, so a window never mixes two stop-free segments. With window 1 the shuffle is the identity (unit-tested); with an unbounded window (whole segment) the attack results were indistinguishable at 100 kb (mean D/T expected-hit ratio 1.003 vs. 1.000 at L = 7; exploratory, 20 genomes).

docs.title: What each decoy is a null for
docs.text:
Matching reverse shuffle Exact (Route 1) exact null for any i.i.d. (and any reversal-symmetric) wrong-peptide law, any genome null for i.i.d. wrong peptides on genomes without heavy repeats; conservative with repeats Tolerant, ≤ m differences (Route 3) same, because the five cost-1 operations are closed under reversal same as exact, with the m-neighbourhood Frameshift splits (M3-08) decoy splits by mirrored adjacency (M3-08) identity map keeps frame adjacency

Neither decoy is a null for wrong peptides that share sequence order with the genome's own proteins (see "Limitations").

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Implementation review (M3-03, src/giap/mapping/decoys.py).

  • The shuffle swaps slot l of a window with a uniform slot in [0, l] in increasing l (Durstenfeld's forward variant of Fisher–Yates), which is uniform over the l! orders by induction; swaps never leave the window (j = s − local[s] + draw), so per-window multisets, * and X positions are preserved exactly (property-tested, tests/property/test_decoys_props.py).
  • Windows restart at * but not at X (X skipped), as the issue specifies.
  • Determinism: one generator for all frames in index order, one draw per shuffled residue (rng.integers(0, local + 1)); reverse draws nothing. Seed-identical runs are byte-identical. Note: the draws are not rng.permutation as the issue text says; this is statistically equivalent, but the stream is fixed by this implementation and must not change silently (golden tables, §6.6).

Attack suite (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_genome_decoys.py). Fast suite: R = 50 giapsim genomes of 100 kb (seeds 20261014 + i); full suite R = 300. For each genome the exact expected hit probability of an i.i.d. peptide drawn from the genome's six-frame residue frequencies is computed on the distinct L-mers of the target and of each decoy (no peptide sampling noise), and three sampled peptide sets are searched.

Null (fast, R = 50) reverse D/T shuffle D/T exact expected hits, L = 7 (mean ± SE; range) 1 (exact) 1.003 ± 0.002 (0.976–1.022) exact expected hits, L = 8 1 (exact) 1.003 ± 0.002 (0.964–1.037) sampled i.i.d. 7-mers, 10⁶ peptides: T = 1,332 D = 1,306 (p = 0.63) D = 1,341 (p = 0.88) sampled tryptic 7-mers (C-term K/R): T = 1,239 D = 1,261 (p = 0.67) D = 1,213 (p = 0.61) sampled 8-mers ≤ 1 substitution, 10⁵ peptides: T = 953 D = 919 (p = 0.45) D = 944 (p = 0.85)

p = two-sided binomial test of D vs T given D + T. Per-genome scatter of the shuffle ratio (SD ≈ 1.2–1.6 % at 100 kb; one 1-Mb genome gave 1.003 / 0.998) is the decoy's own Monte Carlo error, unbiased in the mean; it shrinks with genome size.

Low-complexity genome (same genomes plus 24 simple-sequence repeats of 360 nt — (CAG)n, (GCC)n, (AT)n, (GA)n, A-runs, hexamer repeats — and ten copies of one 1.5-kb element, ≈ 24 % repetitive; R = 10 fast):

reverse D/T shuffle D/T exact expected hits, L = 7 / L = 8 1 / 1 (exact) 1.40 / 1.69 sampled i.i.d. 7-mers 221 / 227 296 / 227 sampled 8-mers ≤ 1 substitution 148 / 158 221 / 158

Repeats shrink the set of distinct target words by ≈ 23 %; the shuffle restores them, so the shuffled decoy over-counts chance hits. This is conservative (FDR over-estimated, power lost for de novo input on repeat-rich genomes), never anti-conservative; the gate asserts exactly that.

Shuffle exactness. Joint uniformity over two 4-aa windows separated by an X (576 cells, 23,040 draws), the window after a *, independence of windows, and position × residue uniformity in a full 50-aa window: all χ² p > 0.001. The test-author's unit test (one 3-residue window, 600 seeds) is adequate as a smoke test (it catches the classic "swap with any slot" bias already at n = 3) but tests neither independence between windows nor the X/* geometry; the attack suite covers those.

docs.title: Limitations (documented, not CI gates)
docs.text:
Exploratory runs, 1-Mb synthetic genomes, 4 × 10⁵ sampled 7-mers each:

Violation D/T reverse D/T shuffle Consequence Wrong peptides share the genome's order-1 (dipeptide) structure: genes and peptides from one asymmetric Markov chain, strength 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.4 0.96 / 0.88 / 0.48 0.99 / 0.96 / 0.62 Both decoys under-count chance hits of "protein-like" wrong peptides. Real proteome dipeptide asymmetry is weak (≈ the 0.1 row); database wrong IDs from a related proteome (search_db = other) are the realistic case. M3-21 must measure this with real protein sequences (TE8 proxy, UniProt K-12 peptides vs. the Nissle genome). Periodic wrong peptides (dipeptide repeats XYXY…) on the low-complexity genome 1.00 0.88 Shuffle is anti-conservative for periodic wrong peptides hitting periodic target repeats (period-3 repeats go the other way, 4.2). Recommendation for M3-10: flag low_complexity placements (e.g. ≤ 3 distinct residues in the peptide) and report them separately rather than relying on the shuffle decoy. De novo reversed stretches with reverse decoys (attack 5) inflated D — Why de novo uses shuffle; quantified in M3-21.

docs.title: Chance hits and the ranking score (M3-09)
The model
docs.text:
A wrong peptide of length L is modelled as L residues drawn independently from the genome's six-frame composition f, and every searchable target window as L residues drawn independently from the same f, independently of the peptide. Then one position matches with probability s = Σ_a f_a², a window is within ≤ m substitutions with probability Σ_{j≤m} C(L, j)(1 − s)^j s^(L−j) (j mismatching positions out of L, each mismatching with probability 1 − s), and the expected number of chance windows is

E(L, m) = N Σ_{j≤m} C(L, j)(1 − s)^j s^(L−j) (§7.2.5, B.2; expected_hits_uniform).

The per-peptide ranking score E_i (expected_hits) conditions on the peptide's residues: position i mismatches a random target residue with probability 1 − f_{a_i}, the mismatch count is Poisson-binomial, and E_i = N · P(≤ m mismatches). Averaged over i.i.d.-f peptides, E_i equals E(L, m) exactly (positions are independent and E_f[1 − f_a] = 1 − s); the calibration test confirms it by simulation at L = 8.

Composition f (residue_freqs): counts of the 19 residue codes over the target frames, I and L merged (the frames are I→L folded before anything else, so neither target nor decoy can match I/L differently); * and X are excluded from f. Query letters outside the 19 (U, O, B, Z, J, X) get f = 0: they never match, so they always count as a mismatch.

N (n_positions) is the number of six-frame codon positions whose first nucleotide lies in the replicon: for a circular replicon one per nucleotide and strand (≈ 2 × genome length), the 120-nt circular extension excluded, but every position near the origin still starts a full window that reads through the extension (origin-crossing windows are searchable and counted once); for a linear contig the last ≤ L − 1 positions of each frame have no full window but are counted (negligible). As the spec defines it, N counts all positions, including * and X and windows that contain them. Those windows can never match, so the number of searchable windows is W_L < N (next section).

Substitutions only. E counts substitution neighbours. The tolerant matcher also accepts adjacent swaps and mass-equivalent blocks at cost 1, so the true cost-≤ m neighbourhood is larger than E assumes (lead default, M3-09 Q1). This does not matter for validity: E is a ranking score, not an FDR estimate. Target and decoy E are computed by the same function from the peptide sequence and the same genome f (decoys keep the target composition exactly, see Genome decoys), so E is exchangeable between a wrong peptide's target and decoy hits; the decoy count D (which uses all operations) calibrates the FDR. An error in E costs power (a worse ordering), never validity. E also counts hit positions with multiplicity, whereas a peptide counts once in the strata: P(≥ 1 hit) ≤ E, ≈ E when E ≪ 1, which is the range that is accepted.

docs.title: Reproduction of B.2
docs.text:
expected_hits_uniform(L, m, 0.069, 1e7) against exact rational arithmetic: relative error ≤ 1.3 × 10⁻¹⁵ in all 21 cells; every cell rounds to the B.2 table (e.g. (7, 0) 0.0744635, (8, 1) 0.559742, (9, 2) 2.36692, (10, 1) 0.00332505, (12, 2) 0.00141835, (14, 1) 1.05295 × 10⁻⁷; L = 6: 1.08, 88.4, 3.04 × 10³). Monte Carlo (tests/calibration/test_chance_hits.py, random 19-letter target of 10⁶ residues with Σf² = 0.069, scaled to N = 10⁷, ≤ 1 substitution):

L simulated (± SE) E(L, 1) ratio B.2 ≤ 1 8 0.561 ± 0.006 0.5597 1.002 0.56 9 0.0440 ± 0.0007 0.0434 1.015 0.043 10 0.00339 ± 0.00009 0.00333 1.020 0.0033

All within the 20 % gate with SE ≤ 2.7 %. The counting kernel is checked against brute force. This reproduces the formula; it says nothing about real six-frame translations, which the attack below measures.

docs.title: When the independence assumption fails
docs.text:
Attack tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_chance_hits.py (statistician). For a peptide drawn i.i.d. from the genome's own f, the exact expected number of hit windows is Σ_{searchable windows t} P(≤ m mismatches | t), mismatch probability 1 − f(t_j) at position j (closed form for m ≤ 2; no peptide sampling, cross-checked against sampled exact hits). It is compared with E(L, m) computed by residue_freqs + expected_hits_uniform on genomes built through build_sixframe (circular, 100 kb, R = 8 per family, seeds from calibration_base). Ratios: stop = W_L / N; cond = observed / (W_L × tail), the error given the stop correction; total = observed / E = stop × cond. Mean over replicates, m = 0 / 1 / 2:

Genome L stop cond (m = 0 / 1 / 2) total (m = 0 / 1 / 2) i.i.d. nucleotides, GC 50 % 8 0.681 0.999 / 0.999 / 0.999 0.681 / 0.681 / 0.681 12 0.562 0.988 / 0.991 / 0.994 0.555 / 0.557 / 0.559 i.i.d. nucleotides, GC 75 % (s ≈ 0.10) 8 0.895 0.993 / 0.995 / 0.997 0.889 / 0.891 / 0.893 12 0.847 0.989 / 0.992 / 0.994 0.838 / 0.840 / 0.842 giapsim (genes, codon structure, AT-rich intergenic) 7 0.748 1.019 / 1.012 / 1.006 0.762 / 0.757 / 0.752 8 0.719 1.027 / 1.018 / 1.011 0.739 / 0.732 / 0.727 10 0.666 1.047 / 1.036 / 1.025 0.697 / 0.690 / 0.683 12 0.618 1.068 / 1.055 / 1.043 0.660 / 0.652 / 0.644 giapsim + 24 simple-sequence repeats of 360 nt (≈ 9 %) 7 0.766 1.82 / 1.42 / 1.21 1.39 / 1.09 / 0.93 8 0.740 2.54 / 1.80 / 1.41 1.88 / 1.33 / 1.04 10 0.691 6.7 / 3.9 / 2.5 4.6 / 2.7 / 1.7 12 0.647 22.6 / 11.7 / 6.4 14.6 / 7.6 / 4.1

(Replicate SE of cond on the i.i.d. genomes ≈ 0.3–0.6 % at L = 8–12; the 1 % deviations at L = 12 are within 2 SE, confirmed with R = 30 at GC 75 %: 0.998 ± 0.002 at L = 8, 0.999 ± 0.005 at L = 12.)

Three effects, with their directions:

  1. Stops and X (factor W_L / N ≈ (1 − p_stop)^L, here 0.56–0.91; p_stop ≈ 3/64 for GC 50 %): N counts positions that cannot start a match. E over-states the absolute chance count — conservative — by a factor 1.1–1.8, more for longer L and AT-rich genomes (more stop codons in non-coding frames). With i.i.d. codons this is the only error (cond = 1 at any composition, including a strongly skewed GC 75 % genome: the model handles composition skew through f).
  2. Heterogeneous composition and dipeptide structure. Coding, antisense and intergenic frames have different residue laws g_k; for an i.i.d.-f peptide E[Π f(t_j)] = Σ_k w_k (Σ_a f_a g_k(a))^L ≥ s^L by Jensen, and codon/dipeptide structure inside genes adds to it. E under-states the conditional count by 2–7 % (growing with L, shrinking with m). On realistic genomes the stop factor dominates, so E stays conservative overall (total 0.64–0.76).
  3. Low complexity. Simple-sequence repeats put long runs of a few abundant residues into the target (poly-A, poly-P, (AR)n, …); windows there have Π f(t_j) ≫ s^L. E under-states the absolute count, strongly and increasingly with L (×1.9 at L = 8, ×15 at L = 12, exact matches). By construction the excess comes from peptides that are themselves rich in the repeat residues (an exact or 1-substitution match to a repeat window needs a near-repeat peptide): those hit far more often than their E_i says, while typical peptides are barely affected. This is the same structure that made the shuffled decoy anti-conservative for periodic wrong peptides (Genome decoys › Limitations, D/T 0.88) and that the reverse decoy preserves exactly.

Consequence. Since E is only a ranking score, none of these errors affects FDR validity as long as the decoy is a valid null (reverse: exact for any i.i.d. law on any genome; shuffle: see Genome decoys). They affect (a) power, through the ordering: the stop factor varies with L, so pooling lengths within a stratum (G3) ranks long peptides slightly too pessimistically relative to short ones (≈ 3–5 % per residue against a factor ≈ 1/s ≈ 14 per residue in E itself: immaterial); low-complexity peptides are ranked too optimistically, which is the case for the low_complexity placement flag recommended to M3-10; (b) any absolute reading of E (a reported "expected chance hits" column, or the §7.2.5 table read as a property of a real genome): E over-states real genomes by 1.3–1.8× and under-states low-complexity peptides by up to an order of magnitude. If E is ever reported as an absolute expectation, use W_L instead of N and flag low-complexity peptides.

docs.title: Numerical accuracy of the Poisson-binomial
docs.text:
giap.stats.poisson_binomial (shared with M4-02) computes the pmf by the standard DP \(\mathrm{pmf}_{i+1}[j] = \mathrm{pmf}_i[j](1 - p_i) + \mathrm{pmf}_i[j - 1]\, p_i\), O(n²) time, O(n) memory. Every step is a convex combination of non-negative numbers, so there is no cancellation: each entry has relative error ≤ ≈ 2n·u (u = 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁶) whatever its size, and tiny tails stay exact to relative precision rather than to absolute 10⁻¹⁶. The cdf and sf are summed directly from the pmf (never 1 − the other), as §8.3 requires. Checks (review, 2026-10-14):

  • brute-force enumeration of all 2ⁿ outcomes, n = 0–12, 260 random p vectors including p^20-skewed ones: max relative pmf error 2.5 × 10⁻¹⁵; cdf and sf for every k ∈ [−1, n + 1] within 10⁻¹⁴ absolute;
  • exact rational arithmetic, n = 60, p ∈ [0, 0.1]: max relative error 6.0 × 10⁻¹⁶ over the whole pmf, including the extreme tail P(X = 60) = 4.75 × 10⁻⁸³;
  • n = 5,000 (M4-02 scale): Σ pmf − 1 = 4 × 10⁻¹⁶, 36 ms;
  • E at L = 40, m = 0 stays positive (7 × 10⁻⁴⁵ for a uniform-f poly-A query at N = 10⁷).

Limits (outside the peptide range, documented only): entries below ≈ 10⁻³⁰⁸ underflow to 0 (n ≳ 230 at p = 0.05 for P(X = n)); expected_hits_uniform uses exact integer binomial coefficients and raises OverflowError for L ≳ 1,000 with m ≈ L/2. The vectorised in-place update reads its right-hand side before assigning, so there is no aliasing.

docs.title: Review findings (M3-09, src/giap/mapping/chance.py, src/giap/stats/poisson_binomial.py)
docs.text:
• B.2: all 21 cells exact to 1.3 × 10⁻¹⁵; examples 1–8 of the issue pass; Poisson-binomial correct against brute force and exact arithmetic (above). Edge cases: m ∉ [0, L] and p ∉ [0, 1] or NaN raise; empty p gives pmf [1]; k < 0 gives cdf 0 and sf 1; k > n gives cdf 1 and sf 0.
  • Origin off-by-two (minor, requested fix). _core_residues keeps a minus-strand codon when its first (5′-on-minus, highest-coordinate) nucleotide is < replicon length. The two minus-strand codons whose 5′ nucleotide is replicon position 0 or 1 lie wholly in the extension in the frame coordinates and are dropped, although they are unique origin-crossing codons, so a circular replicon gets N = 2·length − 2 instead of 2·length (checked at length 9, 10, 11, 300 and 100 kb). Fix: keep a minus-strand codon when its lowest coordinate, first_nt − 2, is < length. Effect on E and f: relative 10⁻⁵, none on rankings or q-values (target and decoy share N). The attack accepts either value until fixed.
  • N includes */X positions as the spec defines it; documented above with its direction (conservative ×0.56–0.91), not a defect.

docs.text: Statistician (M3-09 review, 2026-10-14): approved for expected_hits_uniform, expected_hits, residue_freqs and giap.stats.poisson_binomial as implemented on m3/chance-hits, with the origin off-by-two to be fixed (non-blocking: no effect on any statistical output). Forwarded to M3-10: E is a ranking score only (never report it as an absolute expectation without the W_L correction); low-complexity peptides are ranked too optimistically by E, which reinforces the low_complexity placement flag.

docs.title: π̂_wrong in the stratum FDR (M3-10)
docs.text: Scope: how a π̂_wrong that varies between peptides enters FDR_m(e) (§7.2.5 step 3). In practice this is de novo input in stratum 0, where π̂ is per score bin (step 4, M3-11). Database input in stratum 0 (one π̂ for all) and every stratum m ≥ 1 (π̂ = 1) have a constant π̂, and the rule below reduces exactly to the spec formula there. This section replaces lead decision M3-10 Q2 ("mean π̂ of the targets with E ≤ e"), which is anti-conservative.

docs.title: Model and assumptions
docs.text:
Fix a stratum m and a decoy type. Every mapped query peptide j of that decoy type is searched against target and decoy (lead decision M3-10 Q1). Let π_j = P(j wrong | its score bin) and π̂_j its estimate.

  • A1 (decoy hit ⇔ chance target hit of the same peptide). For a wrong peptide j, (target hit at cost m, its E) and (decoy hit at cost m, its E) have the same law: p_j(e) = P(hit with E ≤ e) for both (Genome decoys; E is computed by the same function for both, M3-09).
  • A2 (decoy hits do not depend on correctness). The decoy hit of j has the same law p_j(e) whether j is correct or wrong: a correct peptide's decoy hits are chance hits too.
  • A3 (π̂ is a peptide-level label). π̂_j depends on the peptide's score bin only, not on its hits; it is the same for the peptide's target and decoy hit.

p_j(e) may vary freely between peptides (length, composition) and may be correlated with π_j.

docs.title: Derivation
docs.text:
The number of false targets with E ≤ e is V(e) = Σ_j 1{j wrong} 1{chance target hit of j, E ≤ e}, so by A1 E[V(e)] = Σ_j π_j p_j(e). Candidate estimators of V(e) and their expectations:

Estimator of V(e) Expectation Unbiased when Q2 as written: π̄_T(e) · D(e), π̄_T(e) = mean π̂ of targets with E ≤ e π̄_T(e) Σ_j p_j(e) π̄_T(e) = Σ π_j p_j / Σ p_j; fails in general (a) π̄_S · D(e), π̄_S = mean π̂ over all searched peptides π̄_S Σ_j p_j(e) Cov_j(π_j, p_j(e)) = 0 (b) W(e) = Σ_{decoy hits j with E ≤ e} π̂_j Σ_j π_j p_j(e) (A2, A3) always (given A1–A3 and π̂ = π)

Why Q2 fails: a correct peptide always has its target hit, a wrong one only by chance, so the targets with small E are mostly correct peptides from the good (low-π) bins and π̄_T(e) is far below the decoy-hit-weighted π̄ that D(e) needs; D counts chance hits of all searched peptides, most of which come from the bad bins. The bias is largest at the top of the list, i.e. at the operating point α = 0.01. Why (a) is not enough: chance-hit rates vary by a factor ≈ 14 per residue of length (M3-09), and low-score de novo bins plausibly hold shorter peptides, so Cov(π, p) > 0 is the realistic case and (a) is then anti-conservative by Σπp / (π̄ Σp).

The "+1" (§7.2.5, B.6) guards the top of the list against D = 0 by pre-counting one decoy. With weights, one more decoy hit can weigh up to max π̂, so the pre-count must be c = max π̂. Using the mean π̂ instead (c = π̄_S) left a small excess on B.6-sized lists with very unequal bins (mean FDP 0.0113 ± 0.0004 at q = 0.01, N = 150, π = 0.02 / 0.9, R = 3,000).

docs.title: Signed rule
docs.text:
Within stratum m and decoy type, one list ordered by E (unchanged), at every target E = e:

FDR_m(e) = (W_m(e) + c) / T_m(e), W_m(e) = Σ over peptides j with a decoy hit at cost m and E_D,j ≤ e of π̂_j, c = max π̂ over all searched peptides of that decoy type in the stratum's input,

and q_i = min over e ≥ E_i of FDR_m(e), clipped to 1; ties as before (a decoy tied with a target counts). Definitions:

  • π̂_j is the peptide's own π̂ by the step-4 route, whether it contributes a target, a decoy or both: database m = 0 the one pi_wrong_database value; de novo m = 0 its pi_denovo (1 if missing); m ≥ 1 always 1. A decoy-only peptide carries its own π̂.
  • "Searched peptides of that decoy type" = every peptide of that source in the costs table that enters the decoy search, i.e. all rows of the source except same_db exact peptides in stratum 0 (they leave both stratum-0 lists). If the set is empty, c = 1. Any de novo peptide without π̂ makes c = 1.
  • Constant π̂ = π: W = π D, c = π, FDR = π (D + 1)/T, identical to the spec and to tda_qvalues(−E_T, −E_D, π, plus_one=True).
  • Monotonicity: q is non-decreasing in E within the stratum; adding a decoy hit, raising any π̂_j of a decoy, or raising c never lowers a q.
  • mapping_fdr rows (per decoy type × length class × m, no threshold): decoys = D (count, as before), fdr_stratum = (W + c)/T with W summed over the class's decoy hits and the stratum's c (NA when T = 0), pi_wrong = (W + c)/(D + 1), the effective π̂, so fdr_stratum = pi_wrong (D + 1)/T still holds and pi_wrong equals the constant π̂ for database input and m ≥ 1.

Suggested interface (implementer's choice, the semantics above bind): stratum_qvalues(e_target, e_decoy, pi_decoy, pi_plus), pi_decoy one weight per decoy, pi_plus = c (scalar in (0, 1]).

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Statistics-only simulation (generator of tests/calibration/test_placement_fdr_lists.py: every peptide draws a chance decoy hit with probability p, wrong peptides a chance target hit from the same law, correct peptides a low-E target hit), de novo stratum 0, N = 4,000, R = 300, mean FDP ± SE at q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 (* = above q + 2 SE); n = mean accepted at q = 0.01.

Scenario Q2 (mean over targets) (a) mean over searched (b) signed n at 0.01 (b) 10 bins π 0.02–0.9, p = 0.25 (calibration test) 0.0143* / 0.069* / 0.130* 0.0098 / 0.050 / 0.100 0.0095 / 0.050 / 0.100 1,063 2 bins π 0.02 / 0.9, p = 0.25 0.0354* / 0.119* / 0.175* 0.0097 / 0.050 / 0.100 0.0095 / 0.050 / 0.100 1,069 constant π = 0.3 0.0100 / 0.050 / 0.097 identical identical 1,932 10 bins, p = 0.05 + 0.4 π 0.0182* / 0.086* / 0.159* 0.0126* / 0.065* / 0.130* 0.0094 / 0.050 / 0.100 949 2 bins, p = 0.05 + 0.4 π 0.0540* / 0.168* / 0.253* 0.0163* / 0.085* / 0.172* 0.0093 / 0.049 / 0.100 796 10 bins, π̂ = 1.5 π 0.0099 / 0.049 / 0.094 0.0072 / 0.037 / 0.073 0.0069 / 0.036 / 0.073 878 2 bins, π̂ = 1.5 π (capped at 1) 0.0312* / 0.108* / 0.171* 0.0086 / 0.045 / 0.089 0.0085 / 0.044 / 0.089 1,005 10 bins, π̂ = 0.5 π 0.0286* / 0.130* / 0.176* 0.0199* / 0.100* / 0.176* 0.0196* / 0.100* / 0.176* 1,497 2 bins, π̂ = 0.5 π 0.0615* / 0.175* / 0.175* 0.0198* / 0.100* / 0.175* 0.0195* / 0.100* / 0.175* 1,496

Small lists (R = 3,000), signed rule: 2 bins N = 150: 0.0000 / 0.044 / 0.095 (n = 0 at 0.01: with c ≈ 0.9 no list of ≤ 90 targets can reach 0.01); N = 300: 0.0054 / 0.048 / 0.097 (n = 33); 10 bins N = 300: 0.0025 / 0.046 / 0.096 (n = 17). With c = mean π̂ instead: 0.0113* / 0.0099 / 0.0089 at q = 0.01 for these three, n = 29 / 70 / 65.

Misestimation. Under-estimating π by 50 % doubles the FDP for every rule (E[W] = ½ E[V]): validity needs π̂ ≥ π, which is why step 4 uses 1 − the lower 95 % bound of the de novo precision. Over-estimating by 50 % is conservative for (b) (FDP ≈ q/1.5); Q2 is anti-conservative even then in the two-bin case.

Attack (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_placement_pi.py, §8.5; N = 2,000 unless noted; R = 50 fast / 300 full): two_bins, two_bins_corr, ten_bins_corr, two_bins_small (N = 300), ten_bins_over (π̂ = 1.5 π), constant must stay at level through placement; a power check asserts that Q2 and (a) exceed q + 2 SE at q = 0.01 and 0.05 on two_bins_corr (full suite: Q2 0.053 / 0.168, (a) 0.016 / 0.085). The signed rule, run on the same generators through a reference implementation, gave (full suite, q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10): two_bins 0.0093 / 0.050 / 0.101, two_bins_corr 0.0088 / 0.049 / 0.100, ten_bins_corr 0.0086 / 0.050 / 0.100, two_bins_small 0.0055 / 0.049 / 0.100, ten_bins_over 0.0064 / 0.036 / 0.073, constant 0.0100 / 0.050 / 0.096.

docs.title: Alternative considered: separate lists per π̂ value (score bin)
docs.text: Running stratum 0 separately per score bin (the Q2 alternative) applies the spec formula with a constant π̂ in each list. It is also valid in every scenario above (it needs A1–A3 only within a bin) and has more power at α = 0.01 on large inputs with unequal bins (N = 4,000: 1,336 vs 1,063 accepted with 10 bins, 1,969 vs 1,069 with 2 bins), less at q ≥ 0.05 and on small inputs (10 bins N = 300 at 0.01: 55 vs 17 for (b), 21 vs 0 at N = 150). It splits a stratum into several lists, so q is no longer monotone in E within a stratum (§7.2.5 step 3 and the M3-10 acceptance criterion), and mapping_fdr would need a bin dimension. It is therefore a spec change for the lead (ADR), not the default; if adopted, the attack above applies unchanged.

docs.title: Forwarded
docs.text:
• Database input, mean PEP. The spec's single π̂ = mean PEP is estimator (a): unbiased only if PEP is uncorrelated with the chance-hit rate. Short peptides have both higher PEP and many more chance hits, so mean PEP can under-state the false-placement share (10-bin correlated scenario: 0.0126 at q = 0.01; database PEPs are small, so the absolute effect is bounded by the PEPs). The same weighting (Σ PEP_j over decoy hits + max PEP) removes the bias but departs from the spec text: lead decision / ADR; M3-21 should measure Cov(PEP, chance-hit rate) on A2.
  • π̂ from the same decoys. The de novo π̂ (M3-11) uses decoy-match rates r_bℓ of the same shuffle; a bin with many chance decoy hits gets a lower precision and a higher π̂, so W and π̂ are positively dependent: conservative.

docs.title: Tests that must change (test-author)
docs.text:
1. tests/unit/test_placement_fdr.py::test_per_target_pi_uses_mean_over_targets_up_to_e → weights on decoys: targets E = 1, 2, 3; one decoy E = 2.5 with π̂ 0.5; c = 0.6: FDR = 0.6/1, 0.6/2, (0.5 + 0.6)/3 → q = [0.3, 0.3, 0.366667].
  2. …::test_denovo_stratum0_uses_per_peptide_pi → de novo m = 0, length 7: targets (E, π̂) = (1, 0.5), (2, 0.6), (3, 0.3); decoy-only peptide E = 2.5, π̂ 0.5; c = max = 0.6: q = [0.3, 0.3, 0.366667]; row (7, shuffle): targets 3, decoys 1, fdr_stratum = 1.1/3 = 0.366667, pi_wrong = 1.1/2 = 0.55. (With the old π̂ 1.0 for the second target: c = 1, q = [0.5, 0.5, 0.5], fdr_stratum 0.5, pi_wrong 0.75.)
  3. …::test_constant_pi_equals_m4_tda_qvalues and the module docstring (FDR(e) line): call with decoy weights np.full(ed.size, pi) and c = pi; equality with tda_qvalues unchanged. Every other unit test (examples 1–10, ties, clipping, π̂ = 1 when missing) is unchanged: their π̂ is constant within the list.
  4. tests/property/test_placement_fdr_props.py: the stratum strategy draws one π̂ per decoy and a scalar c ∈ (0, 1] (≥ max decoy π̂ to mirror placement); test_constant_pi_equals_… as in 3; test_input_order_invariant permutes decoy weights with the decoys; add: raising any decoy π̂ or c never lowers a q. The other properties (q ∈ [0, 1], monotone in E, adding a decoy never lowers q, scale invariance, all placement properties) stay.
  5. tests/calibration/test_placement_fdr_lists.py::test_denovo_per_bin_pi_controls_fdr: generator unchanged (expected to pass, 0.0095 / 0.050 / 0.100 at R = 300); docstring: drop "most favourable case for … mean pi over targets with E <= e" and cite this section.
  6. Spec text docs/specs/M3-10-placement-fdr.md (bullets "π̂ per target" and mapping_fdr rows, Q2) and lead decision 2 in docs/specs/M3-index.md: lead updates them to this rule.

docs.title: Sign-off (π̂_wrong in the stratum FDR)
docs.text: Statistician (M3-10 pre-implementation decision, 2026-10-14): signed for the rule above (decoy-weighted W_m(e) + c, c = max π̂ over the searched peptides of the decoy type). Lead decision M3-10 Q2 (mean π̂ over targets with E ≤ e) is rejected as anti-conservative and blocks merge if implemented. The remaining M3-10 sections (strata and ranking, π̂_wrong sources, same-strain input, calibration) are signed with the implementation review.

docs.title: Strata and ranking (M3-10)
docs.text:
• Search. Every mapped query peptide (non-decoy, q ≤ input.q_value_max or q missing) is searched against the decoy of its own source (database → reverse, de novo → shuffle; both built for mixed input) exactly as against the target (exact for all, tolerant for all ≥ 10 aa; lead decision M3-10 Q1). Each peptide counts once at its best target cost m_T and, independently, once at its best decoy cost m_D (separate search, not competition: a peptide may be a target in stratum 0 and a decoy in stratum 1). Decoy hits are de-duplicated on their mirrored target interval, never placed and never written to peptide_hits.tsv.
  • Lists. One list per decoy type × m ∈ {0, 1, 2}: T = peptides with m_T = m, D = peptides with m_D = m, both ranked by E ascending (M3-09; target and decoy E from the same function and the same genome f). Length classes are pooled inside a list (G3): E already carries the length (≈ ×14 per residue), so pooling only orders long against short peptides by their chance rate; per-class lists would have small T and a +c that dominates (B.6). The per length class × m rows of mapping_fdr.tsv are descriptive: T and D of the class, fdr_stratum = (W_class + c)/T_class with the stratum's c, no threshold; they are not the q-values.
  • FDR and q. FDR_m(e) = (W_m(e) + c)/T_m(e) at every target E (rule and derivation in "π̂_wrong in the stratum FDR"); q_i = min over e ≥ E_i; ties: all entries with E ≤ e count, so a decoy tied with a target counts against it and tied targets get one q; clipped to [0, 1] by M4-01's monotone_q, so with constant π̂ the q-values equal tda_qvalues(−E_T, −E_D, π̂) (unit- and property-tested). Accept at q ≤ stats.alpha.placement (0.01, inclusive).
  • Families (§8.1). Each list is one FDR family: "placed (exact)" = stratum 0, "placed with ≥ 1 difference" = strata 1 and 2 with π̂ = 1, separately per decoy type. Each accepted set has FDR ≤ α; their union has marginal FDR E[V]/E[R] ≤ α exactly and FDR ≤ α up to the weighting of the ratios (each list pays its own +c, which makes the union slightly conservative). A peptide accepted in stratum m is accepted at all its loci of cost m: multi-locus ambiguity is uniqueness (M3-14), not FDR.
  • Effect size. The per-peptide effect measure next to placement_q is the ranking score E (expected chance windows, conservative ×1.3–1.8 on real genomes, see M3-09) and m_T; the list quantities T, D, W, c are in mapping_fdr.tsv. A target-decoy q-value has no CI of its own; its uncertainty is the +c pre-count (B.6).

B.6. Stratum 1, π̂ = 1 (c = 1): 150 targets before the first decoy give FDR = (0 + 1)/150 = 0.0067, all 150 accepted at 0.01; 50 targets and no decoys give 1/50 = 0.02, none accepted. With per-peptide de novo π̂ the floor is c/T with c = max π̂, so a de novo stratum-0 list needs T ≥ c/α targets before the first decoy (90 at c = 0.9): small de novo inputs are conservative by design (attack two_bins_small: FDP 0.0063 at 0.01).

docs.title: π̂_wrong sources (M3-10)
docs.text:
Input, stratum π̂_j Population database, m = 0 superseded by ADR-0019 (see "Cross-strain input and run collapse"): the exact-match estimate of the peptide's length class. Until then: one value, mean PEP if any PEP; else max q ≤ input.q_value_max; else 1 the database peptides of the stratum-0 lists, i.e. all database rows except same_db exact peptides (ADR-0019 also drops contaminants; see "Same-strain input") de novo, m = 0 pi_denovo of the peptide's score bin (1 − lower 95 % precision bound, M3-11); missing → 1 per peptide any, m ≥ 1 1 —

Mean PEP is estimator (a) of the derivation: unbiased when PEP is calibrated and uncorrelated with the chance-hit rate (forwarded to M3-21). Max q estimates the FDR of the whole input list at its own threshold (≤ q_value_max), an estimate of the wrong share of the peptides that enter mapping (test max_q_route: FDP 0.0020 for a true wrong share 0.008, conservative). π̂ = 0 (all PEPs exactly 0) is allowed by the formula and accepts every target; engines report PEP 0 only through underflow, so a mean over thousands of peptides is never 0 in practice. c = max π̂ over the same population (1 if empty or any de novo π̂ missing).

docs.title: Same-strain input (M3-10)
docs.text:
§7.2.5 step 5: database peptides from a search against this genome's own proteins (search_db = same) with an exact target hit get placement_q = 0 and flag same_db, and leave both stratum-0 lists. Rationale: the engine's own target-decoy already controls the identification error against exactly these sequences, and an exact hit of an own-protein peptide is its source locus; the remaining question is uniqueness (M3-14). Their decoy hits at m ≥ 1 still count in D (conservative: a correct peptide's decoy hit is a chance hit, A2). Tolerant hits of same peptides go through steps 1–4 like any other.

Two conditions are needed for the rest of the list to stay valid (attack tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_placement_same_db.py):

  1. Database input only. search_db is filled from input.search_db for every row, de novo rows included (io/peptides.py). A de novo peptide is not from a protein search; the shortcut must require source = database, otherwise every exact de novo hit gets q = 0.
  2. π̂ on the listed population. The same_db exact peptides have left the stratum-0 lists, so they must also leave the mean PEP (and the max-q fallback). They are selected for being correct (an exact hit in their own genome) and carry small PEPs, so averaging them in lowers π̂ for the other peptides that remain in the list. This changes nothing for single-search_db inputs (all other: nothing removed; all same: the stratum-0 database target list is empty), only for mixed inputs such as A1 (K-12 search) and A2 (Nissle's own proteins) in one run, which the per-row search_db column allows.
Attack (R = 50 fast / 300 full; FDP over list-accepted peptides) placement at 9ec53d1 (before fix) corrected rule (reference; = placement at 031378c) denovo_labelled_same: de novo, π 0.02 / 0.9, every row search_db = same 0.175 / 0.175 / 0.175 (full 0.176) 0.0097 / 0.049 / 0.097 (full 0.0093 / 0.049 / 0.099) mixed_same_other: 2,000 same exact (PEP 0.001) + 2,000 other (π = PEP = 0.3) 0.0196 / 0.097 / 0.097 (full 0.0199 / 0.096 / 0.096) 0.0098 / 0.050 / 0.097 (full 0.0100 / 0.050 / 0.096)

(mean FDP at q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10; SE ≤ 0.0016 fast, ≤ 0.0007 full.) Required fixes: same_exact = is_db & (search_db == "same") & (m_target == 0) and pi_wrong_database(df[is_db & ~same_exact], …).

An unresolved search_db = auto reaching placement is treated as other: valid (conservative, the peptide is FDR-controlled), but it loses the same_db shortcut; auto must be resolved to same/other before mapping (M3-17).

docs.title: Cross-strain input and run collapse (ADR-0019, M3-25)
docs.text:
Status: signed off by the statistician (M3-25 review of #124, 2026-10-20; ADR-0019 decisions 1–5). Decision and evidence: docs/adr/ADR-0019-stratum0-pi-hat-exact-share.md (accepted by Khoa 2026-10-20; Slurm 1860123, 1860138, 1860180). This section supersedes the mean-PEP row of "π̂_wrong sources" for database input in stratum 0 and resolves the item forwarded from ADR-0010 (π̂ correlated with the chance-hit rate).

Why mean PEP fails. Two defects, both measured in M3-21:

  1. Cross-strain input (search_db = other). Some correct identifications report the database strain's sequence across a strain difference. They have no exact true locus, so an exact chance hit elsewhere is a false stratum-0 placement, while their PEP measures identification error only and is small. Mean PEP counts only the identification errors among the peptides without an exact origin and under-estimates the false placements by about (π_wrong + δ)/π_wrong, δ = the spanning share of the correct identifications.
  2. Run collapse. §5.3 collapses a peptide's runs with pep = min. The mean of min-collapsed PEPs is not a peptide-level wrong share: with 3 runs M3-21 measured π̂ ≈ 0.0026 against a true wrong share ≈ 0.024. No PSM-level aggregation (min, mean, max, product) is calibrated in general, so placement stops reading PEP instead of changing §5.3's aggregation, which ranking, detection and evidence still use.

The rule. Population P: all database rows except same_db exact peptides (unchanged from M3-10) and except contaminants (M3-25 decision 7 — they are not genome-derived, so they carry no information about the chance-hit rate). Per length class ℓ of mapping.length_classes:

  • n_ℓ = peptides of P in ℓ; k_ℓ = those with no exact target hit (m_T ≠ 0 or no hit at all); r_ℓ = share of n_ℓ with an exact decoy hit;
  • U_ℓ = one-sided 95 % Clopper–Pearson upper bound of k_ℓ/n_ℓ (1 when k_ℓ = n_ℓ), mirroring step 4's "1 − lower 95 % bound";
  • π̂_ℓ = 1 if r_ℓ = 1, else min(1, U_ℓ/(1 − r_ℓ)).

This is the database analogue of the de novo precision estimator with c_l = 1: a peptide with an exact origin always matches, one without matches at the decoy rate. Every peptide of P carries its class's π̂ into ADR-0010's FDR_0(e) = (W_0(e) + c)/T_0(e), with c = max π̂_ℓ over the classes with n_ℓ > 0. A peptide outside every class weighs 1 and does not enter c; an empty class has no weight. Edge cases: r = 0 ges π̂ = U_ℓ, and m < r (fewer exact target than exact decoy matches) clips to 1. m ≥ 1 is unchanged (π̂ = 1). Why per class and not pooled: the no-origin share correlates with the chance-hit rate, which changes by ≈ ×14 per residue of length; an oracle that knows the true pooled no-origin share still fails the short-peptide and padding scenarios (2.19×, 2.02×).

Evidence (failing cells of 18 list-level scenarios, δ × π × q; ADR-0019 Evidence): mean PEP fails 6–14 cells per scenario, a pooled exact share 0–13, the per-class rule 0 everywhere, including PEP deflated 10× (the run collapse) and the length-correlated inputs. Power at δ = 0 relative to mean PEP is 0.984–1.0 at N = 4,000 and 0.85–0.97 at N = 300 (π̂ = 1 instead gives 0.43–0.84 and 0.25). At genome scale the estimated/true false count moves from 0.03–0.46 under mean PEP to 0.96–2.4 under this rule; acceptance at q = 0.01 is unchanged, small or binding lists lose up to ~15 % power.

Limitation and the run warning. If the upstream pipeline kept only genome-matching peptides, k is ~0 by construction and no genome-based rule can be calibrated — mean PEP included (FDP 0.061 at q = 0.01, δ = 0.2). placement therefore raises the run warning input_prefiltered when k falls below the 0.001 quantile of Binomial(n, mean PEP × (1 − r)) over P pooled; this is the one place the row-level mean PEP is still read, and it is read directly; the old pi_wrong_database helper (whose max-q and 1.0 fallbacks would misfire here) was deleted with M3-25 decision 11. The detector inherits PEP's weakness in one direction: a deflated PEP (the §5.3 min over runs, defect 2 above, or an engine that under-reports) lowers the expected count n × mean PEP × (1 − r) towards the realised k, so the test loses power and a genuinely pre-filtered input can pass unwarned. It never fires spuriously for that reason — too small an expectation only hides the warning — and the π̂ it guards does not read PEP at all. An inflated PEP is the conservative direction.

Reporting. mapping_fdr.tsv columns are unchanged, with pi_wrong = (W + c)/(D + 1) now reflecting the class π̂. Read the per-class π̂ from the class table, not from mapping_fdr: a class with no decoy hit has W = 0 and D = 0, so its pi_wrong row is c, the largest class estimate, not that class's π̂_ℓ. The class table is the placement step's stratum0_classes output (mapping/stratum0_classes.parquet, columns length_class, n, k, r, upper, pi_wrong), an optional input of context_stats, which turns it into detection_summary.tsv QC rows stratum0_unmapped_share = k/n (the §7.5.1 genome-inconsistent rate of this population), one for the run and one per length class, each per-class row carrying that class's upper as ci_high. It sits beside genome_inconsistent_rate, which measures another population (C9 other, non-contaminant, over accepted exact placements) and is unchanged.

docs.title: Calibration (M3-10)
docs.text:
Criterion (§8.4 "FDR"): mean FDP over R replicates ≤ q + 2 SE at q ∈ {0.01, 0.05, 0.10}; R = replicates_fast.placement (50) per PR, replicates_full.placement (300) nightly; seeds from tolerances.yaml.

List level (tests/calibration/test_placement_fdr_lists.py, through placement): correct peptides get a low-E target hit, every peptide a chance decoy hit with probability p and wrong peptides an independent chance target hit from the same E law (A1–A2 hold by construction). Review run, 9ec53d1, R = 50, mean FDP ± SE at 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10:
