Scenario FDP n accepted at 0.01 known π = 0.3, m = 0 0.0095 ± 0.0003 / 0.049 ± 0.001 / 0.097 ± 0.001 1,898 known π = 0.3, m = 1 (π̂ = 1, conservative) 0.0026 / 0.015 / 0.030 1,001 calibrated PEP ~ Beta(0.6, 1.4) 0.0103 ± 0.0004 / 0.050 ± 0.001 / 0.096 ± 0.001 1,959 max-q route (true share 0.008) 0.0020 / 0.0020 / 0.0020 3,977 de novo, 10 bins 0.0086 ± 0.0005 / 0.049 ± 0.001 / 0.099 ± 0.001 1,037

Attacks (test_attack_placement_pi.py, through placement, R = 50): two_bins 0.0080 / 0.050 / 0.101; two_bins_corr 0.0085 / 0.049 / 0.099; ten_bins_corr 0.0089 / 0.050 / 0.099; two_bins_small 0.0063 / 0.045 / 0.095; ten_bins_over 0.0066 / 0.036 / 0.072; constant 0.0093 / 0.048 / 0.095 (SE ≤ 0.0017 at 0.01). The rejected rules still fail (power check passes). Same-strain attack: see the table above (failed at 9ec53d1, passes at 031378c).

Genome level, exact route (tests/calibration/test_placement_fdr_genome.py): 100-kb giapsim genomes, tryptic peptides of annotated genes as correct, 20,000 i.i.d. 7–8-mers from the genome's own f as wrong, database input, reverse decoys, PEP = the known wrong share. R = 50: 0.0102 ± 0.0007 / 0.0236 ± 0.0009 / 0.0236 ± 0.0009, 592 accepted at 0.01; 719 chance target hits of wrong peptides in total (the null is exercised). At 0.05 and 0.10 every target is accepted, so the FDP equals the wrong share among targets (0.024 < q). At 0.01 the mean is within 1 SE of q, which is expected: with constant π̂ and an exact reverse decoy the estimator is unbiased up to the +1. Tolerant strata, de novo errors with shuffle decoys, attack 5 (reversed stretches), 1-Mb genomes and real-protein wrong peptides (TE8 proxy) are M3-21.

docs.title: Implementation review (M3-10, src/giap/mapping/placement_fdr.py, 9ec53d1)
docs.text:
Checked against ADR-0010, the final section of docs/specs/M3-10-placement-fdr.md and this note:

  • stratum_qvalues: T(e) and W(e) by searchsorted(side="right") (ties counted against the target, tied targets share one q), monotone_q from M4-01 (running minimum from the loose end, clip to [0, 1]); NaN targets → NaN, NaN decoys ignored; weights and c validated in [0, 1]. Correct. Reduction to tda_qvalues with constant π̂: unit- and property-tested.
  • W and c: per decoy type and stratum; W sums each decoy hit's own π̂ (de novo pi_denovo, missing → 1, clipped to [0, 1]; database the one value; m ≥ 1 → 1); c = max π̂ over all peptides of the source in the costs table, including peptides without any hit, minus same_db exact peptides at m = 0; 1 for m ≥ 1 or an empty population. Correct.
  • mapping_fdr rows: decoy type × m × length class plus all, fdr_stratum = (W + c)/T (NaN at T = 0), pi_wrong = (W + c)/(D + 1), n_accepted per class; peptides outside every length class count only in all. Correct.
  • Flags joined with ;: matches §9 (";-separated controlled vocabulary"). low_complexity (≤ 3 distinct residues, I = L) is the flag this note recommended (M3-03, M3-09), but it is not in the §9.4 placement vocabulary, which may be extended "only through the schema": the lead must add it to the schema/ADR (M3-16) before outputs are written. Not a statistical blocker.
  • Blocking at 9ec53d1, fixed in 031378c: the two same-strain conditions above. The fix is exactly same_exact = is_db & (search_db == "same") & (m_target == 0) and pi_wrong_database(df[is_db & ~same_exact], …). Re-run at 1dafac0 (R = 50 / 300, q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10): denovo_labelled_same 0.0097 / 0.049 / 0.097 (full 0.0093 / 0.049 / 0.099), mixed_same_other 0.0098 / 0.050 / 0.097 (full 0.0099 / 0.050 / 0.096). The list, placement_pi and genome numbers above are unchanged (single-search_db inputs are unaffected). The low_complexity flag was accepted by ADR-0011.

docs.title: Sign-off (Strata and ranking, π̂_wrong sources, Same-strain input, Calibration)
docs.text: Statistician (M3-10 implementation review, 2026-10-14): the four sections above are signed as the method. The implementation is approved at 031378c (re-verified at 1dafac0): the same_db shortcut requires source = database, the database π̂ is computed over the stratum-0 population, and test_attack_placement_same_db.py passes (at 9ec53d1 the FDP at q = 0.01 was 0.175 and 0.0196). Forwarded to M3-21: Cov(PEP, chance-hit rate) on A2; the list-level calibration of tolerant strata with real decoy hits; attack 5.

docs.title: Genome-level calibration (M3-21)
docs.text:
Suites: tests/calibration/test_placement_fdr_sim.py, test_denovo_precision_sim.py, attacks/test_attack5_reversed_stretches.py; truth oracle tests/helpers/placement_truth.py (origins per row type, overlap rule of lead decision 2, unique guard, cost-≤ m_T+1 mutant).

What "exercised" means. A list (decoy type × m) is exercised in a replicate by the number of peptides in it that are false placements (no accepted locus overlaps a true origin), at any q. A gate on a list with no false peptides passes trivially and is a smoke check: it shows the chain runs and accepts, not that the FDR is controlled.

At 100 kb the placement lists are not exercised enough to test the bound. In the fast tier (R = 50, job 1860994) the database-shuffled (π 0.01, 0.05), related other-strain and related db-strain suites had 0 false peptides in every list. The de novo error-model suite and attack 5 had a mean of 0.14 and 0.12 per replicate in shuffle m = 0 and ≤ 0.02 elsewhere. These gates are therefore smoke checks (claimed = ()). The genome-level evidence for stratum 0 comes from two places only:

  • the stressed stratum-0 arm (test_database_stressed_stratum0_placement_fdr, full tier at 1 Mb): short wrong database peptides (7/8-mers of protein sequences that are absent from the genome, as in b2sim --mode short) are injected test-locally with PEP set to the true wrong share. This arm claims reverse m = 0. With δ = 0 (exact PEP) its FDP gate is expected to pass. At 100 kb (K = 2,000, R = 50, job 1860994): 1.6 false peptides per replicate, mean FDP 0.0009 at every q. At 1 Mb (K = 400, R = 300, job 1860995): 2.85 false per replicate, mean FDP 0.00016 at every q, about 17,960 accepted. The fast arm also asserts the estimate check mean(Ŵ0) ≥ mean(V0) − 2 SE: Ŵ0 2.44 vs V0 1.6, because the injected share dominates the pooled π̂ at 100 kb. At 1 Mb the estimate check is a separate test, test_database_stressed_stratum0_estimate_covers_false_placements (calibration_full, R = 100, ΣV0 ≥ 100). It was a strict xfail "ADR-0019 implementation pending" until M3-25 implemented the ADR: mean PEP gave Ŵ0 0.57 vs V0 2.85. The cause is the length-correlated no-origin share. 75 % of the injected peptides are 7-mers, and the 7-mer class has a no-origin share of 0.22 against 0.031 pooled, so a pooled π̂ times all decoy hits under-counts. ADR-0019's per-class π̂ corrects it; the statistician's reference rule gives Ŵ0 3.65 vs V0 3.50 over 6 replicates (review of #113, round 2). Post-ADR, through placement (M3-25, job 1861430, R = 100): Ŵ0 4.306 vs V0 2.75, SE 0.191, ΣV0 = 275 (floor 100) — the check passes, with a ratio of 1.57 against 0.20 under mean PEP. The FDP stays far below q under mean PEP only because the stratum is large;
  • the related db-strain estimate check (test_related_dbstrain_stratum0_estimate_covers_false_placements, full tier, 1 Mb, 5 SNV/kb, R = 100). It requires ΣV0 ≥ 30 false stratum-0 placements and mean W0 ≥ mean V0 − 2 SE (SE of V0 − W0 over lists). Observed (job 1860995, after the B1 origin fix): ΣV0 = 79, mean V0 0.79, mean W0 0.150, SE 0.099. It was a strict xfail until ADR-0019 (exact-match π̂ per length class) was implemented in M3-25. Correct identifications that span a strain difference have no exact origin but small PEP, so mean PEP under-counts their exact chance hits (ADR-0019 Context, defect 1). Post-ADR, through placement (M3-25, job 1861430, R = 100): Ŵ0 1.551 vs V0 0.79, SE 0.107, ΣV0 = 79 (floor 30) — the check passes, with a ratio of 1.96 against 0.19 under mean PEP. Both post-ADR ratios (1.57 and 1.96) sit inside ADR-0019's expected 0.96–2.4 band; the excess over 1 is the Clopper–Pearson bound plus c, and c is set by the most sparsely populated class (a class with k = n forces π̂_ℓ = 1), so most of the conservative margin can come from one small class — read stratum0_classes to see which.

FDR evidence at m ≥ 1 rests on the list-level suites (test_placement_fdr_lists.py, attacks/test_attack_placement_pi.py), not on these genome suites.

Attack 5. Its FDP gate is a smoke check as well. Its content is the decoy-count documentation: de novo reversed stretches searched with reverse decoys inflate the m = 0 decoy count D (mean 9.1 reversed vs 0.5 shuffled per replicate). That is why de novo input uses shuffle decoys.

docs.title: Annotated-stop read-through (M7-16a, ADR-0058)
docs.text:
Code: src/giap/mapping/readthrough.py (sites, cells, mirrored cells), tolerant_dp._verify_core (the consumable-stop case), tolerant.Search(marked), frameshift._FSearch(marked) and nonfs_overlap, steps.mapping.sixframe_index (index format 2, event mapping.stop_sites). Spec: docs/specs/M7-16-stop-codon-readthrough.md; review: statistician, 2026-10-24 (local/stat/m7-16-review.md).

1. The rule. Route 3 (tolerant) may consume a target * only at the annotated stop codon of a CDS or sORF: the last codon of the feature, on its strand, in its frame. Pseudogenes are excluded, and a feature whose last codon is not a table-11 stop (for example a partial gene at a contig edge) is skipped and counted (not_a_stop). The codon is marked at every copy in the origin-extended frames of a circular replicon. The only move over a marked cell is a substitution of one query residue (any letter, U and X included) at cost 1, recorded as substitution; no match, swap, block or near-block reads it, and every other * and every X stays unconsumable. The exact route and the frameshift sides never consume a stop; the frameshift precedence check does see read-through alignments. Peptides shorter than 10 aa never reach route 3 (mapping.tolerant.min_len), so a stop-spanning peptide of 7–9 aa is never placed; at 10–11 aa (k = 1) the stop is the only allowed difference.

2. Counts are exactly symmetric. Each decoy frame carries the target frame's number of marked cells: reverse maps cell p of an n-residue frame to n − 1 − p, shuffle keeps p (stops keep their positions). Every mirrored cell holds *, so the stop-free run lengths on each side are the same, origin copies included. mirror_cells raises if a mirrored cell is not a stop, draws no randomness, and the decoy frames are byte-identical to index format 1 for the same seed.

3. Context mirroring and the measured ratios. Under any i.i.d. peptide law the reverse decoy is exact (read-through D_rt/T_rt = 1 to 1e-16). The local context is mirrored, not kept: gene | * | 3′ flank becomes reversed flank | * | reversed gene. Under a law that is not reversal-symmetric (tryptic, C-terminal K/R) the per-genome read-through D_rt/T_rt was 0.52–1.89 (reverse) and 0.58–1.74 (shuffle) on three giapsim 1-Mb genomes, and 0.81–1.15 (reverse) and 1.14–1.42 (shuffle) on Nissle. The net effect on the total, (D_rt − T_rt)/T_regular, was at worst −9.4 × 10⁻⁴ (giapsim) and −1.3 × 10⁻⁴ (Nissle): exact expected chance mass, Slurm jobs 1889319 (Nissle) and 1889320 (giapsim), script local/stat/m7-16/rt_mass.py. Job 1889319 used a local Bakta run with all four replicons linear (4,686 sites). On the committed recording tests/data/recorded/bakta/1.12.2-full/nissle (all circular; 4,689 sites, 3 not_a_stop) job 1889965 reproduces them: reverse tryptic 0.81–1.14, shuffle tryptic 1.16–1.39, shuffle i.i.d. 1.03–1.18, reverse i.i.d. exactly 1, worst net shift −1.3 × 10⁻⁴, read-through share 0.035–0.082 %. The stressed arm's measured values are under item 8.

4. The added mass is an approximation, not a bound. A window consumes a marked cell only if it contains it, with the other L − 1 residues within m − 1 differences. Relative to E(L, m) of §7.2.5 the added chance mass is approximately G/(N(1 − s)) at m = 1 and 2G/(N(1 − s)) at m = 2 (G consumable cells, N six-frame positions, s the residue-match probability), independent of L and scaling with the gene density G/N. Measured realised shares of the target chance mass: 0.04–0.08 % on Nissle and 0.05–0.20 % on giapsim 1 Mb (i.i.d. and tryptic laws; the top of the range is tryptic at m = 2). On another genome the share is approximately, not at most, the formula's value for its G/N.

5. The read-through ratio is not a subset FDR. D_rt/T_rt does not estimate the false discovery rate of the read-through placements. The list FDR (per decoy type and stratum) does not control that subset, and no output, table or report may present the ratio as one (R3).

6. Expected false read-through placements per run are about α · T_acc(m ≥ 1) · ρ, where T_acc(m ≥ 1) is the number of accepted target placements in strata 1–2 and ρ ≈ 10⁻³ is the read-through share of the chance mass. That is ≪ 1 for any realistic run, but it is not a per-site guarantee.

7. Power. A true read-through peptide with no other difference lands in stratum 1 with π̂ = 1 and the +1 in the decoy count. By Appendix B.6 a stratum-1 list with fewer than about 100 targets ahead of its first decoy accepts none, so cterm_extension has low power on small inputs by design. This is a statement, not a change.

8. What the suites show. The estimator, strata, π̂ and the ranking score E are unchanged (no tolerance, bound, α or R changes).

  • Regression-only (byte-identical by construction: cells=None or no matcher): test_tolerant_recall.py, test_placement_fdr_genome.py, test_placement_fdr_lists.py, attacks/test_attack_placement_*. They cannot see the rule and are regression evidence only.
  • Exercised (run_chain, reaching sixframe_index → map_tolerant with cells): test_placement_fdr_sim.py, test_denovo_precision_sim.py and attack 5. Fast tier (R = 50, 100 kb): main 1890006, branch 1890007. Full tier (R = 300, 1 Mb): main 1890009, branch 1890010. All 10 tests pass in each of the four runs.
  • Every FDP per decoy type, stratum and level is unchanged to 4 significant digits; the largest change is 4.4 × 10⁻¹⁰.
  • The de novo precision diagnostics, the stratum-0 estimate checks and the attack-5 decoy documentation are identical.
  • Accepted target rows that consumed a cell, per replicate at q 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10:
    • 0 in every suite at 100 kb, except related_other_strain (0–1, 2 rows in 2 of 50 replicates);
    • at 1 Mb, related_other_strain 0–5 (200 / 221 / 224 rows; 165 of 300 replicates);
    • attack 5 0–1 (2 rows);
    • 0 elsewhere.
  • All of them are true placements: FDP and the false-peptide exercise are unchanged, and the accepted counts rise by exactly those rows.
  • Counts come from an observer of run_chain: best-cost target rows whose window holds a target cell (holds_cell) among peptides with m_target ≥ 1 and placement_q ≤ q.
  • Stressed arm (test_readthrough_stressed.py; dense 30–40-codon genes, reduced-alphabet coding frame, reverse arm on database input and shuffle arm on de novo input; criteria m ≥ 1 FDP ≤ q + se_multiplier · SE at every level and mean(D_rt) ≥ mean(T_rt) − se_multiplier · SE; a negative control without decoy cells must fail the balance criterion). Fast tier (R = 50, Slurm job 1889791, about 9,250 cells per replicate):
arm mean T_rt mean D_rt SE(D − T) read-through share control D_rt mean FDP at q 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 reverse (database) 121.6 125.4 1.95 1.98 % 0 (fails, as required) 0.0043 / 0.024 / 0.057 shuffle (de novo) 123.6 391.0 2.83 2.02 % 0 (fails, as required) 0.0070 / 0.036 / 0.083

Shuffle D_rt ≈ 3 × T_rt comes from the build, not the cells: every stressed gene's stop is followed 1–3 residues later by the next gene's start M, which the K/P/Y/F peptides never match, so a target window past the stop spends its second difference on it, while the shuffle moves the M. Exact chance mass gives shuffle D/T 2.6–3.6 as built and 0.97 with the start ATG replaced by AAA; reverse is 1.000 either way. It is conservative, but it means the stressed shuffle arm alone cannot see a partial loss of shuffle cells (up to about 2/3); the reverse arm, the no-cells control and the attack's structural checks cover that. - Statistician's attack (attacks/test_attack_readthrough_decoys.py, Slurm 1889956, fast and full pass): exact expected chance mass on the cells sixframe_index writes, L 10, 11, 12, 16. Reverse i.i.d. D_rt = T_rt to rtol 1e-9 in every replicate. Shuffle i.i.d. mean D_rt/T_rt on giapsim 100 kb is 0.97–1.07 (fast, R 50) and 1.03–1.09 (full, R 300); the tryptic worst net shift is −2.2 × 10⁻⁴ against the one-sided margin (≥ −0.01). Cell counts and consumable windows are equal in target, reverse and shuffle at every L. Each broken build fails: no decoy cells, target cells reused for the reverse decoy, a reverse mirror off by one. - Stressed arm, full tier (R = 300, job 1890008): - reverse: T_rt 123.0, D_rt 125.1 (SE 0.92), FDP 0.0038 / 0.024 / 0.057; - shuffle: T_rt 122.9, D_rt 390.1 (SE 1.41), FDP 0.0067 / 0.036 / 0.081; - read-through share 2.0 %; both controls fail, as required; - accepted target rows that consumed a cell 0–5 (reverse) and 0–7 (shuffle) per replicate at q 0.10. - Regression-only, fast tier: branch 1890013 and main 1890090, both 37 passed and 1 xfailed. The gate records are identical apart from durations.

Accepted target rows that consumed a cell, per replicate at q 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10: 0–1 / 0–2 / 0–3 (reverse) and 0–1 / 0–2 / 0–5 (shuffle). The shuffle arm's D_rt is about 3 × T_rt in this dense build: conservative in the direction the check guards (cause: the next gene's start M, explained under the table above). As item 5 says, neither ratio is a subset FDR. - Decoy-balance check (test_readthrough_decoy_balance.py, giapsim 1 Mb null genomes, one-sided, may be vacuous): fast tier (R = 50, job 1889791) vacuous for both decoy types, as expected: T_rt = D_rt = 0, read-through share 0 (mean false target placements T 0.38 reverse, 14.7 shuffle; about 905 cells per genome).

docs.title: 16b reporting: the readthrough flag and the placement-kind counts
docs.text: A peptide_hits.tsv row whose accepted alignment consumes an annotated terminal stop cell carries the flag readthrough (and mappings.gff3 the attribute readthrough_codon), computed from the sites the index was searched with. detection_summary.tsv counts distinct peptides by placement kind, tolerant diff type, placement flag and unmapped reason (section qc, metric n_peptides). These are counts, not rates or FDRs: n is the population the count comes from, never a denominator to report. The flagged rows are a subset of a list accepted at q, and the list FDR does not control that subset (items 5–6); no output describes the readthrough rows as accepted at q on their own.

docs.title: Region tests: O − E and Hodges–Lehmann shift under circular gene-index shifts
docs.text: Implements giap.context.regions (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.5(b), §8.1, Appendix B.4; issue M4-17, docs/specs/M4-17-region-tests.md, ADR-0018 and lead decisions 6–10) and the regions_stats.tsv rows of giap.context.regions_table (issue M4-18, docs/specs/M4-18-regions-stats-table.md, sections "Replicon-level effects" and "Descriptive rows"). Reuses giap.stats.permutation (M4-03), giap.stats.bootstrap and giap.stats.robust (M4-04) and giap.stats.multitest.bh (M4-01). Statistician sign-off: see the end of this note.

docs.title: Index
docs.text: A replicon's index is its eligible genes — not partial and with a p_detect — sorted by start (the origin-crossing gene, stored unwrapped, comes last), numbered 0 … N − 1. Partial genes occur only at linear contig ends and are never indexed, so every shifted set has the same number of eligible genes as the region (lead decision 5). A region's index set I = the indices of its eligible members on that replicon. Members on two replicons (an AMR gene set spanning chromosome and plasmid) give one test per replicon, each on its own shifts, flagged split_contigs.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
• O − E S(I) = Σ_{i∈I} (d_i − p_i); observed = Σ d_i, expected = Σ p_i, effect = S (and its CI) on the O − E scale. The test statistic is the studentised sum T(I) = S(I)/√Σ_{i∈I} p_i(1 − p_i) (ADR-0018 decision 2), recomputed at every shift, so a region whose p_detect sits nearer 0.5 than the replicon's is not anti-conservative (Σ p(1 − p) = 0 gives T = 0 for S = 0, ±∞ otherwise). With one p on the whole replicon T and S give the same p.
  • Residualised abundance (ADR-0018 decision 1, lead decision 10): per replicon, OLS with an intercept of log2 abundance on log(length_aa), log1p(n_observable_peptides) and GRAVY (the §9.3 genes.tsv covariates), fitted on the replicon's indexed genes that are detected with a finite abundance; a non-finite transformed covariate takes that column's median over the fitted genes (minimum-norm solution for rank-deficient designs, so constant covariates only centre a). The residuals ã are fitted once per replicon, so every shift sees the same values.
  • HL shift: the median of all pairwise differences ã_i − ã_j between the region's detected genes with a finite residualised log2 abundance and the replicon's other such genes (hodges_lehmann; mean of the two middle values for an even count). NaN when either side is empty. Detected genes without abundance (policy exclude) drop out on both sides. Comparing within the replicon only keeps a high-copy plasmid's dosage out of the shift (attack 4). Effect, CI and p are on the residual scale: log2 units relative to the covariate expectation, labelled "detectability-adjusted" in the report.
  • HL test statistic (ADR-0018 amendments 1–2, lead decisions 11–16): the shift p comes from the studentised T = HL/√V, recomputed at every shift (studentised_hl_null). V is label-free (amendment 2): V = Var(mean_in − mean_out) = S_in,in/m² + S_out,out/m′² − 2 S_in,out/(m m′), S_A,B the sum of γ(d(i, j)) over detected genes with finite ã in A × B, m, m′ their counts inside / outside the set (hl_variance). γ(h), h = 0 … 30 (LAG_MAX), is the replicon's autocovariance of ã at gene-index lag h (centred on the mean of ã, each lag divided by its number of detected pairs), estimated once per replicon and set to 0 from the first h ≥ 1 with γ(h) ≤ 0 (lag_autocovariance). Lags and d are circular on circular replicons and plain |i − j| (pairs inside the sequence) on linear ones (decision 16). Implementation: c_i = Σ_j ok_j γ(d(i, j)) once per replicon (≤ 61 offsets), then per shift S_in,all = Σ_{i∈set} c_i, S_in,in by pairwise distances inside the set, S_in,out = S_in,all − S_in,in, S_out,out = S_all − 2 S_in,all + S_in,in. Guard (decision 12): when γ(0) ≤ (10⁻⁷ · max |raw log2 abundance|)², i.e. (numerically) constant residuals, V counts as 0 and T = 0 at every shift. Otherwise, a finite V ≤ 0 at the observed or any null shift (the truncated γ need not be positive definite) makes the region's HL p NA with flag hl_variance_nonpositive (fail closed, decision 16). TU labels do not enter V; a missing tu_id on a tested replicon raises ValueError (decision 13; C6 makes it non-null). The reported effect and CI stay HL. Why: a region's detected-gene count can differ strongly from that at shifted positions (≈ 7 vs ≈ 22 of 40 short prophage genes), so raw HL has the wrong spread under the shift null (limitation (iii)); label-free V is immune to TU-label errors (attack A-TU).

docs.title: Null: circular gene-index shifts
docs.text:
I ↦ (I + k) mod N for k = 1 … N − 1 (circular_shifts); on linear contigs only shifts that do not wrap. Exhaustive while N ≤ context.exhaustive_shift_max_genes, otherwise stats.permutations shifts drawn without replacement (choose_shifts). Both statistics are recomputed at each shift; HL shifts with an empty side are dropped, so HL n_perm counts valid shifts.

What the null preserves: region size, the spacing of its members (a block stays a block, a scattered AMR set keeps its gaps), and the replicon's autocorrelation of d − p and abundance; the region is moved, the genome is not rearranged. Under H₀ "the region's position is exchangeable with every other position on the replicon", the observed set is one member of the shift orbit, so the +1-rule p is exact. The circular null is not perfect on simulated data (M4-08's AR(1) restarts per replicon and does not wrap at the origin, one uncorrelated join) — negligible for level.

p = perm_p(S_obs, null, "two-sided"): (1 + #{|S_k − c| ≥ |S_obs − c|})/(1 + K), c the pooled mean of the observed and null statistics (exact under exchangeability; ties within 1e-12 count). K = 0 (a linear contig with no non-wrapping shift) → p NA. p is discrete with floor 1/(1 + K): rows with K < 19 (no p can reach 0.05) are flagged few_shifts.

docs.title: Exact HL at every shift
docs.text: Recomputing HL by enumeration (m·(M − m) differences at each of up to N − 1 shifts) is too slow at 4,500 genes. hl_null sorts the replicon's M observed values once; for each shift the k-th smallest inside-minus-outside difference is found by bisection on its value, counting pairs x_i − z_j ≤ t by binary search in the sorted values and subtracting the inside-inside pairs, for all shifts at once; once ≤ 64 candidates remain they are enumerated. Results equal hodges_lehmann to ~1e-14 (the property suite compares with a naive per-shift loop).

docs.title: CIs: TU-block bootstrap
docs.text: tu_block_bootstrap, B = stats.bootstrap, 95 % percentile. O − E resamples the region's TUs, counting only region members within each TU (a region inside one TU has a degenerate CI). HL resamples inside and outside TUs as two strata (on the residualised abundances; the fit is not repeated per resample). A missing tu_id raises ValueError before any test (decision 13), so every block is a real TU.

docs.title: Multiple testing and flags
docs.text: BH within each (region_type, stat) family (lead decision 5, ADR-0018 decision 3; detection and abundance answer different questions; at least as strict as "within type" for each statistic). Flags: small_region (< 3 eligible genes; tests still run when K > 0; with 0 eligible genes all statistics are NA and n_perm = 0), few_shifts, split_contigs, hl_variance_nonpositive (HL row only; p NA, see above).

docs.title: Calibration evidence
docs.text:
Suite regions (tests/calibration/test_region_tests.py, attacks in tests/calibration/attacks/test_region_tests_attacks.py): M4-07 layout + 60-gene plasmid with its own AMR set, M4-08 AR(1) ρ = 0.5, no region effects, detection from covariates only.

  • Fast run (Slurm 1849058, R = 100 + confirmation block): C2 FDR, A4 (20x plasmid) and every C1 check pass except crispr/hl_shift at α = 0.01 (4/100 then 3/100, bound 2.99/100). An independent 600-replicate run of the same scenario (Slurm 1849100) gives rejection rates 0.012 / 0.040 / 0.072 at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 for that check (all 8 (type, stat) checks within 0.003-0.017 / 0.032-0.077 / 0.072-0.127, also without origin crossing and with ρ = 0): the gate failure looks like seed chance, for the statistician to rule on.
  • A2 (short prophage genes) gates on M4-13 cross-fitted p_detect and waits for PR #83.
  • ADR-0018 implementation (Slurm 1849426 fast, 1849427 full): A2-mid O − E (studentised) passes at α = 0.05 / 0.10 (0.05 / 0.07, R = 100; α = 0.01 unconfirmed 0.03 / 0.02). A2-HL still fails: linear residualisation (lead decision 10) gives 0.07 / 0.04 (fast, α = 0.01), 0.17 / 0.11 (0.05), 0.22 / 0.15 (0.10), and 0.052 / 0.144 / 0.221 at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 in full mode (R = 1,000 per block). Side runs on the same scenario (600 replicates at 1,000 genes / 200 at 4,500): raw HL 0.107 / 0.243 / 0.328 and 0.105 / 0.25 / 0.38, linear 0.033 / 0.112 / 0.185 and 0.055 / 0.14 / 0.195, adding (log length)² 0.025 / 0.09 / 0.14 and 0.05 / 0.12 / 0.18. Residualising on covariates halves the bias but does not remove detection selection; resolved by ADR-0018 amendment 1 (next item).
  • Studentised HL (dd663c0; suites run on that tree, Slurm 1850200 fast / 1850201 full; all pass). Full mode (R = 1,000, α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10):
  • A2-HL 0.002 / 0.024 / 0.064, A2-HL-MAR 0.003 / 0.016 / 0.042;
  • A2-mid O − E 0.005 / 0.034 / 0.073, A2-low O − E (M4-13 p) 0.005 / 0.044 / 0.076;
  • C1 pooled (m = 4, ρ = 0.5): HL 0.007 / 0.049 / 0.096, O − E 0.009 / 0.050 / 0.103; pooled HL at ρ = 0 and 0.9 also pass, as does plasmid AMR at α 0.05 / 0.10. Fast: everything passes; A2-mid O − E at α = 0.01 is unconfirmed (0.03 / 0.02).
  • Label-free lag V (ADR-0018 amendment 2, 04fc8f7; Slurm 1850777 fast, 1850778 full; all pass). Full mode (R = 1,000 per block, α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10):
  • A-TU (region TUs fragmented, pooled m = 4) 0.0115 / 0.0525 / 0.0985 (failed with TU-label V);
  • A2-HL 0.009 / 0.050 / 0.098, A2-HL-MAR 0.012 / 0.041 / 0.090;
  • A2-mid O − E 0.005 / 0.034 / 0.073, A2-low O − E 0.005 / 0.044 / 0.076;
  • C1 pooled HL at ρ = 0 / 0.5 / 0.9: 0.0105 / 0.0505 / 0.102, 0.0085 / 0.047 / 0.096, 0.009 / 0.047 / 0.096; O − E (ρ = 0.5) 0.009 / 0.050 / 0.103; plasmid AMR passes. Fast: everything passes (C1 pooled HL at α = 0.01 and A2-mid O − E at α = 0.01 unconfirmed: 0.02 / 0.0175 and 0.03 / 0.02). hl_variance_nonpositive occurred in 3 of 59,000 HL rows in full mode (all in the ρ = 0.9 null) and 0 of 7,300 in fast mode.
  • A-LIN (statistician, round 4; test_alin_linear_replicon_hl_at_level): no origin crossing, every replicon declared linear, ρ = 0.9, chromosome HL pooled over prophage / BGC / CRISPR (m = 3). Fast (Slurm 1851283, R = 100) 0.0133 / 0.070 / 0.097, full (1851308, R = 1,000) 0.0083 / 0.0453 / 0.0993: pass.
  • C3 power (recorded, not gated; BGC O − E, α = 0.05, R = 100): +10 % 0.11, +20 % 0.21, +30 % 0.46, +50 % 0.88 (local/logs/calibration/regions_power.jsonl).

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: 4,500-gene chromosome, 30 regions, exhaustive shifts, B = 1,000: ~35 s on one core (benchmarks/test_region_tests_bench.py; budget 60 s); the TU-block bootstrap of HL dominates.

docs.title: Limitations (statistician)
docs.text:
• Exactness needs exchangeable positions. The shift p is an exact randomization p only when the region's position is independent of the per-gene data. Two violations matter: (i) detectability confounded with membership (§8.5 attack 2): the unstandardised O − E sum has variance Σ p(1 − p), so a region whose p_detect sits nearer 0.5 than the replicon's is anti-conservative (synthetic, R = 4,000: replicon p ~ Beta(4, 1.5), 40-gene region p ~ Beta(2, 2) gives 0.016 / 0.074 / 0.131 at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10; replicon Beta(0.3, 0.3), region p = 0.5 gives 0.074 / 0.212 / 0.303). The studentised shift statistic Σ(d − p)/√Σ p(1 − p), recomputed at each shift, restores level (0.010 / 0.048 / 0.103 and 0.010 / 0.046 / 0.097); adopted (ADR-0018). The giapsim attack-2 layout (short prophage genes, low p) is the conservative direction (0.004 / 0.019 / 0.047 with p_detect_true) and cannot detect this. (ii) detection-selection bias of HL: HL uses detected genes only. When detection depends on abundance (giapsim detection = "abundance", β_abundance 0.5–1) and the region's genes are short, only its abundant genes are detected: prophage HL rejects 0.089 / 0.21–0.25 / 0.30–0.35 (R = 2,000, mean HL +0.7 to +0.8 log2; control layout without short genes 0.004–0.009 / 0.036–0.048 / 0.080–0.100). Residualising log2 abundance on detectability covariates among the replicon's detected genes before HL (prototype: quadratic in log length) gives 0.017 / 0.067 / 0.103 (R = 300); adopted as the linear fit above (ADR-0018, lead decision 10). Residualising removes the part of a real region shift that the covariates explain (e.g. a prophage that is both short and silent). Correction (review round 2): the R = 300 prototype figure was noise; residualisation removes the location bias but not the failure. The remaining failure is a third violation: (iii) detected-count heterogeneity of HL: only ~6–7 of the prophage's 40 genes are detected (short genes), against ~22 at a shifted position, so the observed HL has a wider sampling distribution than the shift null (same mechanism as (i) for O − E). It fails even when detection does not depend on abundance (A2-HL-MAR below) and even with the exact oracle E[a | x, detected].
  • Replication dosage. Real replicons have an ori → ter gene-dosage gradient (up to ~1–2 log2 in fast growth) that giapsim does not model; circular shifts move the region along it, so HL partly measures position. Report HL as "relative to random positions on this replicon", not as a region-specific regulatory effect.
  • Plasmid copy number cancels exactly (within-replicon comparisons): results are bitwise identical for plasmid_copy_log2 0 and log2 20 on the same seed (3 seeds checked), so attack 4 holds by construction and is best tested as an invariance, not a calibration stream.
  • TU labels enter only the CIs (amendment 2). V is built from gene-index lags, so TU-label errors cannot move the HL p (attack A-TU at level). The TU-block bootstrap still uses the labels, so labels that fragment a region's operons narrow that region's CI; the p is unaffected.
  • V ≤ 0 (decision 16). The truncated γ is not always positive definite. In 60,000+ chromosome HL rows (ρ up to 0.95, ori–ter cosine up to 2 log2) it never happened; on the 60-gene plasmid at ρ ≥ 0.9 it hits 0.15–0.35 % of rows (lags up to 30 cover half the replicon). Those rows lose their HL p, but level is unaffected: under exhaustive shifts the flag is a function of the whole shift orbit, so the same rows would be NA whichever orbit member was observed.

docs.title: Replicon-level effects (plasmids, M4-18)
docs.text:
Plasmids are not tested (§7.3.5(b), §8.5 attack 4). A plasmid region is the whole replicon, so no circular shift moves it, and its contrast with the chromosome mixes gene dosage (copy number) with regulation: nothing in proteomics data separates the two. Each plasmid_* region gets two rows with p_value = q_value = NA, null_model = none, n_perm = 0, method = replicon_contrast, label = dosage_plus_regulation:

  • o_minus_e: the plasmid's own O − E over its eligible genes (E = Σ p_detect, which already carries the detectability model; lead decision 1). No chromosome-rate row.
  • hl_shift: HL of the plasmid's raw log2 abundance against the reference replicons (lead decision 2). Not M4-17's per-replicon residuals: those centre every replicon and give HL ≈ 0 whatever the dosage. Only detected, eligible genes with an observed value enter; imputed genes are excluded on both sides, because the genome-wide median fill (docs/methods/abundance.md) places imputed plasmid genes at the chromosome median and pulls the contrast towards 0.
  • Reference (lead decision 3): the kind = chromosome replicons; without one (draft genomes) every replicon that is neither kind = plasmid nor a plasmid region's contig, flag no_reference_replicon (HL NA with the same flag if that set has no usable gene).
  • CIs: 95 % TU-block bootstrap; for HL with strata plasmid / reference, so every replicate has both sides. Each plasmid draws from its own child stream keyed by its region_id (lead decision 7), so adding a plasmid changes no other row.
  • Fewer than SMALL_REGION (3) eligible genes: every statistic NA, flag small_region.

Depth offset. With --replicon-depth (§5.3), an extra hl_shift row (label = dosage_adjusted, flag depth_adjusted) reports HL − log2(plasmid depth / reference depth), the reference depth being the length-weighted mean over the same reference replicons. Depth is treated as known: the CI is the HL CI shifted by the same constant, so it omits the uncertainty of the depth ratio (deferred, docs/backlog.md). The row is omitted, with a warning from the step, when the plasmid or a reference replicon has no depth, or when HL is NA.

What the HL CI covers (statistician review of PR #110; lead decisions 15 and 16). The estimand is the realised dosage-plus-regulation shift of this plasmid against the reference replicons. The TU-block CI covers it conservatively: 0.997–1.000 for ρ = 0–0.8, with detection from covariates or from abundance (Slurm 1860197, 1860273). It is not a CI for the copy number alone. The plasmid's own TU-level expression adds sd ≈ 0.75 log2 around log2(dosage) at ρ = 0.5 (1.7 at ρ = 0.8), and one genome cannot separate that from dosage. This is why the row is labelled dosage_plus_regulation. It is also why the CI covers log2(20) only 0.80 of the time at ρ = 0.5 (0.58 at ρ = 0.8). No resampling scheme fixes this: circular-block bootstraps reach only 0.85 / 0.71, and a lag-V Wald interval 0.87 / 0.81, which at ρ = 0 is worse than the current CI. The dosage_adjusted row estimates the plasmid's realised regulation under the same conditional reading. Coverage of log2(copy number) is not a gate. The nightly diagnostic test_recorded_plasmid_hl_bias_and_ci_coverage records both coverages and warns when coverage of the realised shift falls below 0.93.

Setup: M4-17 calibration layout, 1,000 chromosome genes, a 60-gene plasmid (median 34 TUs) at log2(20) copies, p = p_detect_true, B = 1,000. Coverage SE ≈ 0.013 at R = 1,000 and 0.02–0.03 at R = 300.

Coverage of log2(20) (Slurm 1860197):

scenario R mean HL − log2 20 (MC SE) sd TU-block (implemented) circular block, L = 2 / 3 / 4 / 6 / auto lag-V Wald ρ = 0.5 (attack default) 1000 +0.006 (0.026) 0.82 0.801 0.836 / 0.849 / 0.849 / 0.847 / 0.852 0.867 ρ = 0 300 +0.078 (0.029) 0.50 0.933 0.923 / 0.917 / 0.913 / 0.893 / 0.907 0.897 ρ = 0.8 300 −0.017 (0.098) 1.70 0.583 0.653 / 0.687 / 0.703 / 0.733 / 0.713 0.807 ρ = 0.5, detection ~ abundance 300 −0.087 (0.049) 0.86 0.843 0.847 / 0.860 / 0.860 / 0.870 / 0.870 0.880

Coverage of the realised shift on the same seeds (Slurm 1860273). T_all is the HL of the true abundance over all eligible plasmid genes against the chromosome's (dosage + regulation, without gene noise or detection). T_tu is log2(20) plus the plasmid-minus-chromosome difference in mean TU-level AR values:

scenario sd(T_all − log2 20) HL − T_all, mean (sd) CI covers T_all CI covers T_tu ρ = 0.5 0.75 +0.004 (0.30) 1.000 0.989 ρ = 0 0.42 +0.009 (0.26) 0.997 0.993 ρ = 0.8 1.70 −0.009 (0.39) 0.997 0.983 detection ~ abundance 0.79 +0.022 (0.33) 0.997 0.987

Selection bias at the null (recorded, not gated). The HL compares detected genes only. When detection depends on abundance, each replicon loses its low-abundance genes, and the two replicons lose different shares, so the raw contrast can be biased at the true dosage. The bias is small. With abundance-driven detection (detection = "abundance", default slope, ρ = 0.5, R = 300), the mean HL − log2(20) is −0.087 log2 (MC SE 0.049), and the mean HL − T_all is +0.022. Its sign depends on the detection slope and on how much of each replicon drops out. Under covariate-only detection the bias is +0.006 (SE 0.026). The result is an effect estimate, never a test.

docs.title: Descriptive rows (prophage subsets, M4-18)
docs.text:
Per prophage and §7.1.7 function subset present in C8 (integrase, repressor, structural, lysis, cargo): subset = the name, stat = o_minus_e, observed = detected eligible members, expected = Σ p_detect, o_minus_e (= effect), o_over_e (NA when E = 0). method = label = descriptive, flag descriptive, CI, p and q NA, null_model = none. Subsets are small (often one to a few genes) and nested in the tested prophage; they are not tested in version 1. Fewer than 3 eligible genes add small_region; 0 eligible genes give NA statistics.

Table rules. M4-17 rows enter with subset = all and the detection columns of both stat rows (observed, expected, o_minus_e, o_over_e, hl_shift_log2), q-values copied (BH is never recomputed). Every row satisfies null_model = none ⇒ p, q NA and n_perm = 0; a p-value ⇒ null_model ≠ none; a q-value ⇒ a p-value (checked by the assembler).

docs.title: Statistician sign-off
docs.text:
Statistician (M4-17 review, PR #89): signed 2026-10-16 (review round 4 below). Rounds 1–3 (2026-10-15, changes requested) are kept for the record.

  • C1 crispr/hl_shift fast confirmed fail: chance. 20,000 null replicates of the fast scenario (Slurm 1849136; same layout, ρ = 0.5, p = p_detect_true) give 0.0083 / 0.048 / 0.096 for that check and 0.0083–0.0103 / 0.045–0.052 / 0.096–0.102 for every chromosome check; 10,000 without origin crossing 0.0080–0.0112 / 0.046–0.055 / 0.087–0.108. Per stream the two-block false alarm is 0.0063 at α = 0.01, R = 100 (fail iff ≥ 3 rejections in both blocks). Seeds are fixed, so the fail repeats until the claim is restructured; no seed change and no tolerance change.
  • False-alarm cost as drafted: ≈ 0.13 per fast run (21 level streams: C1 10, A4 10, A2 1) and ≈ 0.09 per nightly run, against ≈ 0.04 for the whole nightly (ADR-0015). Restructured: C1 one pooled level stream per statistic over the four chromosome types (check_level_pooled, m = 4; rejection indicators of different region types correlate ≤ 0.06 over 20,000 replicates), plasmid AMR at α ∈ {0.05, 0.10} only (K = 59: p ≤ 0.01 is unattainable), O − E at one ρ in full mode (O − E does not depend on ρ under covariate-only detection), A4 as a deterministic invariance test: ≈ 0.018 fast and ≈ 0.017 nightly.
  • Blocking: limitations (i) and (ii) are attack-2 failures (§8.5: a failing attack blocks the merge); the A2 gate errors until M4-13 (#83) is merged (not marked xfail as lead decision 4 allows).

docs.title: Review round 2 (statistician, 2026-10-15): A2-HL root cause and recommendation
docs.text:
Scripts and outputs: local/scratch/review-m4-17/v2/ (exp2–exp5.py, an.py; Slurm 1849806, 1849807, 1849809, 1849826, 1849914; attack test run 1849915). All rates are prophage hl_shift rejection shares at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10, exhaustive circular shifts, ρ = 0.5, β_abundance = 0.5 unless stated.

  1. Decision 10 as implemented fixes the location bias. Mean residualised HL over replicates: −0.07 to −0.09 log2 (raw +0.74). Fit-set, pooling and imputation variants do not matter: pooled chr1 + p1 fit equals per-replicon to ±0.003; adding (log length)² or a cubic in a fitted logistic detectability index (or in the true index) changes rates by ≤ 0.04. The oracle residual a − E[a | true covariate index, detected] (exact under the simulator, Gauss–Hermite) still rejects 0.053 / 0.131 / 0.199. So no covariate adjustment can pass this attack.
  2. Cause: detected-count heterogeneity (limitation (iii)). A2-HL-MAR (short prophage, detection from covariates only, so no selection on abundance): plain HL 0.058 / 0.147 / 0.225 (1,000 genes, R = 2,000) and 0.062 / 0.151 / 0.229 (4,500 genes, R = 1,000). Residualised: 0.051 / 0.131 / 0.207 and 0.063 / 0.152 / 0.227. β_abundance = 1 detects more prophage genes (10 versus 7) and fails less (0.012 / 0.074 / 0.139).
  3. Fix (recommendation (c)): a TU-cluster-studentised HL test statistic, which parallels ADR-0018 decision 2. Keep decision 10's residualisation, gene-index circular shifts, and HL as the reported effect with its CI. The p-value comes from T = HL / √V, recomputed at every shift. V = σ_u²(Σ_t m_t²/m² + Σ_t m′_t²/m′²) + σ_e²(1/m + 1/m′), where:
  4. m_t and m′_t are the detected genes with finite ã in TU t, inside and outside the set;
  5. m and m′ are their totals;
  6. σ_u² (between-TU) and σ_e² (within-TU) are one-way ANOVA moment estimates on the replicon's residualised detected genes, computed once per replicon, with σ_u² truncated at 0. Level (prophage HL, 1,000 genes / 4,500 genes):
  7. A2-HL β 0.5: 0.005 / 0.019 / 0.046 (R = 4,000) and 0.003 / 0.021 / 0.047 (R = 2,000).
  8. A2-HL β 1.0: 0.001 / 0.014 / 0.045 (1,000 genes, R = 1,000).
  9. A2-HL-MAR: 0.003 / 0.016 / 0.038 and 0.001 / 0.014 / 0.037.
  10. A2-mid: 0.004 / 0.025 / 0.052 (1,000 genes, R = 2,000).
  11. C1 pooled over the 4 chromosome types: 0.010 / 0.045 / 0.092 (R = 4,000) and 0.009 / 0.048 / 0.099 (R = 1,000).
  12. C1 plasmid AMR (p1, R = 2,000): 0.000 / 0.043 / 0.095.
  13. Under the attack it is conservative because AR(1) between TUs is not modelled. Power without confounding (prophage +1 log2, R = 500) at α 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10:
  14. TU-studentised: 0.058 / 0.166 / 0.252.
  15. plain HL: 0.048 / 0.156 / 0.246. With confounding (short prophage + abundance detection, +1 log2), TU-studentised gives 0.010 / 0.070 / 0.134 against plain HL's invalid 0.056 / 0.182 / 0.258.

Alternatives tested, all at level: - shifting the region's detected genes within the detected-only gene sequence: 0.004 / 0.019 / 0.044. This changes the spec's null. - scaling by √(m m′/M): 0.002 / 0.010 / 0.028. - Wilcoxon z: 0.001 / 0.009 / 0.026.

Both scaling and Wilcoxon z are over-conservative because they ignore TU clustering. Decision 10 itself needs no amendment. Option (b) is not needed: the attack is claimable once the statistic is studentised. 4. O − E re-check. The studentised O − E statistic passes: - A2-mid (1,000 genes, p = truth, R = 6,000): 0.009 / 0.050 / 0.103, which confirms α = 0.01. - A2-HL data: 0.012 / 0.054 / 0.101 (R = 4,000). - A2-MAR data: 0.008 / 0.051 / 0.104. 5. C1 pooled family. BH within (type, stat) and pooled level per statistic over the 4 chromosome types: - O − E: 0.010 / 0.048 / 0.101 (1,000 genes, R = 4,000) and 0.009 / 0.047 / 0.099 (4,500 genes). - HL (decision 10): 0.008 / 0.045 / 0.094 and 0.010 / 0.049 / 0.099.

All are within the bounds (R = 4,000: 0.0131 / 0.0569 / 0.1095). A single unpooled cell reached 0.072 at α 0.05 (4,500 genes, AMR O − E, R = 1,000; bound 0.064), but an independent seed for the same cell gives 0.052. This is chance, so the pooled restructure stands. 6. New attack null test_a2_short_prophage_hl_at_level_without_abundance_selection (tests/calibration/attacks). It runs the A2-low data with HL and must stay at level. The current code is a confirmed fail in fast mode (Slurm 1849915), as is A2-HL.

Sign-off state: changes requested (blocking). Merge needs the studentised HL statistic (item 3), with A2-HL and A2-HL-MAR passing. This changes the §7.3.5(b) HL test, so it needs an ADR-0018 amendment (decision 4) accepted by Khoa.

docs.title: Review round 3 (statistician, 2026-10-15): studentised HL implementation (dd663c0)
docs.text:
Scripts and outputs: local/scratch/review-m4-17/v3/ (cmp.py, tumis.py, tusplit.py, lagv.py, an.py; Slurm 1850322, 1850439, 1850446, 1850492). Rates are rejection shares at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10, 1,000 genes, ρ = 0.5, exhaustive circular shifts. Bounds at R = 2,000: 0.0144 / 0.0597 / 0.1134.

  1. Formula: matches the reference. tu_variance_components, hl_variance and studentised_hl_null were checked against the round-2 reference (exp5.py tus_) on the same seeds: 114 replicates, 455 regions (A2-HL at 1,000 and 4,500 genes, control, A2-MAR). max |ΔT| = 1.8e-15 over every shift, identical p, identical σ_u² and σ_e² (to 1e-12). The observed T (shift 0) is computed by the same path.
  2. Decision-12 guard: does not hide real regions. It acts on the replicon's σ_u² + σ_e², not on a region's V. With log2 abundances of ~20–30 it triggers only below a residual SD of ~3e-6 log2. Real proteomics quantification is coarser than that by orders of magnitude, so only (numerically) constant residuals reach it. Typical values: σ_u² ≈ 4.0, σ_e² ≈ 0.87, threshold 7.5e-12. A small V caused by a large region never reaches the guard. σ_u² = σ_e² = 0 needs SSE = SSB = 0, i.e. constant data (all-singleton TUs give σ_e² = 0 but σ_u² > 0).
  3. Missing-TU rule: anti-conservative (change requested). A gene without a TU label becomes its own TU. When the missing labels sit in the tested region, the region's V is too small, because its genes are still correlated. Region labels missing:
  4. control: prophage 0.034 / 0.118 / 0.184, BGC 0.040 / 0.114 / 0.191, CRISPR 0.026 / 0.101 / 0.159;
  5. A2-HL and A2-MAR: BGC 0.108–0.111 at α 0.05.

All labels missing stays at level (0.009 / 0.048 / 0.102). C6 makes tu_id non-null, and M4-13 and tu_block_bootstrap refuse NA TU IDs. Either refuse missing labels with a ValueError, or ignore labels on the whole replicon when any indexed gene lacks one. Attack test test_atu_missing_region_tu_labels_do_not_change_the_hl_p accepts either fix and fails on dd663c0. 4. New weakness: region-specific TU fragmentation (attack A-TU). The data are the control, with no region effect. Each region TU on chr1 is cut into 2-gene chunks; the TUs outside the regions are left whole. HL then rejects: - prophage 0.017 / 0.082 / 0.143, BGC 0.020 / 0.080 / 0.144, CRISPR 0.015 / 0.071 / 0.124; - for comparison, true labels give 0.010 / 0.051 / 0.097 and the same cut genome-wide gives 0.008 / 0.049 / 0.104 (R = 2,000).

Over-merging (adjacent TUs merged in pairs) is conservative. An operon predictor that splits prophage or BGC operons more than core operons (different intergenic spacing) would do this. Gate: test_atu_region_specific_tu_fragmentation_hl_at_level, pooled m = 4 as C1, fast and full. Slurm 1850492, fast (R = 100, pooled): 0.015 at α 0.01 (pass); 0.080 then 0.055 at 0.05 and 0.133 then 0.120 at 0.10 (unconfirmed: R = 100 is too small to confirm a rate near 0.08). Full (4,500 genes, R = 1,000 per block, pooled m = 4): confirmed fail at every α, 0.019 / 0.019, 0.071 / 0.072 and 0.130 / 0.126 against bounds 0.0131 / 0.0569 / 0.1095. The full stream costs ≈ 46 min per block on one core. A label-free fix exists (prototype lagv.py). It keeps T = HL/√V but builds V from positions instead of labels: - V = Var(mean_in − mean_out) = Σ_{in,in} γ/m² + Σ_{out,out} γ/m′² − 2 Σ_{in,out} γ/(m m′); - γ(h) is the replicon's autocovariance of residualised detected abundances at circular gene-index lag h, estimated once per replicon, h ≤ 30, truncated at its first non-positive value. - Results:

 | Scenario (R) | Lag V | Raw HL | TU-label V |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Control (2,000) | 0.008–0.010 / 0.049–0.057 / 0.097–0.104 | | |
 | Control, ρ = 0.9 (1,000) | 0.006–0.012 / 0.043–0.052 / 0.087–0.110 | | |
 | A2-HL (2,000) | 0.009 / 0.032 / 0.074 | 0.034 / 0.109 / 0.178 | |
 | A2-MAR (2,000) | 0.010 / 0.045 / 0.087 | 0.061 / 0.136 / 0.216 | |
 | Power, prophage +1 log2, α 0.05 (500) | 0.172 | 0.168 | 0.178 |
  • It is immune to TU-label errors by construction. Its cost is the same order as hl_variance (pairwise distances inside the set).
  • It is a change to amendment 1, so it needs an ADR-0018 amendment 2 accepted by Khoa.
  • Calibration log ("null_fast crispr hl_shift 0.03 at α 0.01: fail"). The record is stale and is not a gating error. local/logs/calibration/regions.jsonl is append-only and holds every run since 09:44. Lines 47–51 and 115–119 are the pre-pooling runs (Slurm 1849058 era, round 1). Jobs 1850200 and 1850201 wrote lines 495–726. They hold no per-type null_fast record, only chr1_pooled, and every check there is pass or unconfirmed. Records carry no run ID, commit or timestamp, so runs cannot be told apart. Harness follow-up for the backlog: add git_head and slurm_job / ts to every record, or write one file per run. The gating needs no fix. Separately, jobs 1850199–1850201 logged head 5a7da49 with the implementation uncommitted; dd663c0 was committed 1 min after 1850201 ended. The numbers stand only if the tree equals dd663c0.
  • False-alarm budget, final gate set (ADR-0015 two-block rule; per-check probability P(block fails)²):
  • Fast: C1 (2 pooled streams × 3 α, plus plasmid AMR 2 × 2 α) 0.010; A2 (4 streams × 3 α) 0.006 at the measured rates (0.030 if every A2 stream sat at its nominal level); total ≈ 0.016.
  • Nightly: C1 (4 pooled + 4 AMR streams) 0.014; A2 0.004–0.009; total ≈ 0.018–0.023.
  • The two A-TU streams add ≤ 0.003 once they pass.

Acceptable against ≈ 0.04 for the whole nightly. A2-mid O − E at α 0.01, R = 100, is the largest single term (0.006, near nominal). No change. 7. Notes: the bootstrap/V inconsistency for missing TU labels (CIs section) goes away with fix 3. Effect and CI are unchanged from round 2 (the HL point estimate on the residual scale).

Sign-off state: changes requested (blocking). - (a) Missing-TU rule: item 3, a small code change, gated by the deterministic attack test. - (b) A-TU: item 4. Either ADR-0018 amendment 2 (label-free lag V, the prototype passes every scenario above), or an explicit waiver by Khoa that keeps A-TU as a documented limitation and marks it xfail with that reason.

Everything else is signed: formula, guard, C1, A2-HL, A2-HL-MAR, A2-mid, A2-low, the A4 invariance, FDR families and the false-alarm budget.

docs.title: Review round 4 (statistician, 2026-10-16): label-free lag V (04fc8f7, 651cf9c) — signed
docs.text:
Scripts and outputs: local/scratch/review-m4-17/v4/ (rev.py, an.py; Slurm 1851233, 1851234 for the side runs, 1851283 / 1851284 for the A-LIN gate). Rates at α = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10, 1,000 genes.

  1. Code equals the v3 reference on the same seeds. lag_autocovariance, hl_variance and studentised_hl_null against lagv.py (round-3 seeds, chr1, every shift): 7,000 replicates, 27,909 regions (control ρ 0.5 and 0.9, A2-HL, A2-MAR); max |Δγ| 1.1e-14, max relative |ΔT| 6.6e-16, identical NaN pattern, identical p in every row (round-3 p reproduced). The prototype double-counts lag n/2 on an even replicon of ≤ 60 genes; the implementation counts it once (correct). Linear γ and V match a naive in-sequence-pair oracle to 7e-15 (400 random replicons, 5–90 genes, every non-wrapping shift).
  2. Linear replicons (decision 16, not in v3): at level. Every replicon set to linear (rates among rows with a p; regions crossing the origin get K = 0 by design): ρ 0.5 HL 0.0084 / 0.0496 / 0.0985 and O − E 0.0084 / 0.046 / 0.098 (R = 4,000 × 4 types); ρ 0.9 HL 0.0089 / 0.0488 / 0.0957; A2-HL 0.0108 / 0.0465 / 0.0968; A2-MAR 0.0076 / 0.0465 / 0.0978; 4,500 genes 0.0057 / 0.0456 / 0.0937 (R = 400). The linear 60-gene plasmid is conservative (K ≈ 14). New gate A-LIN (test_alin_linear_replicon_hl_at_level, fast and full; no origin crossing, ρ = 0.9, HL pooled over prophage / BGC / CRISPR, m = 3; the scattered AMR set can span a linear chromosome, K = 0). Fast 0.0133 / 0.070 / 0.097 (bounds 0.0215 / 0.0752 / 0.1346), pass; full (4,500 genes, R = 1,000, Slurm 1851308) 0.0083 / 0.0453 / 0.0993 (bounds 0.0136 / 0.0580 / 0.1110), pass; ≈ 57 min per block on one core (shard it in the nightly).
  3. V ≤ 0 → NA (decision 16): accepted. Chromosome: 0 of ~60,000 HL rows (circular ρ 0.9 and 0.95, R = 4,000 / 2,000; ori–ter cosine of amplitude 1 and 2 log2 at ρ 0.5 / 0.9). 60-gene plasmid: 6 / 4,000 at ρ 0.9, 7 / 2,000 at ρ 0.95, 2 / 2,000 linear ρ 0.9, 0–1 elsewhere — so the implementer's 3 / 59,000 are small-replicon rows. No bias: with exhaustive shifts the flag is decided on the observed set plus every shift, i.e. on the whole orbit, so it is the same whatever orbit member was observed and the p of the remaining rows stays exact (rates among non-NA rows are at level in every scenario above). The cost is lost HL p on a few small replicons at high autocorrelation; fail-closed is right (a silent fallback would need its own calibration).
  4. Dosage gradient (limitation "Replication dosage"). With a random region position, an ori–ter cosine leaves level intact (1 log2: 0.0097 / 0.049 / 0.102 at ρ 0.5, 0.0106 / 0.049 / 0.092 at ρ 0.9; 2 log2 at ρ 0.9: 0.0105 / 0.052 / 0.100; R = 2,000 / 1,000 × 4 types) and creates no V ≤ 0. The limitation (HL partly measures position) stands as written.
  5. A-TU 0.0525 at α 0.05 (bound 0.0569, n = 4,000 pooled): at level. z = 0.7 against 0.05; the same statistic on the unfragmented control gives 0.0516 (R = 2,000 × 4) and 0.046–0.049 at ρ 0.9. A-TU and the control cannot differ for the lag V (labels do not enter it); the gap to round 3 (0.071) is the fix, not chance.
  6. Fast "unconfirmed" cells: chance, no action. C1 pooled HL α 0.01: 8 / 400 then 7 / 400 (bound 7.98 / 400) against full 0.0085 (n = 4,000) and 0.009–0.010 here (n ≈ 28,000). A2-mid O − E α 0.01: 3 / 100 then 2 / 100 against full 0.005 and round-2 0.009 (R = 6,000). Seeds are fixed, so both cells will keep reporting "unconfirmed" (not a failure) until the replicate streams change.
  7. False-alarm budget, final gate set (two-block rule, P(block fails)², every stream at nominal level except A2-mid / A2-low O − E at their measured conservative rates): fast ≈ 0.034 (C1 0.008, plasmid AMR 0.002, A2 0.016, A-TU + A-LIN 0.008), nightly ≈ 0.023 (C1 0.008, AMR 0.006, A2 0.005, A-TU + A-LIN 0.004). Up from round 3 (0.016 / 0.018–0.023) because A2-HL and A2-MAR are no longer conservative under the lag V; nightly is within ≈ 0.04 (ADR-0015). The largest terms are single R = 100 streams at α 0.01 (0.0063 each); backlog suggestion, not a condition: pool A2-HL and A2-HL-MAR at α 0.01 in fast mode.
  8. Families and outputs (§8.1). Unchanged: BH within (region_type, stat); every row with a p has a q, an effect and a TU-block 95 % CI on the same scale; NA p (K = 0, empty HL side, V ≤ 0) gets NA q and stays out of BH.

Sign-off state: signed. ADR-0018 amendment 2 and decisions 13–16 are implemented as specified; every C1, A2, A4, A-TU and A-LIN gate passes. Rounds 1–3 conditions are all met.

docs.title: Sensitivity analysis: stability of flagged sets under analysis choices
docs.text: Implements giap.context.sensitivity and giap.steps.sensitivity (GIAP_SPEC.md §8.6, §2.4 G9, §7.3.2, §5.2; issue M4-19, docs/specs/M4-19-sensitivity-regions.md, lead decisions 1–18).

docs.title: Variants
docs.text:
output.sensitivity = off runs nothing and writes no sensitivity.tsv. basic reruns under missing=<p> for each policy in abundance.sensitivity other than the primary abundance.missing, and, under the two_peptide tier, single_peptide_detected. full adds top3 (unless abundance.method is already top3; skipped with a log line when the gene table has no Top3 values, i.e. no peptide intensities). UniOP thresholds are M6's family and are not run here.

A variant's gene table is built from the primary one:

  • missing=<p>: the values the primary imputed are reset to missing and M4-14 impute is rerun with policy p on the observed log2 abundances of the detected non-partial genes. Detection and p_detect are the primary's, so O − E statistics are unchanged; only abundance-based ones move.
  • top3: the same imputation applied to top3_log2 instead of the iBAQ values.
  • single_peptide_detected: genes with status single_peptide_unestimated count as detected. M4-14 keeps observed abundances on undetected genes, so these genes enter HL with their observed one-peptide abundance (noisier than a multi-peptide value); the primary policy fills only those with no intensity at all. p_detect is refitted (M4-13) on the new calls with the primary's generator for_step("detectability", seed), so the TU folds are the primary's and only the detection calls differ. The primary is never refitted.

docs.title: Permutations and common random numbers
docs.text:
Every rerun uses B = 199 (stats.permutations), and the primary flagged set is recomputed at the same B, so differences do not come from Monte Carlo error at different B. All calls of a family (primary and every variant) start from one generator state, for_step("sensitivity/<family>", seed); adding a family or a variant changes no other family's draws.

These common random numbers matter only when shifts are sampled:

  • Up to context.exhaustive_shift_max_genes (20,000) genes per replicon, which covers every bacterial replicon, the region tests use all shifts. The flagged sets then use no randomness at all (the generator feeds only the bootstrap CIs, which the flagged sets ignore), so every difference between primary and variant comes from the variant.
  • Above 20,000 genes the shift sample (choose_shifts) and both TU-block bootstrap CIs of every region are drawn from the one family stream, in region order, and the HL bootstrap runs only when HL is finite. Once one region's data differ between primary and variant, every later region's draws differ, so the common random numbers hold only up to that region. Differences then include Monte Carlo error. In the statistician's probe (giapsim fixture with sampled shifts; the variant changed one region's abundances), the O − E p of unchanged regions moved by up to 0.075. A per-region shift stream in M4-17 test_region would remove this (backlog).

For the regions family the flagged set is the IDs <region_id>:<contig>:<stat> of the M4-17 tests with null_model = circular_shift, a p-value, and q ≤ alpha.context (a split_contigs region gives one ID per contig). With context.exhaustive_shift_max_genes = 20000, every replicon of up to 20,000 genes uses all shifts, so the recomputed primary equals the set reported in regions_stats.tsv. Above 20,000 genes the shifts are sampled, the p-value floor is 1/200 = 0.005, and n_primary may differ from the count in regions_stats.tsv.

docs.title: Islands
docs.text:
For the islands family (M5-10) the flagged set is <direction>:<locus_tag> for every gene of every island that M5-06 reports (an island is reported only when its FWER p ≤ alpha.context). The genes are the island's best-window gene list (M5-06 Q3), so a change in how clusters merge shows up as a changed set. The direction is part of the ID: a gene that moves from a high to a low island counts as a change, and a gene in both a high and a low island gives two IDs. The family reruns the M5-06 pipeline (tu_series per C1 replicon on the C5 TUs, then scan_replicons and islands_frame) with both stats.bootstrap and stats.permutations set to 199 for the primary and every variant (the regions family keeps the user's stats.bootstrap). All calls start from the one family stream for_step("sensitivity/islands", seed). The FWER null is a block bootstrap, so the islands sets always use randomness. With B = 199 the smallest attainable p is 1/200 = 0.005.

The recomputed primary is an independent Monte Carlo realisation, not islands.tsv at a coarser p floor. It uses its own stream and B = 199 for both the block bootstrap and the l-hat test, so an island with p near alpha.context can differ from islands.tsv in either direction, not only through the 0.005 floor.

Common random numbers hold only in part. scan_replicons draws the l-hat permutations of every scanned replicon before any bootstrap draw, and how many it draws depends on each replicon's number of scored TUs T. A variant that changes T, or whether a replicon is scanned, anywhere in the genome therefore changes the bootstrap draws of every replicon, including earlier ones. A change of the block length l' at replicon r changes the draws of r and of later replicons only. The triggers are missing=exclude (a TU losing every scored gene, since detected genes without an abundance are not scored, M5-06 step 1) and the single_peptide_detected refit of p_detect. With context.islands.block_len fixed, only T matters. When the draws differ, the set difference includes Monte Carlo error (see Interpretation).

docs.title: Enriched categories
docs.text:
For the enriched_categories family (M8-16) the flagged set is the IDs <collection>:<term>:<kind> of every row with q ≤ stats.alpha.enrichment (0.05). The kind is one of: - gsea: M8-05 abundance GSEA, BH per collection; - ora_over or ora_under: M8-04 detection ORA, BH per ontology and direction (§8.1).

Rows flagged redundant, genomic_cluster or detection_confounded count like any other row. A gsea ID has no direction, so a set whose ES changes sign under a variant still counts as shared.

The collections are built once from the primary gene table, and every run reuses them. The ORA uses the primary's TU folds (tu_folds) when they are given, as the function step does. ORA p-values are analytical (Wallenius), so the ORA IDs change only when the detection calls change, i.e. under single_peptide_detected. Under missing=<p> and top3 they equal the primary's by construction.

GSEA is rerun under every variant (missing=<p>, top3, single_peptide_detected). It goes through R fgsea (fgseaMultilevel, ADR-0038) at n_perm_simple = 199, sample_size = 101 and eps = 0, whatever function.gsea says. Each variant makes its own R calls, so the step needs the giap-fgsea env.

The family is skipped, with the event sensitivity.enriched_categories_skipped, when function is not in modules or no function resource is given. It then writes no rows.

Permutation depth. With eps = 0 the multilevel stage estimates p with no 1/(1 + B) floor. A row can reach q ≤ 0.05 only with p ≤ 0.05·k/m. fgsea refines such small p-values in the multilevel stage, whose precision depends on sample_size and not on n_perm_simple. A p above 0.05 cannot lower any BH q to 0.05 or below. So 199 simple permutations hardly change which rows are flagged.

In the statistician's probe (PR #265 review, Slurm 1876268), the design was: - 1,000 TUs; - 150 sets of 15 TUs, 15 of them shifted; - 20 sets of 40 TUs, 4 of them shifted; - 6 worlds × 21 streams on identical data.

The mean pairwise Jaccard between streams was the same at n_perm_simple 199 and 1,000 in 4 of 6 worlds, and within 0.03 in the other two.

Monte Carlo noise. The flagged set still varies between streams. A set near the BH cut can flip, and one flip moves the cut for the whole collection. In the same probe, two streams on identical data gave different sets in 26–72 % of pairs, and the mean pairwise Jaccard per world was 0.57–0.90.

The recomputed primary uses for_step("sensitivity/enriched_categories", seed) at B = 199. It is therefore an independent realisation, not the set in enrichment_gsea.tsv (stream function.gsea, n_perm_simple 1,000), and n_primary can differ from that table's count.

Common random numbers hold only while a variant ranks the same number of TUs: the tie order, the R seed and fgsea's sampled index sets are then the same. This holds for missing=min, because imputed genes stay ranked. It fails for: - missing=exclude, when a TU loses all its scoring genes; - top3 and single_peptide_detected, when a TU enters or leaves the ranking.

The GSEA differences of those variants include Monte Carlo noise of the size above.

docs.title: Determinants
docs.text:
For the determinants family (M8-16; §8.6 "the determinants CV R² (without its permutation null)") each run repeats the M8-10 chain without its TU-permutation null: - model rows: detected genes with a finite, non-imputed log2 abundance, ribosomal proteins excluded (M8-08 rule 1); - outer GroupKFold(5) TU folds, determinants.repeats repeats; - LightGBM and elastic-net CV; - LightGBM SHAP summed by block; - the attribution table.

Features come from determinants_features.tsv. detected, abundance_log2 and abundance_imputed come from the run's gene table. The folds are drawn from for_step("sensitivity/determinants", seed), and LightGBM is seeded with seed. The recomputed primary is therefore an independent realisation of the fold assignment, not determinants_attribution.tsv (stream determinants.cv).

  • Set. The flagged set is the locus tags flagged abundance_not_explained_by_sequence: model rows whose out-of-fold residual is more than 2 SD from 0. The test is two-sided, uses the run's own residual SD, and flags about 4 % of model rows. A variant that changes the CV R² moves the threshold for every gene. This set is a reversible default (M8-16 Q2) because §8.6 does not define the determinants set.
  • Agreement. A gene is explained in a run when it is a model row and is not flagged abundance_not_explained_by_sequence in that run. "Explained" means only "not flagged at 2 residual SD": it is not a claim that the features predict the gene well. Its block is the block with the largest absolute LightGBM SHAP sum (ties go to the first block in the order transcription, translation, codon, protein, context); it is None when every block sum is 0. The absolute value matters: for a gene predicted below the mean, the block that drives the prediction carries a large negative sum, and M8-08 rule 3 (the largest positive sum) would pick whichever noise block happens to sit just above 0. Under rule 3, agreement floored at about 0.7 whether or not the features carried signal (PR #299 review). agreement is computed over the genes explained in both runs: a gene flagged in either run is left out, and so is a gene whose block is None in both runs. A gene that is a model row in only one run is left out too. This matters for single_peptide_detected and top3, which move genes in or out of the model rows; those genes never enter the denominator. agreement is the share of the remaining genes whose block is the same. A gene with a block in one run and None in the other counts as a disagreement. agreement is NA when no such gene remains. A run compared with itself gives 1 (NA if none of its explained genes has a block). This follows Khoa's decisions of 2026-10-24 (M8-16 lead decision 6, option (a)); before them, agreement covered the top decile only and used rule 3. determinants_attribution.tsv is unchanged: its dominant_block keeps rule 3 and is still reported for the top-decile genes only.
  • Denominator. The number of genes behind each variant's agreement (n_agreement) goes to the event sensitivity.determinants_cv_r2, next to the CV R². §8.6 has no column for it.
  • CV R². The mean LightGBM CV R² of the primary and of every variant goes to the event sensitivity.determinants_cv_r2 (data.cv_r2; data.n_agreement holds the denominators). §8.6 has no R² column, and the manifest's sensitivity block is built from sensitivity.tsv only, so the event is the one record of both.
  • Minimum. A run with fewer than 100 model rows or 25 TUs is not fitted (M8-10 rule 8). If the primary is below the minimum, the family writes no rows and emits sensitivity.determinants_skipped. If a variant is below it, that variant has no row.

What the variants can change. Model rows exclude imputed values. So missing=min and missing=exclude keep the model rows, the TU list, the folds and the LightGBM seed of the primary. Their rows are exact copies of the primary (jaccard 1, or NA when nothing is flagged; agreement 1) and say nothing about robustness. Only two variants can change the determinants rows: - single_peptide_detected, which adds the single-peptide genes, with their one-peptide abundance, as model rows; - top3 under full, which changes every abundance and can move genes in or out of the model rows.

Noise. A variant that changes the model rows also changes the TU list. tu_folds then reassigns the folds, so common random numbers are lost, and the difference includes fold-assignment noise.

Fold-noise reference. The determinants calibration test (tests/calibration/test_determinants_agreement_calibration.py; PR #299 review) reruns planted worlds of 400 genes (log2 abundance = signal × CAI + noise) under fold streams 1–5 against stream 0 on identical data, so only the fold assignment differs: - with negligible signal (mean LightGBM CV R² 0.01–0.08), agreement was 0.73–0.86; - with strong signal (CV R² about 0.55–0.59), it was 0.89–0.99.

On every world, each strong-signal pair beat each no-signal pair; the test gates that separation, not the levels. An agreement of about 0.8 is therefore what fold noise alone gives when the features explain nothing; values near 1 need signal. The Jaccard figures of the earlier probe (PR #265 review, Slurm 1876267: 11 fold streams, CV R² 0.05–0.77) still hold for the flagged set: 0.67–1.0 against stream 0, median about 0.77.

A determinants Jaccard of about 0.7 or more is therefore within fold-assignment noise. Read it together with n_primary, n_variant and n_shared. The denominator of agreement (the genes explained in both runs, most of the model rows) is not in the table; it is n_agreement in the event sensitivity.determinants_cv_r2. Neither jaccard nor agreement has a confidence interval.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
• Flagged sets are small (at most 2 × regions × contigs IDs, usually fewer than 20), so a single flip moves Jaccard by a large step. Read jaccard together with n_primary, n_variant and n_shared.
  • Changes concentrate in flags whose q is near alpha.context (0.05). A flag far below it that disappears under a variant is the signal worth inspecting.
  • BH is recomputed within each rerun's (region_type, stat) family, so each set is at its own FDR. A variant can move a region's q, and so flip its flag, even when that region's p is unchanged.

  • What each variant holds fixed: every variant keeps the region definitions (C7 / C8), the replicon topology (C1), the detectability covariates and B = 199 (the primary is recomputed at the same B). missing=<p> and top3 also keep detection and p_detect, so every O − E p, q and flag is identical to the primary's when shifts are exhaustive; above 20,000 genes they can differ only through sampled-shift noise. single_peptide_detected keeps the observed abundance values and the TU folds of the detectability fit.

  • Islands (M5-10) are flagged by one two-sided genome-wide FWER (both directions), not by BH. Their IDs are genes, so one island flipping moves the Jaccard by that island's share of the genes.

  • Islands whose p lies within about ±0.03 of alpha.context can flip on Monte Carlo noise alone. In the statistician's probe (identical data, 30 independent streams; PR #184 review), a planted island at 2.2 SD gave Jaccard 0 against stream 0 in 59 % of streams; at 3.0 SD it was always 1. At B = 199 the Monte Carlo SD of p at 0.05 is about 0.015. An island lost under a variant whose primary p ≤ 0.01 is the real signal to inspect. The Jaccard has no confidence interval.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
One row per (family, variant): n_primary = |P|, n_variant = |V|, n_shared = |P ∩ V| and jaccard = |P ∩ V| / |P ∪ V| (NA when both sets are empty). agreement is reserved for the dominant determinant block (M8) and is NA for other families.

Signed off by the statistician, 2026-10-20 (PR #117 reviews https://github.com/khoa-yelo/giap/pull/117#issuecomment-6304191087 and https://github.com/khoa-yelo/giap/pull/117#issuecomment-6304219014), conditional on the shared-stream limitation above sampled-shift sizes (backlog: per-region shift streams).

docs.title: Target–decoy q-values and picked FDR
docs.text: Implements giap.stats.tda.{monotone_q, tda_qvalues, picked_fdr} (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.2.5, §7.3.2, §8.3, Appendix B.6; issue M4-01). Used by placement FDR (M3-10, per stratum) and the decoy_picked gene-detection tier (M4-11/12).

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Higher score = better. Callers with "lower is better" statistics pass the negation (placement passes −E).
  • NaN and −inf mean absent (no evidence). +inf is a legal, best-possible score (e.g. a rank transform of q = 0).
  • Thresholds are the distinct observed target scores. At threshold t, T(t) and D(t) count every target and decoy with score ≥ t. A decoy tied with a target is therefore counted against it (the conservative reading, and consistent with "ties go to the decoy" in picking).
  • Output is one value per input target, in input order. Tied targets get equal q.

docs.title: Separate search: tda_qvalues(target, decoy, pi=1, plus_one=True)
docs.text:
FDR(t) = π · (D(t) + 1) / T(t)        (π · D(t)/T(t) if plus_one=False)
qᵢ     = min_{t ≤ sᵢ} FDR(t), clipped to [0, 1]

monotone_q does the second step: given FDR at thresholds sorted strictest → loosest, it returns the running minimum from the loose end. So a target's q is the smallest FDR among all thresholds that would still accept it, and accepting q ≤ α is the same as taking the loosest threshold with FDR ≤ α.

  • The +1. It is the "knockoff+" correction (Barber & Candès 2015; He et al. 2015): it stops D(t) = 0 from producing FDR = 0 when few targets pass. It makes small strata conservative by design: with no decoys at all, q = 1/T, so a stratum needs T ≥ 100 targets above the first decoy to accept anything at 0.01 (B.6: 150 targets → q = 0.0067 accepted; 50 targets → q = 0.02, none accepted).
  • π. π ∈ (0, 1] scales the decoy count to the expected share of wrong targets (π̂_wrong in §7.2.5; 1 for m ≥ 1 strata). π outside (0, 1] (or NaN) raises ValueError. π = 1 is always conservative when there are as many decoys as targets; π < 1 is valid only if π is a conservative (upward-biased) estimate of the true wrong share — see the violation table below.
  • Assumption. Decoys must be a sample from the null-target score distribution with the same number of draws as targets (one decoy search per target search). Separate search has no finite-sample guarantee; the guarantee is asymptotic plus the +1 margin, and the simulations below show it at level.

docs.title: Picked competition: picked_fdr(target_best, decoy_best)
docs.text:
Savitski et al. (2015), applied to genes (§7.3.2). Per gene g, with target score s_g and paired decoy score s̃_g:

  1. Pick. The decoy wins when s̃_g ≥ s_g (a tie counts as a decoy) or when the gene has only decoy evidence. The target wins when s_g > s̃_g or the gene has only target evidence. A gene with neither is in no list.
  2. FDR and q. q over the picked list = tda_qvalues(picked targets, picked decoys) with π = 1 and +1: FDR(t) = (#picked decoys ≥ t + 1)/#picked targets ≥ t, made monotone.
  3. Output. q is defined only for target winners; it is NaN where the decoy wins or neither exists (the gene is then not_detected, decided in M4-12). decoy_wins is true also for decoy-only genes; n_target_wins, n_decoy_wins are reported counts.

Why this controls FDR: for a null gene whose target and decoy scores are exchangeable, the picked label is a fair coin independent of the picked score, so picking is target–decoy competition and the (D + 1)/T rule with the loosest passing threshold is the knockoff+ procedure, which controls FDR in finite samples. A tie is a case where the coin cannot be read; giving it to the decoy keeps the coin at most fair for targets. Decoy-only genes count as decoys, which only lowers T/D and is conservative.

docs.title: What is and is not controlled
docs.text:
Controlled (given the assumptions): the expected share of false entries among targets accepted at q ≤ α — placement FDR within a stratum, gene FDR within the picked list.

Not controlled:

  • FDR for anything aggregated afterwards (genes from peptide q, operons from gene q, §8.7).
  • FDR when the decoys do not mimic null targets (wrong score distribution, missing decoys, different multiplicity). These are input-contract violations; the engine cannot detect them.
  • FWER: one false call at q ≤ 0.01 is expected about once per 100 calls.
  • Per-gene error: q is a set-level quantity; a gene with q = 0.009 is not "99.1 % certain".

docs.title: Simulation evidence
docs.text:
Fast suite (tests/calibration/test_stats_fdr_calibration.py): N = 2000, π₀ = 0.8, null scores N(0, 1), true scores N(3.5, 1), one N(0, 1) decoy per target; picked adds 5 % of genes without a target and 5 % without a decoy. Mean FDP ± SE, seed 20261014:

Method R q = 0.01 q = 0.05 q = 0.10 separate, π = 1 50 0.0076 ± 0.0010 0.0392 ± 0.0021 0.0770 ± 0.0029 separate, π = 1 300 0.0070 ± 0.0004 0.0386 ± 0.0008 0.0771 ± 0.0011 separate, π = true π₀ 50 0.0093 ± 0.0011 0.0497 ± 0.0025 0.0960 ± 0.0029 separate, π = true π₀ 300 0.0088 ± 0.0005 0.0485 ± 0.0009 0.0965 ± 0.0011 separate, π = 1, no +1 300 0.0097 ± 0.0005 0.0409 ± 0.0008 0.0791 ± 0.0011 picked 50 0.0070 ± 0.0010 0.0431 ± 0.0022 0.0949 ± 0.0030 picked 300 0.0076 ± 0.0005 0.0438 ± 0.0009 0.0926 ± 0.0012

All at level; π = 1 is conservative by ≈ π₀, as expected; without the +1 the q = 0.01 margin shrinks to the SE.

docs.title: Attack nulls (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_fdr_engine.py, R = 50 and 300)
docs.text:
