Attack Built to break R = 300 mean FDP at q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 picked, gene sizes log-normal (best of k_g), shared target–decoy gene effect (SD 0.7), scores rounded to 0.1, 5 % target-absent, 5 % decoy −inf heterogeneous multiplicity, correlation, ties 0.0048 / 0.0408 / 0.0859 picked, integer scores (most genes tie) tie rule 0.0017 / 0.0258 / 0.0286 separate, exponential scores on a 0.5 grid + shared batch shift ties, dependence 0.0000 / 0.0142 / 0.0536 global null (every call false), picked and separate, n = 2000 and n = 25 P(any call) = FDR ≤ 0.0033 everywhere

All stay at level with the current implementation.

docs.title: Assumption violations (documented, not CI gates)
docs.text:
These break the inputs, not the code, and show what upstream modules must guarantee (R = 300, N = 2000, π₀ = 0.8):

Violation q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 Consequence for callers tie given to the target (integer scores) 0.029 / 0.214 / 0.233 the ≥ / tie-to-decoy rule is essential; never break ties in the target's favour upstream decoys shifted −0.3 SD below null targets 0.019 / 0.097 / 0.184 decoys must mimic targets (§8.2): same length, composition, multiplicity 10 % of decoys lost at random 0.0085 / 0.052 / 0.106 borderline 20 % of decoys lost at random 0.0099 / 0.059 / 0.122 the §7.3.2 fallback at > 20 % unpaired decoys is too lax: at 20 % loss gene FDR is ≈ 1.2 × nominal. Recommendation for M4-11/12: scale D by 1/(paired share) or fall back at a lower share (≈ 5 %) 30 % of null-gene decoys lost 0.011 / 0.067 / 0.138 as above π = 0.5 when true π₀ = 0.8 0.015 / 0.077 / 0.158 π̂ must be conservative; M3-10's π̂_wrong (mean PEP, max q, de novo lower bound) needs its own calibration in the placement suite

docs.title: Six-frame ORF decoys in the simulator and the class q floor (M7-12, M7-11)
docs.text:
The novel_orf_power scenario writes the decoys a search against giap makedb --six-frame-orfs would give. Each null PSM of a six-frame wrong peptide goes to its target row or to the rev_GIAPORF_… decoy of its makedb entry with probability ½ (stream [seed, 8]). The decoy keeps the null score, and its q and PEP come from the same score function (M7-12 decisions 21, 24). Statistician round 3 (PR #225, tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_m7_sixframe_picked.py) found:

  • The picked label is a fair coin. The coin is drawn independently of the score, so the side that holds an entry's best PSM is fair. Pooled over 27 replicates at 1 Mb, 5575 of 10955 wrong peptides had their best PSM on the target side (0.509, binomial p = 0.064). The q and PEP are one monotone function of the score for targets and decoys alike, so ranking by q and then by score keeps the exchangeability. Under M7-11 rule 2 the procedure is therefore knockoff+.
  • Oracle class FDP is at level. The oracle picks at entry level, within each class, with no GIAP novel code. With 200 ORFs planted per class at 1 Mb, over 15 replicates:
Class q = 0.01 q = 0.05 q = 0.10 intergenic 0.0095 ± 0.0036 0.049 ± 0.008 0.107 ± 0.010 cds_outframe 0.0063 ± 0.0021 0.044 ± 0.004 0.105 ± 0.008 antisense 0.0033 ± 0.0016 0.048 ± 0.007 0.096 ± 0.010
  • The q and PEP on target rows are about 2× conservative. The mixture uses the pre-coin wrong share. After the coin, only half of the null PSMs remain targets. At 1 Mb, target PSMs at q ≤ 0.01 have FDP 0.005, and the sum of PEP is 869 against 608 wrong target rows. A real engine estimates q from the decoys, so its target q is not inflated in this way. Nothing in the picked class FDR reads q or PEP as a probability. Any calibration check of PSM-level q or PEP on this scenario must use the post-coin share instead.
  • Class q floor. (D + 1)/T can never fall below 1/T, so a class with fewer than 1/α = 100 target ORFs calls nothing at α = 0.01. This is not specific to the simulator. In a real genome, the picked class FDR at 0.01 calls nothing in a class with fewer than about 100 detected candidates (M7-11 example 2). The scenario defaults plant 16 per class at 300 kb and 40 at 1 Mb. At those sizes the oracle's minimum class q is 0.056–0.077 at 300 kb (3 seeds) and 0.025–0.028 at 1 Mb (12 seeds), with 0 calls at 0.01 in every replicate. G3 (F1 ≥ 0.9 of called ORFs) is then 0 by construction. At 1 Mb, intergenic planting stops at about 100–145 ORFs (gap supply), whatever the requested count.

docs.title: Scored null decoys on the real K-12 genome (MVP-04, PR #247)
docs.text:
decoys = "scored_null" (giapsim, MVP-04 step 6) models a DIA-NN --report-decoys search against giap makedb --six-frame-orfs. Every null PSM row goes to its target or to its entry's decoy on an independent ½ coin (stream [seed, 8]; scores come from stream [seed, 3]). The decoy keeps the row's score, q and PEP. Protein-entry nulls are real tryptic products of loci with no true peptide, with the locus drawn uniformly (lead decision 9). Statistician review of PR #247 (Slurm 1871592: K-12, 10 seeds; 1871626: attack file):

  • Why the coin gives the picked gene FDR its null. A null gene's PSMs are i.i.d. and their coins are independent of the scores. The side that holds the gene's best row is therefore a fair coin, independent of the picked score, and (D + 1)/T is knockoff+ on the null genes. Targets and decoys carry the same key columns, so the M4-24 shared key is S = {q, pep, score} and there is no decoy_unscored. q and PEP are one monotone function of the score on both sides. The mixture q is at most π_wrong_realised ≈ 0.01, so at π_wrong = 0.01 the ADR-0047 decoy filter removes almost nothing, and what it removes is symmetric. Collisions: 0 in 10 seeds.
  • Why match_wrong decoys are off. They are reversed random proteins that no null target matches. On a true gene they can only take a win from it; on a gene with no target they are a decoy-only win. Either way D grows with no null target behind it, which mixes a conservative bias into the null being measured.
  • The 1/T floor. T ≈ 2,700 target-won genes (b0 −5.25; truth-detected share 0.631), so q_floor ≈ 0.00037 ≪ 0.01. The floor is not what limits the run.
  • The gene-level null is too sparse for the α = 0.01 gates under the search-space split. Protein entries are 12.5 % of the distinct tryptic products, which leaves about 21 protein-entry nulls per run (mean 20.7, range 20–22), about 11 decoy wins (7–15) and about 10 false target-won genes, against T ≈ 2,700.
  • (D + 1)/T at the loosest threshold is 0.004, so the α cut never binds: n_detected = T on 10 of 10 seeds. Realised gene FDP is 0.0037 ± 0.0004.
  • An engine that ignores the decoys would reach only FDP ≈ 0.0076 (0.0073–0.0082), which is below α and below gate 7 (0.02). Gate 7 therefore cannot fail.
  • With the Q2 alternative (a fixed 50/50 split) there are about 83 protein nulls and about 41 decoy wins. The cut binds on 10 of 10 seeds, mean FDP at α = 0.01 is 0.0104 ± 0.0013, and an engine that ignores the decoys reaches 0.029–0.032, so gate 7 can fail.
  • π_wrong 0.03 or 0.05 under the search-space split still leaves the decoy-blind FDP below 0.02.
  • The Q2 fallback (50/50 when there are fewer than 50 gene-level null PSMs) is not monotone. On the 200-kb excerpt, π_wrong 0.05 gives 47 protein nulls (50/50), while π_wrong 0.10 gives 26 (search space).
  • A second gene-level channel. Six-frame nulls on GIAPORF_nterm_extension_* entries place in a gene's nterm_extension class, which assigns to the gene (about 11 undetected genes per K-12 run, next to the ~21 protein nulls). Their rev_GIAPORF_* decoys pair with the gene only when a target row of the entry was accepted, so that the entry is voted to the gene (M7-12 decision 28). If every row went to the decoy side, the gene vanishes instead of being a decoy win. With k rows, P(target wins | the gene is seen) = ½ / (1 − 2^−k), which is 4/7 for k = 3: anti-conservative, and small at K-12 (≈ +0.8 false genes against D ≈ 11).
  • Dense-null attack (tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_mvp04_scored_null.py). This is the 200-kb excerpt at π_wrong 0.05 with the 50/50 split, and it includes the nterm channel. Mean gene FDP at q = 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.10 is 0.0092 / 0.0517 / 0.0915 at R = 50, and 0.0087 / 0.0463 / 0.0866 at R = 300. All pass. A decoy-blind engine is a confirmed failure at 0.01 and 0.05. Two slow tests ("gate 7 can fail", "the α cut binds") check the K-12 run; they were strict xfails under the search-space split.

docs.title: What the evidence run uses (MVP-04 lead decisions 10–16; statistician re-check, Slurm 1872374)
docs.text:
• Fixed 50/50 split (decision 10): half the null peptides, rounded down, go to protein entries, capped by the pool. The search-space share (0.125) is recorded for information only. The pool also holds the loci that the sample strain makes pseudo through a premature stop (decision 16). GIAP sees them as intact, eligible genes. Products that span the stop are skipped. No protein null lands on a recorded pseudo or truncated locus.
  • K-12, seeds 1–10, oracle with the nterm-extension and multi_identical channels:
  • 80–89 protein nulls per run and 81–95 genes with null evidence. Collisions: 0.
  • D = 42.5 ± 1.9 (36–54); T ≈ 2,740.
  • The α = 0.01 cut binds on 10 of 10 seeds.
  • Mean gene FDP at α 0.01 is 0.0109 ± 0.0013 (0.0051–0.0183), at level against q + 2 SE = 0.0126.
  • A decoy-blind engine gives 0.0262 ± 0.0006 (0.0233–0.0287), above gate 7's 0.02.
  • False detected genes come mostly from protein nulls; the nterm channel adds 0–6 per run.
  • At K12_EVIDENCE_SEED: T 2,744, 2,721 detected, FDP 0.0077, decoy-blind 0.0284, which matches Slurm 1872190.
  • Gate 7 catches only gross failures. Per seed, a correct engine has FDP sd ≈ 0.004 and a maximum of 0.018 over 10 seeds. A decoy-blind engine is only 1.2–1.4 × the gate. An engine that inflates FDR by 1.5× (mean ≈ 0.016) would usually still pass. The calibration suites and the dense-null attack own the mean; gate 7 is a single-run check of the gross picture. With one fixed seed the result is deterministic, so this is a power limit, not flakiness.
  • Recorded deviation (decision 13): decision 9 draws the protein-null locus uniformly. The §8.4 gene-FDR generator draws size-proportionally. Picked validity does not depend on it, because each null gene is exchangeable either way. A MAYU-tier check on these inputs would see a different null from its calibration suite.

docs.title: Convergent and sandwich decoys (operons, M6-01)
docs.text:
giap.stats.decoy_fdr reuses monotone_q for the missed-operon family (§7.4.4); the full method and its power analysis are in docs/methods/operons.md. What differs from the separate search above:

  • Decoys are not one per target. CV (convergent) and SW (→ ← →) pairs are whatever the genome has, in different numbers and with a different intergenic-distance mix than the NO targets. The "one decoy per target, same distribution" assumption of tda_qvalues is replaced by within-bin exchangeability: in each distance bin b, |Δ| of a null NO pair and of a decoy have the same distribution. Each bin's decoy tail fraction (D_b + 1)/(N_decoy,b + 1) is scaled by the bin's target count N_NO,b, so the decoys are reweighted to the targets' distance mix and their number no longer matters.
  • The +1 is per bin, so the small-list floor is ≈ π₀ Σ_b N_NO,b/(N_decoy,b + 1) phantom false targets — about B times the single-bin floor, dominated by the bin with the fewest decoys per target. A bin with targets and no decoys contributes all its targets.
  • Two decoy sets, the larger FDR wins, maximum taken before monotonising. CV partners can be less alike than same-strand neighbours (transcriptional interference), which is conservative; SW pairs are farther apart. Reporting the larger guards against whichever set happens to mimic null NO pairs badly in the conservative direction; it does not guard against a set that is more alike than null targets (anti-conservative), which only an attack null can reveal.
  • π₀ = 1 and N_NO,b counts every target, so the estimate is conservative by ≈ π₀.

At NOVEL_PER_CLASS_GATE = 300 the intergenic class is limited by gap supply: 88–122 ORFs have a true peptide over seeds 1–8 at 1M, so in about 3 of 8 replicates it stays above the class q floor at α = 0.01. The other three classes clear it on every seed (M7-12 lead decision 28).

docs.title: Consequence for real genomes
docs.text: The same floor applies outside the simulator. At α = 0.01 the picked class FDR calls nothing in a novel-ORF class with fewer than about 100 target candidates, because q ≥ 1/T. A small class is then reported with zero calls; this is not evidence that it has no novel ORFs. The report states this (M7-13), and M7-12 gates use NOVEL_PER_CLASS_GATE = 300 at 1M (M7-12 lead decision 26).

docs.title: Numerical notes
docs.text:
• Counts use searchsorted on sorted arrays (O(n log n)); no floating-point equality beyond the exact ≥ comparison of the caller's scores. Callers that compute scores on different paths for targets and decoys must round consistently, or a near-tie becomes a target win.
  • monotone_q assumes no NaN in its input (a NaN propagates to all stricter thresholds); the public functions never pass one.

docs.title: Flags: expected, not a bug
docs.text: flags_for (src/giap/variants/flags.py:189-191) implements §7.5.3 literally: strain_difference = any ALT under related; database_derived = an ALT supported by a (database, other) peptide. Both are therefore true for every ALT of this run, and MVP-04 gate 11 requires exactly that (n_rows_missing_flags = 0). Flags are not uniform: 128/428 mass_equivalent, 35 start_codon, 0 multi_nt (the sample carries SNVs only). With a single-source input both flags are constant and carry no information; they discriminate only in mixed inputs. On a real same-strain K-12 search (search_db = same, genome_relation = same) neither flag would appear.

docs.title: Class error rates
docs.text: Implements giap.variants.error_rates (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.5.4, §8.1 row "ALT call is real", §7.5.5 CLASS_ERR; docs/specs/M7-10-class-error-rates.md; statistician review of PR #239).

docs.title: Estimator
docs.text:
• Pairs. A de novo row pairs with a reference row (--reference-peptides, via the C17 table peptide_spectra.parquet) of the same (run, spectrum_id) when the reference row is a target with q_value ≤ 0.01 (REF_MAX_Q, as in M3-11). Preflight rejects a spectrum with two different peptides (ADR-0005), so each spectrum has at most one reference identification.
  • Observations. Each paired de novo row whose peptide supports an ALT site is one observation of each class (alt_type, mass_equivalent) among the ALTs it supports. A peptide supporting two ALTs of different classes counts once in each; two sites of one class count once. mass_equivalent comes from the site's M7-05 flags; frameshifts are their own class (frameshift, false).
  • Error. An observation is an error when the de novo and reference peptides differ after I→L folding.
  • Rate. Per class, class_error_rate = errors / n and class_error_n = n, pooled over all sites of the class and written on every ALT row of the class (and VCF CLASS_ERR). A class with n = 0, a run without --reference-peptides, reference rows without spectrum_id (warning no_spectrum_pairing) or a database-only input give unestimated. A class with observations but no error has rate 0 with its n.

docs.title: Estimand
docs.text:
The rate estimates the share of erroneous reads among ALT-supporting de novo reads whose spectrum a database search identifies confidently. It is not the false-ALT rate among all ALT-supporting reads, and its relation to that rate depends on the reference search. Three biases act, two upward and one downward.

  1. Reference database without the variant: upward, up to degenerate (spec rule 5). When the reference identifications come from a search against the same reference proteome GIAP maps to, a correct ALT read can never agree with its spectrum's reference identification: the ALT peptide is not in that database. Such a spectrum is either not identified confidently (no pair) or identified as some other peptide (an "error"). Every paired observation is then an error, and the estimate is 1 (up to I/L-only ALTs) whatever the true error rate. It is then trivially at least the true rate, which carries no information. tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_class_error_rates.py::test_reference_db_degenerate pins this. The rate is informative only when the reference search could return the ALT peptide: a sample-specific database (the strain's own genome or a variant-aware search), or a panel of known variants. Read a rate of 1 from a reference-proteome search as "not measured", not as "every ALT is false".
  2. Spectrum-quality selection: downward. De novo errors are more common on poor spectra, and poor spectra are less often identified at q ≤ 0.01. The paired spectra are therefore cleaner than the unpaired ones, and the rate is biased low for all ALT-supporting reads (attack test_quality_selection: all-reads truth 0.30, paired truth and estimate 0.20).
  3. Reference false matches: upward, small. q_value ≤ 0.01 bounds the expected false share of the confident reference identifications, not zero. A correct de novo read on a spectrum whose confident reference ID is wrong counts as an error. A wrong de novo read is missed only if the wrong reference ID happens to equal it, which is rare. With de novo error rate e on the paired spectra of a class and false-match share φ among them, the estimate is e + (1 − e)·φ, so the bias is (1 − e)·φ: largest for classes with a low error rate, at most φ, and zero for classes whose reads are all errors. φ is a per-class share: q bounds the FDR of the whole reference list, and a class can sit on spectra with more false matches than average. Attack test_reference_false_matches pins the formula (e 0.2, φ 0.05, estimate 0.24).

So the rate is not an upper bound in general. It is an upper bound only when the reference search lacks the variant, where it is degenerate. With a variant-aware reference it is close to the error rate on confidently identified spectra and, if quality selection matters, low for the rest. No correction is applied in v1; the bias is reported, not removed.

docs.title: Uncertainty and small n
docs.text:
Each rate carries its n, so a binomial interval can be computed from the row. GIAP reports no interval column in v1 (the §7.5.5 schema has none). The recommended reading is the Wilson 95% interval, (p + z²/2n ± z √(p(1 − p)/n + z²/4n²)) / (1 + z²/n) with z = 1.96. At n = 5 and p = 1 it is [0.57, 1]; at n = 20 and p = 0.2 it is [0.08, 0.42]. The interval assumes that observations are independent spectra. One spectrum reported at two charges is one observation, not two. Observations of one class at one site are correlated, because the same error mode repeats. The interval is therefore optimistic when a few sites dominate a class.

No minimum n is imposed: a rate with tiny n is shown, always with its n, and unestimated means exactly n = 0. A low_n flag (n < 20; there the Wilson half-width at p = 0.5 is about 0.2 or more) is a backlog candidate, not a v1 rule.

docs.title: Pooling
docs.text:
Rates are pooled per class over sites (lead decision 2). A site's own reliability is not measured. A site-level rate needs tens of paired spectra per site, and a pilot run gives a few paired ALT-supporting spectra per site at most. The class rate is also a mixture across sites: a class dominated by one bad site inherits that site's rate.

Stop-codon sites (M7-16 rule 11). A read-through site has REF * at an annotated terminal stop. It and the U-over-TGA / O-over-TAG zero-change ALTs are in class (substitution, mass_equivalent = false), and their class_error_rate is that class's pooled rate. The rate is dominated by ordinary SNV sites and does not measure read-through reads: with a reference search on Bakta proteins, which end at the stop, every read-through read is in the degenerate case of bias 1 (the reference cannot contain the peptide). A second-pass search on a makedb --patch database does not lift this, since its identification carries X at the stop, which differs from every de novo residue. The rate feeds only class_error_rate/CLASS_ERR, never confidence (high = n_alt ≥ k), so TE2 does not depend on it.

docs.title: Calibration
docs.text:
• tests/calibration/test_variant_class_error.py, no-variant arm: every ALT-supporting read is an error, so truth and estimate both sit at 0.97–1.0. This arm is a sanity check only; a constant estimator rate = 1 passes it.
  • The same file's planted arm uses giapsim's reference peptides, which are the sample's own identifications and so a variant-aware reference. Truth there is 0.23–0.73 for the substitution and frameshift classes. It is gated two-sided at |bias| ≤ 0.05 (denovo_precision_max_abs_bias) on classes estimated in at least half the replicates; at least two gated classes must have truth below 0.9, so a constant estimator (1 or 0) fails. This is the arm with teeth; it runs nightly (fast, R = 20) and in the full suite (R = 100).
  • Measured planted-arm bias (R = 100, full run, 2026-10-23): frameshift +0.0087 (SE 0.0031), substitution +0.0037 (0.0007), substitution with mass_equivalent +0.0021 (0.0007); block and swap 0 (truth 1). Every informative class is biased up, by 3 to 5 SE for the substitution classes and 2.8 SE for frameshift. The frameshift class is not singled out: its larger SE comes from n ≈ 25 paired observations per replicate against ≈ 470 and ≈ 220. The bias is the reference false-match term (bias 3 above), not quality selection:
  • Against the truth on paired spectra only, the bias is the same: +0.0088, +0.0042, +0.0029. So selection of confident spectra contributes nothing in this scenario. giapsim draws reference confidence independently of de novo errors.
  • In a decomposition over the first 20 planted replicates (statistician, from giapsim truth), the estimate minus the paired truth equals the share of paired observations where the de novo read is correct and the confident reference ID is wrong: 0.016 frameshift, 0.0047 and 0.0041 substitution. No wrong de novo read was masked by an agreeing wrong reference ID.
  • The share of wrong confident reference IDs on these spectra was φ ≈ 0.011 for the substitution classes, near the q ≤ 0.01 threshold. It was 0.020 for frameshift spectra, a small class where a few false matches weigh more. (1 − e)·φ then predicts 0.015, 0.0040 and 0.0033, matching the measured shares.

The bias is therefore expected, has a known sign and size (≤ φ, about the reference FDR), and sits well inside the 0.05 bound. No correction is applied: subtracting (1 − e)·φ needs φ per class, which a real run does not know. - tests/calibration/attacks/test_attack_class_error_rates.py: - test_known_rate_mix plants per-class rates of 0, 0.05, 0.3 and 0.8 and checks exact agreement with a brute-force oracle, |bias| ≤ 0.05 and Wilson coverage. Its traps are I/L, spectrum IDs reused across runs, q = 0.02 rows and confident decoys. - test_reference_db_degenerate and test_quality_selection pin the two biases above. - test_duplicate_charge_rows_count_once checks the one-spectrum-one-observation rule. - M7-13, on M7-12's variant_f1 scenario, adds the arm with a reference search against the reference genome's proteome (the degenerate case, recorded), and a known-rate mix at two de novo error levels.

No result appears here that is not in a committed evidence file; every other number is TBD and its row is pending, naming the issue that will produce it. Kept in the repository and left out of the site navigation (Q-L6 style). Aggregates only (Khoa's 2026-10-24 pilot data rule): no peptide sequences, no DIA-NN rows.

A threshold is never restated more loosely than ci/gates.yaml or tests/calibration/tolerances.yaml define it.

docs.title: 2. Sections (intent only)
docs.text:
1. Abstract (structure only): problem; what GIAP does (one gene table keyed by Bakta locus tags); how errors are controlled; what the Nissle 1917 pilot showed; availability. Numbers only from rows marked supported in §4 at submission time.
  2. Introduction. The question: how much of what a bacterial proteome detects, and how much it holds, is explained by genome context (operons, islands, mobile elements, codon usage, promoters), and how to ask that without the database mismatch of a generic reference.
  3. Design. Inputs (genome, Bakta annotation, peptide or protein tables from any search engine); one gene table keyed by Bakta locus tags; the modules (annotation layers, mapping, gene table and detectability, region tests, autocorrelation and islands, operons, variants, novel ORFs, function, determinants, report, compare). Tools run as separate programs (§5 below).
  4. Error control. One paragraph per family with its estimand and its null, each pointing at its methods note: placement FDR (docs/methods/placement-fdr.md), gene-level FDR, picked and MAYU (docs/methods/detection-tiers.md, docs/methods/mayu-gene-fdr.md), circular-shift region tests (docs/methods/region-tests.md, docs/methods/permutation-and-shifts.md), island FWER (docs/methods/islands.md), operon decoys (docs/methods/operons.md), BH families (docs/methods/multiple-testing.md), the attack nulls and the calibration harness (docs/methods/calibration.md).
  5. Validation. (a) Simulation calibration with the giapsim simulator (the four one-sided criteria of docs/methods/calibration.md); (b) the Nissle 1917 pilot with arms A1 (generic K-12 reference), A2 (matched strain) and A3 (de novo); (c) the true-example assertions TE1–TE8 (GIAP_SPEC.md §11.6).
  6. Performance. Measured wall time and peak memory on FarmShare for the standard run on 16 threads and 64 GB, with the node class; per-tool runtimes.
  7. Availability. PyPI and Bioconda packages, containers pinned by digest, Zenodo DOI, the documentation site, licences (§5 below).
  8. Limitations. What version 1 defers (§6 below), stated before the reader has to ask.

docs.title: 5. Data, code and licence availability
docs.text:
• [ ] Proteomics data: PXD078459 (iProX, Nissle 1917, three wild-type runs), cited by accession; never redistributed by GIAP. Only aggregates and file checksums are committed (validation/pilot/inputs/pxd078459_files.tsv).
  • [ ] Genomes and proteomes: Nissle 1917 GCA_043228065.1; K-12 MG1655 GCA_000005845.2; UniProt K-12 proteome UP000000625 (A1's database). Later work: UTI89 GCA_000013265.1 / PXD053727.
  • [ ] Not redistributed, and why: RegulonDB (its terms; fetched by validation/fetch_regulondb.py, never committed); DIA-NN output rows (Khoa's pilot data rule); DIA-NN itself (proprietary academic licence; the version used is 2.3.1 Academia, not the spec's 2.7.0, docs/adr/ADR-0051-diann-version.md, proposed); the Cascadia checkpoint and vendor SDKs (docs/adr/ADR-0054-a3-external-artefacts.md).
  • [ ] Code: GIAP is MIT-licensed; PyPI and Bioconda packages (TBD, M11-04, M11-10); Zenodo DOI (TBD, M11-13); documentation URL (TBD, M11-07, Q-K9); containers by digest (workflow/conf/containers.config, M11-06).
  • [ ] Third-party licences (NOTICE.md, docs/adr/ADR-0008-tool-pins.md), to be stated in the paper:
  • GPL-3.0 tools (Bakta, Promotech, Promoter Calculator, OSTIR, TransTermHP, BacTermFinder) and AGPL-3.0 antiSMASH run as separate programs; GIAP never imports them (scripts/ci/check_imports.py). R and fgsea run as a separate process (ADR-0038).
  • geNOMAD is licensed for non-commercial use only; a commercial user must drop the module or obtain a licence.
  • KEGG is for academic use; non-academic users need a KEGG licence or the GO and COG collections only.
  • UniOP has no licence file: fetched at a pinned commit, never vendored or pushed as an image.
  • DIA-NN is proprietary (academic licence) and used only for users' own searches.

docs.title: 6. Limitations (what version 1 defers, GIAP_SPEC.md §16)
docs.text:
• Single sample per run: no co-expression or differential context tests across samples.
  • Full validation not done: K-12 PXD075568, UTI89 beyond the A3 fallback, FDRBench entrapment, and the K-12 co-abundance AUROC (§13.2 b7). Release 1.0 is calibrated on simulations and one light pilot.
  • Sealed holdout not used: the EDL933 holdout (PXD068911, §14.5) stays sealed for the full validation; no holdout claim is made.
  • A3 de novo arm is exploratory; its feasibility check covers WT_1 only (C21).
  • Deferred modules: assembly checks from frameshift-spanning peptides, CheckM2 in preflight, proteome mass fractions and the V9 treemap, RO-Crate export, H-NS GC test, prophage induction, RNA-seq and Ribo-seq inputs, the V4 locus browser, taxonomy of unmapped sequences, homology evidence for novel ORFs (changelog.d/+known-limitations.misc.md).
  • Out of scope by design (§16 "No"): the recoding and start catalogue (Sec, prfB +1, dnaX −1, non-ATG starts, Met removal), start-codon correction from N-terminal peptides, signal-peptide or transmembrane prediction, PTM naming or classification, Plass, eggNOG-mapper and MMseqs2/UniRef function annotation, and spectrum searching (GIAP only writes the makedb FASTA). The paper must not imply any of them.

Statistical caveats a reader must apply (each recorded in a cited note):

  • ORA p-values are uncalibrated: every ORA row carries ora_uncalibrated (docs/methods/function.md › Pass-1 limit (decision 13; ADR-0035 decision 3)).
  • Gate M7 is not passed: variant F1 0.838 < 0.9 (docs/adr/ADR-0049-m7-variant-precision.md).
  • Operons: the missed-operon family is near-powerless and vacuous with the shipped decoys; discordance level is claimed only under smooth, monotone σ(abundance) (docs/adr/ADR-0055-operon-discordance-abundance-noise.md).
  • GSEA restricted claim: no level claim for genomically clustered sets; results are conditional on detection; BH spillover from flagged rows is not re-measured on the R engine (docs/adr/ADR-0025-gsea-clustered-sets.md, docs/adr/ADR-0026-gsea-conditional-on-detection.md).
  • Islands outside the validity domain: the FWER is breached at ρ = 0.9 with short ℓ′, and the low direction is a structural zero, so a null result is not evidence of no silenced island (docs/methods/islands.md).
  • Region tests: the HL shift is relative to random positions on this replicon; the ori → ter dosage gradient is not modelled in giapsim (docs/methods/region-tests.md › Limitations (statistician)).
  • Genome decoys under-count chance hits of protein-like wrong peptides (D/T 0.96 at realistic dipeptide structure; docs/methods/placement-fdr.md › Limitations (documented, not CI gates)); the real-protein TE8 check is still owed.
  • Determinants: the permutation p-value ships flagged null_uncalibrated; it fails the §8.5 dependence attacks (C18, docs/adr/ADR-0034-determinants-null-uncalibrated.md).
  • K-12 calibration: the TerminatorNet precision against RegulonDB is a lower bound, and the UniOP AUROC is a K-12 number whose in-sample status is unverified (UniOP's training data are not verified), not a transfer claim (docs/adr/ADR-0022-uniop-terminatornet-cutoffs.md).
  • P(miss) is a probability, not a p-value, and sits outside the BH family (docs/adr/ADR-0056-pmiss-outside-the-bh-family.md).

docs.title: pileup
docs.text:
One row per codon covered by an eligible peptide, with REF, I/L and ALT distinct-peptide counts (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.5.2, §7.5.5, §9.3).

  • Path: tables/pileup.tsv.gz
  • Coordinates: 1-based closed
  • Schema: tables/pileup.schema.json
Field Type Unit Description Constraints contig string — Replicon name (C1 order) required codon_start integer — Lowest coordinate of the codon, 1-based, within [1, length] required; minimum 1 strand string — Strand of the peptides' reading frame required; one of +, - gene string — Locus tag of the same-strand gene framing the codon (smallest tag if several) — aa_pos integer — 1-based residue position of the codon in the gene minimum 1 ref_aa string — Table-11 reference residue of the codon on the strand required n_ref integer — Distinct peptides (I/L folded) reading the reference residue required; minimum 0 n_il integer — Distinct peptides reading I or L at an I/L codon (ambiguous) required; minimum 0 alt_counts string — Semicolon-joined ALT keys with their distinct-peptide counts (X:n;Y:m), most supported first pattern [^:;]+:[1-9][0-9]*(?:;[^:;]+:[1-9][0-9]*)* call string — Codon call required; one of REF, ALT, mixed, no_call

docs.title: variants
docs.text:
Sites with an ALT or mixed call, plus frameshift events (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.5.2, §7.5.5, §9.3).

  • Path: tables/variants.tsv
  • Coordinates: 1-based closed
  • Schema: tables/variants.schema.json
Field Type Unit Description Constraints variant_id string — Variant identifier, numbered from 1 in table order required; pattern VAR_[1-9][0-9]* contig string — Replicon name (C1 order) required codon_start integer — Lowest coordinate of the site's first codon in peptide order, 1-based, within [1, length] required; minimum 1 strand string — Strand of the peptides' reading frame required; one of +, - gene string — Locus tag of the same-strand gene framing the codon — aa_pos integer — 1-based residue position of the codon in the gene minimum 1 ref_codon string — Gene-strand bases of the codon(s) the REF allele spans (6 nt for two-codon events); for a frameshift, the last prefix codon required; pattern [ACGTN]+ ref_aa string — Reference residue of the first codon required alt_aa string — ALT residue(s) (J = I or L); fs+1 or fs-1 for a frameshift required alt_type string — Kind of ALT required; one of substitution, swap, block, frameshift call string — Site call required; one of ALT, mixed confidence string — high: at least variants.high_min_peptides distinct ALT peptides required; one of high, candidate n_ref integer — Distinct REF peptides at the codon required; minimum 0 n_alt integer — Distinct peptides supporting this ALT required; minimum 1 nt_changes integer — Nucleotide changes of the minimal-change ALT codon(s) (G14); NA for unequal-length events minimum 0 alt_codon_vcf string — Forward-strand ALT allele written to the VCF; NA when not in the VCF pattern [ACGTN]+ class_error_rate string — Class-specific error rate (%.6g) or unestimated required; pattern unestimated|[0-9.eE+-]+ class_error_n integer — Paired de novo observations (reads) pooled into the class error rate minimum 0 source string — Semicolon-joined sources of the ALT peptides required; pattern (?:database|denovo)(?:;(?:database|denovo))* flags string — Semicolon-joined flags from the Variants vocabulary (§9.4) pattern (?:mass_equivalent|snv|multi_nt|strain_difference|database_derived|start_codon|stop_codon|vcf_unrepresentable)(?:;(?:mass_equivalent|snv|multi_nt|strain_difference|database_derived|start_codon|stop_codon|vcf_unrepresentable))*

docs.title: novel_orfs
docs.text:
One row per novel ORF candidate (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.6.6, §9.3; ADR-0012 decision 3).

  • Path: tables/novel_orfs.tsv
  • Coordinates: 1-based closed
  • Schema: tables/novel_orfs.schema.json
Field Type Unit Description Constraints orf_id string — Novel ORF ID NOVEL_<contig>_<lowest 1-based coordinate of the longest interval>_<p|m> required; pattern NOVEL_[A-Za-z0-9._-]+_[1-9][0-9]*_[pm] class string — Novel-ORF class (§7.6.1, ADR-0013) required; one of nterm_extension, cterm_extension, intergenic, cds_outframe, antisense, pseudogene, sorf contig string — Replicon ID required strand string — Strand required; one of +, - frame integer — Reading frame (+1..+3, -1..-3) — start_longest integer — 1-based position of the first base of the most upstream start codon, in transcription direction (on '-' the highest coordinate, so start > end there; unlike other tables, not the lowest/highest pair); NA without a start codon minimum 1 start_best_ostir integer — 1-based position of the first base of the start codon with the best OSTIR score, in transcription direction (on '-' the highest coordinate, so start > end there; unlike other tables, not the lowest/highest pair); NA without an OSTIR score minimum 1 end integer — 1-based position of the last base of the stop codon (of the last whole codon when open at a linear end), in transcription direction (on '-' the highest coordinate, so start > end there; unlike other tables, not the lowest/highest pair) required; minimum 1 length_aa_longest integer — Protein length (aa, stop excluded) from start_longest, or from the first peptide without a start codon minimum 1 length_aa_best integer — Protein length (aa, stop excluded) from start_best_ostir, or from start_longest when it is NA minimum 1 start_codon_best string — Start codon at start_best_ostir (or start_longest when it is NA) — n_peptides integer — Distinct peptides (I/L folded) supporting the ORF required; minimum 0 peptides string — Supporting peptides, I/L folded (';'-separated list) — best_peptide_q number — Lowest q-value of the supporting peptides — ostir_tir number — OSTIR translation initiation rate at start_best_ostir — promoter_score number — Best Promotech score upstream of the ORF (second round, M7-08) — promoter_supported boolean — A promoter supports the ORF (ADR-0012) — terminator_downstream boolean — A terminator lies downstream of the stop codon (ADR-0012) — terminator_conf number — Confidence of that terminator (ADR-0012) — terminator_distance_nt integer — Distance from the stop codon to that terminator, nt (ADR-0012) — rbs_supported boolean — The start has RBS support (OSTIR threshold) — class_fdr string — Class-level FDR as a float (%.6g), or 'unestimated' required; pattern unestimated|[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]*)?(?:[eE][-+]?[0-9]+)? called boolean — The ORF is called (§7.6.4) required rank integer — Rank among novel ORFs (M7-09); not the row order minimum 1 overlapping_gene string — Locus tag of the overlapped or extended gene — flags string — Semicolon-joined flags from the controlled vocabulary (§9.4); denovo_only_unsupported: every peptide is de novo, none is a database PSM, and there is no RBS support beyond the class rule (ADR-0050) pattern (?:junction_spanned|homopolymer_junction|class_fdr_unestimated|rbs_supported|no_start_codon|partial|ostir_missing|rbs_threshold_unestimated|junction_unknown|promoter_supported|terminator_supported|readthrough_candidate|denovo_only_unsupported)(?:;(?:junction_spanned|homopolymer_junction|class_fdr_unestimated|rbs_supported|no_start_codon|partial|ostir_missing|rbs_threshold_unestimated|junction_unknown|promoter_supported|terminator_supported|readthrough_candidate|denovo_only_unsupported))*

docs.title: null_regions
docs.text:
Circular-shift null of every tested region and statistic, for V18 (GIAP_SPEC.md §7.3.5(b), §10.2; docs/specs/M9-17-plot-support-analysis.md). The values are the statistic each test compares: for o_minus_e the ADR-0018 studentised sum(d - p) / sqrt(sum p (1 - p)), for hl_shift the studentised T = HL / sqrt(V) of ADR-0018's amendments, not the reported effect. Written by the context_stats step while the file stays under 5 MB (2^20 bytes per MB); otherwise the file holds the 1st-99th percentile grid of each null and its header's fourth column is percentile (1-99) instead of shift_k (schema plot_support/null_regions_grid.json). Not a result table.

  • Path: plots/support/null_regions.tsv
  • Coordinates: —
  • Schema: plot_support/null_regions.json
Field Type Unit Description Constraints region_id string — Region (regions_stats.tsv) required contig string — Replicon the region was tested on (a region split across contigs has one null per contig) required stat string — Test statistic of the region test required; one of o_minus_e, hl_shift shift_k integer — Circular gene-index shift k of the null draw (percentile 1-99 in the percentile-grid form of the file) required; minimum 1 null_value number — The studentised statistic at this shift (or the null's percentile in the grid form); NA when undefined — observed number — The observed studentised statistic the null is compared with required

docs.title: Comparing runs
docs.text:
giap compare compares two or more runs on the same genome. A typical use is the same sample searched in different ways: a database search, a de novo search, or two search engines. Every option is listed in the CLI reference.

giap compare out_db out_denovo out_hybrid --outdir cmp --labels db,denovo,hybrid
Option Meaning RUNS two or more giap run output directories --outdir the comparison directory to write (required) --labels comma-separated run labels, one per run, in the order of RUNS; default: the directory names (repeats get _2, _3, …)

docs.title: Checks (exit code 1)
docs.text:
giap compare stops with exit code 1 when any of these fails:

  • fewer than two runs are given;
  • --labels has the wrong number of labels, or labels that are repeated or empty;
  • a label contains & or ;, or is none or other;
  • a run has no genome SHA-256 in run_manifest.json or preflight/preflight.json;
  • the runs' genome SHA-256 values differ;
  • a run has no tables/genes.tsv;
  • the runs' locus-tag sets differ.

The last check means the runs must share one gene model. Use the same --annotation (or the same Bakta database) for every run you want to compare.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
CMP/
├── tables/compare_detection.tsv    gene x run detection matrix, plus the exact intersections
├── tables/compare_abundance.tsv    pairwise abundance concordance
├── tables/compare_stability.tsv    pairwise Jaccard overlap of result sets
├── plots/V16_compare.svg|png|pdf   plus plots/data/V16_compare.tsv
└── report/compare.html             a self-contained comparison page

The columns are listed in the table reference: compare_detection, compare_abundance and compare_stability.

  • compare_detection.tsv has two kinds of rows. matrix rows give a gene, a run and whether the gene was detected. intersection rows give the number of genes detected in exactly a given set of runs, as in an UpSet plot.
  • compare_abundance.tsv has one row per pair of runs. It uses the genes detected with a measured (not imputed) abundance in both. It gives:
  • Spearman ρ, with a 95 % TU-block bootstrap CI (stats.bootstrap resamples);
  • the Bland–Altman bias and limits of agreement on log2 abundance.

The flag too_few_shared marks pairs with too few shared genes, and scale_differs marks runs whose abundance scales differ. - compare_stability.tsv gives, per pair of runs and per result family, the Jaccard overlap of the flagged sets. The families are islands, operon flags, enriched categories, novel ORFs and ALT sites. both_empty and missing_in:<run> mark sets that are empty, or tables that are absent.

V16 shows an UpSet plot of the detected genes across runs, and the pairwise abundance concordance. compare.html lists each run's directory, genome SHA-256 and detection tier, together with V16 and the tables.

Detection in each run keeps that run's own error control: its tier and gene q-values. A gene that is detected in one run and not another is not, by itself, a significant difference between them. Read the detection tier of each run before you compare counts (see Interpreting results).

docs.title: Converting search-engine output
docs.text:
giap convert turns a search engine's output into the generic peptide table that giap run --peptides reads (see Inputs). Every option is listed in the CLI reference.

giap convert --from diann report.parquet --out peptides.tsv --abundance-out abundance.tsv
giap run --genome genome.fna --peptides peptides.tsv --outdir out

DIA-NN peptides carry intensity, so giap run computes gene abundance from the peptides. The abundance table written by --abundance-out is then not used, even when you pass it with --abundance. It is used only for peptides without intensities (see Inputs › Abundance table). Passing it with --abundance-type maxlfq makes sense only in that case.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Meaning INPUTS one or more input files; several files are read in the order given --from the engine: diann, casanovo, instanovo, cascadia or generic (required) --out the peptide table to write (required) --abundance-out also write a protein abundance table (DIA-NN only) --source database or denovo: the default source for --from generic --search-db same or other: was the search database this genome's own proteins?

docs.title: Engines
docs.text:
--from Status Input Notes diann implemented DIA-NN 2.x report.parquet or report.tsv source = database cascadia implemented Cascadia 0.0.7 result file (.ssl) source = denovo; no q-value or PEP is derived from score generic implemented a generic peptide TSV validates and normalises it, and reports problems casanovo not implemented: exit code 5 — — instanovo not implemented: exit code 5 — —

--from casanovo and --from instanovo are accepted choices, but GIAP 1.0 has no converter for them. Both print "not implemented" and exit with code 5. Until a converter exists, write a generic peptide table yourself (see below).

With --from diann, --source may only be database; with --from cascadia, only denovo. Any other value exits with code 1.

docs.title: DIA-NN
docs.text:
Generic column DIA-NN column peptide Stripped.Sequence (modification syntax stripped) modified_peptide Modified.Sequence protein_ids Protein.Ids q_value Global.Q.Value, else Q.Value pep PEP is_decoy Decoy (present only when DIA-NN ran with diann --report-decoys) intensity Precursor.Normalised, else Precursor.Quantity (0 becomes missing) run, charge Run, Precursor.Charge

--abundance-out writes one row per Protein.Group, with a column maxlfq. The value is the median over runs of PG.MaxLFQ. Missing values, zeros and decoy rows are excluded, and groups with no value are dropped. The command then prints a reminder to use --abundance-type maxlfq with the table. That reminder applies only when the table is used (see above). With any other engine, --abundance-out is an error (no_abundance, exit code 1).

DIA-NN is proprietary software under its own licence. GIAP never redistributes it, and you run it yourself (see Licences). Keep the decoy rows, so that GIAP can use the decoy_picked detection tier.

docs.title: Cascadia
docs.text: peptide is the stripped sequence and modified_peptide the original sequence. score is copied from score, run is the stem of file, and charge is copied from charge. spectrum_id is cascadia:<scan>. Note that Cascadia's scan is a prediction index, not a scan number.

docs.title: Generic
docs.text: The generic converter checks a table you wrote. It strips modifications, such as (UniMod:35), [+15.995], [UNIMOD:35], +15.995 or n[42], and lower-case residues. It then validates every column. --source and --search-db fill the source and search_db columns where they are empty. Booleans are canonicalised, and columns that are not in the generic table are dropped with the warning unknown_column. (giap run keeps unknown columns instead.)

docs.title: Messages and exit codes
docs.text: Problems are printed as giap convert: <severity>: <code>: <message>, with example row numbers. Any error exits with code 1, and no table is written. Warnings and info messages do not stop the conversion. For the full list of exit codes, see Running GIAP.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
GIAP reads one assembled genome and proteomics evidence from the search you already ran. It never searches spectra itself. Run giap preflight to check every input in seconds before a run (see Running GIAP).

Input Option Required Format Genome --genome yes nucleotide FASTA, optionally gzipped Peptides --peptides recommended the generic peptide table (below) Proteins --proteins yes, unless peptides are given protein FASTA Abundance --abundance optional TSV: a protein ID column plus one value column Annotation --annotation optional Bakta JSON (preferred), GFF3 or GenBank (GBFF) Reference peptides --reference-peptides optional the generic peptide table Replicon depth --replicon-depth optional TSV with columns contig and mean_depth Configuration --config optional YAML; see the configuration reference

giap preflight takes --genome, --proteins, --peptides, --abundance and --annotation. giap run takes them all. Without --peptides and --proteins, preflight stops with the error inputs.evidence_present (exit code 1). It does the same when every peptide row was dropped and no proteins were given.

docs.title: Genome FASTA
docs.text:
• The first token of each header is the contig ID. Characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] are replaced by _. The renaming is saved and reported as the warning genome.ids_renamed.
  • Circular replicons. A header that contains circular=true or [topology=circular] marks the replicon as circular. Contigs without either tag are linear. The exception is --set annotation.bakta.complete=true, which declares every contig a complete, circular replicon.
  • Gzipped FASTA is accepted.

Topology matters. On a circular replicon, a gene or peptide can cross the origin, and the statistics wrap around it. On a linear contig, nothing wraps. A gene cut by a contig end is partial and is excluded from detection statistics.

Plain NCBI FASTA. NCBI headers have no topology tag. Preflight therefore reports every contig as linear in the info row genome.topology, which lists each replicon's length, topology and kind. For a complete assembly, add the tag or set annotation.bakta.complete. Preflight also lists contigs shorter than preflight.small_replicon_bp (500,000 bp by default) as putative plasmids or fragments, in the info row genome.small_replicons.

Other genome checks warn on the following:

  • more than preflight.max_contigs_warn contigs;
  • a total length or N50 below the configured minimum;
  • runs of N;
  • a GC content outside preflight.gc_range_warn.

docs.title: Peptide table (peptides.tsv)
docs.text:
The generic peptide table is a UTF-8 TSV with one header row. giap convert writes it from DIA-NN or Cascadia output (see Converting search-engine output). You can also write it yourself. Only peptide is required.

Column Type Meaning peptide text stripped sequence, uppercase A–Z only modified_peptide text engine notation or ProForma; kept for provenance protein_ids text ;-separated engine protein IDs; decoy and contaminant prefixes are recognised (input.decoy_prefixes, input.contaminant_prefixes) q_value number in [0, 1] precursor or peptide q-value (for DIA-NN, the global q-value) pep number in [0, 1] posterior error probability score number engine or de novo score, higher is better is_decoy true/false decoy row; needs protein_ids to pair the decoy with a gene intensity number ≥ 0 linear precursor or peptide intensity, per run run text run or sample name charge integer precursor charge spectrum_id text scan or spectrum ID, unique within run source database or denovo default from input.peptide_source search_db same or other was the search database this genome's own proteins? Default from input.search_db

Columns not in this list are kept, with an info message. Rows are grouped by stripped peptide:

  • q_value and pep take the minimum over a peptide's rows, and score the maximum;
  • is_decoy is true only when every row is a decoy;
  • protein_ids is the union.

Intensities are summed over charges and modified forms within a run. The median across runs is then taken (abundance.run_aggregation). Rows whose stripped length is outside input.peptide_len (7–40 aa by default) are dropped, and preflight reports them under peptides.content.

Decoys help. Keep the search engine's decoy rows, with their protein_ids. GIAP can then use picked target–decoy FDR at the gene level, the decoy_picked tier. With DIA-NN, search with diann --report-decoys. See Interpreting results.

docs.title: Protein FASTA (--proteins)
docs.text:
• The ID is the first token of the header. UniProt sp|ACC|NAME and tr|ACC|NAME resolve to ACC. A protein group written A;B is split.
  • Records of 40 aa or shorter go to the peptide path, and records shorter than 7 aa are dropped with a warning.
  • Allowed letters are the 20 amino acids plus U. X, B, Z and J are counted, and an internal * warns.

Proteins longer than 40 aa are aligned to the genome with miniprot, then tblastn (mapping/protein_hits.tsv).

docs.title: Abundance table (--abundance)
docs.text:
The first column is a protein ID: one that matches --proteins, a locus tag or a gene ID. Exactly one numeric value column is used. Extra columns warn and are ignored. NA and empty cells are missing values.

Scale detection. With --abundance-scale auto (the default), the scale is log2 when any value is negative, or when every value is ≤ 50. Otherwise it is linear. Give --abundance-scale log2 or --abundance-scale linear to override the detection. A negative value is an error only on a linear scale.

Abundance type. --abundance-type declares what the values are: ibaq, top3, maxlfq, intensity or unknown. The default unknown means relative values. Missing values are filled by the policy --abundance-missing (median by default; or exclude, min, zero, mean). Imputed genes carry abundance_imputed = true in genes.tsv.

The abundance table is used only when the peptides carry no intensities.

docs.title: Existing annotation (--annotation)
docs.text:
• Bakta JSON (.json or .json.gz). GIAP uses it as is and does not run Bakta. The Bakta and database versions are read from the JSON. Use this when your search database came from the same Bakta annotation, so that the protein IDs match the locus tags.
  • GFF3 or GBFF from another annotator. Bakta runs with bakta --regions on that file's CDS, so the gene coordinates match. annotation/id_map.tsv maps the source IDs to Bakta locus tags by identical CDS coordinates, and genes.tsv keeps them in source_id.

Preflight recognises the format by its extension: .json, .gff3, .gff, .gbff or .gbk, optionally gzipped.

docs.title: Reference peptides (--reference-peptides)
docs.text:
A generic peptide table from a database search of the same spectra against this strain's proteins. It is used for two things:

  • the de novo precision of de novo peptides (without it, GIAP assumes a value and flags the run c_assumed);
  • the error rates of ALT calls in the variant module.

docs.title: Replicon depth (--replicon-depth)
docs.text: A TSV with the columns contig and mean_depth, for example sequencing depth per replicon. It gives a copy-number offset for plasmid contrasts. Rows flagged depth_adjusted used it.

docs.title: Coordinates in inputs
docs.text: Input GFF3 and GBFF files use their formats' own 1-based closed coordinates. GIAP converts them once on reading. Every output coordinate convention is listed in Outputs › Coordinates.

docs.title: Interpreting results
docs.text:
Every claim GIAP makes carries one of four labels:

  • a q-value;
  • an estimated false discovery rate (FDR);
  • a family-wise error rate (FWER);
  • the label unestimated.

That is the reporting rule. It does not mean every method is calibrated in every situation. Some methods ship in 1.0 with a known calibration failure. Their rows carry a flag, and their p- and q-values are not discovery claims. They are listed in Methods shipped flagged uncalibrated below. Read that section before you report any function, determinant, island, operon or variant result.

This page explains what each label means in GIAP, and what a detection does and does not tell you. The statistical methods behind each estimate are documented one note per method under Methods.

docs.title: q-values, FDR, FWER and unestimated
docs.text:
FDR. The false discovery rate is the expected share of false claims among the claims accepted at a threshold. GIAP estimates it in two ways:

  • from decoys, which are matched false hypotheses:
  • reversed or shuffled genome translations, for placement;
  • convergent and → ← → sandwich pairs, for missed operons;
  • from p-values, with Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) adjustment within a pre-declared family of tests.

q-value. The q-value of a claim is the smallest FDR at which that claim would be accepted. Accepting every row with q_value ≤ 0.05 gives a list with an estimated FDR of at most 5 %. A q-value is a property of the list, not a probability that one row is wrong.

BH and decoy q-values control the FDR within one family only. Nothing is controlled across families. If you scan several tables, expect roughly α × (number of discoveries) false ones in each family (multiple testing).

FWER. The family-wise error rate is the probability of at least one false claim in the whole family. GIAP uses FWER for abundance islands. One family covers the whole run: each window is compared with the maximum statistic over the windows of every scanned replicon. The null comes from a circular TU-block bootstrap of the detrended TU scores. The FWER claim is conditional on a dependence regime (see islands below). It is not an unconditional guarantee.

unestimated. GIAP labels a claim unestimated when the input cannot support an error estimate, for example:

  • gene detection from peptide sequences alone;
  • a test whose null has too few units.

The claim is still reported, so you can inspect it. Do not report it as error-controlled. Flags such as ci_unestimated, class_fdr_unestimated, not_estimable, ora_uncalibrated and null_uncalibrated say which part is missing or uncalibrated (see the flag reference).

Families and defaults. BH applies within the families fixed in code. Here are the main claims, with the default threshold of each (stats.alpha.* in the configuration reference):

Claim Error control Default Peptide placed at a locus placement q-value from genome decoys: one list per decoy type × stratum (0, 1, 2 differences), length classes pooled 0.01 Gene detected gene q-value (tiers decoy_picked, mayu) or unestimated 0.01 Novel ORF FDR per class 0.01 ALT call the 0.01 is the placement-q filter on supporting peptides (stats.alpha.variants); the class error rate is reported, never thresholded, else unestimated (see below) 0.01 Region effect BH within each (region type, statistic) family 0.05 Autocorrelation BH across lags 0.05 Abundance island FWER, run-wide over replicons; conditional on the dependence regime 0.05 Operon discordance BH over the both-detected pairs (both_detected_t); pooled level under smooth, monotone σ(abundance) only 0.1 Missed operon decoy FDR 0.1 Category detection (ORA) BH per ontology and direction; every row ora_uncalibrated: not a discovery claim 0.05 GSEA BH per collection; conditional on detection, with no p_detect adjustment 0.05 Determinant model permutation p-value; every null p null_uncalibrated: not a discovery claim 0.05

Every p-value and q-value is reported, not only the significant ones. Every test row has the columns effect, ci_low, ci_high, method and null_model. Where no CI is estimated, ci_low and ci_high are NA and the row carries ci_unestimated. This is the case for:

  • every GSEA row (NES has no CI, ADR-0027);
  • every ORA row (effect = k − E[K | N], with no CI);
  • the autocorrelation lag rows;
  • the operon discordance rows;
  • the P(miss) rows, whose effect is also NA.

The island CI is a different case. It is descriptive and conditional on selection: the window was chosen as the run-wide maximum. The CI therefore under-covers, essentially never contains zero, and its coverage has not been measured. The island's p_value is the only test.

ALT calls. The class error rate estimates the share of erroneous reads among ALT-supporting de novo reads whose spectrum a database search identifies confidently. It is not the false-ALT rate among all ALT reads. It is biased upwards, up to a degenerate value of 1, when the reference search could not contain the ALT peptide. It is biased downwards by spectrum-quality selection. Read a rate of 1 from a reference-proteome search as "not measured" (variants).

docs.title: Methods shipped flagged uncalibrated
docs.text:
These results are reported, but their p- and q-values are not error-controlled. Do not report them as discoveries.

  • Detection enrichment (ORA): ora_uncalibrated on every row. The detection-probability recalibration is anti-conservative for categories selected on TU size or detection probability (ADR-0035, ADR-0037; function). A skipped fit (tu_recal_skipped) is a second reason for the flag.
  • Determinant model null: null_uncalibrated on every null p. The permutation p is valid only when TUs are exchangeable. It fails under autocorrelation along the genome, positional covariates and detection selection (ADR-0034).
  • Operon discordance outside smooth noise. The discordance level holds under smooth, monotone σ(abundance). With a step change in noise at some abundance (the D-1b-step attack), it is exceeded, and no row is flagged (ADR-0055 Amendment 1).
  • Islands at strong, short-resolved autocorrelation. The FWER breaches its level at TU-level ρ = 0.9 when the bootstrap block is short. No row is flagged (see the next section).
  • Variant-call precision (gate M7). The simulated precision gate G1 and the de novo error attacks A6 are strict expected failures. Gate M7 is not recorded as passed. Mass-equivalent and swap ALTs stay high with the flag mass_equivalent (ADR-0049).

docs.title: Islands: the FWER holds in a stated regime
docs.text:
The island FWER is claimed for these cases (islands › Validity domain, ADR-0021 Amendment 1):

  • TU-level autocorrelation ρ ≤ 0.5;
  • ρ = 0.9 on a chromosome of about 4,500 genes, where the block length is long enough.

It is breached at ρ = 0.9 when the block length ℓ′ is 7 or less (0.095 to 0.208 at α = 0.05). It does not apply at all when context.islands.block_len is fixed. No per-row flag marks a breach, because no statistic reliably detects one. The report instead prints, per replicon:

  • the estimated dependence length ℓ̂ (0 means "not estimated", never "no autocorrelation");
  • the block length block_len;
  • the lag-1 Moran's I of the detrended TU scores.

Use these to judge where your data sit.

docs.title: Operons: discordance and P(miss)
docs.text:
• Discordance (test = both_detected_t in pairs.tsv) is one BH family over the pairs with both genes detected. It holds level only under smooth, monotone σ(abundance), and it has little power at realistic effect sizes (operons).
  • P(miss) (test = one_detected_pmiss) is the model's probability that this partner would be missed if it were co-expressed. It is not a significance level. These rows have q_value NA, sit outside the BH family, and never make a discordance call (ADR-0056). P(miss) is anti-conservative when detectability varies between proteins in ways the model does not see. Thresholding it at 0.05 flagged 0.198 of one-detected rows in a simulated null with such variation, where about 0.05 was expected.

docs.title: GSEA is conditional on detection
docs.text:
Abundance GSEA ranks detected genes only. Its results are conditional on detection, with no p_detect adjustment (ADR-0026): when a set's genes are harder to detect, its detected members are selected for high abundance, and the set can look enriched without any true difference. Islands and operon discordance likewise carry no p_detect adjustment.

  • "No significant set" never means "no enrichment".
  • detection_confounded and genomic_cluster are screens, not guarantees: an unflagged row is not certified (function GSEA › Limits).
  • In a collection that has flagged rows, no FDR claim is made for the unflagged rows. Flagged rows enter the same BH family, and their effect on the other rows has not been re-measured for the R engine.

docs.title: Detection tiers
docs.text:
How GIAP decides that a gene is detected depends on what the input contains. The tier is chosen once per run and recorded in the manifest and in genes.tsv (detection_tier). It is the first of the four below that the input allows:

Tier When Detected means Gene error decoy_picked decoy rows with protein_ids exist, at least 80 % of them pair with a gene, and the decoys share a ranking column (q-value, PEP or score) with the targets gene q ≤ 0.01 by picked target–decoy competition over genes gene q-value mayu otherwise, the accepted peptides carry q-values or PEPs; also chosen when decoys exist but pair too rarely (warning decoy_pairing_low) gene q ≤ 0.01 by a MAYU-style estimate of false genes gene q-value two_peptide otherwise, peptide sequences only at least 2 distinct accepted peptides unestimated protein_list proteins only, no peptides a mapped input protein unestimated (inherited from the search engine)

Decoys without a ranking column cannot be picked. Preflight warns about them, and the tier falls back.

Under two_peptide, a gene with only one peptide gets detection_status = single_peptide_unestimated. It counts as not detected in the primary analysis and as detected in the sensitivity rerun. Partial genes at linear contig ends are partial_excluded. detected_2pep (at least 2 distinct accepted peptides) is reported in every tier.

To get the strongest tier, keep the search engine's decoy rows (see Inputs). Details: detection tiers and MAYU gene FDR.

docs.title: Absence of detection is not absence of expression
docs.text:
GIAP says "detected", never "expressed". A gene can go undetected for reasons unrelated to whether it is made. The protein may be:

  • short, with few observable peptides;
  • membrane-bound, or hard to ionise;
  • below the instrument's detection limit;
  • absent from the search database.

To account for this, GIAP fits a detectability model. It predicts each gene's probability of detection (p_detect) from protein covariates, with cross-fitting. Region O − E tests and ORA compare observed detections with the sum of p_detect, never with raw counts. A region "detected less than expected" is detected less than its proteins' detectability predicts. That is a statement about detection, not about transcription or translation. GSEA, islands and operon discordance work on abundances and have no p_detect adjustment (see above).

detectability_constant. The model is replaced by a constant in any of these cases:

  • fewer than 50 detected eligible genes;
  • fewer than 50 undetected eligible genes;
  • fewer TUs than cross-fitting folds.

p_detect is then the overall detection rate for every gene, and every gene carries detectability_constant. The detection tests still run, but without any adjustment for detectability, and ORA uses ω = 1. Treat their results as unadjusted comparisons. "No gene detected" is only an extreme case of this, where the detection-dependent tests are not_estimable.

docs.title: Placement FDR is not search-engine FDR
docs.text:
Two error rates apply to a peptide, and they answer different questions.

  • The search engine's FDR (the input q_value, pep) asks: is this spectrum matched to the right peptide sequence? GIAP inherits it and does not re-estimate it. Engine precursor q-values may themselves under-control FDR, and they do not control gene-level error (GIAP_SPEC.md §8.7). This is why gene detection uses the gene-level tiers. GIAP's pilot validation measures the realised false discovery proportion by entrapment.
  • GIAP's placement FDR (placement_q in peptide_hits.tsv) asks: given the peptide sequence, is it placed on the right locus of this genome? A short peptide can match a genome window by chance, and more so when mismatches are allowed. GIAP estimates this rate by searching the same peptides against decoy translations of the genome (reversed frames, or shuffled frames for de novo input). There is one list per decoy type and per stratum of 0, 1 or 2 differences, with length classes pooled.

A peptide with a search q-value of 0.001 can still have a placement q-value of 1, for example when it matches the genome only with two substitutions. A peptide counts as evidence for a gene only when all of these hold:

  • it passes the search threshold (q_value ≤ input.q_value_max, when a q-value exists);
  • its placement is accepted (placement_q ≤ stats.alpha.placement, or same_db);
  • its locus class assigns it to the gene;
  • its uniqueness is unique or multi_identical;
  • under --genome-relation same, it is an exact hit.

Peptides rejected by placement FDR are in mapping/unmapped.tsv with reason = rejected_placement_fdr.

mapping/mapping_fdr.tsv lists the targets, decoys, π̂_wrong and FDR per length class and number of differences. Its per-length-class rows are descriptive. They are not the q-values: the q-values come from one pooled list per decoy type and stratum. Details: placement FDR › Strata and ranking.

Same-strain input. Peptides searched against this genome's own proteins (search_db = same) skip the decoy step for exact hits: placement_q = 0 and the flag same_db. Tolerant hits still go through it.

docs.title: Kinds of placement
docs.text:
Each row of mapping/peptide_hits.tsv is one peptide at one accepted locus. The columns route, n_diff, diff_types and flags say how the peptide was placed.

Kind How to recognise it What it means Exact route = exact, n_diff = 0, empty diff_types the peptide occurs verbatim in a six-frame translation (I and L treated as equal) Tolerant route = tolerant, n_diff 1 or 2, diff_types from substitution, swap, block, near_block the peptide matches with up to 1 difference at 10–11 aa, or up to 2 at 12–40 aa; peptides shorter than 10 aa are never placed this way Frameshift route = tolerant, diff_types contains frameshift a ±1-nt frameshift: the prefix lies in one frame and the suffix in the adjacent frame, with at least 4 aa on each side

The difference types count one each:

  • substitution: one residue differs;
  • swap: two adjacent residues swapped;
  • block: a mass-equivalent exchange, such as N for GG or Q for AG;
  • near_block: a near-equal mass exchange, such as W for AD or EG;
  • frameshift: the frame shift itself.

Tolerant placements are judged at π̂_wrong = 1, which is conservative. They carry the flag strain_difference when --genome-relation related, and genes with such evidence carry tolerant_evidence.

In mapping/mappings.gff3, a frameshift placement has two match_part children, one per frame. It also has the attribute frameshift_reread (the base read twice) or frameshift_skipped (the base skipped), giving the 1-based position of that base. In mappings.bed, the two parts are BED12 blocks.

Flags on placements (flags column; full list in the flag reference):

  • readthrough: the tolerant alignment substituted a residue for the annotated stop codon at the end of a CDS or sORF (cost 1, recorded as a substitution). This is evidence of stop-codon read-through, or a C-terminal extension (locus class cterm_extension). mappings.gff3 gives the codon's 1-based position as readthrough_codon. Only annotated terminal stops can be read this way; every other stop codon stays unmatchable. Read-through rows are part of the ordinary placement FDR of their stratum. That FDR does not control the read-through subset on its own.
  • sec_site and pyl_site mark peptides that consume a recoded TGA (selenocysteine, U) or TAG (pyrrolysine, O) codon. They are specified in M7-16 (part 16c) but are not in the 1.0 peptide_hits schema. A 1.0 run does not write them.
  • same_db: an exact hit from same-strain input, accepted without the decoy step.
  • low_complexity: the peptide has at most 3 distinct residues, with I and L counted as one. For such peptides, the chance-hit score E can underestimate chance hits by 1.9× to 15×. The decoys keep the q-value valid, and the flag changes nothing in it (ADR-0011).
  • origin_spanning: the placement crosses the origin of a circular replicon.
  • multi, multi_identical: the peptide has accepted loci in more than one locus class, or in identical gene copies. uniqueness (unique, multi_identical, shared) says whether the peptide supports one gene.
  • engine_protein_mismatch: with same-strain input, the gene GIAP chose is not among the engine's protein IDs.
  • nterm_extension_evidence: the peptide lies upstream of the annotated start, in frame.

docs.title: Empty results
docs.text:
A table with only a header means the step ran and found nothing at its threshold. For example, a header-only tables/novel_orfs.tsv means no novel ORF or start-site candidate passed its class FDR. It is a result, not a failure. Also check:

  • that the input allowed the test;
  • the flags on the rows and the run, such as class_fdr_unestimated.

Likewise, an empty islands.tsv or operon_flags.tsv means no window or pair passed. If no gene is detected, the detection-dependent tests are not_estimable.

An empty result is not evidence of absence. Several tests have little or no power by construction:

  • Low islands. At normal detection rates, the low direction is a structural zero. Even a fully undetected window of 20 TUs cannot reach the critical value. No low island is therefore not evidence that no silenced region exists, unless fewer than about a quarter of genes are undetected (islands).
  • Missed operons. With the shipped decoys (convergent and sandwich pairs), this test made no call in the simulation gate or in any attack. It is near-powerless by construction, so an empty list says nothing about missed operons (operons).
  • Operon discordance. Power is near zero at realistic effect sizes, so few or no flagged pairs is the expected outcome even when discordant pairs exist.
  • GSEA. "No significant set" never means "no enrichment" (see GSEA is conditional on detection).

A file that is missing usually means its module was switched off. run_manifest.json lists switched-off modules under modules_off, and they write no files. A missing tool layer (for example, geNOMAD without its database) appears as the run flag layer_missing:<layer> in logs/events.jsonl, and the tests that need it are skipped or marked. The plots of a switched-off module or missing layer are skipped with a reason (module_off:<module>, layer_missing:<layer>).

docs.title: Wording
docs.text: GIAP's own text follows one rule: "detected", never "expressed". The report, the plot titles and the column names all use it. Every number in the report that comes from a statistic carries its error estimate or unestimated. Please keep the same wording when you write about your results.

docs.text:
• geNOMAD is for non-commercial use only. geNOMAD (module mobile) is licensed for non-commercial use. For commercial use, switch the module off: run with --modules core,bgc,function, and install with giap setup --no-genomad.

Other users need a licence from KEGG. Runs with the function module contain KEGG pathway names, and the manifest records the KEGG retrieval date.
  • GPL and AGPL tools run as separate programs.
