docs.title: Building a search database
docs.text:
giap makedb writes a protein FASTA of the strain for your own search engine. It is optional and a convenience only. GIAP never searches spectra (GIAP_SPEC.md §16), and no FDR is built on this database: decoys and FDR are the search engine's job. Every option is listed in the CLI reference.

giap makedb --annotation bakta.json --db-dir /path/to/db --outdir strain_db
giap makedb --annotation bakta.json --six-frame-orfs --min-orf-aa 20 --no-contaminants \
  --outdir strain_db_orfs
Option Meaning --annotation the Bakta JSON of the strain; required in 1.0 (see below) --genome genome FASTA; default: the sequences inside the JSON --outdir the database directory to write (required) --db-dir the giap setup directory with the contaminant library; default $GIAP_DB_DIR --six-frame-orfs add class-tagged six-frame ORFs --min-orf-aa minimum ORF length in aa (default 20; at least 1) --patch an annotation_patch.gff3 from a previous giap run, whose patched proteins are added --no-contaminants do not append the contaminant proteins

docs.title: What it writes
docs.text:
--outdir receives three files:

  • strain_db.faa, the FASTA, wrapped at 60 columns, with no * and no decoys. It holds:
  • the Bakta CDS and sORF proteins, as >{locus_tag} {product};
  • with --patch, the patched proteins;
  • with --six-frame-orfs, the six-frame ORFs of at least --min-orf-aa residues that are not in frame with an annotated CDS, as >GIAPORF_{class}_{contig}_{start}_{end}_{p|m}, with 1-based closed coordinates. The classes are intergenic, cds_outframe, antisense and nterm_extension;
  • the contaminants, as >CONT_{id}, unless --no-contaminants is given.
  • db_id_map.tsv: one row per FASTA record. Coordinates are 1-based closed, and they are unwrapped across the origin (end > length), as in the tables.
  • makedb_manifest.json: the inputs, options and counts.

docs.title: Requirements and errors
docs.text:
• --annotation is required in 1.0. Without it, giap makedb exits with code 2: running Bakta from makedb is not available. Run giap run first, or Bakta yourself.
  • Without --no-contaminants, the contaminant library must be installed (giap setup --contaminants). Otherwise the exit code is 2.
  • An unreadable or inconsistent annotation or patch exits with code 1.

docs.title: Searching with it
docs.text: Search the FASTA with your engine, letting it generate its own decoys. With DIA-NN, use diann --report-decoys so that the decoy rows reach GIAP. Then convert the results with giap convert. Pass --search-db same when the database was built from the genome you run GIAP on. Exact hits then skip the placement decoy step (same_db; see Interpreting results).

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Every run writes the same tree. Every table has a published schema, and every plot comes with the data behind it. Each table's columns, types, units and constraints are in the table reference. The controlled flag values are in the flag reference.

docs.title: The output tree
docs.text:
OUT/
├── run_manifest.json          versions, database versions and checksums, parameters,
│                              input SHA-256, seeds, per-step time and peak memory
├── resolved_config.yaml       the configuration the run used
├── preflight/                 preflight.json, preflight.md
├── annotation/
│   ├── genes.gff3             merged gene model with source-tagged layers
│   ├── regions.tsv, regions.bed
│   ├── promoters.bed, terminators.bed, terminators_crosscheck.tsv
│   ├── operon_pairs.tsv, tus.tsv, id_map.tsv (only with --annotation GFF3/GBFF)
│   └── tools/                 native outputs of each tool (bakta/, uniop/, genomad/, …)
├── mapping/                   peptide_hits.tsv, protein_hits.tsv, unmapped.tsv, mapping_fdr.tsv,
│                              mappings.bed, mappings.probed, mappings.gff3
├── tables/                    genes.tsv (master), detection_summary.tsv, regions_stats.tsv,
│                              autocorrelation.tsv, islands.tsv, pairs.tsv, operons.tsv,
│                              operon_flags.tsv, pileup.tsv.gz, variants.tsv, variants.vcf,
│                              novel_orfs.tsv, novel_orfs.gff3, novel_orfs.faa,
│                              annotation_patch.gff3, category_summary.tsv,
│                              enrichment_detection.tsv, enrichment_gsea.tsv,
│                              determinants_features.tsv, determinants_model.tsv,
│                              determinants_attribution.tsv, sensitivity.tsv
├── plots/                     Vnn_<name>.svg|png|pdf, data/Vnn_<name>.tsv, support/*.tsv
├── report/                    report.html (self-contained)
├── schemas/datapackage.json   Frictionless descriptor of every published table
└── logs/                      events.jsonl, trace.tsv, timeline.html, nf_report.html, <step>.log

Some files sit outside this list. genetable/, context/ and novel/ hold Parquet intermediates that later steps and giap report read. work/ is Nextflow's work directory. These are not part of the published table set, and their layout may change between versions.

Optional modules that are switched off write no files. run_manifest.json lists them under modules_off (mobile, bgc, function). The function module writes category_summary.tsv, enrichment_detection.tsv and enrichment_gsea.tsv.

docs.title: Main tables
docs.text: Table One row per Reference tables/genes.tsv annotated CDS, sORF or pseudogene: identity, context, evidence, detection, abundance, function, flags genes tables/detection_summary.tsv detection by tier, threshold, feature class and replicon detection_summary mapping/peptide_hits.tsv peptide × accepted locus peptide_hits mapping/protein_hits.tsv protein alignment (miniprot, tblastn) protein_hits mapping/unmapped.tsv unmapped or contaminant peptide or protein, with the reason unmapped mapping/mapping_fdr.tsv placement FDR stratum, or de novo precision bin mapping_fdr tables/regions_stats.tsv region or region-type test regions_stats tables/autocorrelation.tsv lag of the autocorrelation tests autocorrelation tables/islands.tsv abundance island islands tables/pairs.tsv, operons.tsv, operon_flags.tsv adjacent gene pair; TU; flagged pair pairs, operons, operon_flags tables/variants.tsv, variants.vcf, pileup.tsv.gz REF/ALT call at a covered codon; pileup variants, pileup tables/novel_orfs.tsv (+ .gff3, .faa, annotation_patch.gff3) novel ORF or start-site candidate novel_orfs tables/category_summary.tsv, enrichment_detection.tsv, enrichment_gsea.tsv function category; enrichment test category_summary, enrichment_detection, enrichment_gsea tables/determinants_*.tsv gene features; model; attribution determinants_features, determinants_model, determinants_attribution tables/sensitivity.tsv sensitivity rerun of a key result sensitivity

docs.title: Table conventions
docs.text:
Aspect Rule Format TSV, UTF-8, one header row, NA for missing values, one entity per row Sort order contig (in input FASTA order), then start, end, strand and ID Column names snake_case, with units in the name: length_aa, distance_bp, abundance_log2, mw_da IDs Bakta locus tags for genes; NOVEL_<contig>_<start>_<p\|m> novel ORFs; <type>_<n> regions; TU_<n>; ISL_<n> islands Booleans true / false Flags a flags column of ;-separated values from the controlled vocabulary Test results every test row has the columns stat, effect, ci_low, ci_high, p_value, q_value, method, null_model, n_perm; values can be NA, with a flag such as ci_unestimated saying why (see Interpreting results) Parquet with --parquet, an optional Parquet twin of large tables Versions schema_version in the manifest; breaking column changes only in major versions

schemas/datapackage.json describes every published table: each column's type, unit and constraints, and the table's coordinate convention (1-based-closed or 0-based-half-open).

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text:
Files Convention TSV tables, GFF3 (genes.gff3, mappings.gff3, novel_orfs.gff3, annotation_patch.gff3) 1-based closed: start and end are the first and last base VCF (variants.vcf) 1-based, positions within [1, length] BED and proBed (regions.bed, promoters.bed, terminators.bed, mappings.bed, mappings.probed) 0-based half-open: start is the 1-based start minus 1, and end is exclusive (equal to the 1-based last base) plots/data/*.tsv 1-based closed, like the tables

Origin-crossing features. On a circular replicon, a feature can run over the origin:

  • TSV and GFF3 keep one record with end > length, an "unwrapped" coordinate. GFF3 marks the replicon with Is_circular=true on its region line. genes.tsv sets crosses_origin = true and the flag crosses_origin.
  • BED and proBed write two records, named <name>_part1 (from the start to the end of the replicon) and <name>_part2 (from base 0 onward).

Linear contigs never wrap.

Example. The values below are illustrative, not from a real run. Take a circular replicon chr1 of 10,000 bp with two genes:

  • G_0001 on the minus strand, covering bases 1,201–2,100;
  • G_0002 on the plus strand, crossing the origin, covering bases 9,801–10,000 and then 1–300.

tables/genes.tsv (1-based closed; selected columns):

locus_tag  contig  start  end    strand  crosses_origin
G_0001     chr1    1201   2100   -       false
G_0002     chr1    9801   10300  +       true

annotation/genes.gff3 (1-based closed; the origin-crossing gene keeps end > length):

##sequence-region chr1 1 10000
chr1  giap  region  1     10000  .  .  .  ID=chr1;Is_circular=true
chr1  Bakta  CDS     1201  2100   .  -  0  ID=G_0001
chr1  Bakta  CDS     9801  10300  .  +  0  ID=G_0002

A BED file of the same genes (0-based half-open; the origin-crossing gene is split in two):

chr1  0     300    G_0002_part2  0  +
chr1  1200  2100   G_0001        0  -
chr1  9800  10000  G_0002_part1  0  +

Peptide placements follow the same rules. In mapping/peptide_hits.tsv, a placement across the origin has end greater than the replicon length, crosses_origin = true and the flag origin_spanning.

docs.title: Plots and report
docs.text: plots/ holds each plot as Vnn_<name>.svg, .png (300 dpi) and .pdf, as set by report.formats and report.dpi. The exact data behind each plot is in plots/data/Vnn_<name>.tsv. report/report.html is a self-contained page. See Plots and report.

docs.title: Manifest
docs.text:
run_manifest.json validates against src/giap/schemas/run_manifest.schema.json. It records:

  • the status (completed or failed) and the exit code;
  • the command line;
  • tool versions, and database versions with their checksums;
  • the resolved parameters and the SHA-256 of every input;
  • the seeds and the detection tier;
  • per-step time and peak memory;
  • skipped steps and modules_off.

giap compare uses the genome SHA-256 recorded here to check that runs share a genome.

docs.title: Platforms
docs.text:
Where GIAP is tested and which execution profiles are supported.

Stub

Filled by M11-09 (platforms).

docs.title: Plots and report
docs.text: GIAP 1.0 builds 16 plots: V1–V3, V5–V8 and V10–V18. Each plot is written to plots/ as Vnn_<name>.svg, .png and .pdf. The exact data drawn is in plots/data/Vnn_<name>.tsv, with coordinates 1-based closed. Plot titles state the finding, and they are generated from the tables. The palettes are colourblind-safe, and a category keeps one colour across all plots.

docs.title: The plots
docs.text:
ID Name Question Data table V01 circos Where in the genome is the proteome? plots/data/V01_circos.tsv V02 abundance_landscape Is abundance clustered along the chromosome? plots/data/V02_abundance_landscape.tsv V03 locus What happens at this prophage, BGC, island or flagged operon? plots/data/V03_locus.tsv (index) and plots/data/V03_locus_<id>.tsv per locus V05 mapping_sankey Where did my sequences go (route and outcome)? plots/data/V05_mapping_sankey.tsv V06 mapping_fdr Can I trust tolerant hits and de novo peptides? plots/data/V06_mapping_fdr.tsv V07 obs_vs_exp Which regions and categories are detected less than detectability predicts? plots/data/V07_obs_vs_exp.tsv V08 cog_abundance Which functions dominate abundance? plots/data/V08_cog_abundance.tsv V10 correlogram Is there structure along the chromosome beyond operons? plots/data/V10_correlogram.tsv V11 operon_pairs Do operon partners look alike, and which other neighbours do too? plots/data/V11_operon_pairs.tsv V12 variants Where do peptides support ALT residues? plots/data/V12_variants.tsv V13 novel_orfs Which new genes or upstream extensions are supported? plots/data/V13_novel_orfs.tsv V14 enrichment Which functions are high or low (GSEA, detection enrichment)? plots/data/V14_enrichment.tsv V15 determinants What explains abundance (promoter, RBS, codon usage)? plots/data/V15_determinants.tsv V16 compare How do runs or search strategies differ? CMP/plots/data/V16_compare.tsv V17 qc Are the inputs sane? plots/data/V17_qc.tsv V18 stat_diagnostics Are the tests calibrated on this dataset? (diagnostics only, see below) plots/data/V18_stat_diagnostics.tsv

Notes on particular plots:

  • V04 and V09 are deferred. V04 was a locus browser and V09 a mass-fraction treemap. Neither is built in 1.0.
  • V03 draws at most report.max_locus_plots loci (50 by default). The loci are prophages and BGCs with a region test, islands and flagged operon pairs (q ≤ stats.alpha.operon_flags). They are ordered by their error value, NA last, then by kind and ID. The error value is the region or operon q-value, or the island's FWER p-value, so one ordering mixes two scales. Novel ORFs are drawn by V13.
  • V18 shows the detectability reliability curve, p-value histograms per test family and null distributions against the observed statistic. These are diagnostics, not a calibration test. The calibration evidence is the simulation suites in the methods notes. A flat histogram does not certify a method that ships flagged uncalibrated (see Interpreting results).
  • V14 belongs to the function module, so it is skipped when that module is off.
  • V16 is written only by giap compare (see Comparing runs). Every other plot is written by giap run and giap report.

A plot whose input is missing is skipped with a reason. The reasons are input_absent:<table>, module_off:<module> and layer_missing:<layer>. When there is nothing to draw, the plot shows an empty state.

Some plots need more data than the plot TSV holds. These extra tables are in plots/support/: replicon_landmarks.tsv, gc_skew.tsv, variant_windows.tsv, gsea_running.tsv, determinants_shap.tsv, determinants_pd.tsv, null_regions.tsv, null_regions_grid.tsv, null_islands.tsv and null_determinants.tsv. Their schemas are in src/giap/schemas/plot_support/, and all but null_regions_grid.tsv are described in the table reference.

Formats and resolution come from report.formats (default svg, png, pdf) and report.dpi (default 300).

docs.title: The report
docs.text:
report/report.html is one self-contained HTML file:

  • Plotly.js, the CSS and the table-sorting script are inlined;
  • it loads nothing from the network;
  • large tables are linked by relative path rather than embedded.

The report has these sections:

  1. Summary
  2. Inputs and quality control (V17)
  3. Peptide mapping (V5, V6)
  4. Gene detection (V7, V18)
  5. Genome context (V1, V2, V10, V3; islands, region tests, autocorrelation)
  6. Operons (V11)
  7. Variants (V12)
  8. Novel ORFs (V13)
  9. Function (V8, V14)
  10. Determinants of abundance (V15)
  11. Sensitivity
  12. Methods
  13. Provenance (a digest of the manifest)

Table sections show the top rows, sortable and filterable, with a link to the full TSV. These plots have an interactive Plotly version in the report: V2, V5, V6, V7, V8, V10, V11, V14, V15, V17 and V18. The others are static SVG.

docs.title: Rebuilding plots and the report
docs.text:
giap report rebuilds plots/ and report/ from the tables of an existing run, without recomputing any statistics. Every option is listed in the CLI reference.

giap report out                       # all plots and the report
giap report out --plots V02,V07       # only these plots, then the report
giap report out --no-interactive      # a static report (no Plotly)
giap report out --strict              # exit 3 if the report exceeds its size budget

By default, giap report reads the run's own resolved_config.yaml, so thresholds, formats and dpi match the run. --config or --set override them, for example --set report.formats=[svg]. Running giap report twice gives identical plots/data/*.tsv.

The report's size budget is 25 MB. Beyond it, --strict exits with code 3.

docs.title: Running GIAP
docs.text:
giap run checks the inputs (preflight), then runs the analysis through Nextflow. It writes the output tree described in Outputs. This page covers the common options. The CLI reference lists every option with its type and default.

giap run --genome genome.fna --peptides peptides.tsv --db-dir /path/to/db --outdir out

docs.title: Check the inputs first
docs.text:
giap preflight --genome genome.fna --peptides peptides.tsv --abundance abundance.tsv --outdir out

giap preflight runs the same input checks as the first step of giap run, in seconds, and runs nothing else. It writes out/preflight/preflight.json and preflight.md. giap run repeats the checks and stops before Nextflow starts when one fails. In run mode, preflight also checks that the tools and databases of the chosen modules and profile are installed.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
Option Input --genome genome FASTA (required) --peptides generic peptide table --proteins protein FASTA --abundance protein abundance table --annotation Bakta JSON, GFF3 or GenBank --reference-peptides same-strain database peptides for the same spectra --replicon-depth contig, mean_depth table --outdir output directory (required) --db-dir database directory of giap setup; default $GIAP_DB_DIR

The formats are described in Inputs.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
--modules takes a comma-separated list chosen from core, mobile, bgc and function. All four run by default.

Module What it adds Needs from giap setup core annotation and context layers, mapping, the gene table, detection, context statistics, operons, variants, novel ORFs and determinants; always on, even when it is not listed Bakta DB (checked even with --annotation bakta.json) and Promotech models; contaminants recommended (they label contaminant peptides) mobile prophage and plasmid regions from geNOMAD --genomad bgc biosynthetic gene clusters from antiSMASH --antismash function COG, GO and KEGG categories, detection enrichment, abundance GSEA --go --kegg --cog 
giap run --genome genome.fna --peptides peptides.tsv --modules core,function --outdir out

A module that is switched off writes no files, and the manifest lists it under modules_off. Later steps run without it. For example, the region tests then have no prophage or BGC regions.

docs.title: Analysis options
docs.text:
Option Values Config key --genome-relation related (default) or same: is the proteomics from this exact strain? genome_relation --abundance-type ibaq, top3, maxlfq, intensity, unknown abundance.type --abundance-scale auto, log2, linear abundance.scale --abundance-missing median, exclude, min, zero, mean abundance.missing --promoters targeted (upstream windows; default) or genome (genome-wide) annotation.promoters.mode --terminators terminatornet (default) or transtermhp annotation.terminators.tool --add-bactermfinder also run BacTermFinder (opt-in) annotation.terminators.bactermfinder --sensitivity basic (default), full, off output.sensitivity --parquet also write Parquet twins of large tables output.parquet

Every option above is a shortcut for a configuration key. Any key can be set with --config FILE or --set key=value (repeatable; the value is YAML). The order of precedence is: defaults, then the config file, then the command-line flags, then --set. An unknown key exits with code 1. The resolved values are written to OUT/resolved_config.yaml and to the manifest. All keys are listed in the configuration reference.

docs.title: Resources and execution
docs.text:
Option Default Meaning --threads 16 (config threads) threads; the upper limit per task --memory 64.GB memory for the workflow --profile farmshare,apptainer comma-joined Nextflow profiles (see Install) --resume off resume a stopped run in the same --outdir

Resuming. --resume passes nextflow -resume to Nextflow. Tasks whose inputs did not change are taken from Nextflow's cache in OUT/work. Give the same inputs and options as the run you resume. Nextflow's work directories can reach tens of GB per run (GIAP_SPEC.md §3.9). Delete OUT/work once the run is complete and you no longer need to resume it.

The --executor option is a developer feature. It is described in the Developer guide, not here.

docs.title: Seeds and reproducibility
docs.text:
Every random draw (permutations, bootstraps, decoy shuffles, cross-fitting folds) comes from one master seed. --seed sets it, and the default is the config value seed. Each step derives its own stream from the master seed and the step name. The same inputs, options and seed therefore give byte-identical tables. The seed is recorded in run_manifest.json.

giap run --genome genome.fna --peptides peptides.tsv --seed 42 --outdir out_seed42

docs.title: Publication mode
docs.text: --publication raises the resamples to 10,000 permutations and 10,000 bootstrap draws (stats.permutations, stats.bootstrap, and the determinants null determinants.permutations). It also records the setting in the manifest. The default is 1,000 of each. Permutation p-values are (1 + b)/(1 + B), where b counts the permuted statistics at least as extreme as the observed one, out of B permutations. With B = 1,000, the smallest attainable p-value is therefore about 0.001. Publication mode lowers that floor. The run takes longer; measured runtimes are on Runtimes.

docs.title: Strict mode
docs.text: --strict turns preflight warnings into a failure: the run stops before Nextflow starts, with exit code 3. Without --strict, warnings are reported in preflight/preflight.md and the run continues. giap preflight --strict behaves the same way. giap report --strict exits with code 3 when the report exceeds its size budget.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Every giap command uses the same exit codes:

Exit code Meaning 0 success 1 invalid input: preflight errors, a bad option or an unknown configuration key 2 environment error: a tool, database or model is missing (for example nextflow not on PATH, or a giap setup source that cannot be reached) 3 warnings were raised and --strict was given 4 a pipeline step failed 5 internal error (a bug); the message asks you to report it

When a step fails, the manifest names it and points to its log: failed_step and failed_log, from OUT/logs/trace.tsv. An internal error writes OUT/logs/internal_error.log. Please report it at https://github.com/khoa-yelo/giap/issues with the command line and that log.

docs.title: Logs
docs.text:
OUT/logs/ holds the following:

  • events.jsonl: structured warnings and events, one per line;
  • trace.tsv, timeline.html and nf_report.html: Nextflow's task trace and reports;
  • <step>.log for a step that failed.

--log-level (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR) sets how much is printed to the terminal.

docs.title: Runtimes
docs.text:
This page will hold the measured wall-clock times of a standard giap run, from scripts/slurm/benchmark_standard.sbatch (M10-12). Each row will give the median of three runs, with the node class, the date and the GIAP commit. The numbers will come from benchmarks/baseline.json › standard_run and the M10-12 decision record.

Status: pending (M10-12). No standard-run benchmark has been committed yet. The table below is empty on purpose: GIAP's documentation states no runtime that has not been measured.

Run Median (h:mm) Range of 3 runs Peak memory (GiB) Threads / memory Node class Date Commit E. coli K-12, all modules pending (M10-12) pending (M10-12) pending (M10-12) 16 / 64 GB pending (M10-12) — — E. coli K-12, --modules core pending (M10-12) pending (M10-12) pending (M10-12) 16 / 64 GB pending (M10-12) — —

What affects the runtime, qualitatively:

  • --publication raises permutations and bootstrap draws from 1,000 to 10,000;
  • --promoters genome predicts promoters genome-wide instead of in upstream windows;
  • Bakta runs unless --annotation bakta.json is given, and the full database is slower than the light one;
  • the optional modules: antiSMASH (bgc) and geNOMAD (mobile).

Nextflow writes per-task times and peak memory to OUT/logs/trace.tsv and OUT/logs/nf_report.html. The manifest records per-step time and peak memory.

Run

docs.title: Steps that ran
docs.text:
There were 48 tasks: ANNOTATE (19 processes, including 20 PROMOTER_CALCULATOR tasks), MAPPING (5), GENETABLE (2), CONTEXT (2) and OPERONS (1).

  • annotate:
  • PARSE_BAKTA, CODON_USAGE
  • UNIOP_INPUT, UNIOP, OPERON_PAIRS
  • PROMOTER_WINDOWS, PROMOTECH, PROMOTER_CALCULATOR x20, PROMOTER_LAYER
  • TRANSTERM_INPUT, TRANSTERMHP, TERMINATORNET, TERMINATOR_LAYER
  • OSTIR_INPUT, OSTIR, RBS_LAYER
  • TX_LAYER, REGION_LAYER, CONTEXT_LAYERS
  • mapping: SIXFRAME_INDEX, MAP_EXACT, MAP_TOLERANT, PLACEMENT, LOCI.
  • gene table: GENE_TABLE, DETECTABILITY.
  • context: CONTEXT_STATS, SENSITIVITY.
  • operons: OPERONS_STEP (#155).
  • BAKTA did not run. This is #163 working as intended: --annotation bakta.json is now the precomputed Bakta layer, so resolved_config.yaml has annotation.precomputed.bakta_json set. In 1864792 Bakta light ran for 32 min with an 11 GB peak RSS.
  • No M6-02 / M7 / M8 step is wired into the run. workflow/main.nf includes only ANNOTATE, MAPPING, GENETABLE, CONTEXT and OPERONS. src/giap/steps/ has no gsea, determinants, novel-ORF or variant step. The OPERONS step still runs discordance pass 1, with no detection-limit model: giap.steps.operons imports NO_DL_MODEL and does not use giap.operons.detection_limit. So #157 (M6-02), #161 (M7-06), #162/#166 (M8-07/08) and #171/#174 (M8-05/05b) are library code only. This run does not exercise them.

The critical path is now TERMINATORNET: 6 min 1 s realtime at 384 % CPU, against 3 min 41 s in 1864792. It is now the longest task, followed by PROMOTECH (1 min 38 s, 7.4 GB RSS).

docs.title: Schema validation
docs.text:
Every published TSV whose stem has a schema in src/giap/schemas/tables was validated with frictionless. The method is the same as tests/helpers/m4_chain.validate: the descriptor minus the coordinates extension, then Resource.validate(). The script is in the session scratchpad and was run with the venv python and PYTHONPATH=src.

13 of 13 tables are VALID, and every schema in the directory has a published table:

Table Rows (this run) Rows (1864792) Byte-identical? mapping/mapping_fdr.tsv 48 48 yes mapping/peptide_hits.tsv 1645 1645 no (gene IDs are now GSIM_, not KABHIH_) mapping/protein_hits.tsv 0 0 yes mapping/unmapped.tsv 24 24 yes tables/genes.tsv 87 not published new tables/autocorrelation.tsv 163 not published new tables/islands.tsv 0 (header only) not published new tables/detection_summary.tsv 119 87 no tables/regions_stats.tsv 4 4 no (crispr_1 end 62809 becomes 62799) tables/sensitivity.tsv 2 2 yes tables/pairs.tsv 92 88 no tables/operons.tsv 20 16 no tables/operon_flags.tsv 0 (header only) 0 yes

docs.title: Differences from the previous runs
docs.text:
1. The gene model now matches the search IDs. engine_protein_mismatch_rate fell from 0.9951 to 0.00061 (n = 1644), which is the defect #163 fixed. Locus tags are the simulator's GSIM_00005 and onward, not Bakta's KABHIH_0001 and onward.
  2. Gene table: 87 genes, previously 86.
  3. Feature types: 82 cds, 3 sorf and 2 pseudogene. Previously all 86 were cds from real Bakta.
  4. 85 genes have an abundance, previously 82. All 87 have a tu_id.
  5. Flags: detectability_constant 87, top3_lt3 3, shared_evidence 2, pseudogene 2. nterm_extension_evidence (previously 1) is gone.
  6. The simulator truth has 84 genes.
  7. TUs and pairs.
  8. 20 TUs, previously 16; the truth has 35.
  9. 92 pairs, previously 88. By class: OP 67, CV 9, DV 9, SW 6, NO 1. Previously: OP 70, CV 7, DV 7, SW 3, NO 1.
  10. 20 PROMOTER_CALCULATOR tasks, previously 16.
  11. detection_summary has 119 rows, previously 87.
  12. The 18 tier rows are now present (the open MVP-02 item is resolved on main).
  13. basic has 49 rows, previously 35: feature_class rows went from 14 to 28 because of the new sorf and pseudogene classes.
  14. New published tables (M5 merges): genes.tsv, autocorrelation.tsv and islands.tsv. Two context Parquets are also new: context/gene_context.parquet and context/island_diagnostics.parquet.
  15. Warnings are unchanged. The task .command.err files carry the same set as 1864792:
  16. layer_missing:genomad and layer_missing:antismash, from region_layer and context_layers;
  17. from gene_table: contract.tus.extra_column (upstream_start, upstream_end) and contract.id_map.missing_file;
  18. cai_reference_missing, from codon_usage;
  19. detectability_constant (p_detect = overall detected share 0);
  20. a SciPy/NumPy version UserWarning inside the giap-uniop micromamba env.

logs/events.jsonl has 4 events: environment.resources, the two layer_missing events, and operons.missed_operons (all bins 0). 7. Nextflow warns There's no process matching config selector: BLAST. This warning was also in 1864792.

docs.title: Surprising: no gene is detected, and every downstream test is empty
docs.text:
All 87 genes have detected = false, and p_detect is constant at 0. Because of that: - every pair has test = none, and the flags are too_few_op_pairs;unestimated; - operon_flags.tsv is empty; - every autocorrelation row is not_estimable; - islands.tsv is empty; - operons.tsv has detected_frac = 0 for every TU.

1864792 showed the same picture (86/86 undetected), which was attributed to the ID mismatch. #163 fixed the mismatch, but zero detection remains. Root cause, from the outputs and code:

  • gene_q_value is 0.011765 = 1/85 for every gene with evidence.
  • giap.genetable.detection computes the picked-protein FDR as (D(t)/f + 1) / T(t). There are no winning decoys, so D = 0, and T = 85, which gives a floor of 1/85.
  • stats.alpha.identification is 0.01 (the default; resolved_config.yaml is the same as 1864792 apart from bakta_json).
  • So no gene can reach q <= 0.01 on a genome with fewer than 100 evidenced genes. The q-threshold rows in detection_summary confirm this:
q threshold genes detected 0.001, 0.005, 0.01 0 0.02, 0.05, 0.10 85

There are 83 2-peptide detections.

This is a property of sim100k's size together with the +1 correction and the default alpha. It is not a pipeline failure. But it means that sim100k with default config cannot exercise any detection-dependent statistics (M4 regions, M5 autocorrelation and islands, M6 operon tests). The M4-21 golden used alpha 0.05, where 85 genes are detected.

Decisions for the lead (this run changed nothing): - use a larger simulated genome for the MVP run, or - set an alpha of 0.05 for this validation through a run config, or - accept that example 1 ("every test none") holds here only trivially.

docs.text:
Slurm head job 1867835 giap-run-valmvp-a05 (wheat-02) State / exit COMPLETED, 0:0; 48 tasks, 0 failed, 0 cached Wall time 9 min 1 s (08:49:31 to 08:58:32 PDT) Output $GIAP_ROOT/runs/val-mvp-2026-10-22-a05/OUT Run config $GIAP_ROOT/runs/val-mvp-2026-10-22-a05/run_config.yaml, passed as --config

docs.text:
All 13 of 13 tables are VALID (frictionless, same method as section 1):

Table Rows Compared with 1867783 mapping_fdr 48 byte-identical peptide_hits 1645 byte-identical protein_hits 0 byte-identical unmapped 24 byte-identical genes.tsv 87 differs autocorrelation 163 differs islands 0 same (header only) detection_summary 119 differs regions_stats 4 byte-identical sensitivity 2 byte-identical pairs 92 differs operons 20 differs operon_flags 13 was 0

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
• Detected genes: 85 of 87. The 2 not detected are the simulated pseudogenes GSIM_00065 and GSIM_00255. They have 0 peptides and their gene q is NA, so this is correct.
  • Every detected gene still has q = 1/85 = 0.0118.
  • 83 genes are detected with 2 or more peptides.
  • p_detect is still constant, now at 0.977 (detectability_constant). With only 2 non-detected genes, the detectability model has nothing to fit. This is expected.
  • Pair tests:
  • both_detected_t (student_t, within_operon_t) ran on 65 of the 67 OP pairs. The other 2 OP pairs each involve a pseudogene and are no_detection_limit_model;unestimated, because M6-02 is not wired.
  • CV, DV, NO and SW pairs are untested by design.
  • Results: 0 pairs at q ≤ 0.1, 5 at p ≤ 0.05, 0 at p ≤ 0.01. The minimum q is 0.44.
  • The p-values look about uniform (deciles 0.12 / 0.25 / 0.54 / 0.85 / 0.93).
  • Every tested row carries ci_unestimated, as decision pass 1 intends.
  • operon_flags: 13 rows, all conflict_terminator_in_operon. Each is an OP pair with both promoter and terminator evidence between the genes and a concordant abundance pattern. Their q values are 0.84 to 0.99 and lfdr is NA.
  • Autocorrelation:
  • chr1: 79 of 80 Moran's I and join-count rows are estimable, all with p values. One tu_block join-count row is not_estimable. Results: 0 at p ≤ 0.05 and 0 at q ≤ 0.05. The join counts are degenerate: BB = 81 and p = 1, because nearly every gene is detected.
  • plasmid_1 (2 genes): all 80 rows are not_estimable (few_values).
  • The 3 oriter_slope rows are descriptive, and all bootstrap CIs include 0 (pooled 1.04, CI -1.21 to 3.68).
  • Islands: 0 rows.
  • regions_stats is the same as in 1867783.
  • plasmid_1: small_region, n_eligible 2.
  • crispr_1: no genes.
  • bgc_1 and prophage_1 from the sim truth are never tested. The geNOMAD and antiSMASH layers are missing, and this run, like 1864792, does not pass the sim's config.yaml with annotation.precomputed.regions.

docs.title: Comparison with the sim truth
docs.text:
sim100k is a global null for abundance. The default proteomics path draws giapsim.proteomics.gene_log_abundance, which is i.i.d. N(1, 1.5) on the natural-log scale. So there is no TU co-expression, no positional autocorrelation, no ori-ter gradient and no region effect. M4's TU/AR(1) expression model is opt-in and is not used by SIM100K.

So the expected number of true rejections is 0, and every family returned 0: - 65 pair tests: 0 at q ≤ 0.1. About 3.3 p ≤ 0.05 are expected by chance; 5 were observed. - 79 Moran's I and join-count rows: 0. - islands: 0. - slopes: every CI covers 0.

Example 1 ("every test none or nothing significant") now holds non-trivially.

docs.title: What looks odd, statistically
docs.text:
1. Within-operon |Δ log2| is large: median 2.0 and up to 8.8 for truth TU-mates. That is what i.i.d. abundance implies (SD of a difference ≈ 1.5·√2/ln 2 ≈ 3.1 log2). The within-operon t fit therefore models null noise. On this sim the discordance test cannot show power; it can only show calibration. Measuring power needs a sim with TU-coherent abundance.
  2. TU calls are coarse: 20 called TUs against 35 in the truth.
  3. Of the 67 called OP pairs, 22 straddle a truth TU boundary.
  4. |Δ| for those 22 (mean 2.48) is no different from truth TU-mates (2.72), again because of the i.i.d. abundance.
  5. The 13 conflict_terminator_in_operon flags are mostly right: 12 of the 13 flagged pairs cross a truth TU boundary. The terminator evidence catches real UniOP/TU merge errors.
  6. The gene q-value is a single value (1/85) for all detected genes. The tier table puts 0 genes at q ≤ 0.01 and 85 at q ≥ 0.02. This is the 1/T floor from section 1. Detection is all-or-nothing between α = 0.01 and 0.02 on this genome.
  7. Detectability cannot be checked here. It is constant in both runs: 0 detected at α = 0.01, and 85 of 87 at α = 0.05.
